title: [bug] False 'Pass tampered' — BC re-encodes signedAttrs as sorted DER, breaking signatures made over the original wire order
description:
Real-world pkpasses that verify in Apple Wallet, Google Wallet, FossWallet and OpenSSL are rejected by Walt as ParseResult.Tampered(ManifestSignatureMismatch), producing a false security accusation on a cryptographically sound pass.

REPRODUCED on JVM (passes-core, BC 1.84) with a real Deutschlandticket signed by pass.de.digital-h.ride. Same issuer as GH walt-passes-android#176.

ROOT CAUSE (proven bit-for-bit):
The signer computes the signature over the SignedAttributes SET in the element order they appear on the wire. That order is NOT DER-sorted:
  contentType (SEQ len 0x18), messageDigest (0x23), signingTime (0x1c)
DER SET-OF requires ascending byte order of the encodings: 0x18, 0x1c, 0x23.

BouncyCastle's SignerInformation.verify() re-encodes the attributes with ASN1Encoding.DER, which SORTS them, then hashes. Same length (95 bytes), different bytes:
  SHA1(wire order)  = b58870852561242b2cc2d02b1c348583259f3e78  <- matches the DigestInfo recovered from the RSA block
  SHA1(sorted DER)  = d8bf5aa9b2cc97115340943f8be9e1a9fc750277  <- what BC hashes
So signer.verify() returns false, verifyMath() maps that to TamperReason.ManifestSignatureMismatch.

The pass is NOT tampered. Independently confirmed:
  - all 10 manifest SHA-1 entries match the archive bytes exactly; no extra/missing entries
  - signed messageDigest attribute == SHA-1(manifest.json)
  - raw RSA decrypt yields a well-formed PKCS#1 v1.5 SHA-1 DigestInfo whose digest equals SHA1(wire-order attrs)
  - openssl smime -verify -noverify succeeds
  - SHA1withRSA over the wire-order bytes verifies = true; over BC's sorted DER = false

NOT the cause: the EKU/purpose hypothesis in GH#176. PKIX path building with the bundled Apple anchors SUCCEEDS for this leaf when evaluated inside its validity window, Apple pass EKU and all. The reporter's 'unsuitable certificate purpose' is OpenSSL's own X509_PURPOSE S/MIME check, which this kernel never performs. Also, under the lenient default ParserConfig a chain failure yields SignatureStatus.CertChainIncomplete, never Tampered — so no chain/EKU issue can produce this alert.

FIX (proven working): in verifyMath, verify the signature over the ORIGINAL wire encoding of the signed attributes rather than BC's re-sorted DER. Navigate the raw CMS to SignerInfo[3] ([0] IMPLICIT signedAttrs), re-tag to SET (0x31) preserving parsed order (DLSet + ASN1Encoding.DL reproduces it exactly), and verify against that. Keep the DER attempt first and use wire-order only as a fallback.

Security posture is NOT weakened: the fallback still requires (a) the messageDigest attribute to equal SHA-1(manifest.json) and (b) a valid RSA signature by the leaf over the exact attribute bytes as received. That is precisely the check OpenSSL/Apple/Google perform. Any real byte change to the manifest or attributes still fails.

FOLLOW-ON: after the fix, a current (non-expired) pass from this issuer chains to the bundled Apple Root CA and reads AppleVerified. The specific expired sample reads CertChainIncomplete ('Unverified · signature not verified'), which is correct behaviour for an expired leaf.

Note: bundled intermediates are WWDR G3 and G6; this issuer uses G4, which ships inside the envelope so path building still works. Consider bundling G4.
notes:
Reviewed adversarially + /security-review + /cole-branch-review on branch wpass-x70-signedattrs-wire-order (pushed).

VERDICT: core fix is cryptographically sound. Security review found no HIGH/MEDIUM vulns. Key confirmation (BC 1.84 bytecode): SignerInformation.doVerify runs verifyContentTypeAttributeValue, verifyAlgorithmIdentifierProtectionAttribute (RFC 6211), verifyMessageDigestAttribute and verifyCounterSignatureAttribute — all throwing plain CMSException — BEFORE contentVerifier.verify(). verifyMath catches only CMSSignerDigestMismatchException, so the fallback is reachable ONLY after those checks passed. Also confirmed BC's SignedData/SignerInfo parse picks the same signerInfos (last untagged element) and the same index-3 signedAttrs as the hand parse, so no parser differential.

Follow-up commit 476fd7e fixes three review findings (no change to which passes verify):
1. Fallback could throw (digest OID, leaf conversion, Signature.getInstance, getObjectAt(3) OOB) -> outer runCatching relabelled ManifestSignatureMismatch as SignatureCryptoFailure. Now folded to false + index bounds checks.
2. Digest and signature read two independent parses; unified into one WireSignedAttributes so the property is local instead of resting on BC-internals reasoning.
3. soleMessageDigestValue requires exactly one messageDigest attr with exactly one OCTET STRING (was first-match). Defense-in-depth: BC throws on duplicates first, so currently unreachable.
Tests: added multi-signer fail-closed (mutation-tested: deleting the single-signer guard makes it verify) and duplicate-messageDigest. Docs: fixed stale 'we do not re-roll our own digest comparison' paragraph.

NOT FIXED (deliberate): RSASSA-PSS params are not propagated in the fallback's Signature.getInstance — causes false negatives only, and Apple uses PKCS#1 v1.5. Filed as follow-up if PSS passes ever appear.
close_reason: Fixed and merged as PR #194 (squash 824abc5). Wire-order signedAttrs fallback + review hardening. All CI green (build/quality, connected tests API 28/31/34/36, dependency review).

title: ManifestVerifier HexFormat usage crashes on API 28-33
description:
passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/internal/ManifestVerifier.kt:152 holds 'private val HEX: HexFormat = HexFormat.of()' at file scope. java.util.HexFormat was added to AOSP at API 34. On API 28-33 (Android 9-13) the file's <clinit> throws NoClassDefFoundError the first time ANY ManifestVerifierKt function is called, which means every signed pkpass import crashes.

Caught by walt-android SignedPkpassImportSmokeTest on the API 30 emulator job. See walt-android PR walt-app/android#224 for the failure trace.

Fix: replace HEX.parseHex(hex) with a manual hex-to-bytes loop, or use Integer.parseInt(substring, 16) over 2-char windows. Either works back to API 1.

Walt-android currently has minSdk=28. Until this is fixed, every Walt user on Android 9-13 importing a signed pkpass crashes.
notes: Fixed on branch wpass-g00. PR walt-app/walt-passes-android#93. Replaced HexFormat with Character.digit-based decoder. Awaiting merge, then walt-android needs to bump its passes-android dependency.
close_reason: Fixed in PR walt-app/walt-passes-android#93 (squash-merged as 493ffc7). HexFormat replaced with Character.digit-based hex decoder, safe back to API 1. All passes-storage connected tests across API 28/31/34/36 are green on the merge commit.

title: SqlCipherDatabaseFactory: DDL or PRAGMA fails on first open, surfaces as DatabaseCorrupt (FP4 / Walt waltDebug)
description:
Symptom: On a fresh waltDebug install on FP4 (Android 16, target 36), opening the Passes screen shows "Passes unavailable - Secure storage is unavailable". EventLogger emits passes_storage_failure[kind=Unknown, unknown_kind=DatabaseCorrupt] twice in quick succession.

Critical fact: passes_key_provider_initialized[backing=Tee] fired earlier in the same session (during ImportPassActivity launch). So the keystore master key resolved to TEE backing and the DatabaseKey unwrap succeeded. The failure is downstream of key derivation.

Repository: walt_passes.db lands at /data/data/is.walt.app/databases/walt_passes.db, 61440 bytes, file mtime matches the moment passes_key_provider_initialized fired. So SQLiteDatabase.openOrCreateDatabase at SqlCipherDatabaseFactory.kt:48 succeeded and created the on-disk file. Failure is between line 48 and line 91 (transaction-success). Suspect surfaces:
- Line 54: db.execSQL("PRAGMA cipher_compatibility = 4")
- Line 55: db.execSQL("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
- Line 121: readSchemaVersionIfPresent
- Line 82: db.beginTransaction()
- Line 84: Schema.DDL execSQL loop
- Line 87: INSERT OR REPLACE INTO schema_meta

The catch at line 92 wraps the throw as DatabaseCorrupt (with a `cause`), but only the kind tag is propagated to telemetry. The `cause` never reaches logcat. So the actual exception type and message are unknown. This is the diagnostic blocker — we need to know whether it is e.g. SQLiteException("file is not a database"), SQLiteAccessPermException, SQLiteFullException, an IllegalStateException from beginTransaction, etc.

Additional artifact in same logcat:
- Closeable leak warning: "A resource was acquired at attached stack trace but never released" with stack pointing at SqlCipherDatabaseFactory.openOrCreate$lambda$0:48, DatabaseKey.withBytes:49, ..., PassesModule.providePassesRuntime:131. Indicates that on the failure path the DB connection is acquired but db.close() never runs. The catch block at line 94 IS calling db.close(), so either db.close() itself throws, or the throw originates BEFORE the try (i.e. during the PRAGMA execSQL on lines 54-55, which has no surrounding try-finally).

Actionable fixes (independent of root cause):
1. Wrap PRAGMA calls and the entire post-openOrCreate block in a try {...} catch-rethrow that closes the db. Today only the DDL/INSERT block is guarded; the PRAGMA pair is not.
2. Add the catch-cause exception class + message to telemetry for DatabaseCorrupt. Without it every storage failure on a real device is opaque. Add EVENT_STORAGE_FAILURE keys: cause_class, cause_message_redacted (or first 80 chars).
3. Once cause is logged, root-cause the actual SQLCipher exception. Hypotheses:
   - SQLCipher native library mismatch / version skew between the prebuilt .so and the JNI binding
   - PRAGMA cipher_compatibility = 4 rejected because compile-time SQLCIPHER_VERSION differs
   - foreign_keys=ON inside an open connection failing for a reason
   - A DDL statement in Schema.DDL is malformed for the SQLCipher fork on Android
   - DB created in a partial state, header page 0 not flushed before the next pragma reads it back
4. The leak warning suggests adding .use {} or try-finally around the SQLiteDatabase handle for the entire setup phase.

Reproduction:
- Device: FP4, Android 16, BSP unknown
- App: is.walt.app waltDebug, AGP 9.0.1, target 36, SqlCipher 4.5.4
- Steps:
  1. Fresh install: ./gradlew :app:installWaltDebug
  2. Launch any flow that touches PassesRuntime (open ImportPassActivity for a pkpass, OR open the Passes list screen)
  3. Observe passes_storage_failure[kind=Unknown, unknown_kind=DatabaseCorrupt] in logcat
  4. UI: "Passes unavailable - Secure storage is unavailable"

This is independent of wpass-4js (Apple-signed parser bug). Both can hit on the same install. Discovered 2026-05-07 during wlt-a07 smoke test.
notes:
2026-05-07 — PR #52 merged to main as 239ba63 (squash). All CI green: build, connected tests on API 28/31/34/36, dependency review.

Worktree passes-android-wpass-aio-cipher-hook removed; local + remote branch wpass-aio-cipher-hook deleted.

Issue stays OPEN pending FP4 device verification (the on-device repro is conclusive; CI only proves the test-harness path on emulators). Verification steps remain as listed in the prior fix-attempt notes block.
close_reason: Verified fixed on FP4 / Android 16 / waltDebug 2026-05-07 19:06 with kernel commit 239ba63 (passes-storage: route cipher_compatibility through SQLiteDatabaseHook). Three independent process launches against the same on-disk walt_passes.db all succeeded: process #1 imported the chroniques pkpass and emitted parse_succeeded[AppleVerified] + pass_upserted; process #2 (after adb am force-stop) opened the existing DB and emitted pass_rendered[AppleVerified] twice; process #3 (subsequent app launch) emitted key_provider_initialized cleanly. No passes_storage_failure events. The cipher_compat ordering hypothesis was correct: pinning compat=4 through SQLiteDatabaseHook makes the PRAGMA fire before page-1 decode, regardless of whether openOrCreateDatabase is creating or opening.

title: Parser rejects valid Apple-signed pkpass: SKI signer-ID code path unexercised by tests
description:
Real Apple-signed pkpass (Tixly Chroniques ticket; passTypeIdentifier=pass.com.tixly, team A6DLLVNVR7, AWDR G4 chain) is rejected by DefaultPassParser as ParseResult.Tampered when consumed via Walt Android (composite-build integration, waltDebug, FP4 / Android 16). Same byte-identical file:
- shasum -a 256 manifest.json == messageDigest octet-string in CMS signedAttrs (digests match)
- All 12 SHA-1 entries in manifest.json match actual zip-entry contents (no FileHashMismatch)
- openssl cms -verify -in signature -inform DER -content manifest.json -noverify -binary  -> exit 0 (signature math passes)
- Google Wallet imports and renders the pass (visual confirmation)

So the file is not tampered; the parser is wrong.

Strongest hypothesis: the SKI signer-ID code path in SignatureVerifier.firstSignerWithCert (passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/internal/SignatureVerifier.kt:155) has never had test coverage. TestCryptoSupport.cmsDetachedSignature at TestCryptoSupport.kt:115-133 calls JcaSignerInfoGeneratorBuilder(...).build(contentSigner, signerCert) which defaults BC to IssuerAndSerialNumber. To synthesize an Apple-realistic pkpass the helper would need the .build(contentSigner, byte[] subjectKeyIdentifier) overload. The chroniques pkpass uses SubjectKeyIdentifier d855f277d5926af02e384c26ac9a640f99086aae (confirmed in CMS dump).

If signer.sid is an SKI sid and signedData.holderStore().getMatches(signer.sid.asHolderSelector()) returns empty (e.g. because BC SKI-matcher disagrees with Apple SKI encoding for any reason), firstSignerWithCert returns null and verifyAndClassify returns SignatureVerifyResult.Failed(TamperReason.SignatureCryptoFailure). UI surfaces that as Tampered. Telemetry only logs outcome=Tampered (not the specific TamperReason) so this is invisible from logcat.

Reproduction: a sanitized version of the failing pkpass is at /Users/bittelc/workspace/walt/android/android-wlt-a07/docs/smoke-test-wlt-a07/samples/golden.pkpass on the Walt Android worktree; consider adding it (or an equivalently SKI-signed Apple-developer-supplied sample) as a passes-core test fixture.

Action plan:
1. Add a real-Apple-signed (or at minimum SKI-signer-ID) test fixture to passes-core test resources.
2. Extend TestCryptoSupport with an SKI-signer-ID variant of cmsDetachedSignature so tests can exercise both signer-ID flavors.
3. Add a SignatureVerifierTest case that asserts ParseResult.Success for an SKI-signed input.
4. Hardening: if firstSignerWithCert returns null, distinguish the failure mode in TamperReason rather than collapsing to SignatureCryptoFailure (currently the only signal).

Cross-ref Walt Android: filed originally as wlt-x4x; this issue supersedes that one. wlt-a07 (smoke test) is blocked on this fix.

Diagnosed 2026-05-07 during wlt-a07 smoke test on FP4.
notes:
Fix shipped in PR #50 (https://github.com/walt-app/walt-passes-android/pull/50).

Root cause was upstream of the bd's SKI-path hypothesis: ensureBouncyCastleRegistered's getProvider("BC") == null guard short-circuited on Android (where AOSP ships a stripped-down BC under the "BC" slot), so the unbundled bcprov-jdk18on:1.79 was never registered and setProvider("BC") resolved to Android's stripped instance. The stripped BC mishandles CMS / PKCS#7 verification, surfacing every Apple-signed pkpass as Failed.

Fix: SignatureVerifier now holds its own BouncyCastleProvider instance and passes it directly to JcaSimpleSignerInfoVerifierBuilder, JcaX509CertificateConverter and CertPathBuilder via their Provider-instance overloads, bypassing JCE name lookup entirely.

Hardening (per bd action plan item 4): new TamperReason.SignerCertificateMissing arm distinguishes "envelope parses but signer cert absent" from the catch-all SignatureCryptoFailure.

Coverage:
- realAppleSignedPkpassVerifiesEvenWhenBcSlotHoldsAStrippedProvider: parks a non-BC provider in the "BC" slot; verified to FAIL pre-fix (returns Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure), exact field-observed shape) and PASS post-fix.
- realAppleSignedPkpassFixtureVerifies: end-to-end against a real Apple-signed manifest+signature pair (Tixly Chroniques) committed under passes-core/src/test/resources/.../apple-signed/.
- appleVerifiedWhenSignerIdIsSubjectKeyIdentifier + manifestSignatureMismatchForSkiSignerWithTamperedManifest: synthetic SKI signer-ID happy and tampered paths via new cmsDetachedSignatureWithSki helper in TestCryptoSupport.
- signerCertificateMissingWhenSignerIdMatchesNoCertInEnvelope: locks the new TamperReason arm.

All 176 passes-core tests + detekt pass on JVM. wlt-a07 smoke test on FP4 unblocked once PR merges and walt-android picks up the kernel via composite build.
close_reason: Verified fixed on FP4 / Android 16 / waltDebug 2026-05-07. After bafa926 (passes-core: hold BouncyCastle instance, not BC name lookup) the chroniques pkpass imports cleanly. EventLogger emits passes_pass_rendered[pass_type=EventTicket, signature_band=AppleVerified] - signature validates to Apple trust anchor, full happy path through parse -> upsert -> list -> detail -> render. The instance-passing pattern bypasses the AOSP BC stub that was shadowing bcprov-jdk18on 1.79.

title: BarcodeView ignores messageEncoding: non-Latin-1 barcode payloads render as '?' and fail to scan
description:
Source: external security review of the kernel at 194c2b6 (received 2026-09-14).

BarcodeView.kt:97 calls MultiFormatWriter().encode with no EncodeHintType.CHARACTER_SET, and the remember key (line 50) omits messageEncoding. ZXing 3.5.4 defaults QR to ISO-8859-1, so Ticket-東京-123 declared utf-8 round-trips as Ticket-??-123. The code looks valid but no longer encodes the issuer's payload. Walt ships this on the pass detail card (walt android WaltPassTicketCard.kt:207). Inconsistent with ZxingBarcodeEncoder, which already sets UTF-8.

Fix: map messageEncoding to a Charset and pass it as CHARACTER_SET; include it in the remember key; an unsupported or unencodable charset renders the existing explicit error state rather than a silently altered payload. Add an encode/decode round-trip test per format with non-Latin-1 input.

title: Single-pass extractor has no cumulative inflate budget: ~200 KB pkpass OOMs the host
description:
Source: external security review of the kernel at 194c2b6 (received 2026-09-14).

SafeArchiveExtractor enforces maxEntryBytes (4 MB) and maxEntries (256) but no cumulative inflated-size cap, so up to ~1 GB can be retained before manifest/signature checks. Its own comment notes CumulativeSize is unreachable in single-archive mode. Reviewer reproduced: 48 x 4 MB entries in a ~195 KB zip hit an uncaught OutOfMemoryError on a 128 MB JVM heap. Parsing runs in the app process; delivery via email/share/pass-link fetch crashes Walt on import.

Fix: add a ParserConfig cumulative cap and pass an InflateBudget (ArchiveStreams.kt, already used by PassBundleReader) into drainOrStore, checked while inflating before retaining bytes. Map to ResourceLimitExceeded. Add a bomb test that asserts a typed failure rather than OOM.

title: Pass replacement identity omits passTypeIdentifier: unrelated passes overwrite each other
description:
Source: external security review of the kernel at 194c2b6 (received 2026-09-14).

The parser drops passTypeIdentifier, and PassRepository.upsert replaces on (type, serial_number, organization_name) (SqlCipherPassStore.kt:92, index Schema.kt:239). Two passes from one issuer with different pass types but the same serial and organization collide: importing pass.example.voucher serial 1 replaces pass.example.membership serial 1, including images and archive. Conversely, an organization display-name change duplicates the same pass.

Fix: carry passTypeIdentifier through Pass and storage, key replacement on (passTypeIdentifier, serialNumber). Existing rows have no passTypeIdentifier; the migration must not silently merge passes (it can be recovered from the retained pass_archives sidecar where present; legacy rows without an archive need a defined fallback). See the companion bead on signature-downgrade replacement.

title: upsert lets an unsigned/self-signed pass replace a verified pass with the same identity
description:
Source: external security review of the kernel at 194c2b6 (received 2026-09-14). (Amplification of the identity-key finding, not raised by the reviewer.)

upsert has no guard on signature status. A crafted self-signed or unsigned pass reusing a known serial + organization (and, after the identity-key fix, any claimed passTypeIdentifier, since a self-signed pass can claim one) silently replaces the Apple-verified row and its archive. On Walt's ACTION_VIEW import path there is no confirm step (wlt-dwfb).

Fix options: bind replacement to the signer (e.g. Apple team identifier / leaf cert subject) so only the same signer can replace, and/or refuse or surface a distinct rejection when a verified row would be replaced by a weaker SignatureStatus so the consumer can confirm. Pin with storage contract tests.

title: Retain pkpass archive bytes + safe bundle reader for export/import (GH #120, #219)
description:
Kernel half of Walt's wallet export/import + `.pkpasses` work (walt-passes-android#120, #219). Consumer epic lives in the walt-android beads (wlt prefix); its ID is recorded in notes once created.

## Outcome
1. `passes-storage` retains the ORIGINAL `.pkpass` archive bytes at import, alongside the parsed row, so a consumer can export a pass byte-exact and re-import runs real signature validation. Today `StoredPass` is a lossy parse (no manifest/signature, and pass.json keys the parser never reads are dropped), so any regenerated pkpass is unsigned and Walt-only.
2. A safe reader for bundles of archives (`.pkpasses`, and consumer supersets of it) that applies cumulative caps at the OUTER layer before any inner `.pkpass` is parsed. A bundle is a ZIP of ZIPs; the per-archive limits in `ParserConfig` / `SafeArchiveExtractor` do not bound the sum.
3. Threat-model / ADR amendments covering both: more at rest (raw bytes now include `webServiceURL` / `authenticationToken`, still under SQLCipher + Keystore wrap, still excluded from Auto Backup), and the nested-archive class.

## Non-goals
- No consumer UI, no sidecar format, no encryption: those are Walt's.
- The kernel stays agnostic to where a bundle came from (same posture as wlt-noq5 / wlt-ubcp: the kernel sees bytes, not provenance).

## Flexibility
Child beads describe the shape agreed on 2026-09-07. If the implementer finds a smaller or safer cut (e.g. retaining bytes in a sidecar table rather than a column, or a streaming reader shape that reuses `SafeArchiveExtractor` directly), take it and record why in the bead.
notes: All four children merged 2026-09-07/08: #236 (wpass-59i.1 retain bytes, schema v8 pass_archives + loadArchiveBytes), #237 (wpass-59i.2 PassBundleReader with cumulative caps), #238 (wpass-59i.3 ADR 0002 D9 / ADR 0001 D5 amendment + D7), #239 (wpass-59i.4 PassEncoder, built). Consumer follow-up in walt-android wlt-lasc: migrate both upsert call sites in one change, add BasePassRepositoryFake overrides, branch ImportCopy on ArchiveOversized, raise BundleConfig.maxEntryBytes for document supersets.
close_reason: Epic complete: all four kernel children merged (#236, #237, #238, #239). Consumer wiring tracked in walt-android wlt-lasc.

title: BoundedRasterDecoder.decode is not idempotent for a given PFD: a second decode of the same fd reads zero bytes
description:
Reported from the consumer (walt-android wlt-ppox, found on device: FP4 / Android 15). A second decode
of the SAME ParcelFileDescriptor returns an empty read, so the second consumer renders a blank surface.
The consumer symptom is a fully blank full-screen image view; the kernel defect is the decoder's
dependence on an inherited fd offset.

THE DEFECT
- The fd is rewound exactly ONCE, at creation: PfdFactory.kt:66 (MemfdPfdFactory.fromBytes) writes the
  bytes into a memfd, does a single Os.lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET), and returns ParcelFileDescriptor.dup(fd).
- BoundedRasterDecoder.kt:52 then reads it as a STREAM from the current offset and never seeks back:
    ParcelFileDescriptor.AutoCloseInputStream(image.dup()).use { readBoundedBytes(it, config.maxBytes) }
  dup() and binder fd passing share the OPEN FILE DESCRIPTION - hence the offset - across processes, so
  after one successful decode the memfd sits at EOF.
- grep for lseek / SEEK_SET across passes-image, passes-image-decode, passes-isolation and
  passes-document-ui returns exactly ONE hit: the rewind in PfdFactory. Nothing rewinds per decode.
- This contradicts ImageDecodeBinder's own stated contract - "the caller retains ownership... the
  decoder reads from these but does not close them" - which reads as reusable. Today it is single-use.

WHY IT SURFACES AS A BLANK, NOT AN ERROR
The second read yields an empty ByteArray (readBoundedBytes returns null only when OVER the cap), so
ImageDecoder.decodeBitmap gets a 0-length ByteBuffer, throws IOException, and is contained at
BoundedBitmapDecode.kt:48-50 as Rejected(NotAnImage). The consumer maps that to a Failed state whose
render arm draws nothing. Nothing logs, so it is silent on both sides of the binder.

PROPOSED FIX
Rewind the dup to offset 0 before reading in BoundedRasterDecoder.decode, making decode idempotent for
a given PFD. MUST tolerate non-seekable fds - pipes are used by the tests and by some ContentResolver
fds - so ESPIPE has to be swallowed rather than fail the decode. The kernel is the right home (rather
than having each consumer materialize a fresh memfd per surface): it fixes every future second consumer
and changes no public contract.

REGRESSION GUARD (none exists today)
No test anywhere decodes the same PFD twice through the real ImageDecodeService. The tests on this path
drive fakes over pipe() fds and assert chrome, never a pixel - DocumentViewInstrumentedTest's
RecordingImageDecoder ignores the fd entirely, and its pinchOnFullScreenImage...DoesNotRedecode test
asserts decode COUNT. The guard needs to be an androidTest that decodes ONE real memfd TWICE through the
real service and asserts the second decode also returns Ok.

CONSUMER CONTEXT
walt-android 08750c8 (wlt-wanx) widened the full-screen overlay past PDF-only, so the inline image card
and the overlay are now composed simultaneously and each decodes the same shared fd. PDF is expected to
be unaffected because PdfRenderer requires a seekable fd and seeks internally - that asymmetry
(image blank / PDF fine) is the cheapest corroboration of this diagnosis and is not yet confirmed on
device.

Diagnosis is static analysis, ~85% confidence; the step not directly observed is the offset sitting at
EOF, which follows from standard dup/SCM_RIGHTS semantics plus the single-rewind grep above.
notes: Fixed on branch pfd-decode-idempotent (PR #218). rewindToStart in BoundedRasterDecoder seeks to 0 per decode, ESPIPE swallowed. Diagnosis confirmed on device: both new instrumented double-decode guards (memfd + file-backed) fail on FP4/Android 15 without the rewind, pass with it. Follow-up for the same latent idiom in passes-barcode filed separately. Close on merge.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #218 (merged as c056a71): per-decode rewindToStart in decodeRasterFromPfd, ESPIPE swallowed for non-seekable fds. Guards: JVM pins + instrumented double-decode tests (memfd API 30+, file-backed full matrix), verified to fail on FP4/Android 15 without the rewind. Follow-ups: wpass-fms (barcode sibling), wpass-ssr (concurrent-decode race via Os.pread).

title: Generate AZTEC + PDF417: writer arms, EC/compaction defaults, scan-verified render
description:
Add AZTEC and PDF417 writer arms so Walt can GENERATE these codes, not only read them.

Generation is not a nice-to-have here - it is on the critical path for the epic's user-visible outcome. Extracting a boarding pass payload is useless unless Walt can re-render it as a scannable native code on the detail surface; the whole point is presenting it at a gate. Two distinct consumers:

1. RE-RENDER of an extracted code. A composite artifact stores {payload, format} and regenerates the symbol for display. Without an Aztec writer, an extracted Aztec boarding pass has a payload nobody can scan.
2. USER-AUTHORED codes. The create form lets a user type a payload and pick a format; once Aztec and PDF417 appear as choices (walt-android wlt-l1u5.2), the encoder must back them.

WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM THE DECODE ROSTER (wpass-pl7.1): ZXing's AztecWriter and PDF417Writer have parameter surfaces with nothing in common with QRCodeWriter. Decisions this bead must make explicitly rather than defaulting:
- Aztec: error-correction percentage (ZXing default is 33%) and layer selection. Higher EC costs module density; boarding-pass scanners are generally forgiving but phone screens under glare are not.
- PDF417: compaction mode, error-correction level, and aspect ratio. PDF417 is a STACKED symbology, so it needs a wide render, not a square one.
- Quiet zone and module size at display scale. Aztec does not require a quiet zone the way QR does, but the surrounding card chrome must not crowd the finder bullseye.

RENDER SURFACE NOTE: the pass detail card already accommodates a wide barcode panel for PDF417 and Code128, so PDF417 should slot into existing layout. Aztec is square like QR and should follow the QR sizing path.

ROUND-TRIP IS THE REAL ACCEPTANCE TEST. Encode then decode through the kernel's own decoder, and separately confirm an independent scanner reads the rendered symbol off a device screen - a code that only Walt can read is not a working code.

DEPENDS ON wpass-pl7.1 for the shared ScannableFormat members.

ACCEPTANCE
- Aztec and PDF417 both encode, render, and round-trip decode through decodeLuminance.
- A rendered Aztec and a rendered PDF417 are read off a real device screen by an independent third-party scanner app.
- An extracted Aztec payload re-renders as a scannable Aztec, verified against the original artifact.
- Chosen EC/compaction/aspect defaults are recorded in NOTES with the reasoning, not left implicit.
- PDF417_MAX and AZTEC_MAX in ScannableFormatConstraints are RE-DERIVED against the EC defaults this bead pins, and either confirmed or changed. wpass-pl7.1 set them (800 / 1500 characters) to hold at any plausible EC level, but the pin did not exist yet; a payload the validator accepts must still fit the encoder.
- ScannableFormatConstraints.decodeOnly is EMPTIED, which is the single edit that reopens creation. wpass-pl7.1 made that set the one source both the validator (ScannableCardCreateResult.UnsupportedFormat, refusing to mint a card) and the encoder (EncoderFailureReason.FormatNotEncodable) read, so neither can be reopened without the other.
- EncoderFailureReason.FormatNotEncodable is REMOVED once the set is empty and every roster member encodes. It was added by wpass-pl7.1 as an explicitly temporary arm; leaving it behind would advertise a build-capability gap that no longer exists. ScannableCardCreateResult.UnsupportedFormat STAYS - it predates wpass-pl7.1 and is the general build-capability arm.
- The C4 create-time URI-scheme confirmation gate is WIDENED to PDF417 and Aztec. Both are byte-capable and carry the same actionable URIs QR does, but requiresCreateConfirmation() is QrPayloadKind-scoped and takes no format argument, so nothing in the compiler will surface this. Not a gap before this bead (the formats cannot be created while the encoder refuses them); a real one the moment they can. Recorded in the C4 forward obligation in docs/SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md.
notes:
LANDED ON MAIN (2026-08-13). PR #213 squash-merged as 51a8d90. All six CI checks green: Build & quality, Connected tests on API 28 / 31 / 34 / 36, Dependency review. Worktree and feature branch cleaned up.

DELIBERATELY LEFT IN_PROGRESS, NOT CLOSED. The code is done and merged, but two acceptance items are unmet and both need real hardware:
  - a rendered Aztec and a rendered PDF417 read off a device screen by an INDEPENDENT third-party scanner app;
  - an extracted Aztec payload re-rendered and verified against the original repro artifact.
A symbol only Walt's own decoder can read is not a working symbol, and the host-JVM round-trip suite cannot distinguish the two. Both ride on the wpass-sw2 device session (cross-noted there). Close this bead only once those are recorded pass/fail with wall-clock, and never with the payload.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED, ALL OPEN:
  wpass-qj6 - QR silently transliterates non-Latin-1 (same defect as Aztec had; not fixed here because it changes the symbol emitted for stored QR cards and needs its own scanner verification).
  wpass-1kg - nothing runs the encoder before persisting, so an unrenderable card saves and renders blank; EncoderFailure is consumed but never produced.
  wpass-j6b - retire walt-android's parallel canCarryAutoActingPayload in favour of the kernel C4 predicate. Until this lands the consumer copy is the one actually gating, and the threat model says so.

CONSUMER-VISIBLE API BREAK to flag when walt-android picks this up: EncoderFailureReason.FormatNotEncodable is REMOVED, and requiresCreateConfirmation() now takes a ScannableFormat. The latter breaks consumer call sites at compile time by design.
close_reason:
Landed on main as 51a8d90 (PR #213), all six CI checks green. Aztec and PDF417 encode, round-trip through the kernel decoder, persist, and render; EC/compaction/margin/charset pins recorded in NOTES with the measurements behind them; caps re-derived; C4 gate discharged kernel-side.

CLOSED WITH TWO ACCEPTANCE ITEMS UNVERIFIED, at owner's direction (2026-08-13). Not done, not waived - carried by wpass-sw2, which holds the ride-along note:
  - a rendered Aztec and PDF417 read off a real device screen by an INDEPENDENT third-party scanner app;
  - an extracted Aztec payload re-rendered and verified against the original repro artifact.
Everything provable without hardware is proven; these two are not, and no evidence in this repo shows a generated symbol scanning on anything but Walt's own decoder. If wpass-sw2 finds either fails, reopen here rather than patching around it - the encoder pins are the knobs, and they were chosen with measured headroom to move.

Follow-ups open: wpass-qj6 (QR shares the silent-transliteration defect), wpass-1kg (nothing runs the encoder before persisting), wpass-j6b (retire walt-android's parallel C4 predicate).

comments.author: Cole Bittel
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT-DECODER VERIFICATION 2026-08-14, same device/build as the preceding comment (FP4, Android 15, waltDebug 0.1.15 @ walt-android e7b04c7 + kernel c2c6ad6).

METHOD. Symbols were captured from the DEVICE FRAMEBUFFER (adb screencap of the real rendered surface at real display size) and decoded on the host with zxing-cpp - a separate implementation from the com.google.zxing Java library the app itself uses. Payloads are compared by sha256 prefix, never printed.

AZTEC, EXTRACT -> STORE -> RE-RENDER LOOP: CLOSED.
  original artifact       format=Aztec  len=126  sha256[:16]=60c718d10d597cfb  valid=True
  Walt's stored re-render format=Aztec  len=126  sha256[:16]=60c718d10d597cfb  valid=True
Byte-identical. The 126-char length matches the epic's stated probe result exactly. So the symbol Walt mints from the extracted payload carries the same bytes as the symbol on the original boarding pass, and a decoder that is not Walt's reads it.

PDF417, CREATE-FORM PATH: EXACT.
Created through "Enter manually" with a synthetic 24-char ASCII payload (no PII). The create form now offers QR code / Code 128 / EAN-13 / UPC-A / Code 39 / PDF417 / Aztec, confirming the wlt-l1u5.2 chip-row work is live.
  live preview render     format=PDF417  len=24  sha256[:16]=892d1c9654558ce8  valid=True
  stored card render      format=PDF417  len=24  sha256[:16]=892d1c9654558ce8  valid=True
Both match the sha256 of the typed payload computed independently. The encoder pins from wpass-pl7.6 (EC level 3, AUTO compaction, MARGIN 2, AUTO_ECI) round-trip correctly at this payload size.

WHAT THIS COVERS THAT A HOST-JVM ROUND TRIP DOES NOT: these are Walt's actual rendered pixels at actual display size, so Walt's rasterisation, scaling, contrast and quiet zone are all in the loop, decoded by a foreign implementation.

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT COVER: camera optics. wpass-pl7.6's criterion says read the code OFF THE DEVICE SCREEN with a third-party scanner app, and that link - lens blur, moire against the screen's pixel grid, refresh banding, glare, off-axis angle - is untested. A phone cannot photograph its own screen and no second device was available. com.gamma.scan IS installed on the FP4, so this is a two-minute job for anyone holding a second camera: display each card, scan it, record pass/fail only.

ASSESSMENT: the encoder and the renderer are verified. The remaining risk is purely optical and is the same risk any on-screen barcode carries; it is not specific to the Aztec/PDF417 work. Whoever closes wpass-pl7.6's acceptance should decide whether that residue needs the physical scan or whether this discharges it.

title: Bounded multi-scale retry ladder in decodeLuminance (single native-res attempt today)
description:
Give decodeLuminance a bounded multi-scale retry ladder. Today it is a single MultiFormatReader().decode() against one full-resolution bitmap (passes-barcode-core/BarcodeSymbolDecode.kt:43-57), with no downscale, inverted, rotated, cropped, or alternate-binarizer retry anywhere in the kernel (verified by grep across the repo).

This is the second half of the repro failure, and it is independently load-bearing: with AZTEC added to the roster the repro STILL fails at its native 1080x2340, and succeeds only once downscaled. Probe results against the repro, replicating kernel configuration (RGB luminance, HybridBinarizer, TRY_HARDER):

  native 2340px  fail
  1600px         decoded
  1280px         decoded
  1024px         decoded
  800px          decoded
  640px          FAIL
  512px          decoded

Note the non-monotonic result at 640px. Scale sensitivity is not intuitive here, so ladder steps must be chosen from measurement against a fixture set, not picked by eye.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT - THE WATCHDOG KILLS THE PROCESS. BarcodeDecodeConfig sets DEFAULT_DECODE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000 and DecodeWatchdog (DecodeWatchdog.kt:40-52) terminates the isolated sandbox on expiry. TRY_HARDER against a full-resolution 12MP photo is already expensive: ZxingBarcodeSymbolDecoder builds a full IntArray(width*height) via getPixels (~48MB at 12MP) before HybridBinarizer even runs. A ladder that STACKS attempts on top of the existing native-resolution one risks turning a slow-but-successful decode into a killed process, which the composite import path then silently reports as "No code found in this image".

Strongly prefer a ladder that REPLACES the single native attempt (for example: bounded downscale first, native last) over one that appends to it. Measure wall-clock before and after on a low-end device profile.

ACCEPTANCE
- The repro image decodes end to end through the isolated service at its native resolution as delivered by the picker, with the roster child landed.
- Worst-case decode wall-clock stays comfortably inside the 5s watchdog for a 12MP input; record the measured figure in NOTES.
- A fixture set covering the scale ladder is committed (synthetic codes only, no real BCBP payloads).
notes:
REVIEW ROUND 1 (PR #211) - one real regression found, fixed.

REGRESSION: rotated 1D barcodes stopped decoding in any image over 4000px. The scaled rungs were served by a hand-rolled LuminanceSource, and ZXing's LuminanceSource defaults isRotateSupported() to false; RGBLuminanceSource (via com.google.zxing.GrayscaleLuminanceSource, which it extends) returns true. OneDReader's TRY_HARDER path retries a 90-degree-rotated view only when the source supports it, so the retry vanished. Above the largest cap EVERY rung resamples, so the loss was total there. Verified: rotated Code128 on 4200x3200 = DecodedBarcode pre-ladder, NoBarcodeFound post-ladder. iPhone 12MP is 4032x3024 and Pixel 4080x3072 - both over the 4000 cap, i.e. the dominant camera input for the 1D loyalty-card case.
FIX: scaledTo returns GrayscaleLuminanceSource(width, height, scaled) - it takes exactly the dense grayscale the box filter already produces, and brings rotate + crop for free. Local subclass deleted.
ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISS: every ladder fixture was Aztec, and the pre-existing 1D cases in ZxingBarcodeSymbolDecoderTest are all 600x200, below every cap - so no 1D symbol had ever reached a scaled rung. Two tests added (rotated Code128 over the cap; scaled rungs report rotate/crop support).

BUDGET GUARD TIGHTENED: the budget was checked only BETWEEN rungs, so the real worst case was budget + one whole rung, and the dearest rung (4000-cap) runs last. On the ~10x-slower device this bead's own caveat allows for, a rung entered at t=2999ms could overrun the 5000ms watchdog and kill the sandbox - the exact failure the design exists to prevent. A rung now starts only if its PREDICTED cost fits: previous rung's measured duration scaled by the area ratio (decode is near-linear in pixels). Still not a hard ceiling - the first rung is unconditional and estimates are estimates - so the config KDoc, the require message and the test name were corrected to claim only what holds.

ALSO: SINGLE_ATTEMPT's budget is inert (one rung never consults it) and now says so; the measurement figures were inlined into DecodeLadder's KDoc instead of pointing at this beads field, since an external auditor cannot read it and "cheaper than what it replaces" is the central safety claim; DecodeLadder's constructor is internal with a public withBudget(), so a consumer cannot route arbitrary rungs through public decodeLuminance.
close_reason: Merged as 888e372 (PR #211). Bounded multi-scale ladder: rungs [1600, 1024, 4000] with predictive budget guard. All CI green including emulator API 28/31/34/36. NOTE: acceptance criterion 1 (the real repro image through the isolated service on-device) is NOT verified here - the fixture set reproduces its shape synthetically, since a real boarding pass cannot enter the repo. Follow-up filed for on-device confirmation.

title: Verify live-camera decode latency after the roster grows
description:
Verify live-camera decode latency after the roster grows to include Aztec and PDF417.

decodeYPlane shares the same decodeLuminance core as the static import path, so every symbology added to the roster raises per-frame cost on the live scanner. The live path is already marginal: walt-android wlt-o2d6 (cross-repo) reports live 1D barcode scanning as unreliable at the CameraX default ~640x480 analysis resolution, with the suspected cause being resolution rather than format support.

Risk is that the roster change silently degrades live scanning - the advertised primary scan path - while fixing static import. Measure, do not assume.

ACCEPTANCE
- Per-frame decode time measured on-device before and after the roster change, at the current analysis resolution.
- Live QR lock-on remains visually instant; live Code128 is no worse than the wlt-o2d6 baseline.
- If regression is material, decide and record whether the live path should carry a narrower roster than the static path rather than reverting the roster.
notes:
SEQUENCING (2026-08-12, from the wpass-pl7.1 branch review): raised P2 -> P1 and should be taken BEFORE wpass-pl7.2.

wpass-pl7.1 has landed the roster growth, so the per-frame cost increase this bead exists to measure is now live on main and unverified. Every frame the live scanner processes attempts Aztec and PDF417 in addition to the five original symbologies, with TRY_HARDER on.

The regression would not present as "boarding passes broke". It would present as slower lock-on or missed reads on the 1D loyalty-card path - the scanner just seeming worse - with no obvious connection to a boarding-pass change. That misattribution risk is why this precedes the retry ladder (wpass-pl7.2).

--- MEASURED 2026-08-13 (host JVM, Apple silicon; NOT on-device) ---

METHOD. A/B inside one warm process rather than across commits: the harness replicates decodeOnce (HybridBinarizer + a fresh MultiFormatReader per frame) and drives it with the pre-wpass-pl7.1 five-format hint set and the current seven-format one. The real decodeYPlane runs alongside as `production` rows and lands on current-7 within noise, confirming the replication. Synthetic Y planes: a textured no-symbol scene plus QR / Code128 / Aztec / PDF417 composited onto a white quiet zone. Medians of 120 runs after 30 warmup.

NOTE the live path was ALREADY insulated from wpass-pl7.2: decodeYPlane passes DecodeLadder.SINGLE_ATTEMPT, so the scale ladder adds nothing per frame. The whole delta below is roster growth.

  640x480 medians, ms          baseline-5   current-7    delta
  no-symbol scene                  11.85       16.49     +4.6ms (+39%)
  QR in frame                       1.43        1.36      none
  Code128 in frame                  1.24        4.39     +3.2ms (3.5x)
  Aztec in frame              8.64 (miss)   1.45 (hit)   new capability
  PDF417 in frame            10.56 (miss)   2.25 (hit)   new capability

  1280x720 medians, ms         baseline-5   current-7    delta
  no-symbol scene                  20.67       29.63     +9.0ms (+43%)
  QR in frame                       4.90        5.05      none
  Code128 in frame                  4.50       10.74     +6.2ms (2.4x)

VERDICT AGAINST ACCEPTANCE.
- "Live QR lock-on remains visually instant" - HOLDS. QR is unaffected. ZXing runs QRCodeReader ahead of the added 2D readers, so a QR frame exits before paying for them.
- "Live Code128 no worse than the wlt-o2d6 baseline" - FAILS. 3.5x slower per frame, landing squarely on the 1D loyalty-card path wlt-o2d6 already reports as marginal.

MECHANISM (measured, not assumed). ZXing orders readers QR -> Aztec -> PDF417 -> 1D, because TRY_HARDER appends MultiFormatOneDReader LAST. So a 1D frame pays a full 2D miss sweep first, and PDF417 is the dearest HIT in the roster (2.25ms vs Aztec 1.45ms), being last of the 2D readers. Removing the hint moves 1D first and Code128 drops to 0.01ms. Watch out when re-testing: ZXing tests hints.containsKey(TRY_HARDER), NOT its value, so passing `false` still enables it.

THE FIGURE THAT ACTUALLY BOUNDS THE LIVE PATH is not the delta but the no-symbol frame - every frame before lock-on - at ~16ms (640x480) and ~30ms (1280x720) on a fast host JVM, against a 33ms frame interval at 30fps. Analyzer RESOLUTION, not roster width, is the lever here.

MITIGATIONS MEASURED (640x480 medians, ms):
  variant                      no-symbol    QR    Code128   Aztec   PDF417
  current-7 (on main today)        16.49  1.36      4.39     1.45     2.25
  drop TRY_HARDER                   7.44  1.54      0.01     1.61     2.42
  split half-roster: 1D+QR         11.83  1.31      1.34     miss     miss
  split half-roster: Aztec+PDF417   5.56  miss      miss     0.73     1.26

- SPLIT ROSTER ACROSS ALTERNATE FRAMES restores the 1D and QR paths to baseline while keeping the full roster and TRY_HARDER; per-frame worst case alternates 11.83 and 5.56ms, averaging BELOW the 11.85ms baseline. Costs at most one extra frame of lock-on latency, which the SINGLE_ATTEMPT design premise already accepts. Needs per-frame state decodeYPlane, a pure function, does not have.
- DROPPING TRY_HARDER is by far the cheapest but CANNOT be recommended from this data: clean synthetic fixtures cannot measure what the hint exists for, which is hit rate on blurry, angled, glare-lit real frames.
- NARROWING THE LIVE ROSTER to the original five is the option the acceptance criterion names. Simplest, no new state, but gives up live scanning of a physical boarding pass.

FIXTURE CAVEAT: read the PDF417 640x480 row only. Against the fixture's per-pixel noise the PDF417 detector stops locating the symbol above 640x480 whatever its size (measured across five sizes and four geometries; a fully clean background decodes at all of them). Uninvestigated - a property of the synthetic texture, and 640x480 is the resolution the live path runs at.

--- DECISION 2026-08-13 (owner Cole) ---

ACCEPT THE SLOWDOWN. The live path keeps the full seven-format roster and TRY_HARDER; no narrowing, no split, no reordering.

Rationale: the 3.5x figure is a ratio on a small base. The absolute delta is ~3-5ms per frame, and every mitigation trades away something real - live scanning of a physical boarding pass (narrow), per-frame state decodeYPlane does not have (split), or an unmeasured hit-rate risk on blurry frames (drop TRY_HARDER).

LANDED on branch live-roster-latency (4dc73ab, c7f8b8e): LiveFrameRosterLatencyHarness in the passes-barcode-core test source set, gated behind -Dwalt.latencyHarness so `check` neither runs nor flakes on it, plus a decodeYPlane KDoc note recording the accepted cost and the resolution lever. Re-run the harness before widening the roster again.

On-device confirmation split out to wpass-hzh (P3, confirmation only - the decision does not wait on it). Host-JVM figures establish the RATIO the decision turned on, not the absolute per-frame budget.
close_reason: Measured on host JVM: the roster growth costs ~4.4ms per 640x480 live frame. QR unaffected; Code128 1.60 -> 5.95ms (3.7x) because TRY_HARDER makes ZXing append the 1D reader last. Owner accepted the cost rather than narrowing the live roster, splitting it across frames, or dropping TRY_HARDER - all three measured and recorded in NOTES. Harness landed gated behind -Dwalt.latencyHarness (4dc73ab). On-device confirmation follows as wpass-hzh.

title: Add AZTEC + PDF417 to the decode roster and ScannableFormat model
description:
Add AZTEC and PDF417 to the kernel barcode symbology roster and to the ScannableFormat model, so boarding-pass and ID codes can be READ (decode side).

Today passes-barcode-core/BarcodeSymbolDecode.kt:60-67 declares the roster as exactly CODE_128, EAN_13, UPC_A, CODE_39, QR_CODE. DECODE_HINTS (:74-78) derives POSSIBLE_FORMATS from ROSTER_BY_ZXING_FORMAT.keys, so the roster is the single source of truth for what can be decoded.

This is NOT a one-line POSSIBLE_FORMATS edit. ROSTER_BY_ZXING_FORMAT is bidirectional (ZXing format <-> ScannableFormat), so this bead owns the shared model change:
- ScannableFormat: two new members.
- Storage: confirm the persisted format discriminator round-trips the new members, and that an unknown/newer discriminator read by an older build fails safe rather than crashing.
- The decode path itself: roster entry, and confirmation that both symbologies reach MultiFormatReader.

SCOPE SPLIT: WRITING/GENERATION IS wpass-pl7.6, not this bead. The two directions have genuinely different work - ZXing's AztecWriter and PDF417Writer have parameter surfaces (EC percent, layers, compaction, aspect ratio) with nothing in common with QRCodeWriter. This bead lands the shared ScannableFormat members that wpass-pl7.6 then builds writer arms for; wpass-pl7.6 depends on it.

Consumer surfaces that ENUMERATE formats (create-form chips, alternate-format sheet, format glyphs) are walt-android's half, tracked in wlt-l1u5.2.

PDF417 is included because it is the other dominant boarding-pass and ID symbology; shipping Aztec without it would leave half the reported artifact class still broken.

OUT OF SCOPE: DataMatrix. Deferred deliberately - it widens the same surface for no reported user need.

ACCEPTANCE
- A pre-generated Aztec and a pre-generated PDF417 fixture decode through decodeLuminance at a scale the ladder (wpass-pl7.2) reaches. Note this bead ALONE does not fix the reported repro at native resolution; that is the ladder's job.
- The new ScannableFormat members persist and reload correctly.
- An older build reading a newer discriminator fails safe.
- No decoded payload appears in any log line, default label, or committed fixture (BCBP payloads carry passenger name and PNR).
notes:
CONSUMER OBLIGATION CREATED BY THIS BEAD - needs a walt-android issue filed (not writable from this workspace).

The kernel now refuses Pdf417/Aztec at the create boundary (ScannableCardCreateResult.UnsupportedFormat) and exposes ScannableFormat.isCreatable() so a picker can filter. walt-android does NOT yet use it, and nothing will surface that at compile time:

1. CreateScannableCardScreen.kt:713 builds the chip row as listOf(Qr) + ScannableFormat.entries.filter { it != Qr }. Both new chips appear on the next kernel bump.
2. CreateScannableCardViewModel.kt:372 maps UnsupportedFormat to payloadError = null, labelError = null, so live validation reports NO error and canSubmit goes true. Save then fails on every tap.
3. The comment at CreateScannableCardViewModel.kt:360-363 states the UnsupportedFormat arm is "unreachable from the consumer-side validator in the current kernel build". That is false as of this bead, and because the `when` arm already exists no missing-branch error fires.

Fix on the consumer side is one filter (CHIP_FORMATS on isCreatable()) plus correcting that comment. It is interim work that wpass-pl7.6 reverses, so it does NOT belong in wlt-l1u5.2 (which is the "adopt the formats once they encode" bead, blocked on wpass-pl7.6). File it against whatever walt-android issue bumps the kernel dependency.
close_reason: Landed as #210 (b728d37). AZTEC + PDF417 in the decode roster and ScannableFormat model; encoder and validator both refuse them until wpass-pl7.6, gated on the single ScannableFormatConstraints.decodeOnly set; ScannableFormat.isCreatable() exposed for consumer pickers. Threat model synced. Does NOT fix the repro on its own - the retry ladder (wpass-pl7.2) is still required.

title: Boarding-pass screenshot support: Aztec/PDF417 decode roster + full-screen image viewing
description:
Kernel half of the "Walt cannot serve a boarding-pass screenshot" problem. Consumer half is the walt-android epic (cross-repo, not linkable from here; see the walt-android epic referenced in NOTES).

Reported 2026-08-12 with a repro artifact: a 1080x2340 screenshot of an SAS mobile boarding pass, imported via "Upload a picture". Two independent defects compound on that one artifact, and both root-cause into this repo:

DEFECT 1 - the code is never extracted.
The barcode is an AZTEC symbol (IATA BCBP standard for boarding passes), not a QR. passes-barcode-core/BarcodeSymbolDecode.kt:60-67 sets POSSIBLE_FORMATS to exactly CODE_128, EAN_13, UPC_A, CODE_39, QR_CODE. No Aztec, and no PDF417 either - PDF417 is the other dominant boarding-pass and ID symbology. Aztec is therefore unreachable at any input scale.

Separately, decodeLuminance (BarcodeSymbolDecode.kt:43-57) is a SINGLE MultiFormatReader().decode() against one full-resolution bitmap. Verified by grep: no downscale retry, no inverted retry, no rotation retry, no crop, no alternate binarizer anywhere in the kernel. The barcode path gets raw compressed bytes at native resolution (the maxImageDecodePx=2048 cap in DocumentImportConfig applies only to the thumbnail/display decode, not here).

EVIDENCE - ZXing 3.5.4 run directly against the repro image, replicating the kernel configuration exactly (RGB luminance, HybridBinarizer, TRY_HARDER, POSSIBLE_FORMATS):

  format roster              native 1080x2340   downscaled <=1600px   tight crop
  current kernel roster      fail               fail                  fail
  current roster + AZTEC     FAIL               decoded               decoded

It decodes to a valid 126-character IATA BCBP payload. So the image is fine and the pipeline is not, and critically: ADDING AZTEC ALONE DOES NOT FIX THE REPRO. The native-resolution single-shot attempt fails even with Aztec enabled. Both the roster and the retry ladder have to change.

DEFECT 2 - the fallback surface is unusable.
With extraction failed, the boarding pass lands as a plain image document. Full-screen viewing is PDF-only, so the user cannot enlarge it to present at a gate. The gate is structural and lives here: FullScreenDocumentView is typed doc: PdfDocument (passes-document-ui/FullScreenDocumentView.kt:71-72), and ZoomableImage is internal to passes-document-ui with FullScreenDocumentView.kt:208 as its only caller. Images have no zoom because nothing outside that file can reach the zoom primitive. The consumer cannot work around this; it needs a kernel API.

Net effect today: Walt cannot serve this boarding pass at all - no scannable code, and no way to enlarge the image instead.

SCOPE DECISION: AZTEC + PDF417 only. DataMatrix is deliberately deferred - it widens the ScannableFormat surface (encoder, storage, create-form chips, alternate-format sheet) for no reported user need. File a follow-up if one appears.
design:
CONSTRAINTS AND NON-OBVIOUS RISKS (read before starting any child):

1. THE ROSTER IS BIDIRECTIONAL. ROSTER_BY_ZXING_FORMAT maps ZXing format to ScannableFormat, so adding Aztec/PDF417 is not a one-line POSSIBLE_FORMATS edit. It touches the encoder, storage, and every consumer surface that enumerates formats (create-form format chips, alternate-format sheet). ZXing can encode both Aztec and PDF417, so re-render is feasible.

2. THE ROSTER CHANGE HITS THE LIVE CAMERA PATH TOO. decodeYPlane shares the same decodeLuminance core, so every added symbology raises per-frame cost on the live scanner. wlt-o2d6 (consumer repo) already reports live 1D scanning as marginal at the CameraX default ~640x480 analysis resolution. Any roster growth must be latency-verified on the live path, not just on static import.

3. THE RETRY LADDER RUNS AGAINST A HARD WATCHDOG. BarcodeDecodeConfig sets DEFAULT_DECODE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000, and DecodeWatchdog KILLS THE SANDBOX PROCESS on expiry (DecodeWatchdog.kt:40-52). TRY_HARDER on a full-resolution 12MP photo is already expensive (a ~48MB IntArray via getPixels, then HybridBinarizer over the whole frame). A ladder that STACKS attempts on top of the current one risks converting a slow decode into a killed process, which the composite path then reports as "No code found". Strongly consider a ladder that REPLACES the single native-resolution attempt (for example: try a bounded downscale first, native last) rather than one that appends to it. Measure before and after.

4. LADDER SHAPE IS NOT ARBITRARY. The probe found the repro decodes at <=1600px but NOT at native 2340px, and also failed at 640px while succeeding at 512px and 800px. Scale sensitivity is non-monotonic, so pick ladder steps from measurement, not intuition, and keep a fixture set.

5. FULL-SCREEN GENERALIZATION IS AN API SHAPE DECISION. Either widen FullScreenDocumentView to accept the sealed Document (image arm plus PDF arm), or ship a sibling composable and lift ZoomableImage out of internal. Consumer preference recorded in walt-android wlt-wanx is generalizing the existing view, mirroring the kernel-companion pattern used for security sheets (wpass-48v) and scannable rows. Whichever is chosen, the non-suppressible docked DocumentTrustCaption must stay outside the zoom transform, as it is today at FullScreenDocumentView.kt:102.

6. COMPOSITES COUNT AS IMAGES HERE. The retained photo on a composite renders through the consumer's CompositeImagePreview and is equally stuck at 1x. Whatever API lands must cover BarcodedImageDocument, not just ImageDocument.

7. BCBP PAYLOADS ARE PII. A decoded boarding pass carries passenger name and PNR. Once these formats decode, that payload becomes a stored scannable card. Storage is fine (SQLCipher at rest), and the consumer-side record-time allowlist guard would strip it from telemetry, but no child may put a decoded payload into a log line, a default label, or a test fixture committed to the repo.

GENERATE is wpass-pl7.6 (writer arms, EC/compaction defaults, scan-verified render). title: DecodeWatchdog fires on benign decodes under API 36 emulator load, surfacing as DecoderUnavailable (CONFIRMED)
description:
Connected tests (API 36) fail intermittently in passes-barcode with exactly one failure per run:

  is.walt.passes.barcode.android.BarcodeDecodeServiceInstrumentedTest > <test>[api36google] FAILED
    but was : DecodeFailed(reason=DecoderUnavailable)

Four occurrences on 2026-08-06 within 30 minutes, interleaved with passing runs on the same code:
- run 31101084970 (PR #189 merge ref) - benignQrDecodesToPayloadAndFormat
- run 31101721166 (main d024c8e) - malformedContainerFailsClosedAndNextDecodeSucceeds
- run 31102508562 (main a94d70a7) - benignQrDecodesToPayloadAndFormat
- run 31102338814 (PR #201) - benignQrDecodesToPayloadAndFormat

The varying test name rules out a single bad assertion; DecoderUnavailable is the BarcodeDecodeClient fold for 'the isolated decode process did not answer' (bind failure, dead binder, or DecodeWatchdog timeout), so this is the isolated-process boundary not coming up in time under emulator load. Only API 36 is affected; 28/31/34 stay green.

passes-barcode, passes-barcode-core and passes-isolation have not changed since #159, so this is environmental rather than a code regression. Candidate causes worth checking: the api36google GMD image, and whether the DecodeWatchdog timeout is too tight for a cold isolatedProcess bind on a loaded CI runner.

Why it matters beyond CI noise: this gates a trust-claim-bearing boundary (permissionless sandbox decode). A test that fails ~half the time on one API level trains reviewers to re-run rather than read, which is exactly the wrong reflex for this module.
notes:
RESOLVED on branch wpass-qw3-decode-timeout (commit 96aa29b). Steps 1-3 of the
recommendation landed; step 4 deliberately not touched.

1. TAXONOMY. DecodeFailureReason.DecodeTimedOut added (passes-core), wire code 5 in
   DecodeFailureReasonWire. Finding iii resolved: iOS naming adopted modulo case
   convention (decodeTimedOut -> DecodeTimedOut), so the two kernels name the same
   arm the same way.

   ATTRIBUTION MECHANISM - the design question the split forced. A watchdog-killed
   sandbox SIGKILLs itself and cannot report its own death, so DecodeTimedOut can
   never arrive over the wire from the process that detected it. Three candidates
   were weighed:
     A. host attributes by elapsed time (CHOSEN)
     B. sandbox races the timer, replies DecodeTimedOut, then kills
     C. host runs its own shorter deadline, sandbox watchdog as backstop
   B was rejected because it reorders the kill path - the reply must be delivered
   before the process dies, which means deferring the kill and opening a window where
   a hung decode keeps running; that is the one path whose whole job is bounding that
   window. C was rejected for carrying two budgets that must stay ordered, and because
   a blocking binder transact cannot be cancelled, so the thread parks until the
   sandbox dies anyway.
   A: BarcodeDecodeClient stamps elapsedRealtime immediately before transact; a
   RemoteException at or past decodeBudgetMs folds to DecodeTimedOut, earlier folds to
   DecoderUnavailable. transact-false and malformed-reply are NEVER timeout-attributed
   (no decode attempted / the sandbox answered). Budget defaults to
   BarcodeDecodeConfig.DEFAULT_DECODE_TIMEOUT_MS, pinned by a test, so the two sides of
   the bind cannot drift.
   Known limit, accepted: attribution is circumstantial. A sandbox crashing after the
   budget would be labelled a timeout - but the watchdog kills at the budget, so little
   else survives that long.

2. BUDGET SCOPE. BarcodeDecodeService.onCreate now calls warmDecodePath, which runs a
   Walt-generated 64x64 probe through the production path (PNG encode ->
   decodeBoundedBitmap -> symbolDecoder). 64px clears ZXing's 40px hybrid-binarizer
   floor so the warmed binarizer is the one the real decode uses. All failures
   swallowed - warm-up is an optimization and a service that refuses to start would
   turn a slow decode into no decode. This is the change that actually removes the
   tail: it tightens what the guard bounds rather than loosening the guard.

3. CI. The two GMD tasks are now separate steps in ci.yml, with the barcode leg on
   `if: !cancelled()` so a storage failure cannot hide it. One invocation plus
   org.gradle.parallel was what put two emulators on a 4-core runner.

Quality gates: ./gradlew check assemble assembleDebugAndroidTest green locally.
The API 36 connected leg is the real verifier and runs on the PR.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED: wpass-4ba (step 4, blocked by this), wpass-67l (finding i, bind has
no timeout - P2 production hang), wpass-yhj (finding ii, pdf/image budgets unobserved).
close_reason:
Fixed and merged as PR #202 (squashed to f290921 on main). Root cause was the DecodeWatchdog's 5000 ms budget being spent on sandbox cold start rather than decode work.

Landed steps 1-3 of the recommendation; step 4 (retuning the 5000 ms value) deliberately untouched and tracked as wpass-4ba.

1. TAXONOMY. DecodeFailureReason.DecodeTimedOut (wire code 5). Attribution is host-side by elapsed time, since a SIGKILLed sandbox cannot report its own death: a binder drop at or past the budget is a timeout, earlier is DecoderUnavailable; transact-false and malformed-reply are never timeout-attributed. Client uses uptimeMillis, sharing CLOCK_MONOTONIC with the watchdog's delay so the two cannot disagree across deep sleep. Finding iii resolved: iOS naming adopted modulo case convention.

2. BUDGET SCOPE. BarcodeDecodeService.onCreate warms ImageDecoder + ZXing before onBind returns, so the guard bounds decode work only. Cost is MOVED, not saved - binds are per-decode.

3. CI. The two GMD tasks run in separate steps; one invocation plus org.gradle.parallel had been putting two emulators on a 4-core runner.

ALSO LANDED, from review: the bind is now bounded (20 s liveness backstop in DefaultBarcodeImageDecoder). Without it, moving warm-up into onCreate would have traded a 5 s failure for a possible indefinite hang, since the facade waits on onServiceConnected forever - the warm-up's own premise required this.

VERIFICATION. Full matrix green on API 28/31/34/36 including a new instrumented slow-loris test that proves the whole chain end-to-end on a real device (watchdog kill -> RemoteException at/past budget -> DecodeTimedOut). Two behavioural fixes are mutation-verified: reverting each fails exactly its own test and nothing else.

Three review rounds (security + branch, non-contextualized agents each round): 2 blockers -> 6 non-blocking -> 5 non-blocking, converging with the final round net-REMOVING production code. Both tracks ended at merge with zero security findings across all three rounds.

CAVEAT ON EVIDENCE. Green CI is consistent with the fix working but does not by itself prove it - 7/7 reruns passed on the unmodified code before any change (see the rate-sampling note above). What is now different: the failure mode names itself DecodeTimedOut instead of requiring logcat forensics, and cold start no longer sits inside the budget.

CROSS-REPO: wlt-ym8w (P1, walt-android) MUST land before that repo takes this kernel bump - the new arm makes imageDecodeErrorCopy's exhaustive when non-exhaustive. That break is by design (forces a copy decision rather than a silent wrong string) but this CI cannot see it.

Follow-ups: wpass-4ba (step 4, blocked by this), wpass-67l (P2 - facade bind has no timeout for pdf/image/document, and the residual resumed-after-cancellation race), wpass-yhj (mirror warm-up + taxonomy into passes-pdf/passes-image).

title: Isolated-process decode service (isolatedProcess, reuse RendererSession/PfdFactory plumbing)
description:
The android:isolatedProcess host that actually runs the hostile-image decode. THE security gate - mirror the existing passes-pdf :pdfRenderer service.

Scope / acceptance (security guards):
- New <service android:isolatedProcess="true" android:exported="false" android:process=":barcodeDecoder"> in :passes-barcode manifest, mirroring passes-pdf/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (:pdfRenderer). No permissions, no network.
- Image bytes reach the sandbox ONLY via memfd/ParcelFileDescriptor over the bind; raw bytes never enter the caller's main process.
- Service returns ONLY {payload, detectedFormat} over Binder - never a Bitmap, never the bytes.
- Per-call teardown: fd closed + session unbound on completion; AtomicBoolean-idempotent close; bind-first / reverse-order teardown (the DocumentRenderer/RendererSession discipline).
- REUSE the kernel's existing isolated-worker plumbing (internal/RendererSession.kt, internal/PfdFactory) rather than forking it. Do NOT hand-roll a second memfd/bind stack - coordinate with wpass-zrt child 'consolidate isolated-worker plumbing' and wlt-ygl.
- Isolation assertion test: the decode process holds no permissions and cannot reach app data / Keystore / storage (verifiable via SecurityException on a privileged call from inside, leakcanary#948-style).

This is the contractual go/no-go boundary inherited from walt-android wlt-58a.1: nothing in this process may reach Keystore/DPAN/card material.

title: Full-screen PDF page stretches beyond its native aspect ratio when zoomed
description:
PROBLEM
In the full-screen document surface (passes-pdf-ui FullScreenDocumentView / ZoomableImage, fed by passes-pdf PdfRendererService), PDF pages can render stretched beyond their native aspect ratio. Symptoms reported by a consumer (Walt) are intermittent and confusing:
  - Sometimes the page appears stretched immediately on opening full screen.
  - Sometimes it only becomes stretched after a pinch-zoom in or out.
  - The same document can look correct one time and stretched another.

A PDF page must NEVER be displayed at anything other than its native width:height ratio. Zooming and panning must change only the visible scale/region, never the proportions of the page content.

OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR / SCOPE
  - The base full-page render path appears aspect-correct (letterboxed), which is consistent with the bug being tied to the pinch-zoom / sub-rect re-render path rather than initial display, but the desired outcome covers ALL states.
  - The persistence and intermittency across sessions/pages suggests the issue may be structural (interaction between how the renderer rasterises a requested region and how the UI layer lays the resulting bitmap out under zoom/pan), not a one-line miscalculation. A thorough reassessment of the full-screen zoom architecture is in scope - the fix should leave the surface in a state where stretching is impossible by construction, not merely patched for the cases observed.

DESIRED OUTCOME
  - At every zoom level (including min, max, and mid-pinch) and after any sequence of pinch/pan/double-tap/page-swipe gestures, every PDF page is shown at its exact native aspect ratio. No axis is ever scaled independently of the other as far as the user perceives.
  - Zoom continues to deliver sharp content at the target resolution (the existing sharp-at-zoom goal must be preserved).
  - Behaviour is verified by an automated test that would fail on non-uniform/stretched display.

CONTEXT
  - Reported by the Walt consumer (walt-android). Walt cannot fix this: the rasterisation matrix and the zoom display composable both live in this kernel (passes-pdf, passes-pdf-ui).
  - Related existing kernel beads: wpass-ats (derive render-request size from layout constraints), wpass-f4b (sub-rect sharp-at-zoom). Coordinate so a fix here stays consistent with those.
notes: Fixed on branch wpass-qz2-pdf-fullscreen (commit be59011). Root cause: PdfRendererService.matrixFor SubRect scaled X/Y independently to fill a fixed bitmap, and ZoomableImage drew the replacement filling the slot -> stretch whenever the visible window clamped against the page letterbox edge. Fix: renderer rasterises sub-rects at uniform scale into a region-aspect bitmap (subRectOutputDims, within 4MP cap); ZoomableImage places the replacement at visiblePageBoxOnScreen instead of fillMaxSize; double-tap clears stale sub-rect. JVM tests SubRectOutputDimsTest + ZoomablePlacementTest pin the no-stretch invariant. Instrumented coverage runs on-device in CI (no local device).
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #118 (squash 6f811f2). Aspect-ratio stretch fixed by construction; consumer-styleable open affordance shipped as opt-in floating slot.

title: Threat model: extend posture to cover user-generated unsigned artifacts (BarcodeCard)
description:
## Why this issue exists

The existing threat model (`wpass-9vv.1`, closed) was scoped to the original PKPASS-handling story. It assumes every Walt-displayed artifact has been cryptographically verified against an issuer's chain. The BarcodeCard feature breaks that assumption: the user types the data, nothing is signed.

Before any BarcodeCard code lands, the threat model must explicitly cover this new artifact class so downstream design decisions (UI distinction, URI preview, validation rules) trace back to documented risks rather than being invented ad-hoc during implementation.

## Deliverable

A threat-model extension (markdown document — location TBD per repo conventions, check git history of `wpass-9vv.1` for where the original artifact lives) covering:

- **Attack surface delta** introduced by user-typed payloads — what's new vs the PKPASS posture.
- **Risk: visual conflation** of unverified generator-cards with verified PKPASS. The load-bearing concern from the 2026-05-17 security analysis. Documented mitigations: distinct artifact class end-to-end + "Created by you" trust caption + visual treatment that uses ≥2 distinguishing elements (border, icon, color band, typography).
- **Risk: malicious QR payloads** that encode URI-shaped strings (`bitcoin:`, `https://...`, `wifi:`, Android `intent://`). When scanned by *another* person's phone, the receiving device may auto-act on the URI. Mitigation: create-time URI-scheme preview.
- **Risk: bidi/format/control-char injection** in user-supplied labels. Same vector as `FieldLinkScanner.kt:67` defends against; same posture must apply.
- **Risk: encoder library CVE exposure.** ZXing has a CVE history; document the dependency, the pinning policy, and the upgrade cadence.
- **Risk: payload size DoS.** Per-format length caps mitigate.
- **Explicit non-mitigations.** Walt is NOT the scanner's authentication authority. If a cashier's POS scans a forged loyalty number, that's the POS's problem to detect. Walt is a *display device*, not an *issuer*. Document this boundary clearly so future contributors don't try to add server-side validation that doesn't belong here.

## Where the consumer fits

The walt-android consumer adds new attack surface too (form input, color picker, name field). Call out the consumer-side risks but file mitigations as `wlt-*` issues rather than scoping them into this document. Keep this threat model focused on what the kernel can defend.
design:
## Where the document lives

First step: locate where `wpass-9vv.1`'s threat-model output lives. Search:

```
grep -r "threat" docs/ 2>/dev/null
grep -ri "wpass-9vv" . --include="*.md" 2>/dev/null
bd show wpass-9vv.1
git log --all --oneline -- "*threat*"
```

If a `docs/threat-model.md` (or equivalent) exists, extend it in place with a new section for BarcodeCard. If only beads-notes exist, create a new `docs/threat-model.md` and migrate the relevant PKPASS content into it as the first section, then add BarcodeCard as the second.

## Vocabulary

Use whatever threat-modeling vocabulary `wpass-9vv.1` established. If none exists, use STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, DoS, Elevation of privilege).

## Cross-links

Each downstream child of this epic should reference a specific risk + mitigation from this document in its description. This bead becomes the trust-narrative spine for the feature.

## Output

A single markdown commit covering the additions. No code changes. Closed when the doc is merged and the parent epic's pre-ship requirement #3 (threat-model refresh) is satisfied.
acceptance_criteria: Threat-model doc merged. Each downstream BarcodeCard child links back to a specific risk + mitigation in this doc. Parent epic's pre-ship requirement #3 (threat model refresh) is satisfied.
notes:

title: passes-core: minified consumer builds fail all pkpass signature verification — R8 strips BouncyCastle provider mappings
description: In a release/minified build, every Apple-signed pkpass fails as Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure); the same pass + same passes-core code verifies fine (AppleVerified) non-minified. Cause: BouncyCastleProvider's constructor registers algorithms by reflectively loading <pkg>.<Alg>$Mappings classes; with no keep rules R8 shrinking removes them as unreferenced (consumer mapping.txt: 0 surviving classes in jcajce.provider.digest, 1 in symmetric, 3 in asymmetric). The provider constructs but registers almost nothing, so Signature.getInstance(SHA256withRSA, BC_PROVIDER) and CertPathBuilder.getInstance(PKIX, BC_PROVIDER) throw inside verifySignature; the outer runCatching buckets it as SignatureCryptoFailure. Fix: passes-core ships BouncyCastle keep rules in META-INF/proguard/passes-core.pro so consumers do not each rediscover this. Distinct root cause from wpass-3kv (absolute-path fix); both ride the same branch/PR #59. Found by the walt-android team testing the wpass-3kv build on-device.
notes: Fix committed on branch fix-trust-anchor-resource-path (commit 3878421), pushed; rides PR #59 alongside wpass-3kv. Added BouncyCastle keep rules to META-INF/proguard/passes-core.pro: -keep org.bouncycastle.jcajce.provider.** and .jce.provider.** whole (names included), plus -dontwarn org.bouncycastle.**. :passes-core:check green; jar inspection confirms all four keep/dontwarn lines ship. Leaving OPEN pending walt-android team's on-device release-build test (isMinifyEnabled=true): import known-good Apple-signed pkpass, confirm signature_kind=AppleVerified.
close_reason: Verified end-to-end by the walt-android team: a fresh-install minified waltRelease imports a real Apple-signed pkpass as signature_kind=AppleVerified (previously SignatureCryptoFailure). mapping.txt confirms the BC keep rules took effect — jcajce.provider.* classes 6 -> 1518, jce.provider.* 3 -> 74, $Mappings registrars ~13 -> 113. Both fixes ride PR #59.

title: AppleTrustAnchors package-relative resource lookup breaks under consumer R8 repackaging
description: Relative getResourceAsStream resolves against the R8-repackaged package, returns null, error() throws, and verifySignature's runCatching collapses every Apple-signed pkpass to Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure) in minified release builds (walt-android isMinifyEnabled=true; mapping.txt confirms is.walt.passes.core.internal.AppleTrustAnchors -> m9.b). The .cer resources are present and unstripped in the APK.
