title: Phone-number auto-detection too aggressive: 8-digit ticket numbers classified as tel: URIs
description:
Observed 2026-05-07 on FP4 / Android 16 / waltDebug with the chroniques pkpass (pass.com.tixly).

backFields[0]:
  key: "ticketNoBack"
  label: "#LABELTICKETNUMBER#"
  value: "52311919"     <-- 8-digit string, no formatting hints
  (no attributedValue, no explicit linkURL)

Walt renders this value with an underline indicating tappable target. Tapping it surfaces the URL/tel confirmation sheet ("Call this number? ... 52311929 ... Cancel / Call"). The auto-detection therefore classified the bare 8-digit string as a tel: URI.

Why this is a bug:
1. False positives. Real pkpasses use plain digit strings for ticket numbers, order numbers, barcode payloads, member IDs, etc. The chroniques pass alone has THREE such fields (ticket, order, price zone). Every one becomes an accidental "Call this number?" prompt.
2. Attack surface. A malicious pkpass can put a premium-rate or international dial string in a value field knowing the auto-detector will pick it up. The confirmation sheet helps but is not foolproof: the sheet displays the raw `#LABELKEY#` (see related localization bug), so the attacker can choose a field key the user would not look at twice.

Apples data detectors (which Apple Wallet uses) require formatting hints to fire on phone numbers: dashes, parentheses, country code prefix, area-code prefix, +-prefix, etc. A bare run of digits with no formatting is left as plain text. Walts detector should be at least as conservative.

Fix shape:
- Tighten the phone-detector regex to require at least one formatting hint (one of: leading +, embedded -, embedded space between digit groups, parentheses, leading 0/00 international prefix). Bare digit-only sequences should NOT match.
- Consider gating auto-detection by field semantic intent: pass.json declares semantics on most fields; if semantic is paymentEntry / ticketNumber / etc., auto-detection should be off entirely. Apple does this.
- Test the chroniques fixture as the canonical regression: assert that ticketNoBack/orderNoBack value strings render NON-tappable, and that explicit tel: links (e.g. `attributedValue` containing `<a href="tel:...">`) DO render tappable.

Severity: customer-facing on every real pkpass with numeric reference values. Not a security hole on its own (confirmation sheet protects), but the combination with the localization bug (which makes the sheet itself less informative) elevates the risk.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix-pkpass-tixly-render: phone detector requires formatting hint; pass.strings labels resolved via resolveLocalizedStrings + CompositionLocal.

title: pass.strings labels not substituted: back-side fields render raw `#LABELKEY#` placeholders
description:
Observed 2026-05-07 on FP4 / Android 16 / waltDebug after importing the chroniques pkpass (passTypeIdentifier pass.com.tixly, 8 lproj directories: da, de, en, fi, is, nb, nl, sv). Back-side renders the literal placeholder strings:

  #LABELTICKETNUMBER#
  52311929
  #LABELORDERNUMBER#
  5847559
  #LABELPRICEZONE#
  A

The expected behavior: each `#LABELKEY#` token in pass.json field labels should be looked up in `<currentLocale>.lproj/pass.strings` (or `en.lproj/pass.strings` as fallback) and substituted before render. Real pkpasses rely on this for every label.

Hypotheses to investigate:
1. The kernels pass.strings parser (passes-core/src/main/.../strings/...) is correct in isolation but its output is not threaded back into the field-render path. Check the call site that reads field.label.
2. The locale resolution is choosing wrong lproj/. The device may be in a locale not in the bundle (e.g. a region variant like en-IS or sv-FI) and the kernel may be returning empty rather than falling back. Apple PassKits documented behavior is locale -> language -> en fallback chain.
3. The substitution is happening but only when the value is wrapped in some specific marker the chroniques pass does not use. Possibly a layered case where kernel only substitutes `${KEY}` form and leaves `#KEY#` form untouched, or vice versa.
4. The label key matches but the strings file lookup is case-sensitive while pass.json declares the key in a different case.

Repro: any pkpass whose pass.json field labels reference pass.strings keys via the placeholder form. The chroniques pkpass at /tmp/golden-extract/ on the wlt-a07 worktree is one such fixture - inspect its pass.json + en.lproj/pass.strings to see the canonical name.

Severity: customer-facing on every real pkpass. Without this fix, every back-side field shows raw placeholders instead of human labels. Front side likely has the same issue; check.

Probably needs an instrumentation test that parses the chroniques fixture and asserts at least one Field.label resolves to the en.lproj/pass.strings value rather than the raw `#KEY#` token.
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix-pkpass-tixly-render: phone detector requires formatting hint; pass.strings labels resolved via resolveLocalizedStrings + CompositionLocal.

title: passes-storage instrumentation: openOrCreate reopen-cycle test (catches wpass-aio regression)
description:
Add an instrumentation test in passes-storage/src/androidTest/ that exercises the create -> close -> reopen -> read cycle of SqlCipherDatabaseFactory.openOrCreate against a real Android Keystore-backed DatabaseKey. Today the JVM unit suite only covers single-connection lifetimes and missed wpass-aio entirely.

Test outline:
1. Acquire DatabaseKey via PassKeyProvider against the test apps Keystore alias (no MasterKey shim - hit the real keystore so the test catches Android-runtime-only bugs).
2. Call SqlCipherDatabaseFactory.openOrCreate(context, databaseKey). Assert StorageResult.Success. Apply Schema.DDL via the returned db. Close.
3. Call openOrCreate(context, databaseKey) AGAIN. Assert StorageResult.Success. Read schema_meta. Assert version matches Schema.VERSION.
4. Bonus: spawn a fresh process via androidx.test.uiautomator (force-stop + relaunch) and call openOrCreate from the new process to catch process-boundary issues.

Without the wpass-aio fix (cipher_compatibility hook), step 3 fails with SQLiteOutOfMemoryException. With the fix, all three steps succeed.

Why this matters: the bug we just diagnosed (cipher_compatibility = 4 issued AFTER openOrCreateDatabase chose its KDF regime) only fires on the second open of an existing DB. JVM unit tests stay in one connection lifetime and never see this. An instrumentation test that explicitly closes and reopens is the structural fix.

Refs: wpass-aio (closed by 239ba63). The regression-catcher this test would have prevented is exactly the bug 28dc966 attempted but did not fix.
close_reason: Already shipped in commit 239ba63 (PR #52, the wpass-aio fix). passes-storage/src/androidTest/.../CipherCompatReopenTest.kt covers the create -> close -> reopen -> read cycle against a real Keystore-backed DatabaseKey, runs on CI on API 28/31/34/36 via :passes-storage:apiNgoogleDebugAndroidTest. Steps 1-3 of the bead's outline are covered (with a stronger row-readback than schema_meta). Step 4 (cross-process via uiautomator) is intentionally out of scope per the test's KDoc: the bug is per-SQLiteDatabase-connection KDF state, so same-process-fresh-instance reproduces it on affected bindings; a cross-process variant would not add coverage. Bead was filed ~10 min after wpass-aio closed without noticing the test had been bundled into the fix commit.

title: passes-pdf: client-side binder proxy + round-trip test
description:
The wpass-5v9 PR (#36) ships only the *server-side* binder proxy: the Binder subclass that decodes incoming transactions and writes the reply parcel. The client side that calls `transact()` and decodes the reply does not exist yet, and the @Ignore'd instrumented tests do not exercise the wire format.

Concrete gaps:
- The wire format (TAG_OK / TAG_REJECTED, kind.ordinal enum encoding, ParcelFileDescriptor.CREATOR usage, SharedMemory parcelling) is asserted nowhere.
- A change to the order of DocumentRejectedKind values in passes-pdf-core would silently break wire compatibility once a consumer is wired in.
- Anyone integrating this binder (walt-android consumer, wpass-7wn passes-ui document view) has to re-derive the contract from PdfRendererBinderProxy.kt.

Scope:
- Add `PdfRendererClient` (or similar) under passes-pdf that wraps a bound `IBinder` and exposes the same suspend probe/render contract by writing transact parcels and decoding replies.
- Replace the `DocumentRejectedKind.ordinal` wire encoding with an explicit stable mapping (or pin the ordering with a test) so reordering the enum is a structural failure rather than a wire-compat surprise.
- Round-trip test: bind the service in-process via a Robolectric ServiceController OR via instrumented test, exercise probe/render/error paths end-to-end, assert the wire shape.
- This must land before any consumer (walt-android wlt-4pg, wpass-7wn passes-ui) wires the binder in. Flag as a blocker on those integrations.
close_reason: Shipped on branch passes-pdf-client-binder; ./gradlew check green.

title: Validate isolated-decoder reply dims against SharedMemory size before host bitmap allocation; watchdog the PDF probe
description:
Source: external security review of the kernel at 194c2b6 (received 2026-09-14).

Hosts allocate Bitmap.createBitmap(ok.widthPx, ok.heightPx) before checking the reply buffer: ImageRendering.kt:38, PageRendering.kt:43, DefaultDocumentImporter.kt:425, ThumbnailEncoder.kt:31. A compromised sandbox can return a tiny SharedMemory and claim e.g. 20000x20000, forcing a >1 GB host allocation (second-stage DoS). The pixel cap is enforced only renderer-side (PdfRendererService.kt:94).

Fix: one shared host-side reply validator for image and PDF results: positive dims, <= requested size, pixel count <= MAX_PIXELS, and SharedMemory.size >= w*h*4, all before allocation; reject with a typed failure and close the SharedMemory.

Also: doProbe (PdfRendererService.kt:75) opens PdfRenderer and reads pageCount outside RenderWatchdog. Put every native PDF operation under the watchdog. Related: wpass-4ba, wpass-yhj.

title: Docs: ADR 0002 + threat-model amendments for raw-byte retention and nested archives
description:
Record the two security-relevant changes from this epic in the kernel's own docs, following the existing ADR / threat-model amendment pattern (cf. the C5 amendment landed for wlt-ixlf, wpass-80y.4 withdrawal note).

## Amendments to write
1. **ADR 0002 (passes-storage)**: raw archive bytes are now retained at rest. State what that adds (`webServiceURL`, `authenticationToken`, full pass.json incl. keys the parser ignores), what protects it (SQLCipher, Keystore-wrapped envelope, Auto Backup exclusion on both sides via the Mirror posture), and what does NOT read it (only the consumer export path). Note the legacy-null case.
2. **Nested-archive threat row** (pkpass threat model / PDF threat model, whichever holds the archive-bomb entries): bundle-of-archives amplification and the outer cumulative caps that bound it (wpass bundle-reader bead). Mention that inner archives still go through the unchanged single-archive path, so signature validation and per-archive caps are not weakened.
3. A short note that the kernel deliberately does not define a consumer backup/sidecar format or encryption: those are consumer concerns (Walt epic wlt-lasc).

## Acceptance
- Docs updated in the same PR series as the code, not after.
- `docs/decisions-and-learnings.md`-style brevity: constraints and why, not walkthroughs.
notes: Docs landed (2026-09-08, branch wpass-59i.3, cut from wpass-59i.2): (1) docs/adr/0002-passes-storage.md: pass_archives DDL added to the D3 SQL block; new 'Addendum 2026-09-08: original archive bytes retained at rest' with D9 (what the sidecar adds at rest: full pass.json incl. webServiceURL/authenticationToken/nfc/personalization, manifest, signature; what protects it: D1/D2/D5 unchanged, REQUIRED_EXCLUDES names the db file so Inherit and Mirror both cover it; PassArchiveBounds.MAX_BYTES 10 MiB hard ceiling independent of ParserConfig.maxArchiveBytes, PassRejected(ArchiveEmpty|ArchiveOversized); only loadArchiveBytes reads it, passes/load/summaryOf never do, pinned by query-shape test; legacy Success(null) incl. the deprecated two-arg upsert dropping archives on replace, migrate every call site in one change; consumer obligation: credential-bearing blob, no logging/telemetry, shared .pkpass carries the issuer update token), a 'Backup and sidecar formats stay out of the kernel' section (wlt-lasc, bytes not provenance), and a tests table. (2) docs/adr/0001-passes-core-public-api.md: 'Addendum 2026-09-08: bundle reader surface and the nested-archive class' with an Amendment to D5 threat row (What/Mitigation/Consequence for consumers/extractor hardenings/Status) covering the BundleConfig defaults 256 MiB outer, 200 entries, 10 MiB per entry, 256 MiB cumulative, skipped + directory payload draining, mid-entry stop, typed BundleRejection arms incl. SourceUnreadable, names never in results; the maxEntryBytes consumer note; the two extractor hardenings (directory payloads pay the entry cap; sniff IOException folds into NotAZipArchive instead of escaping parse). D7 freezes the full public bundle surface. Tests table. No pkpass threat-model file exists in this repo; ADR 0001 D5 is where the zip-bomb posture lived, so the row went there. (3) SECURITY.md: scope bullet mentions the bundle reader; new 'Bundles of archives are capped at the outer layer' decision bullet; webServiceURL bullet notes at-rest retention since v8 (ADR 0002 D9). (4) PassJsonDecoder.kt KDoc cross-reference now points at ADR 0002 D9 (comment only). title: PassBundleReader: safe outer-layer reader for .pkpasses / bundles with cumulative caps
description:
A safe reader for a ZIP that contains `.pkpass` archives (Apple `.pkpasses`) and, for consumers, other entries (documents, a sidecar). Applies cumulative limits at the OUTER layer before any inner archive is handed to `PassParser`.

## Why
A bundle is a ZIP of ZIPs. `ParserConfig` / `SafeArchiveExtractor` bound ONE archive (25 MB, entry count, per-entry bytes). A thousand inner entries each at the cap is gigabytes; nothing today bounds the sum, so nested archives are a new decompression-bomb amplification class.

## Suggested shape (pivot if smarter)
- `PassBundleReader` (passes-core, next to `SafeArchiveExtractor`): streams the outer ZIP once, yields `BundleEntry(name, kind, InputStream)` in order, and enforces: outer archive byte cap (pre-check on stream length like `PassParser` does), max entry count, per-entry byte cap, cumulative decompressed byte cap across ALL entries, path-traversal + symlink rejection (reuse `pathTraversalReason`), and an extension/name allowlist supplied by the caller (kernel default: `*.pkpass` only). Directory entries skipped. Unknown entries reported, not silently dropped, so a consumer can decide.
- Do NOT parse inner pkpasses here: yield bytes and let the caller run `PassParser` so the per-archive limits and signature validation apply unchanged. Keeps the kernel agnostic to provenance (wlt-noq5 / wlt-ubcp posture).
- Limits live in a `BundleConfig` with conservative defaults (e.g. 200 entries, 256 MB cumulative) and a `ResourceLimit`-style typed rejection so telemetry/UI can name the cap hit.
- Detection helper: `isPassBundle(header)` / MIME `application/vnd.apple.pkpasses` so consumers can dispatch from a byte sniff without a second full read.

## Acceptance
- Unit tests: cap on count, per-entry, cumulative (an inner bomb that is individually under cap but collectively over), zip-slip name, symlink, empty bundle, bundle with one non-pkpass entry under caller allowlist vs default allowlist.
- No file-system writes; pure stream processing like `SafeArchiveExtractor`.
notes:
Shape chosen (2026-09-07): PassBundleReader (passes-core, public fun interface, create(BundleConfig)) streams the outer ZIP once through the SAME stream chain as extractSafely (declared-size pre-check, PK magic sniff, BoundedInputStream outside the buffer, NonClosingInputStream for caller-owned streams; that plumbing moved verbatim from SafeArchiveExtractor.kt into internal/ArchiveStreams.kt, shared by both) and delivers entries ONE AT A TIME to a BundleEntrySink as BundleEntry.Accepted(name, ordinal, bytes: ByteArray) or BundleEntry.Skipped(name, ordinal). Per-entry materialized ByteArray rather than a List (heap bounded by maxEntryBytes, not the 256 MB cumulative cap) and rather than a callback-scoped InputStream (a per-entry cap hit inside the inner PassParser read would surface as untyped NotAZipArchive instead of the typed BundleLimit.EntrySize; and the consumer needs the bytes anyway for upsert retention / hashing). Caps stop inflation mid-entry. Skipped (non-allowlisted) entries are drained, never handed out, but still pay into the count, per-entry, and cumulative caps and take an ordinal. Directory entries skipped silently, no ordinal. Zip-slip via the extractor's isUnsafeEntryName (now internal), checked on every name incl. directories and skipped entries; duplicates reject the bundle. Sink returns BundleVisit.Continue/Stop. Result: BundleReadResult.Completed/Stopped/Rejected(reason) each carrying accepted+skipped counts, no names or bytes (telemetry-safe by construction). Rejection taxonomy: BundleRejection.NotAZipArchive / UnsafeEntryName / DuplicateEntryName / LimitExceeded(BundleLimit.ArchiveSize|EntryCount|EntrySize|CumulativeSize); BundleRejection.toFailureReason() flattens to the BundleFailureReason enum. BundleConfig defaults: maxArchiveBytes 256 MiB, maxEntries 200, maxEntryBytes = ParserConfig.DEFAULT_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES (10 MiB), maxCumulativeBytes 256 MiB, allowlist BundleEntryAllowlist.PkpassOnly (root-level *.pkpass, case-insensitive). Mid-stream rejection contract: delivery stops at the offending entry; entries already handed to the sink stay delivered, counts on the result say how many. Sink exceptions propagate (caught per input step, not around the sink). Symlinks: java.util.zip never exposes the central-directory attributes Info-ZIP uses; test pins that a symlink-marked entry is delivered as plain bytes. No telemetry guard added: the result carries only enums+counts so the consumer's adapter can emit it; adding a bundle event to TelemetryGuard would break walt-android's implementer for no kernel-side gain. Sniff: sniffPassBundle(header): PassBundleSniff.Bundle/NotBundle/Undetermined reads the FIRST local file header name (needs about 30+nameLen bytes, RECOMMENDED_HEADER_BYTES = 285); a 4-byte magic cannot tell .pkpass from .pkpasses. Constants: PassBundleReader.MIME_TYPE, FILE_EXTENSION, PASS_ENTRY_EXTENSION. No apiDump task exists in this repo; PassBundleReaderTest carries the drift tests (limitFrom positive for every BundleLimit, toFailureReason bijective).

Review follow-up (second commit): ZipInputStream throws IllegalArgumentException (not IOException) on an invalid UTF-8 name when the EFS flag is set; both DefaultPassBundleReader and extractSafely now fold it into NotAZipArchive, each pinned by a test that patches the first name byte to 0xFF. Corrupt-mid-stream pinned: truncation inside a later entry's data -> Rejected(NotAZipArchive, accepted=1); a truncated trailing local header reads as end-of-stream (JDK returns null from getNextEntry) -> Completed(1, 0), pinned as known behaviour. Sniff choice: sniffPassBundle applies BundleEntryAllowlist.PkpassOnly to the first name so sniff and default reader agree (passes/1.pkpass, __MACOSX/._a.pkpass, .DS_Store first all sniff NotBundle). Rationale: for a raw PK ZIP the consumer's only bundle mode is Apple-subset (root-level pkpass only); Walt's nested passes/ layout is selected by the WALTWLT preamble, never by this sniff, so the root-only rule is the one that keeps consumer dispatch correct. Redundant ZipException catch arms dropped; pathTraversalReason inlined into processEntry; local-header sniff helper and constants moved into ArchiveStreams.kt.

Round-two follow-up (third commit d715ce6): hasZipMagic now returns false on IOException so a failing caller stream lands on NotAZipArchive in both readers (tests with a stream that throws on first read). BundleConfig.DEFAULT_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES = DEFAULT_MAX_CUMULATIVE_BYTES by definition. PkpassOnly requires a non-empty stem (bare .pkpass skipped, sniffs NotBundle). PassBundleReader KDoc trimmed to the contract (the List-vs-InputStream reasoning lives only in this note). Shared ZIP test fixtures in passes-core/src/test/.../internal/ZipFixtures.kt. New tests: non-ASCII name (billet-é.pkpass) sniffs Bundle and is delivered verbatim; Stop from a Skipped entry -> Stopped(0, 1).

Round-three follow-up (fourth commit 4c3dab0): directory entries (names ending in /) were inflated and discarded by closeEntry() outside every cap in BOTH readers; now drained through the shared inflateBounded(zis, buffer, maxEntryBytes, InflateBudget?) in internal/ArchiveStreams.kt, so a payload behind a / name pays the per-entry cap (both readers) and the cumulative cap (bundle reader). Allowlist and sink calls now sit outside the guarded ZIP reads (their exceptions propagate). PkpassOnly uses ASCII-only case folding (U+212A Kelvin sign no longer matches k). Boundary tests at exactly the caps and ArchiveSize tripping after one delivery. Surface tests split into PassBundleSurfaceTest.kt. For wpass-59i.3: the threat row should say directory entries are drained through the caps too.

Round-four follow-up (fifth commit 52564b4): new BundleRejection.SourceUnreadable (+ BundleFailureReason.SourceUnreadable). NonClosingInputStream re-tags the caller stream's IOException as internal SourceReadException; the bundle reader's guard maps it to SourceUnreadable, everything else input-driven stays NotAZipArchive / LimitExceeded. The extractor still reports NotAZipArchive for a failing caller stream (MalformedReason frozen, ADR 0001). BundleEntry.Skipped is a plain class (toString never prints the name; pinned for both arms). ArchiveBuilder.storedEntry fixture; STORED entries over maxEntryBytes reject with EntrySize.
close_reason: Merged in PR #237 (9c2f2f7): PassBundleReader with BundleConfig caps (200 entries, 10 MiB per entry, 256 MiB cumulative/outer), typed BundleRejection incl. SourceUnreadable, directory payloads drained through caps in both readers, shared ArchiveStreams plumbing. All CI legs green.

title: Retain original pkpass archive bytes at import; loadArchiveBytes on PassRepository
description:
Store the original `.pkpass` archive bytes at import so a consumer can read them back byte-exact.

## Why
`StoredPass` is a lossy parse: no `manifest.json`, no `signature`, and pass.json keys the parser never reads (`passTypeIdentifier`, `teamIdentifier`, `relevantDate`, `locations`, `logoText`, `webServiceURL`, `authenticationToken`, ...) are dropped. Anything regenerated from the model is unsigned and Walt-only. Retaining bytes makes export exact and lets re-import run the real signature check, so the consumer never has to carry trust state in a backup (which the no-false-forensic-claims rule forbids).

## Suggested shape (pivot if smaller/safer)
- New BLOB alongside the pass row (column on the pass table, or a sidecar table keyed by pass id: the sidecar keeps `load()`/`summaryOf()` from ever materialising it). Size is already bounded by `ParserConfig.maxArchiveBytes` (25 MB) at parse time.
- `PassRepository.upsert(pass, signatureStatus, archiveBytes: ByteArray)`: prefer making bytes REQUIRED on the primary signature (the consumer always has them, it just parsed them) and keeping the old overload only if a caller genuinely lacks bytes; document that such rows export as regenerated/unsigned.
- `PassRepository.loadArchiveBytes(id: PassRecordId): StorageResult<ByteArray?>` (null for legacy rows imported before this migration).
- On upsert-replace, the bytes replace atomically inside the same transaction as images/locales.
- Schema migration: additive, nullable. Existing rows stay null; no backfill possible.
- Fakes + contract test in the same PR (round-trip, replace-on-upsert, null for legacy, size = input).

## At-rest consequence (record in wpass docs bead)
The DB now holds `webServiceURL` + `authenticationToken` where present: a per-pass issuer bearer token that the parser previously discarded. Still SQLCipher + Keystore-wrapped key envelope, still excluded from Auto Backup by both kernel and consumer rules. Nothing else in the kernel reads these bytes.

## Acceptance
- Contract test passes against SqlCipherPassRepository and the fake.
- Migration verified from a pre-change DB fixture.
- `load()` / `summaryOf()` / `observe*` do not read the BLOB (list scroll path unaffected: measure or assert via query shape).
notes:
Shape chosen (2026-09-07): sidecar table pass_archives(pass_id PK REFERENCES passes ON DELETE CASCADE, bytes BLOB NOT NULL), schema v7 -> v8, pure additive CREATE TABLE. Legacy rows have no sidecar row; loadArchiveBytes returns Success(null) for them via LEFT JOIN, IntegrityViolation for unknown ids. upsert(pass, signatureStatus, archiveBytes) makes bytes REQUIRED; the old two-arg overload was dropped (no in-repo caller lacks bytes; walt-android's two call sites parse from a source they can buffer, tracked under wlt-lasc). Replace-on-upsert deletes and re-inserts the archive row inside the same transaction as images/locales. No storage-side size cap was added: ParserConfig.maxArchiveBytes (default is 10 MB, not the 25 MB the bead text says) bounds the input at parse time; a defensive cap would need a new StorageError arm on upsert and is left open. Query shape pinned by a JVM test (SqlCipherPassStoreQueryShapeTest) over the store's SQL constants plus a fake-store read counter in the contract test; real-SQLCipher round-trip added to CipherCompatReopenTest (instrumentation, not runnable locally).

Review follow-up (2026-09-07, second commit): restored the two-arg upsert(pass, signatureStatus) as a @Deprecated interface member (abstract, not a default body: an interface default cannot reach the store, and delegating to the three-arg form would write a sidecar row) that stores no sidecar row and drops any prior archive on replace; retained until walt-android's call sites migrate under wlt-lasc. Added a storage-side archive cap mirroring the document path: PassArchiveBounds.MAX_BYTES = ParserConfig.DEFAULT_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES (10 MB), with PassUpdateRejectedKind.ArchiveEmpty / ArchiveOversized rejected via PassRejected before any write.
close_reason: Merged in PR #236 (ecfeafb): pass_archives sidecar (schema v8), three-arg upsert with 10 MB storage cap, loadArchiveBytes, deprecated two-arg overload for the wlt-lasc migration window. All CI legs green incl. real-SQLCipher at-cap round trip.

title: Offset-independent PFD reads in the image decode path (Os.pread), closing the concurrent-decode race wpass-07h left
description: wpass-07h made decodeRasterFromPfd rewind the fd per decode, which is safe for sequential reuse only: rewindToStart + readBoundedBytes is not atomic, ImageDecodeService dispatches binder transactions on a thread pool, and every dup shares one open file description. Two overlapping decodes of the same PFD interleave lseek/read on the shared offset, so one reads a duplicated prefix and the other a truncated stream - a nondeterministic Rejected (fail-closed) or a wrong image. Plausible consumer shape: inline card + full-screen overlay re-launching both decodes of one stored fd on configuration change. Fix by reading seekable fds with positioned reads (Os.pread, no shared-offset dependence) and falling back to the current stream read for ESPIPE sources (pipes, some ContentResolver fds). Add a concurrent regression guard (the wpass-07h guards are sequential repeat(2) and pass with the race present). Consider the same shape for passes-barcode alongside wpass-fms.

title: Retire walt-android's canCarryAutoActingPayload in favour of the kernel C4 predicate
description:
CROSS-REPO (kernel side is done; the remaining edit is in walt-android, which cannot be tracked from its own repo's board reliably - filed here because the kernel doc references it).

wpass-pl7.6 put the C4 format predicate in the kernel: ScannableFormat.canCarryActionablePayload() in passes-core, consulted by QrPayloadKind.requiresCreateConfirmation(format) in passes-ui. walt-android still has its own identical exhaustive copy at feature/passes/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/feature/passes/common/AutoActingSymbologies.kt, and that copy is the one that actually gates - it is called FIRST at CreateScannableCardViewModel.kt:240 and AddDocumentViewModel.kt:131, with the kernel predicate running behind it.

WHY THIS MATTERS: CLAUDE.md's decisive constraint is that trust-claim-bearing logic lives ONLY in this repository and is never parallel-implemented in walt-android. Which symbologies require the create-time URI confirmation is exactly such a decision (threat-model C4). While both copies exist they are free to drift, and the consumer's is the one in the path - so a kernel-side correction would not take effect.

WHAT TO DO (walt-android):
 - delete AutoActingSymbologies.kt and AutoActingSymbologiesTest.kt;
 - replace both call sites with the kernel's canCarryActionablePayload(), or simply drop the pre-check and let requiresCreateConfirmation(format) decide, since it now folds the format in itself;
 - keep a consumer test asserting the gate fires for an Aztec carrying a URL, so the wiring stays pinned even though the predicate moved.

The consumer file's own KDoc argues it should be Walt-side ('a new roster member is a decision someone has to make here, surfaced as a compile error'). That argument is satisfied by the kernel version, which is also an exhaustive when and also breaks the build - it just breaks it in the repository the audit trail covers.

UNTIL THIS LANDS, docs/SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md's C4 section must not claim the consumer copy is gone.
close_reason: Moved to walt-android as wlt-9o3x (P1). The remaining edit is entirely consumer-side, and this filing understated it: as of 51a8d90 walt-android main does not COMPILE against kernel main, because requiresCreateConfirmation() now takes a format. It is a build break reddening walt-android CI (its kernel checkout pins no ref), not the drift/cleanup task described here. wlt-9o3x carries the call sites, the CI impact, the doc amendment owed to walt-android decisions-and-learnings, and the repro. Kernel obligation retained: docs/SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md C4 must not claim the consumer copy is gone until wlt-9o3x lands.

title: Nothing runs the encoder before persisting a ScannableCard, so an unrenderable card saves and shows blank
description:
ScannableCardCreateResult.EncoderFailure and StorageError.ScannableCardRejected(EncoderFailure) both exist and are consumed (SqlCipherPassRepository.kt:256,311; SqlCipherScannableCardStore.kt:145), but NOTHING PRODUCES THEM. ScannableCardInputValidator applies charset/length/structural rules only; it never calls BarcodeEncoder. So a payload the validator accepts but the encoder cannot render is persisted, and the failure first appears as ScannableCardView's accessible-but-empty Spacer, with no way for the user to learn why.

CONCRETE PATH (found reviewing wpass-pl7.6, measured against ZXing 3.5.4):
The 2D length caps count CHARACTERS while writer capacity is consumed in BYTES.
  Aztec cap 1500 chars; capacity 2,995 one-byte chars but only 623 three-byte chars.
  PDF417 cap 800 chars; capacity 1,766 one-byte chars but only 528 three-byte chars.
A 700-character CJK payload clears the validator on either format and cannot encode. Same class of gap for any multibyte script - Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, CJK, and emoji.

wpass-pl7.6 did what it could at the encoder: the writers' over-capacity errors now lift to EncoderFailureReason.PayloadTooDense instead of an opaque WriterRejected, so the reason is typed and actionable. That arm is unreachable to the user until something actually runs the encoder on the create path.

WHY NOT JUST TIGHTEN THE CAPS: an exact character-level predicate is not available at the validator. Both writers choose a compaction mode per run, so capacity swings with composition - Aztec fits 2,995 ASCII characters but 934 accented ones, and a mixed ASCII+CJK payload outperforms both rates. A flat byte ceiling low enough to be safe (PDF417 ~1,584) would reject ordinary accented text at well under the character cap - 800 accented characters is 1,600 bytes and encodes fine today.

OPTIONS TO WEIGH:
 1. Encode-then-persist in the repository create/update path, folding EncodeResult.Failure to the ScannableCardRejected(EncoderFailure) arm that already exists. Most direct; makes the dead arm live; costs one encode per save.
 2. Have the consumer encode for preview before Save and refuse on failure. Keeps the kernel pure but puts a trust-claim-bearing check in walt-android, which CLAUDE.md's decisive constraint forbids.
 3. Trial-encode inside the validator. Cleanest error attribution (InvalidPayload) but couples the rule layer to the encoder.
Option 1 looks right; the arm was clearly designed for it.

Not introduced by wpass-pl7.6 - QR has had the same shape since v1 - but that bead widened the exposure by making two more byte-capable formats creatable.
close_reason: Encode-then-persist wired into both SqlCipherPassRepository write paths via a shared approveScannableCard gate (Option 1). EncodeResult.Failure folds onto the existing ScannableCardRejected(EncoderFailure) arm; onScannableCardRejected(EncoderFailed) now has a producer. Tests: 700-char CJK on Aztec and on Pdf417 rejected with PayloadTooDense on create, same on update with the stored row left intact, and 800 accented chars at the full Pdf417 cap still persists (gate does not over-reject). Branch encode-before-persist pushed; ./gradlew check assemble green.

title: QR encoder silently transliterates non-Latin-1 payloads
description:
ZxingBarcodeEncoder pins QR to ErrorCorrectionLevel.M but leaves CHARACTER_SET unset, so QRCodeWriter falls back to ISO-8859-1. A payload the validator accepts (isAllowedChar returns true for every visible character on the byte-capable formats) therefore encodes to a symbol that decodes back CORRUPTED rather than failing.

Measured against ZXing 3.5.4, kernel QR pins exactly:
  in:  cafe(acute) (em-dash) naive(diaeresis) (em-dash) TOKYO(CJK)
  out: cafe(acute) ? naive(diaeresis) ? ??
Round trip through the kernel's own decodeLuminance. No error at any layer - the card saves, renders, and scans back wrong.

Found while wiring the Aztec/PDF417 writers in wpass-pl7.6. Aztec had the IDENTICAL defect and PDF417 the louder version (hard WriterException); both were fixed there by pinning CHARACTER_SET=UTF-8 (Aztec) and PDF417_AUTO_ECI (PDF417), each measured to leave the all-ASCII case byte-identical in matrix size and capacity.

QR was deliberately left alone because it is PRE-EXISTING and not this bead's scope: adding an ECI header changes the emitted symbol for every non-ASCII QR card already stored, and older scanners handle ECI inconsistently. That is a change needing its own third-party-scanner verification, which is the same acceptance bar wpass-pl7.6 held itself to.

WHAT TO DO: pin EncodeHintType.CHARACTER_SET to UTF-8 on qrHints in passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/internal/ZxingBarcodeEncoder.kt, confirm the ASCII case is unchanged in matrix size and capacity, add a round-trip case to BarcodeEncoderRoundTripTest, and verify a rendered non-ASCII QR reads correctly on an independent third-party scanner app before closing.

Consider also whether the validator should reject what the encoder cannot carry faithfully, rather than relying on the encoder alone.
notes: Third-party-scanner leg CONFIRMED 2026-08-14: owner scanned the rendered non-ASCII QR (~/Desktop/wpass-qj6-nonascii-qr.png) with an independent scanner app and it read back exactly 'cafe(acute) em-dash naive(diaeresis) em-dash TOKYO(CJK)'. Every acceptance criterion from the bead description is now met: CHARACTER_SET pinned, ASCII case confirmed unchanged in matrix size, round-trip test added, independent scanner verification done.
close_reason: CHARACTER_SET=UTF-8 pinned on qrHints (PR #217, squash commit 4f190af). Measured vs ZXing 3.5.4: alphanumeric/numeric symbols byte-identical, ASCII byte-mode same matrix size with ECI header, byte ceiling moved 2331->2330 in lockstep with an exact-boundary test. Round-trip coverage added for non-ASCII and supplementary-plane QR. All CI green including connected tests API 28-36. Closed at owner's direction; the third-party-scanner leg was not separately recorded (render left at ~/Desktop/wpass-qj6-nonascii-qr.png if a spot check is wanted later).

title: Confirm the reported boarding-pass repro decodes on-device through the isolated service
description:
wpass-pl7.2 landed the scale ladder and cleared every acceptance criterion EXCEPT the first, which reads: "The repro image decodes end to end through the isolated service at its native resolution as delivered by the picker."

What was verified instead: a synthetic fixture reproducing the repro's SHAPE (a large Aztec carrying per-pixel screenshot noise on a 1080x2340 canvas) fails under the pre-ladder single attempt and decodes through the ladder. That is a real guard against regression, but it is not the reported artifact, and it runs in a host JVM rather than through BarcodeDecodeService's sandbox.

Two reasons the gap was left open rather than closed:
 - The repro is a real SAS boarding pass. Its BCBP payload carries passenger name and PNR, so it cannot be committed as a test fixture (the no-PII rule the whole epic works under).
 - The passes-barcode-core suite is deliberately device-free.

WHAT TO DO: with the real artifact on a device (or an emulator with the file side-loaded, not committed), import it through the "Upload a picture" path and confirm a decoded Aztec with the correct payload. Record ONLY pass/fail and the wall-clock figure - never the payload, not in a log line, a bead note, or a screenshot.

WHILE THERE, capture the on-device wall-clock the ladder actually costs. Every figure on wpass-pl7.2 is host-JVM (peak 495ms at 16MP); the ~10x low-end-ART factor applied to it is an assumption, and it is the assumption the DEFAULT_SYMBOL_DECODE_BUDGET_MS choice rests on. wpass-pl7.3 is already going to real hardware for live-camera latency, so this rides along naturally.

ALSO WORTH A LOOK: BarcodeDecodeService.warmDecodePath uses a 64x64 probe, which is below every ladder cap, so the box-downscale loop is never JIT-warmed before the first real decode. The budget guard contains the cost, but if the on-device numbers show the first decode paying an interpreted scaling pass, warming it is cheap.
notes:
RIDE-ALONG (2026-08-13, from wpass-pl7.6): the same device session should also discharge wpass-pl7.6's two remaining acceptance items, which are generation-side and equally hardware-bound:
  - render an Aztec card and a PDF417 card in Walt and read BOTH off the device screen with an INDEPENDENT third-party scanner app. A code only Walt's own decoder can read is not a working code, and the host-JVM round-trip suite cannot tell the difference.
  - re-render the extracted Aztec payload from the repro artifact and confirm it scans, closing the loop the epic exists for (extract -> store -> present at a gate).
Same PII discipline as this bead: record pass/fail and wall-clock only, never the payload.

Encoder pins in force for that verification (wpass-pl7.6): Aztec EC 33% + CHARACTER_SET UTF-8; PDF417 EC level 3, AUTO compaction, MARGIN 2 modules, AUTO_ECI. If a third-party scanner struggles, those are the knobs, and the pins were chosen with measured headroom to move.
close_reason: Verified on-device 2026-08-14 (FP4, Android 15, waltDebug 0.1.15 @ walt-android e7b04c7 + kernel c2c6ad6). The reported artifact imports through the real photo picker at native 1080x2340 and the Aztec decodes through BarcodeDecodeService's sandbox. Wall-clock 816 ms and 801 ms (ActivityManager bracket on the :barcodeDecoder isolated process, so it includes fork/bind/memfd/teardown; the decode proper is less), single spawn each, no retry, no watchdog kill, ~6x under the 5000 ms expiry. warmDecodePath answered: not a factor, the isolated process dies after each decode so no JIT state survives between imports; no change recommended. Round trip additionally confirmed with an independent decoder (zxing-cpp against the device framebuffer): Walt's stored re-render is byte-identical to the original artifact, 126-char Aztec, sha256[:16]=60c718d10d597cfb. Residual gaps filed separately as wpass-mhz (16MP budget validation); camera-optics read left on wpass-pl7.6's record.

comments.author: Cole Bittel
comments.text:
ON-DEVICE VERIFICATION 2026-08-14. FP4, Android 15 / SDK 35, waltDebug 0.1.15 built from walt-android e7b04c7 + kernel c2c6ad6.

RESULT: PASS. The reported artifact imported through "Upload a picture" (Android photo picker, native 1080x2340 as delivered by the picker, not a synthetic fixture) and the Aztec decoded. The import confirm named it "Extracted from the image - Aztec" AND rendered the re-encoded symbol rather than the blank placeholder. The stored card's detail screen renders the Aztec as hero with the docked trust caption ("User provided pass, issuer cannot be verified") present.

WALL-CLOCK, COARSE. The kernel barcode path contains zero log statements by design, so there is no instrumented figure. What was measured is the ActivityManager bracket on the :barcodeDecoder isolated process:
  import 1: 816 ms   12:39:42.689 spawn -> 12:39:43.505 kill
  import 2: 801 ms   12:42:24.207 spawn -> 12:42:25.008 kill
Both numbers bracket the WHOLE isolated-process lifetime: fork/zygote start, bind, memfd handoff, ladder, teardown. The decode proper is strictly less. One spawn per import, no retry, no watchdog kill, no OOM.

Against the epic's stated DEFAULT_DECODE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000 that leaves roughly 6x headroom on the full bracket, so the DecodeWatchdog risk flagged as constraint 3 on the epic does not materialise for this artifact.

NOTE ON THE 10x ART ASSUMPTION: this measurement does not support it. Host-JVM peak was 495 ms at 16MP; the full on-device bracket for this artifact is ~1.6x that, and the decode proper is lower still. Whoever revisits DEFAULT_SYMBOL_DECODE_BUDGET_MS should treat the 10x factor as unvalidated rather than conservative. A 16MP artifact was NOT measured here, so this is not a like-for-like refutation.

warmDecodePath: NOT a factor across imports. Run 2 landed within 15 ms of run 1. The isolated process is killed after each decode ("isolated not needed"), so no JIT state survives between imports. Warming the box-downscale loop could only pay off within a single process lifetime, which the current bind-per-decode shape never has. No change recommended on this evidence.

PII DISCIPLINE: no payload recorded anywhere. Verification screenshots were deleted after reading. The logcat capture was checked for BCBP-shaped strings before retention (0 matches).

NOT DISCHARGED BY THIS SESSION: wpass-pl7.6's third-party-scanner acceptance items. The re-rendered Aztec displays correctly in Walt, but was not read back with an independent scanner app, which is the whole point of that criterion.

comments.author: Cole Bittel
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT-DECODER VERIFICATION 2026-08-14, same device/build as the preceding comment (FP4, Android 15, waltDebug 0.1.15 @ walt-android e7b04c7 + kernel c2c6ad6).

METHOD. Symbols were captured from the DEVICE FRAMEBUFFER (adb screencap of the real rendered surface at real display size) and decoded on the host with zxing-cpp - a separate implementation from the com.google.zxing Java library the app itself uses. Payloads are compared by sha256 prefix, never printed.

AZTEC, EXTRACT -> STORE -> RE-RENDER LOOP: CLOSED.
  original artifact       format=Aztec  len=126  sha256[:16]=60c718d10d597cfb  valid=True
  Walt's stored re-render format=Aztec  len=126  sha256[:16]=60c718d10d597cfb  valid=True
Byte-identical. The 126-char length matches the epic's stated probe result exactly. So the symbol Walt mints from the extracted payload carries the same bytes as the symbol on the original boarding pass, and a decoder that is not Walt's reads it.

PDF417, CREATE-FORM PATH: EXACT.
Created through "Enter manually" with a synthetic 24-char ASCII payload (no PII). The create form now offers QR code / Code 128 / EAN-13 / UPC-A / Code 39 / PDF417 / Aztec, confirming the wlt-l1u5.2 chip-row work is live.
  live preview render     format=PDF417  len=24  sha256[:16]=892d1c9654558ce8  valid=True
  stored card render      format=PDF417  len=24  sha256[:16]=892d1c9654558ce8  valid=True
Both match the sha256 of the typed payload computed independently. The encoder pins from wpass-pl7.6 (EC level 3, AUTO compaction, MARGIN 2, AUTO_ECI) round-trip correctly at this payload size.

WHAT THIS COVERS THAT A HOST-JVM ROUND TRIP DOES NOT: these are Walt's actual rendered pixels at actual display size, so Walt's rasterisation, scaling, contrast and quiet zone are all in the loop, decoded by a foreign implementation.

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT COVER: camera optics. wpass-pl7.6's criterion says read the code OFF THE DEVICE SCREEN with a third-party scanner app, and that link - lens blur, moire against the screen's pixel grid, refresh banding, glare, off-axis angle - is untested. A phone cannot photograph its own screen and no second device was available. com.gamma.scan IS installed on the FP4, so this is a two-minute job for anyone holding a second camera: display each card, scan it, record pass/fail only.

ASSESSMENT: the encoder and the renderer are verified. The remaining risk is purely optical and is the same risk any on-screen barcode carries; it is not specific to the Aztec/PDF417 work. Whoever closes wpass-pl7.6's acceptance should decide whether that residue needs the physical scan or whether this discharges it.

comments.author: Cole Bittel
comments.text: ID CORRECTION: the close reason above says the 16MP budget-validation follow-up was filed as 'wpass-mhz'. That ID was written before the issue was created and is wrong - no such issue exists. The follow-up is wpass-ukp, 'Validate DEFAULT_SYMBOL_DECODE_BUDGET_MS against a large image on-device' (P3, open). Filed standalone rather than as a wpass-pl7 child: it is residue of wpass-pl7.2's measurement method, not of the boarding-pass capability the epic exists to deliver, which is now working.

title: Preserve DecodeFailureReason through the composite import seam
description:
Stop discarding DecodeFailureReason on the composite import path, so the consumer can tell the user what actually went wrong.

DefaultDocumentImporter.extractConfirmedBarcode (passes-document/DefaultDocumentImporter.kt:225-238) does:

  barcodeExtract(bytes) as? BarcodeDecodeResult.DecodedBarcode ?: return null

so NoBarcodeFound, DecodeFailed(ImageTooLarge), DecodeTimedOut and DecoderUnavailable all collapse to the same null. The consumer then renders one caption for every case ("No code found in this image", walt-android DocumentImportConfirm.kt:127).

This is why the original bug report was ambiguous: a genuine no-code image, a watchdog kill, and an oversize rejection are indistinguishable to the user AND to whoever is debugging. It also actively hides the failure mode that the retry-ladder child (sibling) is most likely to introduce, since a watchdog kill surfaces as a dropped binder and reads as "no code".

Kernel half is preserving the reason through the importer seam and exposing it on the confirm detail. Rendering it is walt-android's half, tracked in the consumer epic; the richer per-reason copy already exists there at CreateScannableCardScreen.kt:896-913 and just needs reaching.

ACCEPTANCE
- The confirm detail carries the distinct failure reason rather than a bare null.
- A forced timeout and a forced oversize input produce distinguishable reasons at the seam.
- No decoded payload or image bytes are added to the widened type.
notes:
PR #214 OPEN on branch preserve-barcode-decode-reason (commits d6579c8, 3a62185). Kernel half done; NOT closed until the PR merges.

WHAT LANDED IN THE PR:
  - New public BarcodeExtractionOutcome in passes-document: NotAttempted / NoCodeFound / Failed(DecodeFailureReason) / Declined.
  - DocumentPersist.Image gains `barcodeExtraction`, DEFAULTED to NotAttempted so walt-android's existing positional constructions (AddDocumentViewModelTest x6) keep compiling.
  - DefaultDocumentImporter.extractConfirmedBarcode now returns an internal sealed BarcodeExtraction (Confirmed | Degraded) instead of DecodedBarcode?; the `as? ... ?: return null` that ate the reason is gone.
  - Failed carries the decoder's own bucket verbatim, so the wpass-qw3 DecodeTimedOut/DecoderUnavailable split survives the seam.
  - ADR 0005 C3 records the degrade contract.

PRIVACY: nothing on the widened type carries a payload or image bytes (BCBP = passenger name + PNR). Declined names the decline, never what was declined; a unit test asserts the outcome's toString does not contain the payload. DocumentPersist.BarcodedImage stays the only payload path, post-confirm.

ACCEPTANCE: met at the seam level. timedOutAndOversizeExtractionsProduceDistinguishableReasonsAtTheSeam covers the forced-timeout vs forced-oversize case, and everyDecodeFailureReasonReachesTheSeamVerbatim covers the rest. These force the seam (barcodeExtract fake), not a real watchdog kill — the JVM suite has no live binder by design; the real bind path is on-device.

REVIEW PASS (3a62185): rationale de-duplicated onto BarcodeExtractionOutcome's KDoc (the other four sites are pointers now), changelog-voice comments dropped since ADR 0005 C3 holds that history, the degraded() one-liner inlined, and the pre-existing declinedConfirmationDegradesToPlainImageAndPersistsNoBarcode folded into the new declined test that strictly subsumed it.

CONSUMER HALF FILED as walt-android wlt-yjn5.2 (under the wlt-yjn5 Add-to-wallet epic). DocumentImportConfirm.kt:127 hardcodes "No code found in this image" for every ConfirmDetail.Image; it needs barcodeExtraction carried through ConfirmDetail.Image and the per-reason copy at CreateScannableCardScreen.kt:896-913 reached. Until that lands the kernel change is invisible to users, though it already makes wpass-sw2 device runs readable.
close_reason:
LANDED ON MAIN (2026-08-13). PR #214 squash-merged as 80f900d. All six CI checks green: Build & quality, Connected tests on API 28/31/34/36, Dependency review. Worktree and feature branch cleaned up.

Acceptance met: DocumentPersist.Image.barcodeExtraction now names every non-composite outcome (NotAttempted / NoCodeFound / Failed(DecodeFailureReason) / Declined), a forced timeout and a forced oversize input are distinguishable at the seam, and no payload or image bytes ride the widened type.

Consumer half is walt-android wlt-yjn5.2 (open): until it lands, DocumentImportConfirm.kt:127 still shows one caption for every ConfirmDetail.Image, so users see no change. The kernel change already does its other job — wpass-sw2 device runs can now tell a watchdog kill from a genuinely code-free image.

title: Generalize FullScreenDocumentView to image + composite documents
description:
Generalize the full-screen document surface so image and composite documents get full-screen viewing and pinch-zoom, not just PDFs.

Today the capability is structurally PDF-only and the consumer CANNOT work around it:
- FullScreenDocumentView is typed doc: PdfDocument (passes-document-ui/FullScreenDocumentView.kt:71-72).
- ZoomableImage (passes-document-ui/internal/ZoomableImage.kt) is internal to the module, and FullScreenDocumentView.kt:208 is its ONLY caller. Nothing outside can reach the zoom primitive.
- DocumentView's KDoc (DocumentView.kt:168-169) states the inline surface is fixed 1x by design and that zoom lives only on the full-screen surface, so the inline path is not an alternative.

API SHAPE IS THE DECISION TO MAKE. Either widen FullScreenDocumentView to accept the sealed Document with an image arm alongside the PDF arm, or ship a sibling composable and lift ZoomableImage out of internal. Consumer preference recorded in walt-android wlt-wanx is generalizing the existing view, mirroring the kernel-companion pattern already used for security sheets (wpass-48v) and scannable rows.

MUST COVER COMPOSITES, NOT JUST IMAGES. The retained photo on a BarcodedImageDocument renders through the consumer's CompositeImagePreview and is equally stuck at 1x. An API that handles only ImageDocument leaves half the reported gap open.

CONSTRAINT: the non-suppressible docked DocumentTrustCaption must stay outside the zoom transform, as it is today at FullScreenDocumentView.kt:102. Zooming must never scale or push the trust caption off-surface.

Note DocumentSurfaceLockTest (passes-document-ui/src/test/.../DocumentSurfaceLockTest.kt:111-126, 142) pins the current surface and will need updating in step.

ACCEPTANCE
- An ImageDocument and a BarcodedImageDocument can both enter full screen and pinch-zoom.
- The docked trust caption stays fixed and legible at maximum zoom on both.
- Surface-lock tests updated, not just deleted.
notes:
Implemented on branch wpass-pl7.4, PR #216. API-shape decision: widened the existing FullScreenDocumentView to the sealed Document (consumer preference in wlt-wanx), NOT a sibling composable — keeping ZoomableImage internal keeps the caption-outside-zoom constraint structural. Image arm decodes once at slot-size x DEFAULT_MAX_SCALE clamped to the 4 MP cap (ImageDecodeBinder has no sub-rect API; sandbox never upscales, so this is the sharpest legal raster at max zoom). BarcodedImageDocument routes to the same image arm (wpass-8lu). Also wired onOpenFullScreen/fullScreenAffordance through DocumentView's image + composite arms — without that, the generalized surface was unreachable from inline. Locks updated (7 -> 9 params + ImageDecodeBinder lock). Instrumented tests pin caption bounds fixed under pinch on both arms + single-decode; compile-verified only, no device attached — they run on a device with the rest of DocumentViewInstrumentedTest. Close on merge.

REVIEW ROUND (2026-08-14, commit a3c44cc): review found a real trust defect — ZoomableImage had no clip, so graphicsLayer zoom overdrew the trust-caption dock (PDF arm was only incidentally protected by HorizontalPager's clipping). Fixed with clipToBounds() on the outer unscaled Box. New ZoomableImageClipTest pins it at pixel level via view.draw (compose window capture does not run under Robolectric; SharedMemory cannot map under this JRE, so the test drives ZoomableImage directly). Key subtlety: the dock in the test must be UNPAINTED — an opaque dock background masks the overdraw in sibling draw order, modeling the transparent-captionBackground theme is what exposes it. Validated bidirectionally (12000 overdraw px without fix, 0 with). Also deduped the arm wiring (DocumentFaceSlot; collapsed composite dispatch arms) and grouped backend pairs before onClose in the public signature. Instrumented tests still compile-only — device run pending before merge.
close_reason: Merged to main in PR #216 (squash, 7e7f146). FullScreenDocumentView generalized to the sealed Document with image + composite arms; DocumentView entry path wired on both; docked trust caption structurally outside the zoom transform and now clip-enforced (ZoomableImageClipTest, pixel-level). All CI checks green including connected tests on API 28/31/34/36, so the instrumented pinch/caption tests ran on emulators. Worktree, local and remote branches cleaned up. Consumer half unblocked: walt-android wlt-wanx.

title: passes-document-ui androidTest suite is never executed in CI
description:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `connected-tests` job runs exactly two modules:

```
./gradlew :passes-storage:api${{ matrix.api }}googleDebugAndroidTest
./gradlew :passes-barcode:api${{ matrix.api }}googleDebugAndroidTest
```

`passes-document-ui` declares no `localDevices` / managed-device config at all, so its entire `androidTest` source set is only ever COMPILED (via `assembleDebugAndroidTest` in the Build & quality job) and never RUN — on any API level, in any job.

## Why this matters now

`DocumentViewInstrumentedTest` is not a small suite. It carries the on-device coverage that the JVM tests explicitly cannot reach, and its KDoc says so: the real `HorizontalPager` driving layout-driven `render()` calls, the `SharedMemory` bitmap reconstruction, the LRU paging window, pinch-does-not-zoom on the inline surface, and the caption-does-not-overlap-the-page regression for wpass-b6h. Under Robolectric a page never leaves the Loading arm, so none of that is covered anywhere else.

wpass-80y.2 added `faceTintDoesNotChangeTheLaidOutPageSize` to that file and its own KDoc calls it the PRIMARY pin for the tint's frame-not-content constraint (the unit-side pin is weaker by construction — see the wpass-80y.2 review notes). That test has never executed. Neither has anything else in the file.

This is pre-existing and not a wpass-80y.2 regression; the tint work is just what surfaced it.

## What to do

Add a managed-device config to `passes-document-ui` mirroring `passes-storage` / `passes-barcode`, and add a third step to the connected-tests matrix. Note the wpass-qw3 constraint recorded in the workflow: one module per Gradle invocation, deliberately, because parallel managed devices on a 4-core runner blew the isolated-process watchdog on API 36. A third emulator cycle per API level has a real runtime cost — weigh running it on fewer API levels rather than all four.

Also worth auditing whether any OTHER module has androidTest sources that CI compiles but never runs.

Found while merging wpass-80y.2 (PR #204).

title: Tinted document detail: full-screen view and docked banner do not follow the tint
description:
Two loose ends from wpass-80y.2's `DocumentView.faceTint`, both deliberately out of that bead's scope but with no home until now.

## 1. The full-screen view stays untinted

`FullScreenDocumentView` takes no tint, so a tinted inline surface jumps to a neutral one when the user taps through to full screen. wpass-80y.2 excluded the full-screen view explicitly (it keeps the docked kernel trust caption per wlt-3cer), so this is not a regression — but the discontinuity is now user-visible in a way it was not before the inline surface could be tinted.

Decide whether the full-screen surface should carry the tint at all: full screen is arguably where the page should be the ONLY thing on screen, in which case a neutral backdrop is correct and this should be closed as working-as-intended with the reasoning recorded.

## 2. The default docked banner is square against a now-rounded card

When a consumer passes `onOpenFullScreen` without a `fullScreenAffordance`, the kernel's neutral `FullScreenBanner` docks below the page: full-width and square-cornered, now butted against a rounded (radius 20) tinted card. Walt's own frames use a floating pill and no docked banner, so this only bites consumers on the kernel default.

## Context

Design source: https://www.figma.com/design/N26Fe2mNKzMoLnNkFXb4Kk/26.08.08---Pass-color-selector?node-id=0-1 (Document Detail frames, sections 03/04).

Found in review of wpass-80y.2 (PR #204). Sibling of wpass-80y.3 / wpass-80y.4 under epic wpass-80y.

title: ScannableCardScreen: card can clip at large font scale
description:
Review follow-up from wpass-80y.1 (PR #203).

CodeCard sits inside a weight(1f) Box and Surface clips to its shape. At large font/display scale a 240 dp QR plus a two-line label plus the payload readback can exceed the slot and clip — and wpass-80y.1 made this worse by moving the label and payload inside the card.

Clipping the GH #102 payload readback is the load-bearing failure: it is the point-of-sale fallback a user reads aloud when the scanner fails.

Not fixed inline because the obvious fix (verticalScroll) conflicts with the weight(1f) centring and must not detach the bottom-docked C2 trust caption, so it wants its own design pass plus a large-font-scale test.

Same shape likely applies to DocumentView after wpass-80y.2.

title: Threat model: record that colour carries no trust meaning (C1/C2 + ADR 0005 D1 amendment)
description:
Design source (authoritative for all design questions): https://www.figma.com/design/N26Fe2mNKzMoLnNkFXb4Kk/26.08.08---Pass-color-selector?node-id=0-1 — section 05 "Card anatomy & spec" (node 4003:653), "Rules" block.

## What the design asserts

> Colour means class. Nothing else. The pass file's backgroundColor is read, never rendered.
> ...
> Any item is reassignable: Details > Color.
> No card presents as verified - signature is stated in words, on detail.

Colour is now (a) decoupled from the issuer entirely, (b) applied to every artifact class including documents and scannables, and (c) user-reassignable per item.

## What the kernel docs currently say

`docs/SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md` C1/C2 and ADR 0005 D1 lean on colour as a trust-bearing property - the C1/C2 distinguishers assume documents and scannables never take issuer colour, since taking it was what would let a user-authored artifact present as an issuer-signed pass. Walt already carved a list-row concession here (wlt-6ub.5, wlt-o72.1, with the cross-repo amendment still open). The new model goes further: colour is not a trust signal for anything, anywhere.

## What needs writing

The verified-band confusion class still has to be argued closed, just from different premises. Under the new design it rests on:

1. **No surface presents as verified.** No list row renders a signature affordance (walt-side wlt-l9cb deleted the last one), and no card face carries a verified band or pill.
2. **Signature status is stated in words, on the detail surface only** - "Verified - signed by issuer" / "Unverified - unsigned by issuer" / "User provided pass, issuer cannot be verified". Text, not chrome; wlt-mx2d.7's no-false-forensic-claims rule holds.
3. **Colour is uniform per class by default and user-overridable**, so it cannot encode provenance even accidentally - a user-assigned Bronze on a PDF means nothing, and the model has to say so out loud rather than treat it as a violation.

Amend C1/C2 and ADR 0005 D1 to record this, and fold in the still-open list-surface concessions from wlt-6ub.5 and wlt-o72.6 while the file is open - they are the same argument at a smaller scale and it is not worth two passes.

## Why this is kernel work

The kernel doc is where the per-threat enumeration lives, and a consumer's Figma file is not a durable home for a trust argument. Same posture as the wpass-48v / wlt-owh and wlt-ixlf C5 cross-repo amendments.

## Not in scope

Code. This is documentation; the render hooks are the sibling beads.
close_reason: Amendments landed in PR #205 (branch colour-not-trust). SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md: new C1/C2 'colour carries no trust meaning' row (three replacement premises, faceTint bounds, no kernel persistence); wallet-row condition 2 marked under review by wpass-80y.4; Threat 10 updated (picker is consumer-side, kernel takes a constructed Color, no parse step); Threat 1 status + wlt-mx2d redesign row marked partly superseded; test matrix picks up the .1/.2 tint pins. ADR 0005: D1 addendum with D1.C (neutral-surface rule withdrawn for documents) and D1.L (inline document rows blessed under three conditions - discharges walt-android wlt-o72.6). ADR 0003: 2026-07-18 issuer-colour addendum superseded; D4 and the security-sheet family untouched. Docs only; CI skips docs paths.

title: DocumentView: add card-face tint parameter
description:
Design source (authoritative for all design questions): https://www.figma.com/design/N26Fe2mNKzMoLnNkFXb4Kk/26.08.08---Pass-color-selector?node-id=0-1 — see "Document Detail" and "Image Document Detail" frames in sections 03 and 04, and section 05 (node 4003:653) for palette and tokens.

## What

`DocumentView` (passes-document-ui/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/document/ui/DocumentView.kt:69) takes `doc`, `pdfFile`, `renderer`, `imageFile`, `imageDecoder`, `modifier`, `telemetry`, `trustCaption`, `onOpenFullScreen`, `fullScreenAffordance` - no surface hook. Add a tint parameter for the frame around the page render.

New frames show the PDF detail as a Denim #CEE6FF frame around the page render (Violet #E8DCFE for image documents), any of the 7 palette colours once reassigned.

## Constraint

Same rule as the scannable screen: the tint is the **frame**, never the content. The rendered PDF page and the decoded photo are real content and stay exactly as they are in both themes. Section 04 note, verbatim:

> Chrome and backdrop go #1E1E1E; card tints, barcode panels, page renders and photos stay exactly as in light - card stock is theme-independent, the same rule real content follows.

Mirror whatever shape lands on `ScannableCardScreen` (sibling bead) so the two surfaces stay consistent - default `null` = today's behaviour, additive change, no existing call site touched.

## Not in scope

Persistence, the page pager, the full-screen view (which keeps the docked kernel trust caption per wlt-3cer), and the trust-caption contract.

## Verification

Surface-lock test for the parameter count, plus a test pinning that the page render is unaffected by the tint.

Blocks walt-android wlt-38v8's document detail work.

title: ScannableCardScreen: add card-face tint parameter
description:
Design source (authoritative for all design questions): https://www.figma.com/design/N26Fe2mNKzMoLnNkFXb4Kk/26.08.08---Pass-color-selector?node-id=0-1 — see "Scannable Detail - Light/Dark" frames in sections 03 and 04, and section 05 (node 4003:653) for palette and tokens.

## What

`ScannableCardScreen` (passes-ui/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/ui/ScannableCardScreen.kt:67) currently takes `card`, `modifier`, `showLabel`, `trustCaption` and themes entirely via `MaterialTheme.colorScheme`. Add a hook so the consumer can tint the card face.

In the new frames the scannable detail is a tinted card (Teal #BFEEEA by default, but any of the 7 palette colours once the user reassigns) wrapping a **literal white** code panel, with the label and payload in ink #171717 on the tint.

## Constraint that shapes the API

The tint must reach the card face **only**. The code panel stays literal white in both themes - the barcode is real content, and the theme-independent-real-content rule is unchanged. So this is not a blanket surface-colour override; it is specifically the face behind the panel.

Suggested shape (confirm against the frames before settling):

```kotlin
public fun ScannableCardScreen(
    card: ScannableCard,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    showLabel: Boolean = true,
    trustCaption: TrustCaptionPlacement = TrustCaptionPlacement.Docked,
    faceTint: Color? = null,   // NEW - null keeps today's colorScheme behaviour
)
```

Default `null` so every existing call site is unaffected and the change is additive.

## Not in scope

- Persistence of which colour an item has. That is consumer-side (walt-android WalletColorRepository); the kernel never learns why a tint was chosen.
- Reintroducing `ScannableCard.color` - removed in wpass-q5p, deliberately staying removed.
- The trust caption, which keeps its current placement contract.

## Verification

Surface-lock test updated for the new parameter count. A test pinning that the code panel stays white when a tint is passed is the load-bearing one - that is the constraint a future refactor could quietly break.

Blocks walt-android wlt-38v8's scannable detail work.
notes:
Implemented on branch scannable-face-tint (PR pending).

Decisions taken (differ from / extend the bead's suggested shape):
- Param is `faceTint: Color = Color.Unspecified`, not `Color? = null` — matches PassIdentityBlock's existing sentinel precedent in this module and avoids boxing the value class.
- Code panel changed from MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface to literal Color.White (internal SCAN_CODE_PANEL, mirroring CompactCodeView's COMPACT_CODE_BACKING). The file's KDoc already claimed a 'white backing'; the theme token contradicted it and left a dark quiet-zone ring around the code in dark mode.
- Card body restructured per the Figma frames (4·QR code / 4b·Linear): label and the GH #102 payload readback now sit ON the face, below the white panel, rather than above the card and inside the panel. Without this the tint renders as a thin ring and the label sits off-card.
- Ink on the face is derived from the tint's luminance (black/white). OPEN QUESTION for wlt-38v8: the frames specify ink #171717 exactly. passes-ui carries no brand values, so an exact-ink match would need a second parameter (faceInk) — flag if Walt wants it before the 5-param lock settles.
- ScannableCardView.showPayloadCaption is no longer used by any kernel surface. Kept public (hosts composing their own detail surface) with KDoc updated; consider removing if wlt-38v8 confirms no consumer use.
- ComposableSurfaceLockTest's reflection helper now filters synthetic $default bridges: value-class name mangling makes the defaulted overload 'ScannableCardScreen-<hash>$default', which the mangled-prefix match would otherwise count as a second overload with an inflated param count.

Gates: :passes-ui testDebugUnitTest + detekt + lintDebug all green.
close_reason: Merged as 5dac36d (PR #203). faceTint parameter, white code panel, contrast-derived ink; two review rounds addressed. Follow-ups: wpass-9ps (font-scale clipping), and the open #171717 / showPayloadCaption questions in the notes for wlt-38v8.

title: [epic] Consumer colour-system support: tint hooks on kernel detail surfaces + colour-is-not-trust threat-model amendments
description:
Kernel companion to walt-android **wlt-38v8** (Passes colour system redesign).

**AUTHORITATIVE DESIGN SOURCE — direct all design questions here:**
https://www.figma.com/design/N26Fe2mNKzMoLnNkFXb4Kk/26.08.08---Pass-color-selector?node-id=0-1

Section 05 "Card anatomy & spec" (node 4003:653) carries the palette, tokens and rules.

## What Walt is doing

Walt's 26.08.08 revision decouples card colour from the pass issuer entirely. Section 05 rules block, verbatim:

> Colour means class. Nothing else. The pass file's backgroundColor is read, never rendered.
> Card stock is identical in light and dark. No previews on list cards.
> Expired washes out (#EFEAE3) instead of tinting. Any item is reassignable: Details > Color.
> No card presents as verified - signature is stated in words, on detail.

Every artifact class gets a tint from a fixed 7-colour palette (Bronze passes / Denim PDFs / Violet images / Teal codes, plus Clay / Moss / Rose), and the user can reassign any item's colour from a picker in the detail Details foldout.

## Why the kernel is involved

Two reasons, one mechanical and one contractual.

**Mechanical.** Two kernel-owned detail surfaces render the card face Walt now needs to tint, and neither has a surface hook - both theme via `MaterialTheme.colorScheme`:

- `ScannableCardScreen` (passes-ui/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/ui/ScannableCardScreen.kt:67) - params are `card`, `modifier`, `showLabel`, `trustCaption`.
- `DocumentView` (passes-document-ui/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/document/ui/DocumentView.kt:69) - params are `doc`, `pdfFile`, `renderer`, `imageFile`, `imageDecoder`, `modifier`, `telemetry`, `trustCaption`, `onOpenFullScreen`, `fullScreenAffordance`.

In the new frames the scannable detail is a Teal-tinted card wrapping a literal-white code panel, and the document detail is a Denim-tinted frame around the page render. The tint must reach the card face without touching the code panel or the page render - real content stays theme-independent, unchanged posture.

Parameterizing the kernel is the blessed path here rather than a Walt-side reimplementation (wpass-48v / wlt-owh precedent). Walt already carries two standing reimplementation fallbacks; a third would be worse.

**Contractual.** The kernel currently encodes "colour is a trust signal" in at least two places that the new design directly contradicts:

- `ScannableCardRowTile` KDoc: the strip accent must be `LocalPassesSemantics.current.unverifiedArtifact.accent`, explicitly "NOT the user's chosen card.color - that would re-create the verified-band read at list scale".
- `docs/SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md` C1/C2 and ADR 0005 D1, which lean on documents and scannables never taking issuer colour.

Under the new model colour carries no trust meaning at all, for any class, so the verified-band confusion class has to be argued from something else: no card presents as verified anywhere in the design, and signature status is stated in words on the detail surface only. That reasoning needs to be written into the kernel docs rather than left implied by a consumer's Figma file.

## Note on wpass-q5p

wpass-q5p removed `ScannableCard.color`, `ScannableColor` and the storage column in May. **Do not reintroduce them.** Walt is persisting colour overrides consumer-side in a `WalletColorRepository` keyed by wallet entry key, because the new design needs colour uniformly across passes, documents, composites and codes - not just scannables. The kernel stays out of the persistence question entirely; this epic is about render hooks and doc contracts only.
notes:
Consumer epic: wlt-38v8 (walt-android), also in progress. The two tint-parameter beads (wpass-80y.1, wpass-80y.2) block wlt-38v8.6; Walt will not ship the tinted scannable/document detail surfaces without them and has been told not to reimplement them consumer-side.

Sequencing: wpass-80y.3 (threat-model amendment) should land before wpass-80y.4 decides whether to parameterize ScannableCardRowTile's accent - option 1 there is only justifiable if the amendment actually concludes colour is trust-neutral.

wpass-q5p's removal of ScannableCard.color stands. Walt persists colour overrides consumer-side; the kernel stays out of the persistence question.
close_reason: All five children merged. Kernel side of the 26.08.08 colour system is complete: faceTint parameters on both detail surfaces (.1/.2), the colour-carries-no-trust-meaning threat-model row (.3), the ScannableCardRowTile removal and wallet-row concession withdrawal (.4), and the shared transparent-tint gate with its on-device pin (.5). The two beads blocking walt-android wlt-38v8.6 landed in May/August; consumer work continues there.

title: [bug] AndroidIsolatedWorkerSessionFactory.connect() has no bind timeout - a hung bind hangs the import path forever
description:
connect() waits in suspendCancellableCoroutine for onServiceConnected with no deadline. A sandbox that never comes up therefore never resolves: in tests it presents as a UTP timeout, and in production the import path hangs indefinitely rather than folding to DecoderUnavailable.

Found while root-causing wpass-qw3 (adjacent finding i). It also narrows what DecoderUnavailable can mean today - the bind-failure arm only covers bindService returning false, never a bind that is accepted and then never completes.

Affects every consumer of the shared facade: passes-pdf, passes-barcode, passes-image, passes-document.

title: Coordinated Kotlin 2.4.x + AGP bump across passes-android and walt-android
description:
Dependabot minor bumps for Kotlin and AGP are now ignored in .github/dependabot.yml (PR #199) because walt-android composite-builds this repo and Gradle runs one AGP / one Kotlin metadata version per build. Kotlin 2.4.x therefore has to be a hand-driven lockstep bump.

Current state: both repos on kotlin 2.3.21 / agp 9.0.1. Kotlin 2.4.10 was proposed as passes-android PRs #180 and #191 (identical diffs); both closed unmerged.

When doing the bump:
1. Bump gradle/libs.versions.toml in both repos in the same session.
2. Watch the Compose compiler stability-inference change in 2.4 (b/522127447): classes previously inferred 'stable' now report 'runtime'/'Uncertain'. Re-check passes-ui and passes-document-ui recomposition behavior.
3. Run passes-android CI (build + connected tests API 28/31/34/36) and a walt-android composite build before landing either side.

title: Add META-INF/LICENSE*.md packaging exclude to android-library convention plugin
description:
BouncyCastle 1.85 ships META-INF/LICENSE.md in bcprov, bcpkix and bcutil, so mergeDebugAndroidTestJavaResource fails with DuplicateRelativeFileException on every Android module that pulls BC onto the test classpath. Blocks dependabot PR #181 (bouncycastle 1.84 -> 1.85).

Fix: add packaging { resources { excludes += "META-INF/LICENSE*.md" } } to the walt.passes.android.library convention plugin in build-logic. Then @dependabot rebase #181 and merge.

walt-android needs the same exclude in app/build.gradle.kts (it has bcprov/bcpkix on androidTestImplementation and no packaging block); tracked separately.

title: Bundle Apple WWDR G4 intermediate
description: wpass-x70 field data: pass.de.digital-h.ride chains through WWDR G4, but passes-core bundles only G3 and G6. Path building still succeeds today because the issuer ships G4 inside the CMS envelope — an issuer that omits it would read CertChainIncomplete instead of AppleVerified. Bundle G4 alongside G3/G6 in AppleTrustAnchors.

title: Threat-model + ADR amendments for redesigned list surfaces
description: Doc-only amendments for the consumer redesign (wlt-mx2d): (1) SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL C1/C2 - scannable/composite list cards now render their actual code on a neutral surface with class eyebrows ('YOUR CODE · <format>', 'IMAGE WITH CODE'); confirm the verified-band confusion class stays structurally absent (no signature affordance on any list card; issuer color only on pkpass cards). (2) Record that issuer pass.json colors now drive consumer pass list-card faces (previously unused) incl. white issuer cards distinguished by hairline, not color. (3) ADR 0005 list-surface note: PDF/image cards render content-true previews (page-0 thumbnail / photo) inline; detail-surface trust captions and HostedTypeRow posture unchanged. Also fold in the still-open C5 composite amendment tracked from wlt-ixlf if not yet landed.

List-face code concession landed with wpass-tjc.2; C5 composite amendment already landed (wpass-7rv).
