title: Allow consumer to relocate/suppress trust captions so they can fold into a host 'details' row
description:
Consumer (Walt) wants to consolidate the trust signal into a single 'Pass type' row inside its own host-rendered Details section (values: Image / Scanned / Pkpass / PDF / 'Image, Scanned'), instead of the bottom-docked ScannableCardTrustCaption ('Created by you') and DocumentTrustCaption ('User-provided document. Walt has not verified the source.').

Today both captions are non-suppressible by design: no enabled param, no theme token that hides them, no ScannableCardScreen/DocumentView overload that skips them, enforced by ComposableSurfaceLockTest and DocumentSurfaceLockTest. They anchor threat-model C2 (SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md) and ADR 0005 D5/D8.

Need a kernel decision + API so a host can move the trust claim to an equivalent, always-present surface (e.g. a kernel-blessed 'trust claim' slot or a verified-placement contract the host satisfies) WITHOUT collapsing the defense, plus the corresponding threat-model amendment (C2 / ADR 0005 D5). If the conclusion is 'cannot be relocated', document that so the consumer stops trying. Blocks Walt-side wlt-3cer (Pass type row held pending this).
close_reason: Resolved as a C2/D5 POLICY CHANGE (not just an API add), per kernel-owner direction. TrustCaptionPlacement is Docked | HostedTypeRow on ScannableCardScreen and DocumentView. HostedTypeRow: kernel renders NO trust caption on the detail surface; the host carries provenance via its own 'Pass type' row (Image/Scanned/Pkpass/PDF/'Image, Scanned'), which MAY sit in a collapsed-by-default foldout. This blesses neutral-type-label substitution and not-always-visible placement — a deliberate weakening of the detail-surface mitigation, recorded honestly in SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md (C2 'Pass type' row concession, with residual risk) and ADR 0005 (D5.T addendum). C1 list-level distinction carries the load. Consumer-side pin moves to 'host renders a Pass type row' (walt-android wlt-3cer). Tests + detekt green. Supersedes the earlier 'relocatable, not suppressible' (Hosted) design on this branch.

title: Security review: BarcodedImageDocument untrusted-content surface (wpass-8lu)
description: PublicApiSurfaceTest flags a new Document arm as a deliberate untrusted-content surface add (ADR 0005). Review: barcode extraction stays in the isolated worker on a second memfd of the once-read bytes; only payload+format cross; degrade-on-failure cannot leak; confirm-before-persist holds; stored payload is opaque (no execution); no EXIF/XMP/payload-derived label extraction.
notes:
SECURITY REVIEW — BarcodedImageDocument composite arm (wpass-8lu). Verdict: PASS, no blockers.

Isolation invariant (load-bearing) — HOLDS:
- grep of passes-document/src/main: NO BitmapFactory / ImageDecoder / MultiFormatReader / RGBLuminanceSource / decodeByteArray on source bytes in host code. The only decode calls are the isolated facades BoundedImageDecoder.decode (image) and BarcodeImageDecoder.decode (barcode), both of which bind permissionless sandbox services. Barcode extraction reuses the EXISTING passes-barcode isolated binder (wpass-zrt) — no new binder method, no new isolated service, no widened extraction surface.
- Only {payload, ScannableFormat} (pure BarcodeDecodeResult from passes-core) crosses the binder; never a Bitmap, never source bytes.
- The barcode seam runs on its own memfd (pfdFactory.fromBytes(bytes)) built from the SINGLE bounded read; the source fd is read once. Holding compressed bytes in a host ByteArray is not a decode and is not the RCE surface.

One-artifact / degrade / confirm:
- Composite = one documents row (image row + non-null barcode pair); no host-side join. Verified by storage round-trip test.
- confirmBarcode runs BEFORE persist; declined/failed confirm or no-code/extract-failure -> degrade to ImportedImage. confirm-hook non-cancellation throw is swallowed to 'declined' so a confirm-UI bug cannot fail the import or persist an unconfirmed barcode. CancellationException is rethrown (structured concurrency).
- First-detected-code only (ZXing MultiFormatReader stops at first); roster allowlist unchanged.

No-PII / no-extraction:
- Decoded payload is NEVER logged or sent to telemetry (reuses the image onImportSucceeded event: byte count/format/dims only). Confirmed by grep (no Log/println of payload).
- No EXIF/XMP/payload-derived label extraction (D4 holds); displayLabel is consumer-supplied.
- Stored payload is opaque TEXT, never executed/evaluated.

Informational (non-blocking):
1. barcodeExtract(bytes) is not individually try/caught in extractConfirmedBarcode; matches the existing imageDecode seam posture (production facades return *Failed/Unavailable rather than throwing on binder error). Consistent, not a regression.
2. barcode_payload is not length-capped at storage (image bytes + label ARE capped). Bounded in practice by physical symbol capacity (~a few KB max, e.g. QR); the consumer's BarcodeEncoder fails closed (PayloadTooDense) so display degrades gracefully. Optional future hardening: add a storage cap.
3. When the consumer DISPLAYS the payload as text, give it the same Unicode-bidi isolation (FSI/PDI) treatment as any user-controlled string — same as existing ScannableCard payloads; no new surface.

PublicApiSurfaceTest arm-set lock was updated deliberately (a third untrusted-content Document arm), which is the intended security-review tripwire.
close_reason: Security review complete against committed code: isolation invariant verified, one-artifact/degrade/confirm/no-PII all hold, 3 informational non-blocking notes recorded. (Parent wpass-8lu stays open pending push + on-device e2e.)

title: First-class composite artifact: image + extracted/generated barcode (one wallet item)
description:
Add a first-class composite artifact that bundles a stored image with an extracted/generated native barcode (decoded payload + chosen symbology) as ONE wallet item. Follow-on to the image-document generalization (wpass-i9x): where wpass-i9x adds image as a Document arm with no code, this composite carries BOTH the image AND a barcode derived from it.

Consumer requested by walt-android epic wlt-yjn5 (Add-to-wallet UX rethink). The consumer team will wire UI/data on top once the kernel type + isolated extraction land; this kernel bead is the blocking dependency for consumer wlt-u3tk -> wlt-2ub2.

Origin: GH walt-passes-android#74 lineage (barcode-less image passes -> now image-WITH-barcode). Distinct from ScannableCard (code, no image) and Document.Image (image, no code).
design:
API SHAPE (kernel team decision 2026-06-17, flagged for consumer wlt-u3tk -> wlt-2ub2):

PLACEMENT: third Document arm, NOT a new tower. BarcodedImageDocument = ImageDocument + (barcodePayload, barcodeFormat). Reuses the whole image isolation/storage/UI substrate; degrades to ImageDocument when no code.

1. MODEL (passes-document-core, +api edge to passes-core for ScannableFormat):
   data class BarcodedImageDocument(id: BarcodedImageDocumentId, displayLabel, byteCount, widthPx, heightPx, barcodePayload: String, barcodeFormat: ScannableFormat, importedAtEpochMs, provenance) : Document

2. STORAGE (passes-storage, schema v6->v7): two nullable cols barcode_payload TEXT, barcode_format TEXT on documents. Non-null pair + image format = composite row. DocumentInsert.BarcodedImage(...); DocumentRow gains barcodePayload: String?, barcodeFormat: ScannableFormat?. loadDocumentBytes/Thumbnail unchanged (kind-agnostic).

3. IMPORT (passes-document, +edge to passes-barcode): image branch runs the EXISTING isolated BarcodeImageDecoder (passes-barcode sandbox) on a second memfd of the same once-read bytes. Confirm-before-usable via new param confirmBarcode: suspend (payload, ScannableFormat) -> Boolean (default { _,_ -> true }). On DecodedBarcode AND confirm==true -> persist DocumentPersist.BarcodedImage -> result ImportedBarcodedImage(doc). Else (no code, decode-fail, or rejected) -> persist DocumentPersist.Image -> ImportedImage(doc). Nothing persisted before confirm. Decoded payload reaches the consumer's BarcodeCreateConfirmSheet through the confirmBarcode hook.

4. UI (passes-document-ui): DocumentView/DocumentTile gain a BarcodedImageDocument branch that routes the IMAGE to the existing ImageDocumentView/tile (same imageFile/imageDecoder pair). The kernel does NOT render the generated barcode here: the two UI towers stay independent. Consumer composes the barcode via passes-ui ScannableCardView + BarcodeEncoder.encode(payload, format) for the format switcher (re-encode any ScannableFormat from the stored payload). One artifact id -> one wallet row (image thumbnail).

ISOLATION INVARIANT preserved: barcode extraction never runs in host process; only payload+ScannableFormat cross the binder (BarcodeDecodeResult), matching wpass-i9x.
notes:
PR REVIEW RESPONSE (2026-06-17):
- Rec 1 (untested confirm-hook exception contract): FIXED. Added confirmHookThrowingNonCancellationDegradesToPlainImage (IllegalStateException -> ImportedImage, persists Image) and confirmHookCancellationPropagatesOutOfImportAndPersistsNothing (CancellationException propagates, nothing persisted).
- Rec 2 (extraction on every image + composite as silent default): FIXED, stronger than suggested. confirmBarcode is now nullable with null DEFAULT = composites are opt-in AND extraction is SKIPPED entirely (no isolated barcode round-trip) when no hook is supplied. Plain-image import is back to zero barcode cost (wpass-i9x parity) and an incidental photo barcode is never silently turned into a composite. Consumer passes a hook to opt in; { _,_ -> true } still available for accept-all. Added withoutAConfirmHookExtractionIsSkippedAndTheResultIsAPlainImage. ADR C3 + DocumentImporter KDoc updated.
- Rec 3 (ByteArray referential equality): NO ACTION (verified parity) - existing Pdf/Image arms have no custom equals/@Suppress; new BarcodedImage arms match exactly; reviewer agreed none required.
- Minor (long KDoc / schema index): no action, as the reviewer noted.
All passes-document tests + detekt + ktlint green; androidTest compiles.

title: Rename passes-pdf-core -> passes-document-core and passes-pdf-ui -> passes-document-ui (module/package naming debt from wpass-i9x)
description:
Naming debt surfaced by the wpass-bsf review. After wpass-i9x generalized Document to cover images, the kind-agnostic model and UI now live in modules named 'pdf':

- passes-pdf-core (package is.walt.passes.pdf) holds the sealed Document supertype, ImageDocument, DocumentId, DocumentRejectedKind, DocumentTelemetryGuard - not just PdfDocument. CLAUDE.md's description of the module ('PdfDocument model, header sniffer...') is already stale.
- passes-pdf-ui holds the image render arm (ImageDocumentView/DocumentImage) and api-depends on passes-image (build.gradle.kts:27).

The trap is sharper because passes-document ALREADY exists (the importer/sniff orchestrator). A newcomer hunting the Document model reasonably opens passes-document and does not find it - it is in passes-pdf-core.

PROPOSED SHAPE (mechanical rename, no behavior change):
- passes-pdf-core -> passes-document-core
- passes-pdf-ui   -> passes-document-ui
- package is.walt.passes.pdf -> is.walt.passes.document for the kind-agnostic Document types (PdfDocument/PDF rendering stay as arms inside).

CLEAN BOUNDARY: only the two modules that genuinely became kind-agnostic move. The SERVICES passes-pdf and passes-image keep their names (PdfRenderer really is PDF-specific; ImageDecodeService really is image-specific). Result is coherent, not half-renamed.

COST / SEQUENCING (the reason to do it soon, not later): this is a cross-repo breaking rename of the is.walt.passes.pdf package. walt-android (closed source) imports it directly - every consumer import site moves. wlt-fizc (consumer image-document wiring) has NOT landed yet, so the import surface is still small. Do this BEFORE wlt-fizc wires DocumentRenderer/DocumentDetailScreen against the old package, or the rename surface multiplies. Coordinate the cut with the consumer side (cross-repo: wlt-fizc).

Update CLAUDE.md architecture rules + module list as part of the rename.
notes: PR #159 (branch wpass-xmp-rename). Mechanical rename done + pushed. Key non-obvious finding: passes-pdf (service) and the new passes-document-core now SHARE the is.walt.passes.document package as a deliberate split package (no FQN collisions; verified). Consequence: same-package imports in the passes-document module had to be removed (detekt UnusedImports), and two passes-pdf KDoc lines needed shortening (MaxLineLength, 'document' is +5 vs 'pdf'). Local 'check assemble assembleDebugAndroidTest' green. CROSS-REPO: wlt-fizc (walt-android consumer wiring) must import the FINAL package names is.walt.passes.document(.ui); this PR was sequenced to land first. Awaiting CI (Build & quality + Connected API 28/31/34/36).
close_reason: Renamed passes-pdf-core->passes-document-core and passes-pdf-ui->passes-document-ui (package is.walt.passes.pdf->is.walt.passes.document, .ui variant). PR #159 squash-merged to main (1b1c70e). All CI green (Build & quality + Connected API 28/31/34/36). Review fixes applied (manifest comments, test method name, build comment, blank line). Worktree + branches cleaned up.

title: Step 3: Isolated image-decode service (ImageDecoder in sandbox, raster-return)
description:
Part of wpass-i9x. New isolated worker service mirroring passes-pdf's PdfRendererService but simpler: one 'page', ImageDecoder (no PDFium, no SDK-34 floor). Decodes the ORIGINAL user-image bytes inside the sandbox and returns a bounded raster to the host via SharedMemory (same return mechanism the PDF renderer uses). Binds through passes-isolation (IsolatedWorkerSession). Reuses the consolidated bounded decoder from Step 1.

SECURITY ACCEPTANCE (the whole point):
- [ ] No user-image codec ever runs in the host process - import AND view route decode through this sandbox.
- [ ] Only a bounded raster (Walt-produced) crosses the binder; host displays that, never re-decodes the original.
- [ ] Caps (dimension/area/format) applied pre-allocation in the listener; OOM/Throwable contained; matches the static-image barcode posture.
close_reason: Built passes-image isolated image-decode service (PR #155, merged feb362c). ImageDecodeService decodes original user-image bytes in an isolatedProcess sandbox and returns only a bounded ARGB_8888 raster over SharedMemory; binds through passes-isolation, reuses passes-image-decode decodeBounded; caps applied pre-allocation, OOM/Throwable contained; own ImageDecodeRejectedKind taxonomy (not flattened into DocumentRejectedKind). 56 JVM tests + instrumented suite green on API 28/31/34/36.

title: Step 4: ImageDocument arm + DocumentImporter sniff/branch + storage format column
description:
Final step of wpass-i9x. Add the ImageDocument arm to sealed Document (widthPx/heightPx instead of pageCount; its own sealed reject taxonomy: NotAnImage / dimension-too-large / decode-failed - NOT merged into PDF DocumentRejectedKind). Add a DocumentImporter that magic-byte-sniffs PDF vs image and branches to the right backend (salvage CPinelli's header sniffer + telemetry-guard shape + reject enum from PR #146, re-homed; decode moved to the Step-3 sandbox). Generalize storage: insertDocument (PassRepository.kt:119) gains a kind/format discriminator + image dims; SQLCipher documents table gets a format column; loadDocumentBytes/loadDocumentThumbnail already kind-agnostic. Reuse DocumentTrustCaption/Theme verbatim; add the single-image (no-pager) render arm in DocumentView.

Acceptance: image import end-to-end (sniff -> isolated decode -> bounded thumbnail -> persist original), image renders via DocumentView with the unchanged trust caption, ADR 0005 amended to bless Document = PDF | image.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #156 (squash-merged to main). ImageDocument arm end-to-end: sealed Document + ImageDocument (passes-pdf-core), passes-document import orchestrator (sniff/branch to passes-pdf or passes-image sandbox), storage v6 (format + dims, sealed DocumentInsert), DocumentView image arm with non-suppressible trust caption, ADR 0005 amended. On-device tests green across API 28/31/34/36.

title: Step 1: Consolidate duplicated bounded ImageDecoder into one shared primitive
description:
Prep for wpass-i9x. The bounded ImageDecoder + OnHeaderDecodedListener decode (dimension/area caps before allocation, format allowlist, 1x1-on-reject, full Throwable/OOM containment) exists in TWO places today:
- passes-barcode/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/barcode/android/BoundedBitmapDecoder.kt (decodeBoundedBitmap, isolated/sandbox use)
- passes-ui/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/ui/BoundedImage.kt (decodeBoundedBitmap, in-process pkpass display)
Extract one shared primitive both consume. NO behavior change - existing tests (ComposableSurfaceLockTest, barcode decode tests) stay green. This pays down existing duplication and gives wpass-i9x step 3 a single audited decode helper to reuse in the new isolated image service.

Acceptance: one decode helper, both call sites delegate, no test changes beyond import paths, both decode postures (in-process for pkpass / isolated for hostile files) unchanged.

Behavior unchanged, zero test changes. detekt/tests/assemble green. Pushed branch wpass-gnp-bounded-image-decode.

title: Step 2: Promote PdfDocument -> sealed Document + DocumentView dispatcher (PDF-only arm)
description:
Part of wpass-i9x. Promote PdfDocument to 'sealed interface Document { id; displayLabel; byteCount; importedAtEpochMs; provenance }' with PdfDocument as the SOLE arm for now. Turn DocumentView (passes-pdf-ui) into a dispatcher on the sealed type. No image arm yet - this step must leave behavior identical and all surface-lock/trust tests green (DocumentSurfaceLockTest, DocumentTrustSurfaceTest, the application/pdf + ACTION_SEND bytecode scans). Provenance.UserProvided single-arm trust-policy comment generalizes unchanged. This is the structural seam that lets step 4 add the image arm without touching the PDF render path.

Acceptance: sealed Document compiles, PdfDocument is an arm, DocumentView dispatches, zero behavior/test-assertion changes.

title: Generalize Document to cover images (PDF + image, one isolation harness)
description:
Support barcode-less image passes (insurance/membership cards, screenshots, photographed physical cards) requested in GH issue #74. Rather than add a 4th artifact tower (the approach in community PR #146, which builds parallel passes-image-* modules), generalize the existing Document concept so PDF and image are two arms of one artifact sharing one isolation substrate, one trust/UI surface, and one storage/telemetry pattern.

Origin: GH walt-passes-android#74 (issue), #146 (community PR by CPinelli - salvageable as the module/test base; see acceptance criteria for what must change).

KEY FRAMING (verified against code 2026-06-16):
- 'One harness' = one isolation substrate (passes-isolation) + one trust/UI surface (Document* in passes-pdf-ui, already generically named) + one storage/telemetry pattern. It is NOT one decoder: PDF uses android.graphics.pdf.PdfRenderer (PDFium, SDK 34+ floor) and image uses ImageDecoder (SDK 28+). Two thin decode backends under one umbrella is correct, not a smell.
- The trust caption text ('User-provided document. Walt has not verified the source.') and DocumentSemantics/Theme are reused verbatim for images.

SECURITY (load-bearing, the reason this is not just 'merge #146'):
The kernel already runs two decode postures - in-process capped (passes-ui/BoundedImage, for pkpass-embedded assets, residual risk accepted) and ISOLATED capped (passes-barcode/BoundedBitmapDecoder, for arbitrary user-chosen files, the hostile-input surface, CVE-2023-4863 libwebp class). A user-imported image file is the hostile surface and MUST take the isolated posture. PR #146 decodes with BitmapFactory IN-PROCESS at both import (DefaultImageImporter) and view (host ViewModel, per ImageDocumentView KDoc) - this reintroduces the exact codec-RCE surface the barcode sandbox exists to contain, on full-res persisted bytes re-decoded on every view. That design defect is the blocker.
design:
Sequencing (each step independently shippable + test-gated; keeps DocumentSurfaceLockTest / DocumentTrustSurfaceTest / the application-pdf + ACTION_SEND bytecode scans green):
1. Consolidate the duplicated bounded ImageDecoder (exists twice today: passes-barcode/BoundedBitmapDecoder.kt and passes-ui/BoundedImage.kt) into one shared primitive. No behavior change.
2. Promote PdfDocument -> sealed Document { id; displayLabel; byteCount; importedAtEpochMs; provenance } with PdfDocument as the only arm; DocumentView becomes a dispatcher. Tests stay green (PDF-only).
3. New isolated image-decode service mirroring PdfRendererService (simpler: one page, ImageDecoder, no SDK-34 floor) - decode original bytes in-sandbox, return a bounded raster via SharedMemory, bind through passes-isolation, reuse the step-1 primitive.
4. Add the ImageDocument arm (widthPx/heightPx instead of pageCount), DocumentImporter that sniffs PDF-vs-image and branches, and storage generalization (insertDocument in PassRepository.kt:119 gains a kind/format discriminator + image dims; documents table gets a format column; loadDocumentBytes/Thumbnail already kind-agnostic).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] User-imported image bytes are NEVER decoded in the host process. Decode runs in the isolated worker (passes-isolation); only a bounded raster crosses the binder back, matching the static-image barcode posture. No BitmapFactory on user-image bytes anywhere in the host process.
- [ ] Image reject taxonomy is its own sealed arm (NotAnImage / dimension-too-large / decode-failed), not flattened into the PDF DocumentRejectedKind.
- [ ] Trust caption is the existing non-suppressible DocumentTrustCaption, reused unchanged for images.
- [ ] Original bytes persisted (wlt-o72.3 precedent); every decode-for-display re-runs in the sandbox.
- [ ] No content extraction (EXIF/XMP); displayLabel supplied at import time (no-extraction-from-content discipline).
- [ ] ADR 0005 amended to bless Document = PDF | image.
notes: Follow-up filed 2026-06-17 from the wpass-bsf review: wpass-xmp tracks the module/package naming debt (passes-pdf-core/-ui hold kind-agnostic Document* after this epic). Sequence wpass-xmp BEFORE consumer bead wlt-fizc lands, to keep the cross-repo is.walt.passes.pdf package rename surface small.
close_reason: All steps complete: wpass-gnp (shared ImageDecoder), wpass-gyn (sealed Document + dispatcher), wpass-6yp (isolated image-decode service), wpass-bsf (ImageDocument arm + DocumentImporter + storage v5->v6) all closed; discovered wpass-xmp (module rename) closed; composite follow-on wpass-8lu merged (PR #160). Epic delivered.

title: passes-barcode-core: retry inverted luminance for still-image decode (GH #134)
description: GH #134: scanning a barcode from an image is unreliable. Root cause: decodeLuminance runs a single HybridBinarizer pass and ZXing's readers never flip contrast, so light-on-dark codes (dark-mode screenshots, white-on-black labels) yield no locatable symbol. Fix: add alsoInverted param to decodeLuminance; still-image path (ZxingBarcodeSymbolDecoder) opts in to a second pass on source.invert(); camera path (decodeYPlane) unchanged. Same roster/hints - wider contrast, not a wider allowlist.
close_reason: Not implementing now; captured as a note-to-self on GH #134 instead.

title: JVM test suite for the live frame-decode path (writer round-trip, stride, failure arms, allowlist)
description:
JVM unit tests for the live frame-decode adapter: round-trip through ZXing's writer (mirroring the existing decode-contract tests), synthetic Y-plane fixtures with and without row/pixel-stride padding, the no-symbol (`NotFoundException`) and reader-exception failure arms, and allowlist enforcement (non-roster symbologies such as PDF417/Aztec rejected).

No instrumented / managed-device leg required, because the live path invokes no Android image codec (unlike the static path, whose `ImageDecoder` step needs the `:barcodeDecoder` sandbox + device tests). Runs on plain JVM.
acceptance_criteria: Coverage parity with the static decode-contract tests; stride-padding cases covered; no-symbol + reader-exception arms asserted; allowlist rejection asserted; runs on plain JVM (no managed-device leg).
notes: Also pin decodeYPlane's require() preconditions (added in wpass-7xo.5): non-positive dims, pixelStride < 1, rowStride < width*pixelStride, and undersized Y-plane buffer should each throw IllegalArgumentException. These geometry guards are the security-relevant boundary and are not yet covered by the .5 smoke tests.
close_reason: Exhaustive JVM suite for decodeYPlane added (17 tests): stride padding (rowStride/pixelStride + boundary), no-symbol + ECC-exceeded failure arms, PDF417/Aztec allowlist rejection, and all four require guards + accepted boundaries. :passes-barcode-core:check green. PR #131.

title: Pure-JVM YUV-frame decode adapter (PlanarYUVLuminanceSource -> decodeLuminance)
description:
Add a pure-JVM frame-decode entry to `passes-barcode-core`: `decodeYPlane(yPlane: ByteArray, width: Int, height: Int, rowStride: Int, ...)` (final signature TBD) that constructs ZXing `PlanarYUVLuminanceSource` from the camera luminance plane, strips row/pixel-stride padding (ZXing #1387), and calls `decodeLuminance`, returning `BarcodeDecodeResult`.

NO CameraX / Android dependency in the kernel: the consumer (walt-android) extracts the Y plane from its `ImageProxy` and passes bytes + geometry in. This is the reusable surface the consumer `ImageAnalysis` analyzer calls per frame. Honors the same symbology allowlist and faithful-payload contract as the static path (returns only `{payload, ScannableFormat}`; no interpretation).

Blocked by the module extraction. Input contract (formats/strides to accept) is informed by the HAL-variability spike, but the `byte[]` + geometry signature is robust to its outcome, so this is not hard-blocked on it.
acceptance_criteria: decodeYPlane in passes-barcode-core, pure JVM (no CameraX/Android dep); correct dataWidth/dataHeight/left/top/rowStride handling; allowlist enforced (PDF417/Aztec rejected); returns only {payload, ScannableFormat}.
close_reason: decodeYPlane added to passes-barcode-core: PlanarYUVLuminanceSource from camera Y plane delegating to decodeLuminance; zero-copy rowStride strip + pixelStride repack (ZXing #1387); pure JVM, allowlist enforced, returns only BarcodeDecodeResult. Smoke tests green. PR #130.

title: Extract pure-JVM passes-barcode-core (shared decode core for static + live paths)
description:
Create a new pure-JVM Gradle module `passes-barcode-core` and move the trust-claim-bearing symbol decode into it: `decodeLuminance(LuminanceSource)` plus the symbology allowlist (`ROSTER_BY_ZXING_FORMAT`, `DECODE_HINTS`) currently `internal` in `passes-barcode`'s `ZxingBarcodeSymbolDecoder.kt`. Add `com.google.zxing:core` as the new module's dependency; `passes-barcode` (Android) depends on it and keeps only the `Bitmap -> RGBLuminanceSource` adapter, delegating to the core. `ScannableFormat` / `BarcodeDecodeResult` stay in `passes-core`; `passes-barcode-core` depends on `passes-core` for them.

Purpose: one decode implementation shared by the existing isolated still-image path AND the new in-process live-camera path (the `passes-barcode-core` option wpass-zrt explicitly left open). Mirrors the existing `passes-pdf` / `passes-pdf-core` split.

Update CLAUDE.md architecture rules: nine -> ten modules, new dependency edges (`passes-barcode -> passes-barcode-core -> passes-core`). Foundation for the YUV frame adapter and its tests.
acceptance_criteria: New passes-barcode-core pure-JVM module (no Android deps); existing wpass-zrt tests green; static-image decode behavior unchanged; CLAUDE.md module list + dependency rules updated (9 -> 10 modules).
close_reason: Extracted pure-JVM passes-barcode-core; decode moved + tests green, CLAUDE.md updated (10 modules)

title: Security analysis (completed): live-camera decode attack-surface delta vs static-image decode
description: Completed research + threat analysis that is the go/no-go evidence base for the parent epic. No code; durable record only. Full report in the design field.
design:
# Live-camera barcode/QR decode — security analysis (COMPLETED 2026-06-05)

Status: research complete, no code written. This bead is the durable record of the
threat analysis that motivates the parent epic. It supersedes nothing; it is the
go/no-go evidence base for building live camera scanning on the Walt passes kernel.

## Question / scope

Can the wpass-zrt barcode-from-image decode be extended to LIVE camera scanning (user
points the camera at a bar/QR code -> import as a new pass), and does doing so enlarge
the exploitable attack surface for an app that will hold payment-card material
(DPAN, LUK) behind the hardware-backed Android Keystore?

Compared paths:
- (A) STATIC image file (already shipped, wpass-zrt): attacker-influenced bytes parsed
  by a native still-image codec (libwebp/libjpeg-turbo/libpng/libgif/Skia), then ZXing.
- (B) LIVE camera: CameraX `ImageAnalysis` `YUV_420_888` frames -> ZXing
  `PlanarYUVLuminanceSource` -> pure-JVM `com.google.zxing:core`.

## Method

- Deep-research harness: 5 search angles, 23 sources fetched, 92 claims extracted, 25
  adversarially verified (3-vote, majority-refute kills), 22 confirmed, 3 refuted.
- Code map of `passes-barcode` and `passes-isolation` in this repo.
- Reconstruction of the static-image threat model (the former
  `docs/barcode-from-image-security-analysis.md`, folded into walt-android epic wlt-58a
  and deleted as a standalone file).

## Headline verdict

A correctly-built live path carries a CATEGORICALLY SMALLER native attack surface than
the static-image feature already accepted. The single worst vector that justified
isolating the static path — attacker-controlled compressed file -> native still-image
codec RCE — is STRUCTURALLY ABSENT from the raw-YUV camera path. Live decode therefore
does NOT need the isolated sandbox and should run in-process. The genuine new cost is
the `CAMERA` runtime permission (a privacy/capability/blast-radius consideration, not an
RCE vector), plus ordinary code footprint. Card data stays protected by the Keystore and
is unreachable from the camera/ZXing path by any memory-corruption route.

## Verified findings (with citations)

1. CODEC ABSENCE (high; 3-0). CameraX `ImageAnalysis` outputs already-decoded raw pixels
   (`YUV_420_888` default, `RGBA_8888` opt-in via `setOutputImageFormat`). ZXing's
   `PlanarYUVLuminanceSource` consumes only the planar Y luminance `byte[]` with
   crop/window/rotate array ops and performs ZERO JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF/Skia container
   parsing. A verifier read the 5442-byte master-branch source: no codec imports, pure
   `System.arraycopy`/indexing over a `final byte[] yuvData`. Non-fatal caveat: CameraX
   YUV buffers carry row/pixel-stride padding (ZXing #1387) that production code must
   strip before constructing the source — a logic op on already-decoded bytes, no parser.
   Sources: github.com/zxing/zxing .../PlanarYUVLuminanceSource.java ;
   developer.android.com/media/camera/camerax/analyze

2. ZXING RISK CLASS (high; 3-0). Feeding camera frames to `com.google.zxing:core` adds
   only pure-JVM logic-bug/DoS risk (GC pressure on continuous scan), never native
   memory-safety/RCE. Every documented ZXing memory-corruption CVE (CVE-2021-28021/
   -42715/-42716) is in the C++ `zxing-cpp`/`stb_image.h` static-container path, not the
   JVM YUV class. The repo's own `ZxingBarcodeSymbolDecoder.kt` documents it:
   "com.google.zxing:core is Apache-2.0 and 100% JVM ... adds ZERO native attack surface."
   This makes the live-decode logic risk identical IN KIND to the static path's pure
   decode layer, while the static path ADDITIONALLY carries the native codec surface.

3. STATIC-FILE NATIVE RCE IS REAL AND WEAPONIZED (high; 3-0). Existence proofs that
   decoding an attacker-supplied encoded still-image file is a live native-RCE surface
   the raw-YUV path avoids:
   - libwebp CVE-2023-4863: heap overflow / OOB write (CWE-787), fixed in libwebp 1.3.2,
     on CISA KEV, exploited in the wild. Root cause native C in the lossless decoder
     (BuildHuffmanTable). [nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-4863]
   - Skia/SkSwizzler PNG CVE-2019-1987: OOB write in `onSetSampleX` of SkSwizzler.cpp,
     RCE from a crafted PNG in a privileged process. [AOSP 2019-02-01 bulletin]
   - Samsung Quram CVE-2025-21042: native OOB write in `libimagecodec.quram.so` from a
     crafted DNG, used in the wild to deploy LANDFALL spyware; delivered as a FILE over
     WhatsApp and auto-parsed by system process `com.samsung.ipservice` on MediaStore
     insertion. Patched SMR Apr-2025. [Project Zero 2025/12; Unit42 LANDFALL]

4. ATTRIBUTION PRECISION (high; 3-0). The marquee in-the-wild Android case (LANDFALL)
   exploited Samsung's PROPRIETARY Quram DNG parser, NOT libwebp/libjpeg/png/gif/Skia.
   DNG is still a still-image container parsed by a native codec, so it stays in path (A),
   but cite it as Quram/DNG. The exactly-on-target open-source/AOSP examples are libwebp
   CVE-2023-4863 and Skia/PNG CVE-2019-1987.

5. CAMERA-SUBSYSTEM CVE REACHABILITY (high; 3-0). The cited camera-subsystem CVE
   (CVE-2016-0826 in libcameraservice/mediaserver) is an access-control / privilege-
   escalation bug (CWE-264) exploited by a malicious LOCAL app calling the camera-service
   dump without authorization (AV:L, UI:R, CVSS v3.0 7.8). It is NOT a frame-decode
   memory-safety bug and is NOT reachable by device-originated sensor pixels. Camera-
   subsystem risk is dominated by local-app/privilege concerns, distinct from the
   encoded-input parsing risk of the static-file path. [nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2016-0826]

6. CAMERA PERMISSION CONTROLS (high; 3-0). Holding `android.permission.CAMERA` is bounded
   by platform controls: Android 11+ one-time "Only this time" grants (temporary, revoked
   on app close); Android 12+ always-on status-bar privacy indicator whenever camera is
   active. The Critical RCEs that historically reached privileged Android processes were
   media-FILE/codec bugs requiring a crafted compressed file, not raw sensor data.
   Sources: developer.android.com/about/versions/11/privacy/permissions ;
   source.android.com/docs/core/permissions/privacy-indicators ;
   AOSP 2016-03-01 bulletin.

7. ML KIT vs ZXING for a degoogled channel (high; 3-0). ML Kit barcode scanning has a
   "bundled" artifact (`com.google.mlkit:barcode-scanning`) that statically links the
   model at build time — no Play-Services download, runs without Play Services. The
   "unbundled" artifact (`com.google.android.gms:play-services-mlkit-barcode-scanning`)
   is a hard Play-Services dependency. HOWEVER even bundled ML Kit is closed-source Google
   code and can throw `MlKitException`/model-unavailable on some custom ROMs. For the
   walt.is degoogled trust/auditability posture, pure-JVM `com.google.zxing:core` remains
   the cleaner, fully-auditable choice. No reason to revisit the wpass-zrt decision.
   Sources: developers.google.com/ml-kit/tips/installation-paths ;
   developers.google.com/ml-kit/vision/barcode-scanning/android

8. JPEG-CAPTURE PITFALL + PAYLOAD THREAT (medium; inferred from scoping of claims 2,3).
   The security property holds ONLY on the raw-YUV `ImageAnalysis` path. `ImageCapture`
   yields a compressed JPEG; decoding any saved photo routes bytes back through a still-
   image codec, reintroducing exactly the libwebp/Skia/Quram surface. Separately, the
   decoded PAYLOAD (malicious URL/crafted string) is the SAME logical threat regardless of
   static-vs-live capture and must be mitigated DOWNSTREAM by classification/validation +
   user confirmation, never in the capture layer. The capture layer emits only
   `{payload, ScannableFormat}` with no interpretation.

## Refuted claims (DO NOT over-claim)

- (0-3) The AOSP camera architecture page does NOT cleanly establish "no still-image codec
  anywhere in the HAL-to-service path." The verified codec-absence claim rests on the
  `ImageAnalysis` OUTPUT format + ZXing's consumption, not on a blanket claim about HAL
  internals. (This does not weaken the conclusion: the HAL processes sensor data, not
  attacker-chosen encoded bytes.)
- (1-2) The HAL/service trust-boundary framing was contested.
- (1-2) The claim that Android 11+ STRUCTURALLY BARS a compromised app from background
  camera access was REFUTED. Do NOT claim the OS prevents covert background camera use.
  Rely on the weaker verified controls (one-time grants, status-bar indicator) PLUS the
  app's own foreground-only design discipline.

## Residual risks that cannot be designed away

- Holding `CAMERA` is an irreducible privacy-surface increase (mitigated, not eliminated,
  by indicators + one-time grants + foreground-only discipline).
- The decoded payload is an unavoidable output of ANY barcode decode and must be handled
  by downstream classification/validation + explicit user confirmation regardless of
  capture method.
- An image-codec 0-day remains the static path's residual (contained by the existing
  sandbox); the live path simply does not invoke that surface.

## Open questions / evidence gaps (resolve before/while building)

1. In-process vs isolated for LIVE decode: no external consensus was verifiable. Analysis
   strongly supports in-process (no codec to contain; the isolation transport cannot
   stream frames). Record as an explicit design decision.
2. OEM HAL format variability: confirm that every device/HAL the walt.is channel targets
   delivers `ImageAnalysis` as raw demosaiced `YUV_420_888` (vs an implementation-defined/
   differently-strided/PRIV format that needs extra handling and could conceivably invoke
   a codec). The stride-padding nuance (ZXing #1387) hints at variability.
3. Bundled ML Kit empirical reliability/telemetry on the de-Googled ROMs walt.is targets
   (only relevant if the ZXing decision is ever revisited — it should not be).
4. The downstream classification/validation + user-confirmation contract for payloads in
   a payment-card wallet (URL allowlisting, scheme restrictions, B3-style confirmation
   sheet). This is the one surface with equal risk across static and live capture and is a
   CONSUMER (walt-android) responsibility, reusing `QrPayloadClassifier` +
   `ScannableCardInputValidator`.

## Code-map findings (the reuse seam)

- `ZxingBarcodeSymbolDecoder.kt:62` — `decodeLuminance(source: LuminanceSource):
  BarcodeDecodeResult` is deliberately Bitmap-free, file-free, JVM-unit-testable, with
  zero coupling to the bounded-codec step or the isolated service. Today the static path
  feeds it an `RGBLuminanceSource` built from a decoded `Bitmap` (line 46). A live path
  would feed it a `PlanarYUVLuminanceSource` built from the camera Y plane. SAME core.
- The still-image codec (`ImageDecoder.decodeBitmap`) lives ONLY in the front-end
  `BoundedBitmapDecoder`, never in the decode core.
- `passes-isolation` transport is one-shot `fromBytes(ByteArray)` over synchronous,
  blocking `transact()`. Verdict: NOT suitable for ~30fps streaming. So the sandbox is
  both unnecessary (no codec) and the wrong tool (cannot stream) for live decode.
- `ScannableFormat` and `BarcodeDecodeResult` already live in pure-JVM `passes-core`
  (no ZXing dependency). The ZXing `decodeLuminance` core is pure-JVM but currently
  `internal` to the Android `passes-barcode` module.

## Architecture conclusion

This is a NEW epic, not a tweak to the `BarcodeImageDecoder` facade. The facade, the
memfd transport, and the sandbox do not extend to live frames.

Kernel vs consumer split (mirrors wpass-zrt / wlt-58a, where the picker ENTRY POINT was
consumer-side and the kernel owned the DECODE):
- KERNEL (this repo) owns the trust-claim-bearing decode: extract a pure-JVM
  `passes-barcode-core` holding `decodeLuminance` + the symbology allowlist, plus a
  pure-JVM YUV-frame adapter (build `PlanarYUVLuminanceSource` from a Y-plane `byte[]` +
  width/height/rowStride). No CameraX dependency needed — the consumer extracts the Y
  plane and passes bytes in. Both the existing isolated still-image path and the new
  in-process live path then call ONE decode implementation (the `passes-barcode-core`
  option wpass-zrt explicitly left open).
- CONSUMER (walt-android, file separately) owns the CameraX `ImageAnalysis` pipeline,
  the preview UI, the `CAMERA` permission request, lifecycle, user confirmation, and
  routing the payload through `QrPayloadClassifier` + `ScannableCardInputValidator`.

## Load-bearing constraints for any implementation

1. Raw-YUV `ImageAnalysis` ONLY. Never `ImageCapture` (JPEG). Any "scan from a saved
   photo" affordance MUST route through the existing isolated `BarcodeImageDecoder`, not a
   new in-process codec call.
2. Faithful payload return; no auto-act. Downstream classification/validation + explicit
   user confirmation before creating a pass.
3. Foreground-only camera discipline (self-imposed; not an OS guarantee).
4. Kernel decode core declares NO `CAMERA` permission and stays pure-JVM.

## Primary sources

- github.com/zxing/zxing .../com/google/zxing/PlanarYUVLuminanceSource.java
- developer.android.com/media/camera/camerax/analyze
- developer.android.com/media/camera/camerax/mlkitanalyzer
- nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-4863 (libwebp)
- vulmon.com/vulnerabilitydetails?qid=CVE-2019-1987 ; AOSP 2019-02-01 bulletin (Skia PNG)
- projectzero.google/2025/12/android-itw-dng.html ; unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/landfall-is-new-commercial-grade-android-spyware/ (Quram DNG / LANDFALL)
- nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2016-0826 (camera service EoP)
- developer.android.com/about/versions/11/privacy/permissions ; source.android.com/docs/core/permissions/privacy-indicators ; AOSP 2016-03-01 bulletin
- developers.google.com/ml-kit/tips/installation-paths ; developers.google.com/ml-kit/vision/barcode-scanning/android
close_reason: Research + threat analysis complete (deep-research harness: 22/25 claims verified; code map of passes-barcode/passes-isolation; static-image threat-model reconstruction). Full report retained in design field. Go/no-go evidence base for parent epic wpass-7xo.

title: [epic] Live camera barcode/QR scanning -> pass import: kernel decode core (consumed by walt-android wlt-mwj)
description:
Kernel-side companion epic for LIVE camera barcode/QR scanning: a user opens the camera, points it at a bar/QR code, and Walt imports it as a new pass. This is the live-capture sibling of wpass-zrt (barcode-from-a-static-image). It was consciously deferred by the product owner on 2026-05-17 ("No camera or image-upload payload entry in v1 ... Sibling feature, file separately") and is greenfield/untracked until now.

DECISIVE SECURITY FINDING (full evidence in the completed child report bead): a correctly-built live path carries a CATEGORICALLY SMALLER native attack surface than the static-image decode already shipped. CameraX `ImageAnalysis` delivers already-decoded raw `YUV_420_888` sensor pixels; ZXing's `PlanarYUVLuminanceSource` consumes only the Y-plane `byte[]` with no JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF/Skia container parsing. The single worst vector that justified isolating the static path — attacker-controlled compressed file -> native still-image codec RCE (libwebp CVE-2023-4863 class) — is STRUCTURALLY ABSENT from the raw-YUV path. Therefore live decode does NOT need the `:barcodeDecoder` isolated sandbox and runs IN-PROCESS, reusing the same pure-JVM `decodeLuminance` core. (The `passes-isolation` transport is one-shot/blocking and cannot stream frames anyway.)

KERNEL SCOPE (this repo): only the trust-claim-bearing decode. Extract a pure-JVM `passes-barcode-core` holding `decodeLuminance` + the symbology allowlist, plus a pure-JVM YUV-frame adapter (`PlanarYUVLuminanceSource` from a Y-plane `byte[]` + width/height/rowStride). No CameraX dependency in the kernel — the consumer extracts the Y plane and passes bytes in. Both the existing isolated still-image path AND the new in-process live path then call ONE decode implementation (the `passes-barcode-core` option wpass-zrt explicitly left open). The kernel decode core declares NO `CAMERA` permission and stays pure-JVM.

CONSUMER SCOPE (walt-android, file separately, analogous to wlt-58a where the picker entry point was consumer-side): the CameraX `ImageAnalysis` pipeline, preview UI, `CAMERA` permission request, lifecycle, user-confirmation sheet, and routing the decoded payload through `QrPayloadClassifier` + `ScannableCardInputValidator`.

LOAD-BEARING CONSTRAINTS (contractual): (1) raw-YUV `ImageAnalysis` ONLY — never `ImageCapture`/JPEG; any "scan from saved photo" routes through the existing isolated `BarcodeImageDecoder`, not a new in-process codec call. (2) Faithful payload return, no auto-act; downstream classification/validation + explicit user confirmation before pass creation. (3) Foreground-only camera discipline (self-imposed; the OS does NOT structurally bar background camera for a compromised app). (4) Pure-JVM ZXing, not ML Kit (degoogled walt.is auditability; decision unchanged from wpass-zrt).

NET: enabling live scanning does not meaningfully enlarge the exploitable surface and is SAFER than the static path on the catastrophic-RCE axis. The genuine new cost is the consumer-declared `CAMERA` permission (privacy/capability/blast-radius), a product decision, not an RCE risk. Card data (DPAN/LUK) stays Keystore-protected and unreachable from the camera/ZXing path.

Related: wpass-zrt (static-image kernel epic, closed), wlt-58a (static-image consumer epic in walt-android, closed). A consumer epic for live capture should be filed in walt-android.
notes:
CROSS-REPO COORDINATION (live-camera scanning, 2026-06-05). Mirrors wpass-zrt <-> wlt-58a. Two trackers, no bd edges between them, so the provider/consumer dependency is documented here on BOTH epics.

walt-passes-android (this epic, wpass-7xo = PROVIDER, kernel decode core) -- unblocks --> walt-android (wlt-mwj = CONSUMER, live-capture epic).

Bead mapping:
- wpass-7xo.2 (extract pure-JVM passes-barcode-core: decodeLuminance + symbology allowlist) — DONE. Establishes the one shared decode implementation both the isolated static-image path (passes-barcode) and the in-process live path call.
- wpass-7xo.5 (pure-JVM YUV-frame adapter: PlanarYUVLuminanceSource from a Y-plane byte[] + width/height/rowStride -> decodeLuminance) BLOCKS wlt-mwj's CameraX ImageAnalysis integration: the consumer extracts the Y plane and passes bytes in; the kernel takes NO CameraX dependency and declares NO CAMERA permission.
- wpass-7xo.6 (JVM test suite for the live frame-decode path) is the kernel-side counterpart to the consumer's integration tests on wlt-mwj.
- wpass-7xo.3 (OEM HAL ImageAnalysis output-format spike) and wpass-7xo.4 (decision: live decode runs in-process, not in the :barcodeDecoder sandbox) inform the consumer's pipeline shape on wlt-mwj.

Consumer-facing contract wpass-7xo delivers to wlt-mwj: a pure-JVM decode core (decodeLuminance) + a Y-plane byte[] adapter, in-process (NOT the one-shot/blocking isolated transport, which cannot stream frames). Consumer owns CameraX ImageAnalysis (raw YUV_420_888 ONLY, never ImageCapture/JPEG), preview UI, CAMERA permission request, lifecycle, foreground-only discipline, user-confirmation sheet, and routing the decoded payload through QrPayloadClassifier + ScannableCardInputValidator. Any "scan from saved photo" still routes through the existing isolated BarcodeImageDecoder (wpass-zrt), not a new in-process codec call.
close_reason: Kernel epic complete (6/6 children). Delivered the trust-claim-bearing live-camera decode core in passes-android: pure-JVM passes-barcode-core extraction (wpass-7xo.2) with shared decodeLuminance + symbology allowlist; decodeYPlane Y-plane adapter (wpass-7xo.5, PR #130) handling rowStride/pixelStride/mirroring; JVM test suite (wpass-7xo.6); in-process placement decision recorded as ADR 0008 (wpass-7xo.4); deep-research security analysis (wpass-7xo.1); and the OEM HAL output-format spike (wpass-7xo.3) confirming structural codec-absence across all walt.is targets with no contract change (ADR 0008 follow-up resolved, PR #133). No CameraX dependency, no CAMERA permission in the kernel. Consumer capture/UI/permission/payload-routing work continues in walt-android wlt-mwj, unblocked against the confirmed contract.

title: BouncyCastle 1.79->1.84 as coordinated kernel+consumer pair
description: Kernel ships bcprov/bcpkix on the consumer's RUNTIME classpath; consumer test-pins BC 1.79 only. ACTION: merge kernel #45 (1.79->1.84) TOGETHER with a walt-android PR bumping its androidTest BC pin 1.79->1.84 so consumer crypto tests exercise the shipped provider. Gate: kernel PKCS7/CMS/X.509 sig suite green on 1.84 (already green) + consumer crypto androidTests green; skim BC 1.79->1.84 notes for CMS/path-validation default changes. Lower risk (no compile coupling). Resolves the hold on wpass-68v.2/#45.
notes: MECHANISM CONFIRMED: walt-android CI (quality.yml) checks out walt-app/walt-passes-android @ main into passes-android/passes-android-main and composite-builds it (-PwaltPassesPath). So the consumer follow is just: after kernel #45 merges to kernel main, RE-RUN walt-android #257's CI (it re-checks-out kernel main = 1.84 -> consistent resolution resolves -> App Release Smoke passes), then merge #257. No republish, no fresh PR; #257's catalog change is already correct. waltPasses=0.1.0-SNAPSHOT artifact path is the CI-without-kernel fallback only; CI does check out the kernel. EXECUTION (user chose kernel-first 2026-06-04): 1) user approve+merge #45; 2) re-run #257 CI; 3) user approve+merge #257.
close_reason: BouncyCastle 1.84 landed in lockstep both repos. Kernel #45 merged first (bcprov/bcpkix 1.84); walt-android #257 then went fully green against the 1.84 kernel (App Release Smoke pass - consistent-resolution conflict gone) and merged. Synthesizer (consumer androidTest) and verifier (kernel runtime) now share one BC 1.84 surface.

title: Align kernel Kotlin to consumer 2.3.10 (kernel must not lead consumer)
description: Composite-build rule: kernel Kotlin must be <= consumer (walt-android on 2.3.10). Kernel currently 2.2.21; Dependabot #44 targets 2.4.0 which is the WRONG direction (kernel ahead of consumer -> metadata 'compiled with newer Kotlin' risk). ACTION: close #44 (2.4.0) and instead bump kernel to exactly 2.3.10 to match consumer and close the 2.2->2.3 drift. Gate: assemble walt-android against this kernel branch. title: Security test/verification suite (malformed corpus, decompression bombs, hostile payloads, isolation assertion)
description:
Adversarial kernel-side test suite, mirroring passes-pdf instrumentation discipline (PdfImporterInstrumentedTest). The bar is materially higher than FossWallet's (which has zero of these; ships in-process, no caps, native zxing-cpp, main-thread no-try/catch - open crash #625; reachable by any app via ACTION_SEND image/*).

Cases:
- Malformed-image corpus: truncated/corrupt JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF, polyglots, wrong-extension, 0-byte, EXIF-laden -> assert the sandbox returns NoBarcodeFound/DecodeFailed or dies alone; the caller process and result channel are unharmed.
- Decompression-bomb cases: tiny files declaring 100+ MP, pixel-flood PNGs -> assert the header cap rejects pre-full-decode; no OOM escapes the sandbox.
- Hostile-payload cases: the decoder returns raw bytes faithfully (bidi/RTL-override, zero-width/control chars, oversized, javascript:/intent:/custom-scheme URLs, homoglyph domains, SQL-ish) - assert these are returned verbatim for the CONSUMER's passes-core QrPayloadClassifier + ScannableCardInputValidator to reject (the kernel decoder must NOT silently mangle payloads, and must NOT auto-act).
- Isolation assertion: prove the :barcodeDecoder process holds no permissions and cannot reach app data / Keystore / storage (SecurityException on a privileged call from inside).
- Facade surface-lock test (per wpass-zrt.1).

AC references: walt-android docs analysis 3.2, 3.5, 4.7.
notes: Headline runtime isolation assertion now LANDED (PR #128, branch barcode-isolation-probe-suite). decodeProcessCannotReachAppDataOrKeystore binds a test-only isolatedProcess probe and proves from inside the sandbox: app-data read blocked, Keystore containsAlias blocked, socket(AF_INET) denied with EACCES, and code ran in an isolated UID (99402 on FP4). The two former @Ignore skeletons are gone; raw-transact parcel probe also landed. Over-area bomb + 0-byte + truncated-PNG corpus cases added. All 8 instrumented scenarios green on physical FP4 (Android 15). The probe infra was the only remaining blocker (was tracked in wpass-6mg). Close on PR #128 merge.

title: Barcode decode with pure-JVM ZXing (com.google.zxing:core); ML Kit rejected; zxing-cpp contingency
description:
Decode the barcode from the bounded bitmap using pure-JVM ZXing inside the :barcodeDecoder sandbox.

LIBRARY DECISION (from the security analysis):
- USE com.google.zxing:core (pure JVM/Kotlin) - ZERO native attack surface. Native (C/C++/JNI) code sits outside the JVM security model, has full process address-space access, and inherits all granted permissions; a buggy native decoder can compromise the whole process. Pure-JVM removes that surface entirely (verified: Android 'use of native code' risk doc + NativeGuard).
- REJECT ML Kit Barcode Scanning. Decode is on-device, BUT: (1) it is NOT zero-telemetry - sends performance/utilization metrics and contacts Google servers periodically (ML Kit Terms, verified), breaking 'data never leaves the device'; (2) the unbundled variant + Google code-scanner REQUIRE Google Play Services to download the model, disqualifying for the degoogled/GrapheneOS walt.is channel; (3) a 'Google does not store code-scanner data' claim was REFUTED in research. Only the bundled variant avoids a Play-Services runtime dep, and it still phones home telemetry.
- zxing-cpp (io.github.zxing-cpp:android, Apache-2.0) is a CONTINGENCY ONLY: adopt if ZXing-Java detection proves inadequate AND it stays inside this sandbox. Never in a caller's main process. Its native PDF417/Aztec/DataMatrix decoders have NO confirmed CVE but ALSO no confirmed fuzzing clearance - treat as unquantified (gates adoption).

Acceptance:
- com.google.zxing:core in :passes-barcode (sandbox side); symbology allowlist passed to the reader (do not enable every format blindly).
- Verify com.google.zxing:core license (presumed Apache-2.0, confirm) + open-advisory check before adding the dependency.
- PRIVACY: confirm the chosen path does NO network and needs NO Play Services - pure on-device computation, which strengthens Walt's data-never-leaves-device stance.

AC references: walt-android docs analysis 2.2, 2.3, 2.6, 4.2, 4.6.
notes: Implemented in PR #125 (branch wpass-zrt.4-zxing-decode). ZxingBarcodeSymbolDecoder backed by com.google.zxing:core 3.5.4 (Apache-2.0, zero native surface; no open advisory). POSSIBLE_FORMATS pinned to the ScannableFormat roster allowlist; out-of-roster -> UnsupportedBarcodeFormat; payload returned faithfully (no classification here). BoundedBitmapDecoder pins ALLOCATOR_SOFTWARE for pixel-readable bitmap. JVM tests round-trip all 5 roster formats via ZXing writer + PDF417 allowlist-exclusion + blank-image arm; :passes-barcode:check green. On-device instrumented decode (benignQrDecodesToPayloadAndFormat) remains @Ignore'd -> wpass-zrt.5. Awaiting PR merge before close.
close_reason: Merged in PR #125 (squash 9aa0fd0). Pure-JVM ZXing decode (com.google.zxing:core 3.5.4, Apache-2.0) with ScannableFormat roster allowlist; JVM round-trip tests for all 5 formats + PDF417 allowlist-exclusion. On-device UPC-A/EAN-13 fidelity and ReaderException corpus deferred to wpass-zrt.5.

title: Bounded bitmap decode inside the sandbox (decompression-bomb + size/dimension/format caps)
description:
Decode the picked image to a bitmap INSIDE the :barcodeDecoder sandbox with pre-decode caps. The image-codec step is the dominant RCE surface (CVE-2023-4863 libwebp / CVE-2020-16010 class) and the decompression-bomb DoS surface.

Acceptance (security guards):
- Platform ImageDecoder with a header-decoded dimension + megapixel cap applied BEFORE full decode (the same setOnHeaderDecodedListener decompression-bomb lever passes-ui BoundedImage uses, but for analysis not display - BoundedImage itself is display-only/capped-raster and cannot be reused for barcode pixels).
- Upstream file-size cap before decode.
- Format allowlist (image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, ...).
- Off-main-thread; full Throwable containment incl. OutOfMemoryError; a sandbox crash returns DecodeFailed, never an ANR/crash in the caller.
- No payload/PII/bytes in logs (kernel telemetry stays enum-only).

AC references: walt-android docs/barcode-from-image-security-analysis.md 2.4, 2.5, 3.1, 3.3.
notes:
Implemented on branch wpass-zrt-3-bounded-decode (commit c334ae0). Landed in :passes-barcode:
- BarcodeDecodeConfig (file-size 25MB, per-side 12000px, area 50MP, 5s timeout, MIME allowlist jpeg/png/webp/heif/heic)
- BoundedBitmapDecoder: bounded fd read + ImageDecoder header-listener caps (reject before allocation), full Throwable/OOM containment
- DecodeWatchdog + ProcessKiller: timeout-then-kill (slow-loris guard, the PR #123 follow-up)
- BarcodeSymbolDecoder.NotYetImplemented seam for wpass-zrt.4
- BarcodeDecodeService wires read->bounded decode (watchdog)->symbol decode->recycle->close, off-main-thread, no logging
JVM tests green (size cap, header-cap table, watchdog kill path, orchestration containment+teardown); detekt/ktlint/lint pass.
REMAINING (owned by wpass-zrt.5): on-device fixtures (benign/bomb/malformed/over-cap) + CI device matrix to un-ignore the instrumented bomb assertion. Format allowlist maps disallowed container -> ImageDecodeFailed (no image-format reason in DecodeFailureReason).

Bounded bitmap decode with file-size/dimension/megapixel caps, MIME allowlist, decode watchdog (timeout-then-kill), full Throwable+OOM containment, off-main-thread, no logging. JVM tests + quality gates green. On-device fixtures/CI matrix remain wpass-zrt.5.

title: New :passes-barcode module + BarcodeImageDecoder facade (analog to PdfImporter.create())
description:
Define the single consumer-facing entry point so consumers (walt-android, others) never hand-roll bind/memfd plumbing - directly avoids the wlt-ygl parallel-implementation anti-pattern that DocumentRenderer fell into.

Scope:
- New Gradle module :passes-barcode mirroring :passes-pdf (Android host + facade). Wire into settings.gradle.kts. Open: whether pure result types live in :passes-core (reuse ScannableFormat) or a new :passes-barcode-core; default to passes-core unless the type graph argues otherwise.
- Public facade BarcodeImageDecoder with a create()/decode() entry analogous to PdfImporter.create() / DefaultPdfImporter. Suspend fun decode(source) returning a sealed result.
- Sealed result type: DecodedBarcode(payload: String, format: ScannableFormat) | NoBarcodeFound | DecodeFailed(reason). Reuse passes-core ScannableFormat for the format arm.
- Input is an image SOURCE handed across the bind (ParcelFileDescriptor / memfd), NOT a Bitmap and NOT raw bytes in the caller process.
- Facade returns ONLY {payload, format} - no Bitmap, no bytes, no auto-action. Classification/validation stays in the existing passes-core QrPayloadClassifier + ScannableCardInputValidator (consumer routes the payload there).
- Surface-lock test for the facade (mirrors ScannableCardSurfaceTest discipline): the public API exposes exactly the documented parameters/result arms.

AC references: walt-android docs/barcode-from-image-security-analysis.md 4.2-4.4; consumer wlt-58a.1.
close_reason: Delivered :passes-barcode module + BarcodeImageDecoder facade, BarcodeImageSource (ContentUri|FileDescriptor), pure BarcodeDecodeResult in passes-core (DecodedBarcode|NoBarcodeFound|DecodeFailed + DecodeFailureReason roster), and PublicApiSurfaceTest. Default impl returns DecoderUnavailable until isolated service lands in wpass-zrt.2. Tests/detekt/lint green; pushed on branch passes-barcode-facade.

title: [epic] Hosted isolated-process barcode/QR-from-image decode facade (consumed by walt-android wlt-58a)
description:
Kernel-side companion to walt-android epic wlt-58a (decode a barcode/QR from a user-picked static image to pre-fill a ScannableCard / import a pass). Decision (2026-06-03): KERNEL-HOSTED. walt-android chose to host the decode in the kernel rather than declare its own isolated service.

WHY KERNEL-HOSTED (the decision): runtime isolation is identical whether the kernel or the app declares the isolatedProcess service (same merged manifest, same OS-enforced isolated-UID + isolated_app SELinux sandbox - verified vs AOSP app-sandbox + Chromium android-sandbox docs). So this is a software-engineering call, not a security one. Kernel-hosted wins on REUSE: the kernel already owns the only isolatedProcess boundary (passes-pdf, android:process=:pdfRenderer) and the bind/memfd plumbing (internal/RendererSession.kt, internal/PdfPfdFactory.kt) behind the PdfImporter.create() facade. A Walt-declared service would re-create that orchestration - exactly the parallel-implementation anti-pattern wlt-ygl is trying to remove (DocumentRenderer already hand-rolled + drifted from these classes). Hosting decode here keeps the whole hostile-input trust boundary (PDF sandbox, BoundedImage decompression-bomb cap, QrPayloadClassifier, ScannableCardInputValidator) centralized and threat-modeled in one repo.

WHAT TO BUILD: a kernel facade analogous to PdfImporter.create() - call it BarcodeImageDecoder - that takes an image source (ParcelFileDescriptor/memfd over the bind), runs a BOUNDED platform ImageDecoder + pure-JVM ZXing decode INSIDE a new isolatedProcess service, and returns ONLY a sealed result {DecodedBarcode(payload, ScannableFormat) | NoBarcodeFound | DecodeFailed(reason)} over Binder. Natural home: a new :passes-barcode module mirroring :passes-pdf (host + facade); decode result types can reuse ScannableFormat from :passes-core (open: whether to add a :passes-barcode-core for pure types). Classification/validation is NOT re-done here - consumers route the returned payload through the existing passes-core QrPayloadClassifier + ScannableCardInputValidator.

SECURITY GATE (inherited from wlt-58a.1, contractual): decode runs isolatedProcess=true, exported=false, no permissions, no network; image bytes reach the sandbox only via memfd/PFD over the bind and NEVER the caller's main process; the service returns only {string, format}; per-call teardown; nothing reaches Keystore/DPAN/card data.

Full threat model, library/CVE research, and pros/cons of the decision: walt-android repo docs/barcode-from-image-security-analysis.md (sections 3.4, 4.2, 4.3, 4.3.1). Related kernel work: wlt-ygl DocumentOpener facade consolidation (share the isolated-worker plumbing rather than fork it).
design:
THREAT MODEL + LIBRARY RATIONALE (kernel-relevant subset; folded in from walt-android's security analysis, 2026-06-03, deep-research verified). Full analysis incl. existing-Walt-pattern map + privacy + FossWallet deltas lives on the consumer epic wlt-58a (walt-android tracker) design field. Per-step guards on wpass-zrt.1-.6.

WHY DECODE MUST BE ISOLATED (the gate, wpass-zrt.2): the image-codec step is a demonstrated, exploited-in-the-wild RCE class - libwebp CVE-2023-4863 (0-click heap overflow); CVE-2020-16010 (Chrome ConvertToJavaBitmap heap overflow chained w/ CVE-2020-15999 sandbox escape). In-process decode of an attacker image can reach the host process's full address space + permissions. Project Mainline modularizes media/codec on Android 10+ (Play-system-updatable) BUT the 'still-image codec is mainline-patchable' framing was REFUTED (swcodec carries audio/video Codec2, not still-image; libwebp/libjpeg/libpng/libgif may be in the platform graphics module) - so out-of-band patching is NOT guaranteed, esp. older/degoogled devices. Isolation is therefore required, not a backstop. The consumer's process will hold DPAN/tap-to-pay material; nothing in :barcodeDecoder may reach Keystore/DPAN/card data.

THREAT VECTORS (Likelihood x Impact):
- Malicious image -> codec RCE before any barcode logic. Impact CRITICAL if in main process; isolation reduces to sandbox-only. The whole point of this epic.
- Decompression-bomb DoS (High likelihood, trivial). Mitigated by header dimension/megapixel + file-size caps before full decode (wpass-zrt.3); in the isolated process only the sandbox dies.
- Malicious payload injection: the decoder must return raw bytes FAITHFULLY and NOT auto-act; downstream classification/validation is the consumer's job via passes-core QrPayloadClassifier + ScannableCardInputValidator.

LIBRARY: pure-JVM com.google.zxing:core (zero native attack surface). Native C++/JNI is outside the JVM security model w/ full address-space access + all app permissions (Android use-of-native-code doc + NativeGuard, verified). ML Kit rejected (telemetry phone-home + Play-Services dep breaks the degoogled walt.is channel + 'data never leaves device'; code-scanner no-storage claim refuted). zxing-cpp (Apache-2.0) contingency only, sandboxed, IF detection inadequate - its native PDF417/Aztec/DataMatrix decoders are fuzzing-UNCLEARED (gates adoption).

RESIDUAL (cannot be designed away): image-codec 0-day w/ no patch at exploitation time -> isolation CONTAINS (permissionless sandbox), does not PREVENT; a 2-bug sandbox-escape chain stays theoretically possible (Low) - same residual the existing :pdfRenderer sandbox already accepts.

CONSUMER: walt-android epic wlt-58a (kernel-hosted decision). See CROSS-REPO COORDINATION in the description/notes.
notes:
CROSS-REPO COORDINATION (kernel-hosted decision, 2026-06-03). Two trackers, no bd edges between them, so the dependency graph is documented here on BOTH epics.

walt-passes-android (this epic, wpass-zrt = PROVIDER)  -- unblocks -->  walt-android (wlt-58a = CONSUMER).

Bead mapping:
- wpass-zrt.1 (BarcodeImageDecoder facade/module) + wpass-zrt.2 (isolatedProcess decode service, P1) BLOCK walt-android wlt-58a.1 (Walt cannot integrate until these land).
- wpass-zrt.3 (bounded bitmap decode) absorbs the work formerly tracked as walt-android wlt-58a.2 (now CLOSED/superseded).
- wpass-zrt.4 (pure-JVM ZXing decode) absorbs walt-android wlt-58a.3 (now CLOSED/superseded), AND owns the answers to walt-side spike questions: Q2 (zxing-cpp PDF417/Aztec/DataMatrix fuzzing), Q4 (com.google.zxing:core license/advisories), Q5 (ZXing detection adequacy gating the zxing-cpp contingency).
- wpass-zrt.5 (kernel security/isolation tests) is the kernel-side counterpart to walt-android wlt-58a.6 (Walt integration tests).
- wpass-zrt.6 (consolidate isolated-worker plumbing) is the kernel counterpart of walt-android wlt-ygl (DocumentOpener facade); coordinate so PDF render + barcode decode share one memfd/bind stack.

Consumer-facing contract wpass-zrt must deliver to wlt-58a.1: suspend decode(image source via Uri/PFD) -> {payload, ScannableFormat} | NoBarcodeFound | DecodeFailed; runs in :barcodeDecoder isolatedProcess; raw bytes never cross back to the caller's main process; permissionless; per-call teardown.
close_reason: All 7 children complete (wpass-zrt.1-.6 + wpass-6mg); barcode decode facade, isolated-process service, bounded decode, ZXing decode, security suite, plumbing consolidation, and CI leg all landed
