title: DocumentView full-screen affordance is not consumer-styleable (shape/icon/placement baked in)
description:
PROBLEM
The full-screen open affordance rendered inside passes-pdf-ui DocumentView (the FullScreenBanner composable, shown when onOpenFullScreen is wired) is a full-width, square-cornered bar with centered text. DocumentSemantics only exposes fullScreenBannerLabel plus background/foreground colors. The composable hardcodes:
  - full-width layout (fillMaxWidth, docked below the pager),
  - no corner rounding / no pill shape,
  - text-only content (no icon),
  - centered text alignment.

A consumer (Walt) needs the affordance to be a centered rounded pill with a leading glyph, floating over the bottom of the page surface, to match its product design. None of that is reachable through the current semantics, so the consumer must suppress the kernel banner entirely (onOpenFullScreen=null, losing the kernel-provided page-tap target) and reimplement the affordance on its own side.

DESIRED OUTCOME
  - A consumer can present the open-full-screen affordance in its own visual register (shape, corner radius, optional leading icon, alignment/placement, padding) WITHOUT giving up the kernel-provided behaviour (the tap-to-open page target and the discoverability hint), and without forking DocumentView.
  - The trust-surface guarantees of DocumentView are unaffected (the non-suppressible DocumentTrustCaption and the no-share/export/print contract must remain intact regardless of how the affordance is styled).
  - Existing consumers that pass only a label + colors keep working unchanged (backward compatible default).

CONTEXT
  - Reported by the Walt consumer. Walt will ship a Walt-side pill button as the interim fallback (tracked in walt-android wlt-cjv), mirroring the existing WaltDocumentCloseButton / WaltSecuritySheets / DocumentSummaryRow fallback-then-collapse pattern. Once a kernel API lands, the Walt-side affordance should collapse onto it.
  - Note CloseFullScreenButton in FullScreenDocumentView already uses a host-supplied closeButton slot - that slot pattern is prior art for how the open affordance could be made host-supplied, but the solution is open.
notes: Implemented on branch wpass-qz2-pdf-fullscreen (commit a10b43d) per android-team decision 1A. Added DocumentView fullScreenAffordance composable slot (mirrors FullScreenDocumentView closeButton); host owns shape/icon/label/padding, kernel keeps page-tap target + non-suppressible trust caption. Affordance floats bottom-centre over the page. Default = existing neutral banner (backward compatible). Param count 6->7, DocumentSurfaceLockTest updated. No new DocumentSemantics tokens. Instrumented test added (runs on-device in CI).
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #118 (squash 6f811f2). Aspect-ratio stretch fixed by construction; consumer-styleable open affordance shipped as opt-in floating slot.

title: resolvePassDisplayIdentity gap: add overload that does not require a full Pass (Summary-shaped)
description:
wpass-up1 shipped `resolvePassDisplayIdentity(pass: Pass, userLabel: String?, locale: PassLocale)`, which performs locale substitution via `pass.resolveLocalizedStrings(locale).lookupOrSelf(...)`. The bead's acceptance criterion was that walt-android can call the resolver from PassSummaryRow, but PassSummaryRow only has `PassSummary`, not `Pass`:

- `PassSummary.organizationName` is the raw column value (not locale-substituted).
- `PassSummary` does NOT carry the `locales` table -- the kdoc explicitly says "does not pay for image or locale I/O".

Consequence: the list-row consumer cannot call the resolver as shipped without materializing a `StoredPass` for every row, defeating the projection.

## Fix

Add an overload alongside the existing one:

    public fun resolvePassDisplayIdentity(
        organizationName: String,
        userLabel: String?,
        localizedStrings: LocalizedStrings = LocalizedStrings.Empty,
    ): PassDisplayIdentity

PassSummary callers pass `LocalizedStrings.Empty`, in which case `lookupOrSelf` is a pure pass-through and the resolver fences the raw `organizationName` verbatim. Callers that DO hold a resolved table (e.g. a detail-screen path that wants Summary's shape) can pass it in.

Existing `(Pass, String?, PassLocale)` overload delegates to the new one by computing `pass.resolveLocalizedStrings(locale)` first.

Note: the separate UX issue that PassSummary.organizationName stores the raw key (so list rows of pkpasses with `#ORGNAME#` keys will show the raw key rather than the localized name) is a walt-android storage-projection concern, not a kernel API gap, and is out of scope here. The trust contract -- show the signed organizationName, FSI/PDI-fenced -- holds either way.

## Acceptance

- New overload exists with the documented signature.
- Pass-bearing overload delegates so the trust logic remains in one place.
- JVM-pure tests cover: no locales table (Empty), localized table substitutes, equality suppression against substituted name, FSI/PDI fence.
- walt-android can call the new overload from PassSummaryRow.
close_reason: Landed as PR #113 (squash 7c58e20). Summary-shaped overload (organizationName, userLabel, localizedStrings) added; Pass-bearing overload delegates. Five new resolver tests + delegation-equivalence test. PR review tightened KDoc and reflection-lock comments. 6/6 CI checks green.

title: resolvePassDisplayIdentity needs a PassSummary overload; current API can't be called from the list-row consumer it was designed for
description:
## Follow-up to wpass-up1 (commit 8d7d832)

The merged commit message explicitly names walt-android's wallet list row (PassSummaryRow) as the intended consumer of the new resolver. The resolver itself takes Pass, not PassSummary:

    public fun resolvePassDisplayIdentity(
        pass: Pass,
        userLabel: String?,
        locale: PassLocale = PassLocale("en"),
    ): PassDisplayIdentity

The list-row consumer holds PassSummary, not Pass. PassSummary is the indexed-column projection (passes-storage PassRepository.kt:252) that exists precisely so the wallet list doesn't pay for image/locale I/O on every row. The resolver's first step

    val strings = pass.resolveLocalizedStrings(locale)
    val displayOrganizationName = strings.lookupOrSelf(pass.organizationName)

requires the full Pass for the locales table. PassSummary.organizationName is the raw `passes.organization_name` column value (stored by SqlCipherPassStore.kt:113 / :135 without substitution), and PassSummary doesn't carry locales at all.

Net: the API as shipped is unreachable from the consumer it was designed for. Three workaround shapes for the consumer all have problems:

1. Load the full Pass per visible row. Defeats PassSummary; pays the image-bytes deserialization cost per scroll. Not viable.
2. Inline trim + equality + isolate locally on the consumer side. Exactly what ADR 0007 D6 forbids and what wpass-up1 was meant to prevent.
3. Wait for a PassSummary-friendly overload. This bead.

## Suggested shapes (not prescriptive)

Option A: overload the resolver to accept PassSummary directly:

    public fun resolvePassDisplayIdentity(
        pass: PassSummary,
        locale: PassLocale = PassLocale("en"),
    ): PassDisplayIdentity

Caveat: locale substitution is unavailable without the locales table. The overload would have to either:
  - skip step 1 (use organizationName as-is), or
  - drop the `locale` parameter entirely on this overload, or
  - read substitution from a new optional `localizedOrganizationName` field added to PassSummary at the storage layer.

Option B: add `localizedOrganizationName: String` (eagerly resolved for the storage-default locale at insert time) onto PassSummary, then the existing single-string trim + equality + isolate path on the consumer side is enough — and at that point the consumer's logic is so minimal that a tiny PassSummary helper (just trim + equality + isolate against a single resolved string) might still be worth shipping kernel-side to keep ADR 0007 D6 honest.

Option C: re-shape PassRepository to return Pass-projection on observe so consumers can call the existing resolver directly. Heaviest; goes against the original PassSummary cost rationale.

Walt-side leans toward A with the "skip locale substitution" behaviour documented (locale substitution of organizationName is rare; PassSummary callers already accept this limitation by design). B is also fine but expands the storage projection and bumps a migration.

## Consumer status

walt-android wlt-4d4 is in_progress and blocked on this. The walt-side wire-up is a one-call substitution once an API the consumer can actually call lands.

## Acceptance

- PassSummaryRow can call a kernel-blessed resolver to obtain the (primary, eyebrow) fenced pair with no consumer-side trim / equality / fence logic.
- Whatever overload lands, the JVM-pure PassDisplayIdentityTest's coverage extends to it.

title: PassIdentityBlock has no list-row variant; consumers can't safely render userLabel+orgName in a fixed title+subtitle row
description:
## Problem (from a consumer, walt-android)

PassIdentityBlock (passes-ui/PassIdentityBlock.kt) is the canonical renderer for the userLabel + signed organizationName pair (ADR 0007 D5/D6). It produces a 2-line vertically stacked output.

walt-android's wallet list row is a fixed shape: a single title slot + a single subtitle slot, owned by the consumer (PassSummaryRow in feature/passes/list/PassesListScreen.kt). PDFs and scannable cards already render correctly in this shape because their display labels are single strings on the kernel types (DocumentRow.displayLabel, ScannableCard.label). For pkpass, PassSummary.userLabel is exposed but there is no kernel-blessed way for the consumer to derive the (primary, eyebrow) string pair without re-implementing the trust logic that PassIdentityBlock owns:

- trim
- treat empty userLabel as no-override
- case-insensitive ASCII compare against the localized organizationName, suppress override when equal
- FSI/PDI bidi-isolation on both strings

Dropping PassIdentityBlock into the row's title slot doesn't fit (it's a 2-line Column, the row wants a single-line title + a single-line subtitle authored by the consumer).

## Consumer-visible symptom

If a consumer ignores userLabel in the list row (status quo in walt-android, tracked as wlt-4d4), users rename a pkpass on the detail screen but the wallet list row still shows the unchanged signed organizationName. The rename appears broken even though storage and detail rendering work fine.

If a consumer inlines the trust-comparison logic to derive the title themselves, they duplicate PassIdentityBlock's normalization rules - the exact smell ADR 0007 D6 was meant to prevent (\"every UI surface that presents a pkpass's primary visible identity MUST route through this composable\").

## What the consumer needs

A kernel-blessed way to obtain the resolved (primary, eyebrow) string pair for a given (pass, userLabel, locale) tuple, suitable for plugging into a consumer-authored single-line title + single-line subtitle row. The fence (FSI/PDI), the normalization, and the equality-suppression rule should remain in the kernel.

## Suggested shapes (not prescriptive; kernel team picks)

Option A: extract a pure helper alongside PassIdentityBlock that returns a small value class:

    public data class PassDisplayIdentity(
        public val primary: AnnotatedString,   // userLabel when distinct, else organizationName
        public val eyebrow: AnnotatedString?,  // organizationName when overridden, else null
    )

    @Composable
    public fun rememberPassDisplayIdentity(pass: Pass, userLabel: String?, locale: PassLocale): PassDisplayIdentity

PassIdentityBlock would internally consume this helper, so the trust contract has a single source of truth.

Option B: ship a row-shaped composable variant (e.g. PassIdentityRow) that takes consumer-provided title and subtitle text styles + colors so the consumer can match its own row chrome but the kernel still owns the layout decision.

Option C: leave PassIdentityBlock as-is and document an officially supported pattern, with a public function exposing just the resolution + fence (e.g. resolvePassDisplayIdentity(...) returning Pair<String, String?>). Closest to a pure helper; consumer applies styling.

Trade-offs:
- A keeps styling fully consumer-side, easiest to drop into varied row chrome (walt-android's row uses one-off display type scales, not Material).
- B is the strongest trust posture (kernel owns the render) but the most opinionated about row layout - may not fit every consumer.
- C is the smallest API surface and the cleanest factoring; the FSI/PDI fence happens inside the resolver, styling is consumer's job.

The walt-android side leans toward A or C - the wallet list row has a one-off type scale (ROW_TITLE_FONT_SIZE 14sp / ROW_SUBTITLE_FONT_SIZE 12sp) that a kernel composable would need to be heavily parameterized to match.

## References

- ADR 0007 D5 (\"both must be displayed\")
- ADR 0007 D6 (PassIdentityBlock is the canonical renderer)
- Existing tests in passes-ui/src/test/.../TrustClaimSurfaceTest.kt (\"PassIdentityBlock is the canonical renderer of the user-supplied / signed identity pair\")
- Consumer issue: walt-android wlt-4d4

## Acceptance

- Whatever shape lands, walt-android can call it from PassSummaryRow and get the same trust contract as PassIdentityBlock with no duplicated normalization logic on the consumer side.
- Existing PassIdentityBlock callers continue to work unchanged (or migrate cleanly to the new shared helper if that is how the refactor goes).
- Trust-surface tests cover the new entry point.
notes: Option A+C hybrid landed on branch pass-identity-row-helper (commit f967a5f, pushed). Pure resolver resolvePassDisplayIdentity returns PassDisplayIdentity(primary, eyebrow) with both lines already FSI/PDI-fenced; PassIdentityBlock now delegates so the trust contract has one source of truth. Tests: passes-ui suite 89/89 green; new PassDisplayIdentityTest covers null/blank/empty override, distinct override, equality suppression (raw and localized), locale fallback, bidi fence, and parameter-count lock against accidental @Composable. Detekt clean. Open PR next.
close_reason: Landed as PR #112 (squash 8d7d832). resolvePassDisplayIdentity ships in passes-ui; PassIdentityBlock delegates to it; JVM-pure resolver tests + PR review feedback applied; all 6 CI checks green.

title: [epic] Rename APIs for documents, scannable cards, and pkpass (companion to walt-android wlt-4dn / GitHub #75)
description:
Parent epic bundling the three kernel-side APIs needed for walt-android wlt-4dn / GitHub walt-app/walt-passes-android#75 (allow renaming of passes).

Each slice is a distinct storage / trust-model story; they share only that the consumer (walt-android) needs a mutate-after-create path for the artifact's display title.

**Slices**:
- **wpass-hhq** — updateDocumentLabel(DocumentRecordId, String): cleanest. Single mutable column, validator mirrors insertDocument's MAX_LABEL_CHARS arm. No trust implications.
- **wpass-lay** — updateScannableCard(ScannableCardRecordId, ScannableCardCreateInput): re-runs ScannableCardInputValidator on update; covers both #75 rename and #100 edit-payload in one surface.
- **wpass-7xa** — passes.user_label nullable column + updatePassUserLabel + trust-caption ADR amendment. Highest risk: a naïve title-override would silently decouple displayed identity from signed identity. Needs ADR work before code.

**Sequencing suggestion**: ship wpass-hhq first (cheapest, unblocks the consumer slice with the most user reach). Then wpass-lay. Save wpass-7xa for after the ADR conversation lands.
close_reason: All three kernel-side slices shipped: wpass-hhq (PR #109), wpass-lay (PR #110), wpass-7xa (PR #111, includes ADR 0007 trust-caption rule + PassIdentityBlock kernel composable). Consumer-side rename UI, tile re-wire, and core/data-passes Hilt wiring are tracked separately in walt-android (wlt-4dn.3 / wlt-4pg) and are out of scope for this kernel epic.

title: Add user_label side-channel override for pkpass with trust-caption decoupling
description:
Companion bead for walt-android wlt-4dn.3 / GitHub walt-app/walt-passes-android#75. Highest-risk kernel change in the rename epic; touches the trust model.

**Problem**: pkpass titles come from the *signed* pass.json (logoText / organizationName / description). They are part of the trust bond -- 'this pass identifies itself as issued by Delta'. Letting users override the visible title silently decouples the displayed identity from the signed identity. Same shape as the #69 verifier-name swap.

**Proposal**:
1. Add a nullable user_label column on the passes table (NULL = no override; show signed title as today).
2. Add PassRepository.updatePassUserLabel(id: PassRecordId, label: String?): StorageResult<Unit>. NULL clears the override.
3. Expose user_label on PassSummary and StoredPass.
4. **Trust caption changes**: when user_label is set, the trust caption MUST include the signed organizationName / description so the issuer identity is never hidden. Consumer themes the surface; kernel sets the rule. Document this as ADR 0006 (or amendment to ADR 0002).

**Open**:
- Which signed string anchors the caption -- organizationName or description? Probably organizationName (issuer brand), with description as a secondary if needed.
- Does updating user_label bump updated_at? Probably yes; sort order should reflect user attention.

**Blocks**: walt-android wlt-4dn.3.

**Do not start until**: the trust-caption decoupling shape is agreed (ADR amendment landed in this repo).
notes: ADR 0007 accepted and implementation landed in PR #111 on branch wpass-7xa-adr-user-label. Phase 1 (ADR conversation) + Phase 2 (schema migration v4->v5, PassRepository.updatePassUserLabel API, PassIdentityBlock kernel composable, PassFront re-wire, full test coverage) both complete. Awaiting PR review/merge before close. Closes the parent epic wpass-osf once merged alongside the consumer-side wlt-4dn.3 wiring in walt-android.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #111 (squash-merged as commit f015d3e). ADR 0007 accepted; schema v4->v5 migration, PassRepository.updatePassUserLabel API, PassIdentityBlock kernel composable with FSI/PDI fences + maxLines/overflow caps, PassFront re-wire, full unit + connected test coverage. Worktree and feature branch (local + remote) cleaned up. Parent epic wpass-osf can now close pending walt-android wlt-4dn.3 consumer wiring.

title: Add updateScannableCard API to PassRepository
description:
Companion bead for walt-android wlt-4dn.2 and partially for GitHub walt-app/walt-passes-android#100. walt-android needs to mutate a stored ScannableCard after creation for GitHub #75 (rename) and #100 (edit created codes).

**API shape options**:

A) Narrow (label only):
suspend fun updateScannableCardLabel(id: ScannableCardRecordId, label: String): StorageResult<Unit>

B) Full update:
suspend fun updateScannableCard(id: ScannableCardRecordId, input: ScannableCardCreateInput): StorageResult<Unit>

Option B re-runs ScannableCardInputValidator and re-derives any inferred-format resolution, mirroring createScannableCard. This is the simpler kernel surface (one validator, one path) and covers both #75 (rename) and #100 (edit payload) in one API.

**Recommendation**: B. The validator is the single insert-time choke point per existing KDoc; running it on update too preserves that invariant. Cost: re-validating on a label-only change is harmless.

**Behavior**: single UPDATE pass on the scannable_cards row (transactionally re-runs ScannableCardInputValidator first; on rejection no UPDATE happens). Re-emit observeScannableCards. No telemetry event.

**Surface-lock**: extend the existing ScannableCard surface-lock test.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #110 (merged 790c578). updateScannableCard API added to PassRepository following wpass-hhq pattern; validator-before-load precedence, no success telemetry, rejection channel shared with createScannableCard.

title: Add updateDocumentLabel API to PassRepository
description:
Companion bead for walt-android wlt-4dn.1. walt-android needs to mutate DocumentRow.displayLabel after import for GitHub walt-app/walt-passes-android#75 (allow renaming of passes).

**API shape**:
suspend fun updateDocumentLabel(id: DocumentRecordId, label: String): StorageResult<Unit>

**Validation**: enforce DocumentBounds.MAX_LABEL_CHARS at this layer just like insertDocument does. Reject with StorageError.DocumentRejected(DocumentStorageRejectedKind.LabelTooLongAtStorage) on overflow. Reject empty / blank labels with a new arm (LabelEmpty?) or reuse the size arm with a min-1 bound -- decide based on what kernel surface-lock tests are easier to extend.

**Surface-lock**: add test asserting the new method exists and the validation arms fire. No breaking changes to existing callers.

title: Fix #92: PDF QR disappears in dark mode (transparent page background)
description: GitHub issue #92. Bitmap.createBitmap(ARGB_8888) defaults to transparent. PdfRenderer.Page.render() does not fill white before drawing, so PDFs with implicit white backgrounds rasterise transparent. Compose then composites them over the dark Material surface, leaving black QR squares against a dark background = invisible. Per Android docs, the caller must clear the bitmap to the desired background. Fix is bitmap.eraseColor(Color.WHITE) before p.render() in PdfRendererService.rasterise (passes-pdf/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/pdf/android/PdfRendererService.kt:145).
notes: PR #105 opened: https://github.com/walt-app/walt-passes-android/pull/105

title: 1D barcodes render only a few pixels tall in ScannableCardView
description:
## Symptom

When a ScannableCard is opened in `ScannableCardScreen`, 1D barcodes (Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, UPC-A) render at the correct width but only a few pixels tall — a thin strip with a tall whitespace band below it. Confirmed across multiple users / devices. QR codes are unaffected (they look correct).

## Analysis

The bug is the interaction between two pieces:

1. `passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/internal/ZxingBarcodeEncoder.kt:89-96` calls every 1D writer with `(width = 0, height = 0)`:

       Code128Writer().encode(payload, ZxingFormat.CODE_128, 0, 0)
       Code39Writer().encode(payload, ZxingFormat.CODE_39, 0, 0)
       EAN13Writer().encode(payload, ZxingFormat.EAN_13, 0, 0)
       UPCAWriter().encode(payload, ZxingFormat.UPC_A, 0, 0)

   The comment says this is intentional ("natural minimum … renderer scales at draw time"). In this mode ZXing's 1D writers return a `BitMatrix` that is exactly **1 module tall** (`matrix.height == 1`). QR is square, so this codepath produces a usable matrix for QR but a single-row strip for all four 1D formats.

2. `passes-ui/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/ui/ScannableCardView.kt:49-60` turns the matrix into a `Bitmap` of `(width × 1)` pixels and paints it with:

       Image(
           painter = BitmapPainter(image = bitmap.asImageBitmap(), filterQuality = FilterQuality.None),
           ...
           modifier = modifier.defaultMinSize(minWidth = 320.dp, minHeight = 96.dp),
       )

   `Image` defaults to `ContentScale.Fit`, which preserves the painter's intrinsic aspect ratio. With a ~200:1 source bitmap painted into the full-height `Box(weight(1f).padding(24.dp))` from `ScannableCardScreen.kt:59-73`, `Fit` scales width to fill the container and collapses height to `containerWidth / matrixWidth` — a couple of pixels tall, with the remaining ~90+ dp left as whitespace below.

This is a pure passes-ui / passes-core issue. Walt's consumer (`feature/passes/.../ScannableCardDetailScreen.kt`) gives the kernel composable `Modifier.fillMaxWidth().weight(1f)`, so full height is available; nothing on the Walt side constrains the rendered barcode.

For contrast: `passes-ui/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/ui/BarcodeView.kt:50-58` (the pkpass renderer) does not hit this. It encodes with explicit `widthPx = minWidthDp * 3`, `heightPx = minHeightDp * 3`, so the matrix comes back at usable pixel dimensions. The new ScannableCard path is the only consumer using the `(0, 0)` "natural minimum" approach.

## Reproduction

Open any saved scannable card whose format is Code 128 / Code 39 / EAN-13 / UPC-A. Observe the barcode is the correct width but only a few pixels tall. Switch to a QR card to confirm QR renders correctly.

## Options for fixing (not prescribing one)

Both have been considered; either resolves the symptom.

- **(a)** Renderer-side: set `contentScale = ContentScale.FillBounds` on the `Image` in `ScannableCardView` (at least for 1D formats). `FilterQuality.None` is already set, so a single-row bitmap stretches vertically nearest-neighbor, which is exactly the desired result for a 1D barcode and preserves the kernel's stated "per-module upscale stays nearest-neighbor, module edges remain sharp" contract. Smallest change, smallest bitmap.

- **(b)** Encoder-side (or `toMonochromeBitmap`-side): produce a matrix / bitmap that is already several modules tall for 1D formats, so the painter's intrinsic ratio is reasonable and `Fit` works without modification. Mirrors what `BarcodeView` already does for pkpass barcodes. Larger bitmaps; keeps `Image`'s defaults intact.

Trade-off and the choice between them is left to the implementer; flagging that the comment in `ZxingBarcodeEncoder` ("renderer scales at draw time") points at (a) being the originally intended split, while (b) brings the two barcode renderers (ScannableCardView, BarcodeView) into the same shape.

## Notes

- Regression guard worth adding alongside the fix: a `ScannableCardView` screenshot or layout test for one 1D format asserting the rendered barcode height fills (not collapses inside) its container.
- `BarcodeEncoderTest` only asserts `matrix.height > 0` for the 1D formats (`BarcodeEncoderTest.kt:24, 33`), so the 1-row matrix is technically within the existing contract — if the fix lands on the encoder side, that test should tighten.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #99 (squash a5d94d0): per-format ContentScale in ScannableCardView — FillBounds for the four 1D symbologies, Fit retained for QR.

title: passes-ui: wire UiTelemetryGuard into BarcodeCreateConfirmSheet
description:
## Why this issue exists

wpass-lzi.9 shipped BarcodeCreateConfirmSheet without a telemetry: UiTelemetryGuard parameter. The other passes-ui security surfaces (B3UrlConfirmSheet, PhoneConfirmSheet, EmailConfirmSheet, PassImportConfirm, BoundedImage) all take a guard and emit show/confirm/dismiss (or decode-rejected) events.

UiTelemetryGuard's docstring states its purpose is "detect a spike in dismissals (possible UX regression or social-engineering pattern)." The create-time gate is currently invisible to that dashboard, so a future UX that nudges users into auto-confirming intent / unknown-scheme arms cannot be caught by walt-android.

The omission was deferred from wpass-lzi.9 because adopting the existing UiTelemetryGuard surface as-is requires a non-trivial policy decision: SecurityIntentKind has three arms (Url / Phone / Email) modeled around back-field click-time triggers, and PassType is PKPASS-specific (BoardingPass / EventTicket / ...) with no ScannableCard member. Picking a path needs the walt-android telemetry consumer in the room.

## Deliverable

Choose one of:

1. Extend SecurityIntentKind with a BarcodeCreate arm (or arms-per-QrPayloadKind-family) and reuse the existing onSecuritySheetShown / Confirmed / Dismissed methods.
2. Add a sibling enum (BarcodeCreateKind) and a parallel method family on UiTelemetryGuard (onBarcodeCreateGateShown / Confirmed / Dismissed).
3. Some hybrid (e.g. reuse the existing methods but add a new PassType-shaped enum for the create-time context).

Whatever path is chosen:

- Add telemetry: UiTelemetryGuard as a fourth parameter to BarcodeCreateConfirmSheet.
- Fire show on first composition (LaunchedEffect(payloadKind)), wrap onConfirm with confirm-event, wrap onCancel + onDismissRequest with dismiss-event.
- Bump ComposableSurfaceLockTest's three-param lock to four.
- Update COMPOSABLE_SIGNATURES.md's BarcodeCreateConfirmSheet entry (added in wpass-lzi.9 follow-up) with the new param and event semantics.
- PublicApiSurfaceTest's uiTelemetryGuardEventsAreEnumsAndPrimitivesOnly lock gets the new arm / method.

## Acceptance criteria

- BarcodeCreateConfirmSheet takes UiTelemetryGuard and emits the show / confirm / dismiss events.
- The chosen surface change (new SecurityIntentKind arm vs. new method family) is documented in the issue's closing notes and reflected in COMPOSABLE_SIGNATURES.md.
- :passes-ui:check green.
notes: Surface decision: Option 2 (sibling BarcodeCreateKind enum + onBarcodeCreateGate{Shown,Confirmed,Dismissed} method family). SecurityIntentKind methods take a PassType, which is PKPASS-only (no ScannableCard member); reusing them would have required either a PassType.ScannableCard arm (corrupting the trust model) or a fake PassType (corrupting telemetry). BarcodeCreateKind mirrors QrPayloadKind's non-PlainText arms 1:1 (PlainText short-circuits the gate, so no event ever fires for it). ComposableSurfaceLockTest's three-param lock bumped to four + a contains-UiTelemetryGuard assertion. Documented in COMPOSABLE_SIGNATURES.md.
close_reason: Shipped in #88 (squash-merged). Sibling BarcodeCreateKind enum + onBarcodeCreateGate{Shown,Confirmed,Dismissed} method family on UiTelemetryGuard; ComposableSurfaceLockTest bumped to 4 params + contains-UiTelemetryGuard assertion; PublicApiSurfaceTest, Noop-full-surface, and enum-arm coverage extended; COMPOSABLE_SIGNATURES.md updated.

title: passes-ui: expose FieldLinkScanner (or per-row composable) for flat back-field rendering
description:
Parent: wpass-hy2 (Passes R2 UX redesign kernel hooks).

## Consumer

walt-android wlt-b19 (PKPASS detail flat back-field rows) needs to render pass back-fields as flat rows on the orange gradient (no kernel `Surface` card), and the bead explicitly forbids hand-rolled regex: \"FieldLinkScanner is canonical.\"

`FieldLinkScanner` and `LinkSpan` are currently `internal` in `passes-ui`. The kernel epic wpass-hy2 lists the `PassBack` flat-row variant as a *non-goal* (\"Walt stops calling PassBack on its detail screen; kernel PassBack stays for other consumers\") - but Walt has no public API to call the scanner from. The non-goal entry is in tension with the wlt-b19 \"do not hand-roll regex\" constraint.

## Options

(a) Expose `FieldLinkScanner` and `LinkSpan` as `public` so Walt can call `FieldLinkScanner.scan(value, source)` directly and build its own `AnnotatedString` + `ClickableText` per row. Minimal surface bump; lets Walt reuse `SourceField` (already public).

(b) Add a public `PassBackField(field, organizationName, onUrlIntent, onPhoneIntent, onEmailIntent, modifier)` composable that renders one back-field row (label + value with link spans) WITHOUT the `Surface` card wrapper. Walt lays out N of these inside its flat container. Bigger surface bump but encapsulates the link-spans + ClickableText recipe so consumers don't reimplement it.

Default plan: (a) - smallest, cleanest. (b) only if multiple consumers will end up duplicating the buildAnnotatedFieldValue + ClickableText glue.

## Trust contract

Either option preserves the existing trust contract: the scanner's bidi-spoofing rejection, RFC 3986 URL class, phone digit-count + adjacency hints, email shape - all stay inside the kernel object. Consumers cannot construct a `LinkSpan` themselves with a different intent target; the only ingress is `scan()`.

## Cross-repo

- Consumer epic: wlt-byd (walt-android).
- Blocked bead: wlt-b19 (R2.4b - PKPASS detail flat back-field rows).
close_reason: Promoted FieldLinkScanner + LinkSpan to public in is.walt.passes.ui. Trust contract preserved (scan() remains the only LinkSpan ingress). PR #83.

title: Cross-repo: handoff spec for walt-android (wlt-*) consumer wiring of BarcodeCard
description:
## Why this issue exists

The user-facing entry point — the "+" → "Create a barcode card" flow with the form, format picker, color picker, and name field — lives in **walt-android**, not in passes-android. This bead produces the **handoff spec** the walt-android team needs to wire the consumer side up.

The actual implementation lands as `wlt-*` issues in walt-android's tracker. The 2026-05-17 auto-classifier blocked creating `wlt-*` issues from this repo's session, so this bead documents what needs to be filed so a future walt-android session can file them quickly.

Without this bead, the kernel work above sits unused because no consumer surface invokes it.

## Deliverable

A markdown spec document committed to this repo. Location: check `docs/handoffs/` or `docs/integration/` — use whatever pattern exists; if none exists, create `docs/handoffs/barcode-card-consumer-wiring.md`.

Content:

- **Kernel API summary.** The exact `passes-core` types the consumer calls:
  - `BarcodeCardCreateInput(payload, format, label, color)` → `BarcodeCardInputValidator.validate()` → `BarcodeCardCreateResult`
  - `BarcodeEncoder.encode(payload, format)` (called internally by the validation/persist pipeline; consumer rarely calls directly)
  - `QrPayloadClassifier.classify(payload)` for the QR preview path
- **Storage API.** `BarcodeCardRepository` interface — consumer wires the implementation into its DI graph.
- **UI surfaces.** Composables the consumer embeds:
  - `BarcodeCardTile` in the home lane
  - `BarcodeCardScreen` as the destination of tile taps
  - `BarcodeCreateConfirmSheet` as the gate at the end of the create flow
- **Create flow (sequence):**
  1. Consumer's "+" entry point
  2. Consumer's format picker (picks one of the 5 v1 formats)
  3. Consumer's payload input field (live-validated against `BarcodeFormatConstraints`)
  4. Consumer's label input field (live-validated)
  5. Consumer's color picker
  6. On submit: consumer calls `BarcodeCardInputValidator.validate(input)`
  7. If result is `InvalidPayload` / `InvalidLabel`: show inline error, return to form
  8. If format is QR: consumer calls `QrPayloadClassifier.classify(payload)`. If not `PlainText`: show `BarcodeCreateConfirmSheet`, await confirm/cancel
  9. On confirm (or non-QR): construct `BarcodeCard`, call `BarcodeCardRepository.insert`
  10. Navigate user back to home with new card in the "Your barcodes" lane
- **Lane placement guidance:** default to a separate "Your barcodes" lane below verified passes. Document the rationale (trust UX distinction).
- **Camera path explicitly EXCLUDED for v1.** Note this prominently. Camera capture is a follow-on feature, not v1 scope.
- **wlt-* issues to file.** A numbered list of proposed `wlt-*` issues with titles and one-paragraph descriptions each, so a future walt-android session can refile them in 5 minutes. Suggested minimum:
  - `wlt-*` "BarcodeCard create flow UI (form, picker, color, name)"
  - `wlt-*` "BarcodeCard home-lane integration (`BarcodeCardTile` placement)"
  - `wlt-*` "BarcodeCard DI wiring (`BarcodeCardRepository` implementation injection)"
  - `wlt-*` "BarcodeCard edit/delete UX (overflow menu, confirm sheet)"
  - `wlt-*` "BarcodeCard screen brightness max-while-visible"

## Acceptance lives in the spec doc

This bead is closed when the markdown spec is merged and a `bd remember` is written pointing to it so future walt-android sessions surface it via `bd memories barcode-card`.

2. Kernel API reference (with `file_path:line_number` cites for each public type)

title: passes-ui: BarcodeCardTile + 'Created by you' trust caption distinct from verified-pass treatment
description:
## Why this issue exists

The home-screen tile and the surrounding chrome for a `BarcodeCard`. This is the **most visually load-bearing piece** per the 2026-05-17 security analysis: if a BarcodeCard tile looks identical to a verified-PKPASS tile, Walt's trust UX is undermined for ALL passes (not just generator-cards). The "trust signal" of the verified badge stops standing out, and the next phishing PKPASS gets scrutinized less.

This bead implements the load-bearing "distinct artifact class in the UI" pre-ship requirement.

## Deliverable

In `passes-ui`:

- `BarcodeCardTile(card: BarcodeCard, onClick: () -> Unit)` @Composable for the home lane
- `BarcodeCardScreen(card: BarcodeCard)` — full-screen scannable view wrapping `BarcodeCardView` (Child 7) plus chrome (label, format hint, trust caption)
- **Explicit trust caption: "Created by you"** (final wording is a product decision — see Notes)
- **Visual distinction from verified passes via at least TWO of:**
  - Different border treatment (e.g., dashed vs solid)
  - Different icon (e.g., pencil/hand-edit glyph instead of issuer logo)
  - Different color band along one edge
  - Different typography weight or family for the title
- Lane placement: per parent epic open question #4 — default to **separate "Your barcodes" lane** below verified passes, unless overridden
- Theming via `PassesTheme` / `PassesSemantics`
- Preview screenshots showing **side-by-side** with a verified-pass tile to make the distinction visible at review time

## Critical constraint

The "Created by you" caption must:
- Remain visible at every tile size (don't truncate)
- Use a typographic weight that survives glance-level viewing
- Use a color that meets WCAG AA contrast against the tile background

If the user can hide / dismiss / disable the caption via any UI affordance, this bead is incomplete.

## Behavior

- Tapping the tile navigates to `BarcodeCardScreen` (full-screen scannable view)
- Long-press / overflow menu items (delete, rename) are CONSUMER responsibility — out of scope
design:
## Module + file location

- Module: `passes-ui`
- Package: same as Child 7
- Files: `BarcodeCardTile.kt`, `BarcodeCardScreen.kt`

## Trust caption styling

Add a new semantic role to `PassesSemantics`:

```kotlin
@Immutable
data class PassesSemantics(
    // existing roles...
    val unverifiedArtifactCaption: TextStyle,
    val unverifiedArtifactAccent: Color, // for border/band
)
```

Default values are placeholders; walt-android fills them with real brand tokens (per CLAUDE.local.md: "walt-android is authoritative for fonts/colors/tokens"). Document the contract clearly in the KDoc so the consumer knows it must supply both.

## Visual distinction

Recommended combination for v1:
- **Border:** a thin dashed border (1.5dp, 6dp-2dp dash) instead of the solid border verified passes use
- **Icon:** small hand-edit glyph in the corner where verified passes show the signature checkmark
- **Caption:** "Created by you" in `unverifiedArtifactCaption` style, always visible at the bottom of the tile

Picking 2-of-3 satisfies the "≥2 distinguishing elements" rule; picking 3 is better.

## Side-by-side preview

```kotlin
@Preview(showBackground = true)
@Composable
fun TilePreview_BarcodeVsVerified() {
    Row { /* verified pass tile + barcode card tile */ }
}
```

Commit this preview screenshot to the repo (or via screenshot test) so reviewers can eyeball the distinction.

## Tap behavior

Tile `onClick` is a callback. The CONSUMER decides what it does (probably navigate to `BarcodeCardScreen`). The recommendation is straight-to-scannable (no detail screen first) but that's a consumer decision documented in Child 10's handoff spec.

## Tests

- Snapshot of tile alongside verified-pass tile (visual diff)
- Snapshot of `BarcodeCardScreen` showing full-screen barcode + trust caption
- Verify `unverifiedArtifactCaption` text is present in the rendered tree at all tile sizes
acceptance_criteria: Tile + screen composables; side-by-side preview with verified-pass tile shows clear distinction at glance; reviewed by product before merging; caption visible at all tile sizes; :passes-ui:check green.
notes:
Open questions:
1. Exact trust-caption wording: 'Created by you' (recommended) / 'Unverified' / 'Self-issued' / 'Walt-generated'. Product decision.
2. Lane placement: separate 'Your barcodes' lane below verified passes (recommended) vs same lane vs mixed sorted by recency. Product decision.
3. Trust-caption icon: hand-edit glyph (recommended), pencil, person? Material Symbols has options.
4. Tap behavior: straight-to-scannable (recommended) vs detail-screen-first?
5. New PassesSemantics roles needed: 'unverifiedArtifactCaption' (TextStyle) and 'unverifiedArtifactAccent' (Color). Name TBD.
6. WCAG AA contrast for caption vs tile background: must verify with chosen color tokens.
close_reason: ScannableCardTile + ScannableCardScreen + non-suppressible ScannableCardTrustCaption landed via PR #86. PassesSemantics extended with UnverifiedArtifactStyle (sibling to signatureBadge — never reused). Four redundant visual distinguishers (dashed border + leading band + 8dp corner radius + pencil-glyph caption) implement C1/C2. ComposableSurfaceLockTest grew shape locks (1/3/2 user-visible params, no overloads). :passes-ui:check + full repo check green.

title: passes-ui: BarcodeCardView — render barcode matrix to Compose Image
description:
## Why this issue exists

The actual on-screen barcode the cashier scans. Takes a `BarcodeMatrix` from Child 3's encoder and produces a Compose composable that draws the barcode bitmap at the maximum scannable size.

Without this bead, even with the data model, encoder, and storage in place, the user has no way to see the barcode.

## Deliverable

In `passes-ui`:

- `BarcodeCardView(card: BarcodeCard, modifier: Modifier = Modifier)` @Composable
- Matrix → Android `Bitmap` conversion (this is where the Android boundary is — `passes-ui` is allowed Android deps)
- Layout-aware sizing: use `BoxWithConstraints` to fill the available width; height computed from format's aspect ratio (1D barcodes are wide rectangles; QR is square)
- Fixed quiet-zone padding (4 modules per ZXing convention)
- Bars rendered black-on-white for max scanner contrast (NOT themed — see Design notes for rationale)
- Accessibility: `contentDescription` includes the format name (e.g., "QR code" or "Code 128 barcode"). Do NOT include the raw payload in the contentDescription (don't leak loyalty IDs via TalkBack to nearby listeners).
- `@Preview` per format showing a known-input render
- Screenshot tests (if the project uses Paparazzi or Roborazzi)

## Critical constraints

- **Bars stay black-on-white.** Scanner reliability requires it. The *frame* around the barcode (in Child 8's tile/screen wrapping) can be themed; the bars themselves cannot.
- **No "Created by you" caption here.** That's Child 8's responsibility (the tile/wrapping surface owns trust signaling). This composable just draws pixels.
- **No brightness manipulation.** That's a consumer responsibility (system-level concern, outside the trust surface). Document this in the KDoc.

## What this bead does NOT include

- Tile / lane integration (Child 8)
- Trust caption (Child 8)
- Click handling / navigation (consumer)
- Detail screen / metadata view (Child 8)
design:
## Module + file location

- Module: `passes-ui` (Android + Compose)
- Package: alongside existing pass rendering — propose `is.walt.passes.ui.barcode`
- File: `BarcodeCardView.kt`

## Rendering approach

Two options:

1. **Canvas-based rendering** — use `androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas` with `drawRect` per module. Pro: vector-clean, no allocation per frame. Con: 250×250 QR with `drawRect` per cell can be slow on first composition.

2. **Bitmap-based rendering** — build an `android.graphics.Bitmap` once from the matrix, wrap with `BitmapPainter` in an `Image`. Pro: efficient, single texture upload. Con: bitmap allocation; needs careful DPI handling.

**Recommended:** option 2 (Bitmap). Build the bitmap in a `remember(card.id, size)` block so it's stable across recompositions. Use `Bitmap.Config.ALPHA_8` if monochrome — smaller memory footprint.

```kotlin
@Composable
fun BarcodeCardView(card: BarcodeCard, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    val matrix = remember(card.payload, card.format) {
        BarcodeEncoder.encode(card.payload, card.format).getOrThrow()
    }
    val bitmap = remember(matrix) { matrix.toBitmap() }
    Image(
        bitmap = bitmap.asImageBitmap(),
        contentDescription = card.format.accessibilityLabel(),
        modifier = modifier.aspectRatio(matrix.aspectRatio),
        filterQuality = FilterQuality.None, // crisp pixel edges
    )
}
```

## DPI / scaling

Use `FilterQuality.None` (or `paint.isFilterBitmap = false`) so the bitmap renders with crisp module edges, not blurry interpolation. Scanners hate blurred barcodes.

## Theming

Inject `PassesTheme` / `PassesSemantics` for any chrome around the barcode (background color of the parent, padding tokens). Bars themselves are not theme-bound.

## Tests

- Snapshot test (Paparazzi/Roborazzi) per format with a fixed payload
- Light + dark mode renders (only the chrome should change)
- Verify `contentDescription` does NOT contain the raw payload
acceptance_criteria: Composable + per-format @Preview + snapshot tests (Paparazzi/Roborazzi if available); contentDescription does NOT leak raw payload; light + dark mode renders pass; :passes-ui:check green.
notes: Implementation landed on branch scannable-card-storage-ui; PR #85 bundles this with wpass-lzi.6. ScannableCardView renders a card via BarcodeEncoder into a 1-bit-per-module bitmap painted nearest-neighbor (FilterQuality.None) for scanner sharpness. Per-symbology min sizes mirror BarcodeView (240dp square for Qr; 320x96dp for the four 1D symbologies). Encoder failures render as a same-sized Spacer placeholder. Card chrome (background tint, 'Created by you' caption) stays off this surface; it belongs on the tile in wpass-lzi.8.
close_reason: Merged via PR #85 at commit 6539706

title: passes-storage: BarcodeCard schema + migration + CRUD + backup exclusion
description:
## Why this issue exists

Persist `BarcodeCard` instances under the same SQLCipher-with-Keystore-derived-key posture as existing passes. **New table** (NOT a column on the `passes` table — see parent epic's "distinct artifact class" pre-ship requirement #1).

Without this bead, the kernel can encode and render barcodes but nothing persists — every card would be lost on app close.

## Deliverable

In `passes-storage`:

- New table `barcode_cards` with columns matching the `BarcodeCard` data class from Child 2:
  - `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`
  - `payload TEXT NOT NULL`
  - `format TEXT NOT NULL`
  - `label TEXT NOT NULL`
  - `color_argb INTEGER NULL`
  - `created_at INTEGER NOT NULL` (epoch millis)
- Schema migration script (additive, no touch to `passes` table)
- `BarcodeCardRepository` interface (in `passes-storage`, or split contract to passes-core if existing pass repos follow that pattern — check):
  - `suspend fun insert(card: BarcodeCard)`
  - `suspend fun update(card: BarcodeCard)`
  - `suspend fun delete(id: BarcodeCardId)`
  - `suspend fun getById(id: BarcodeCardId): BarcodeCard?`
  - `fun observeAll(): StateFlow<List<BarcodeCard>>`
- **Backup exclusion:** confirm the new table is covered by the existing Android Auto Backup exclusion. The existing config should already exclude the encrypted DB file at the file level; this bead must verify and document.
- **Irreversible deletion:** deleting a `BarcodeCard` must follow the same secure-delete posture as deleting a `Pass`. Investigate the existing pass-delete flow (SQLCipher `VACUUM` + overwrite or similar) and apply it here.
- Tests:
  - Schema migration round-trip (open empty DB at prior version, migrate, insert/read)
  - CRUD round-trip for each operation
  - Observer fires on insert/update/delete
  - Deletion test that verifies the row is actually gone (not just soft-deleted)

## Critical constraints

- **Same SQLCipher key as passes.** DO NOT introduce a separate Keystore-derived key. Single key, single backup-exclusion config, single secure-delete posture.
- **Same DB file as passes.** Single DB → single key → single backup config.
- The new table is independent — no foreign keys to or from the `passes` table.
design:
## Module + file location

- Module: `passes-storage` (Android-only)
- Package: alongside existing pass storage — propose `is.walt.passes.storage.barcode`
- Files: `BarcodeCardRepository.kt`, `BarcodeCardDao.kt` (if using Room) or `BarcodeCardStore.kt` (if hand-rolled SQLite)

## Persistence library

Match what existing pass storage uses. Likely Room over SQLCipher. Check the existing pass storage:

```
find passes-storage -name "*.kt" | xargs grep -l "Database\|SQLCipher\|Room\|Dao"
```

If Room: add a new `@Entity`, `@Dao`, and bump the database version. Add a `Migration` from the prior version that creates the new table.

If hand-rolled: add a migration script in whatever format the existing code uses.

## Migration

Additive only. Old DBs missing the new table get an additive migration. No data backfill needed (no existing barcode cards).

Bump the database version constant by exactly 1.

## Backup exclusion

Check `app`-level `BackupAgent` config or `data_extraction_rules.xml` / `backup_rules.xml`. Per CLAUDE.md the encrypted DB is already excluded from Android Auto Backup at the file level — adding a table to that DB inherits the exclusion automatically. **Verify**, don't trust. Add a test if a config-validation test exists.

## Irreversible deletion

Per CLAUDE.md, passes-storage has "irreversible deletion logic." Find the existing pass-delete path:

```
grep -r "VACUUM\|secure.*delete\|overwrite" passes-storage --include="*.kt"
```

Apply the same posture to `BarcodeCardRepository.delete`. If the existing logic operates on the whole DB after any delete, no new code is needed — but verify the new delete path actually triggers it.

## Threading

Suspend functions for CRUD. `StateFlow` for observation. Match the existing pass-repo conventions exactly.

## Tests

Use the existing in-memory SQLCipher test harness from `passes-storage` tests. One test per CRUD op, one for migration, one for backup exclusion (config check), one for irreversible deletion.
acceptance_criteria: New table + migration + repo; migration tested up + down; CRUD round-trip; observer fires on update; backup exclusion verified; secure-delete posture matches existing pass-delete; :passes-storage:check green.
notes: Implementation landed on branch scannable-card-storage-ui; PR #85 bundles this with wpass-lzi.7. Schema v3 adds scannable_cards table inside walt_passes.db (file-level Auto Backup exclusion already covers it). PassRepository gains createScannableCard / loadScannableCard / deleteScannableCard / observeScannableCards; validator rejections surface as typed StorageError.ScannableCardRejected. Telemetry adds onScannableCardCreated/Deleted/Rejected. Renamed BarcodeCard -> ScannableCard per wpass-lzi.1 decision. update() is NOT implemented (passes don't have update either; delete+create is the natural flow for an immutable user-typed artifact).

title: passes-core: input validation — length caps, charset rules, bidi/control-char rejection
description:
## Why this issue exists

Validate user-supplied payload and label strings before they enter the data model. This is the input-hygiene seam: every payload that reaches the encoder (Child 3) or the storage layer (Child 6) must have passed through here first.

Mirrors the input-hygiene posture in `FieldLinkScanner.kt:67` (bidi/format/control-char rejection) and extends it with format-aware charset and length checks.

Without this, a malicious payload could:
- Encode-fail at render time (poor UX)
- Inject bidi override characters that visually misrepresent the label
- Exceed scanner-realistic limits and silently truncate

## Deliverable

- `BarcodeCardInputValidator` (object or class) that takes a `BarcodeCardCreateInput` and returns either the validated input or a `BarcodeCardCreateResult.InvalidPayload(reason)` / `InvalidLabel(reason)`.
- Sealed sub-families:
  - `PayloadRejection`: `TooLong(actual: Int, max: Int)`, `WrongCharset(format: BarcodeFormat, offendingChar: Char)`, `ContainsControlChar`, `Empty`
  - `LabelRejection`: `TooLong(actual: Int, max: Int)`, `ContainsBidiChar`, `ContainsControlChar`, `Empty`
- Per-format charset rules (codified as one table in one place):
  - `Code128` — ASCII subsets A/B/C (0x00–0x7F minus some controls)
  - `Code39` — `[A-Z0-9 \-.\$/+%]`
  - `Ean13` — exactly 13 digits, last digit must match the check-digit algorithm
  - `UpcA` — exactly 12 digits, check-digit valid
  - `Qr` — full UTF-8 allowed, bidi/control chars still rejected
- Per-format length caps (recommend: Code128 80, Code39 80, Ean13 13, UpcA 12, Qr 2000)
- Label validation: reject Unicode `Cf` (Format) and `Cc` (Control) chars; allow regular Unicode text including emoji (the label is human-readable)
- Trim leading/trailing whitespace on payloads before validating
- Unit tests per format covering: valid input, too long, wrong charset, embedded bidi marker, embedded null byte, leading/trailing whitespace

## Defense-in-depth note

These validations don't replace the encoder's own checks (Child 3 still catches encoder-level failures). They catch malicious or malformed inputs *earlier* and with friendlier error messages.
design:
## Module + file location

- Module: `passes-core`
- Package: same as Children 2 and 3
- Files: `BarcodeCardInputValidator.kt`, `BarcodeFormatConstraints.kt`

## Bidi/control detection

Reuse the helper from `FieldLinkScanner` if exposed; otherwise port it. The check is:

```kotlin
fun Char.isBidiOrControl(): Boolean {
    val type = Character.getType(this).toByte()
    return type == Character.FORMAT || type == Character.CONTROL
}
```

(Note: `Character.FORMAT` covers RTL/LTR override chars. `Character.CONTROL` covers C0/C1 control codes.)

## Check-digit algorithms

EAN-13 and UPC-A both use modulo-10 weighted check digits. Recommend either:
1. Validate at this layer (reject if user-supplied check digit is wrong), OR
2. Auto-compute and append if user supplies only the data portion

**Recommended:** option 1. Users typing from the back of a physical card will include the full number including check digit. Auto-computing risks producing a card that disagrees with the cashier's stored ID.

## Charset implementation

Define `BarcodeFormatConstraints` as a single source of truth:

```kotlin
internal object BarcodeFormatConstraints {
    fun maxPayloadLength(format: BarcodeFormat): Int = when (format) { ... }
    fun isAllowedChar(format: BarcodeFormat, char: Char): Boolean = when (format) { ... }
    fun validateStructural(format: BarcodeFormat, payload: String): PayloadRejection? = ...
}
```

Keeps all constraints in one file for the threat-model doc to reference.

## Tests

One test class per format. Property-based testing (kotest property) would be nice but not required — table-driven tests are fine.
acceptance_criteria: Per-format unit tests covering valid, too-long, wrong-charset, bidi-marker, control-char inputs; integration with BarcodeCardCreateResult sealed family; :passes-core:check green.

title: passes-core: ZXing-JVM encoder integration; produce barcode matrix from payload + format
description:
## Why this issue exists

Add the barcode encoding capability to `passes-core`. The data model from sibling Child 2 defines `BarcodeFormat`; this bead turns `(payload, format)` into a renderable matrix.

**Library choice: ZXing-JVM** (`com.google.zxing:core`, Apache 2.0). Mature, audited, pure JVM. NOT ML Kit (proprietary, Google-shipped, wrong fit for Walt's degoogled user base).

## Deliverable

- New dependency: `com.google.zxing:core:<pinned-version>` in `passes-core/build.gradle.kts`. Pin to a specific version; document the version in the threat-model doc per Child 1.
- `BarcodeMatrix` data class — opaque wrapper around the encoded bit matrix. Properties: `width: Int, height: Int, modules: BooleanArray` (or `Array<BooleanArray>` — decide based on memory/access patterns). Do NOT expose ZXing's `BitMatrix` type directly — consumers must not see ZXing in our public API.
- `BarcodeEncoder` (object or class) facade with:
  - `fun encode(payload: String, format: BarcodeFormat): Result<BarcodeMatrix>`
  - Per-format dispatch to the correct ZXing writer (`Code128Writer`, `EAN13Writer`, `UPCAWriter`, `Code39Writer`, `QRCodeWriter`)
  - Synchronous (encoder is fast — <50ms for any realistic input)
  - Catches ZXing exceptions and returns `Result.failure` with a descriptive message
- Integration with `BarcodeCardCreateResult.EncoderFailure` from Child 2
- Unit tests:
  - One round-trip test per format (encode → known matrix dimensions)
  - One failure test per format (input that ZXing rejects)
  - License-check test that asserts the ZXing dep is on the allowed-license list (if such a test exists in the repo)

## Critical constraint

`passes-core` must remain Android-free. ZXing's `core` artifact is pure JVM; explicitly NOT pulling in `zxing-android` or `zxing-android-embedded`. Verify by running `./gradlew :passes-core:dependencies` and confirming no `androidx.*` or `android.*` transitive deps.
design:
## Module + file location

- Module: `passes-core`
- Package: same as Child 2 (`is.walt.passes.barcode` or whatever Child 2 chose)
- Files: `BarcodeEncoder.kt`, `BarcodeMatrix.kt`

## Dependency

Add to `passes-core/build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation("com.google.zxing:core:<version>")
}
```

Check `gradle/libs.versions.toml` for the dep-pinning convention; add a `zxing` version key there if that's the pattern.

## ZXing API mapping

ZXing's `MultiFormatWriter` accepts any format, but per-format writers are simpler and avoid accidentally enabling formats outside the v1 roster. Use the format-specific writers and have `BarcodeEncoder` dispatch via `when (format)`.

ZXing produces a `BitMatrix`. Convert to `BarcodeMatrix`:

```kotlin
fun BitMatrix.toBarcodeMatrix(): BarcodeMatrix {
    val modules = BooleanArray(width * height)
    for (y in 0 until height) for (x in 0 until width) {
        modules[y * width + x] = this[x, y]
    }
    return BarcodeMatrix(width, height, modules)
}
```

(Flat array is more cache-friendly than nested arrays for the render path in Child 7. Decide.)

## Quiet zone

ZXing handles its own quiet zone for most formats. Don't add an extra one here; let the render layer (Child 7) decide on visual padding.

## Threading

Synchronous API. Callers (storage layer, UI create flow) wrap in their own dispatcher. Document this in the KDoc.

## License check

If the project has a license-allowlist test (e.g., `LicenseAuditTest`), add ZXing's Apache 2.0 to the allowed list. If no such test exists, file a follow-up bead (out of scope for this child).

title: passes-core: BarcodeCard data model + BarcodeFormat enum + sealed result family
description:
## Why this issue exists

Defines the `BarcodeCard` artifact class in `passes-core` (pure JVM, KMP-friendly). This is the type every other module reasons about for generator-cards. Per the parent epic's pre-ship requirement #1, `BarcodeCard` is a **SIBLING** of `Pass`, not a subtype — they share no parse pipeline, no signature posture, no UI lane.

This bead is the foundation: nothing else can move until the data types exist.

## Deliverable

In `passes-core` (new package — propose `is.walt.passes.barcode` or check existing conventions):

- `BarcodeCard` data class: `id: BarcodeCardId, payload: String, format: BarcodeFormat, label: String, color: ArgbColor?, createdAt: Instant`
- `BarcodeCardId` value class — type-safe ID wrapper (mirror `PassId` pattern if it exists)
- `BarcodeFormat` sealed interface or enum — v1 roster per parent epic open question #1; recommended set: `Code128`, `Ean13`, `UpcA`, `Code39`, `Qr`
- `BarcodeCardCreateInput` data class — the raw, pre-validation input the consumer passes in (`payload`, `format`, `label`, `color`)
- `BarcodeCardCreateResult` sealed interface:
  - `Success(card: BarcodeCard)`
  - `InvalidPayload(reason: PayloadRejection)` (sealed sub-family — defined here as the contract; populated by Child 4)
  - `InvalidLabel(reason: LabelRejection)` (sealed sub-family)
  - `UnsupportedFormat(format: BarcodeFormat)`
  - `EncoderFailure(reason: String)` (populated by Child 3)
- Unit tests covering: construction of each type, exhaustive `when` over the sealed result family, default values, equality semantics
- Update `PublicApiSurfaceTest` (or equivalent) to allow the new public types

## Critical constraint

**`BarcodeCard` does NOT extend, implement, or share an interface with `Pass`.** If a future caller wants "all displayable artifacts in Walt," they can build a `sealed interface DisplayableArtifact` at the consumer layer or a higher kernel layer — but this bead does NOT introduce such a unifying type, because doing so would re-create the trust-conflation risk the parent epic explicitly avoids.
design:
## Module + file location

- Module: `passes-core` (pure JVM, no Android deps)
- Package: new, propose `is.walt.passes.barcode` — check existing package naming in passes-core first
- Files: `BarcodeCard.kt`, `BarcodeFormat.kt`, `BarcodeCardCreateInput.kt`, `BarcodeCardCreateResult.kt`

## Patterns to mirror

- Sealed result family: `passes-core/src/main/kotlin/.../PassParser.kt:27` (`ParseResult` family). Same exhaustiveness, same no-throw posture, same documentation style.
- Value class for IDs: search passes-core for `value class` and `@JvmInline` to find the convention.

## Serialization

Use `kotlinx.serialization` annotations (`@Serializable`) on `BarcodeCard` so Child 6 (storage) can serialize without reflection. `BarcodeCardId` should be `@JvmInline value class` with custom serializer if storage stores raw String IDs.

## Time type

Use `kotlinx.datetime.Instant` for `createdAt` if passes-core already uses kotlinx-datetime. If passes-core sticks with `java.time.Instant`, use that — match the existing convention exactly. Check `bd show wpass-9vv.3` and the storage module for the answer.

## Color

`ArgbColor` already exists in `passes-ui-core` (per CLAUDE.md). passes-core CANNOT depend on passes-ui-core (would invert the dep direction). Two options:
1. Define `BarcodeCardColor` as a simple `Int` ARGB in passes-core; let `passes-ui-core` provide a conversion extension.
2. Promote `ArgbColor` into a new pure-JVM type and have passes-ui-core re-export.

**Recommended:** option 1. Smaller surface change, clearer module separation. Discuss before implementing if option 2 looks cleaner once you've read the code.

## Testing

- One test per result arm
- Construction tests for `BarcodeCardCreateInput` with edge values (empty string, max length, null color)
- Snapshot test of the public API (`PublicApiSurfaceTest`-style) so accidental API breakage is loud
acceptance_criteria: All new types exported; sealed result family covered exhaustively in tests; PublicApiSurfaceTest (or equivalent) updated; :passes-core:check green.
notes:
Open questions:
1. Final naming: BarcodeCard? GeneratorCard? UserCard? Decide before merge (parent epic open question #2).
2. Format roster for v1: recommend Code128 + EAN13 + UPCA + Code39 + QR. Confirm before merge.
3. Time type: kotlinx.datetime.Instant vs java.time.Instant — match existing passes-core convention.
4. Color: passes-core can't depend on passes-ui-core. Use Int ARGB in core (recommended) or promote ArgbColor to a pure-JVM type.
5. Should a unifying 'DisplayableArtifact' interface exist? NO — explicitly avoided to preserve trust UX distinction.
