title: Manual barcode-card generator: type a payload, get a scannable Walt artifact
description:
## Why this epic exists

Walt currently can only ingest vendor-issued, signed artifacts (PKPASS, PDF). Most plastic cards in real wallets — library cards, regional grocery loyalty, gym memberships, pharmacy points, dentist reward cards — are NOT PKPASS-issued. The card *is* a number; the barcode on the back is just a picture of that number. Users want Walt to display that picture so they can leave the plastic at home.

This epic adds a new artifact class — `BarcodeCard` — that lets a user type in a payload (number, alphanumeric, URL) and pick a barcode format, producing a Walt artifact that renders the barcode scannably on screen.

## Why now

- Addresses the single most upvoted GitHub feature request: walt-app/walt-passes-android#66 (5 reactions, top of the list).
- Converging cluster of issues #66, #74 (image upload), #77 (camera capture), #64 (vague "QR support") all share the same underlying user need: "I have a card, get it into Walt."
- Per the 2026-05-17 discovery session in this repo, this is the **highest-leverage import-side bet** — unlocks the ~10x long-tail of cards that have no PKPASS equivalent. Walt's current PKPASS/PDF surface is the small set; this is the large set.

## Decisive architectural posture

**`BarcodeCard` is a new artifact CLASS, not a `Pass`.** It has no signature because there is nothing to sign (the user typed the data). The kernel must preserve the invariant "every `Pass` you see has been cryptographically verified." `BarcodeCard` ships as a SIBLING type — separate data model, separate storage table, separate UI lane, separate trust caption.

This is the **load-bearing concern** from the 2026-05-17 security analysis: if generator-cards look identical to verified PKPASS cards, Walt's trust UX is undermined for ALL passes, not just the new ones.

## What's in scope

- `passes-core` (pure JVM): `BarcodeCard` data model, `BarcodeFormat` enum, sealed result family, ZXing-JVM encoder integration, payload + label validation, URI-scheme classifier for QR payloads
- `passes-storage`: new table + migration + CRUD + backup-exclusion + irreversible-deletion path
- `passes-ui`: `BarcodeCardView`, `BarcodeCardTile`, "Created by you" trust caption with visual distinction, create-time URI-scheme confirmation dialog
- Threat-model refresh covering the new artifact class
- Cross-repo handoff spec for the consumer-side UI (form, picker, lane integration) — actual implementation lands as `wlt-*` issues in walt-android's tracker

## What's explicitly OUT of scope for v1

- **Camera-based payload entry.** Deferred by product owner 2026-05-17. Manual typing only.
- Photo-as-pass / JPEG upload (GitHub #74, #77) — sibling feature, file separately.
- PDF QR extraction (GitHub #60, #67, both closed but recurring) — sibling feature, file separately.
- TOTP / HMAC-OATH secret generation — out of mission.
- App Links / Add-to-Walt vendor cooperation — long-term.

## Pre-ship requirements (non-negotiable, from 2026-05-17 security analysis)

1. **Distinct artifact class end-to-end** (data, storage, UI caption). NOT a `Pass`.
2. **URI-scheme preview at create time** for QR payloads.
3. **Threat model refresh** before v1 merges.

## Source documents

- GitHub issues: walt-app/walt-passes-android#66 (top, 5 reactions), #74, #77, #64
- Discovery session 2026-05-17 (in this repo's conversation transcript)
- Existing threat model: `wpass-9vv.1` (closed) — does NOT cover this artifact class
- Security pattern to mirror: `passes-ui/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/ui/SecuritySheets.kt:40` (`B3UrlConfirmSheet`)
- Sealed-result-family precedent: `passes-core/.../PassParser.kt:27`
- Input-hygiene precedent: `FieldLinkScanner.kt:67` (bidi/format/control char rejection)
design:
## Module distribution

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `passes-core` (JVM) | Data model, BarcodeFormat enum, sealed result types, ZXing encoder facade, input validation, QR URI-scheme classifier |
| `passes-storage` (Android) | New `barcode_cards` table, migration, CRUD, backup exclusion, irreversible deletion |
| `passes-ui` (Android Compose) | `BarcodeCardView` (matrix → bitmap), `BarcodeCardTile` (home lane), "Created by you" trust caption, create-time URI-scheme confirmation dialog |
| walt-android (consumer, closed source) | Entry form UI, format picker, color picker, name field, lane integration, persistence wiring — filed as `wlt-*` issues |

## Encoder choice

**ZXing-JVM** (`com.google.zxing:core`, Apache 2.0). Pure JVM, no Android deps, mature, audited.

NOT ML Kit — proprietary, Google-shipped, wrong fit for the degoogled user base that drives Walt's North Star.

## Trust UX distinction (load-bearing)

`BarcodeCardTile` must be visually distinct from a verified PKPASS tile by at least two means: a different border treatment, a different icon, a different color band, or a different typography weight. Pick two for redundancy. The "Created by you" caption must remain visible at every tile size and never truncate.

## Recommended dependency order (child-to-child)

```
ThreatModel (P1, no code deps but informs everything)
    ↓ informs
DataModel ─→ Encoder ─→ UIRender ─→ UITile ─→ ConsumerSpec
         ├→ Validation ─→ ConsumerSpec
         ├→ URIClassifier ─→ URIDialog ─→ ConsumerSpec
         └→ Storage ─→ UITile
```

Hard blocking edges (encoded as bd `blocks` dependencies):
- DataModel blocks: Encoder, Validation, URIClassifier, Storage, UIRender
- Encoder blocks: UIRender
- URIClassifier blocks: URIDialog
- Storage blocks: UITile
- UIRender blocks: UITile
- UITile, URIDialog block: ConsumerSpec

Soft order (work-order preference, not encoded as blockers):
- ThreatModel should happen first so downstream design choices have something to trace back to.

## Theming contract

Use existing `PassesTheme` / `PassesSemantics` (from `passes-ui-core` per CLAUDE.md). May need to add one new semantic role for `unverifiedArtifactCaption` — discuss in Child 8.

## Walt-android theming source of truth

Per `CLAUDE.local.md`, walt-android is authoritative for fonts/colors/tokens. The `passes-ui` work here exposes the *contract* (theme slots, semantic roles) — the consumer fills in the real values.
acceptance_criteria:
## Epic-level definition of done

- All 10 children closed.
- Pre-ship requirements satisfied: distinct artifact class end-to-end, URI-scheme preview at create time, threat model refreshed and merged.
- A user can create a barcode card via the walt-android consumer, see it in its own lane with a clear "Created by you" caption, and have it scanned by a cashier's scanner.
- A user attempting to create a QR card with a URI-shaped payload sees the create-time preview before persistence.
- `:passes-core:check`, `:passes-storage:check`, `:passes-ui:check` all green.
- New module surface tests updated (`PublicApiSurfaceTest` equivalents).
- Threat-model document committed; each child's mitigation traces back to a documented risk.
notes: Naming decision (2026-05-17): artifact class will be called ScannableCard / ScannableFormat (not BarcodeCard). Format-agnostic, covers both 1D barcodes and 2D codes (QR/Aztec/DM/PDF417). Trust caption: 'Created by you' (non-suppressible). Locked in via wpass-lzi.1 threat model PR #80. Children .2-.10 should rename references at claim time.
close_reason: All 11 children complete; epic deliverables met

title: Expose a public PDF thumbnail-render surface for consumer list rows
description:
Source: walt-android bead wlt-q6n.6 (PDF page-1 thumbnail rendering pipeline for the
redesigned passes list). The Walt consumer needs to render a page-0 thumbnail per PDF
row in a dense LazyColumn (~36dp tile, many rows visible). Today the kernel exposes
the binder primitives (`PdfRendererBinder`, `PdfRendererClient`, `PdfRendererService`)
plus the in-process consumer affordances `decodePage`, `renderOrDiscard`, and
`RenderedPageCache<V>`, but the latter three are `internal` to `passes-pdf-ui` and
only consumed by `DocumentView` / `FullScreenDocumentView`. A list-of-rows consumer
that wants thumbnails has two bad choices today:

1. Reimplement `decodePage` / SharedMemory cleanup / cache-eviction discipline
   feature-side. This duplicates the kernel-owned guarantees (correct ashmem
   close in all cancellation paths, access-ordered LRU with bitmap-recycle on
   eviction, the `renderOrDiscard` NonCancellable wrapper around
   `binder.transact`).
2. Use the existing `DocumentTile(thumbnail: ImageBitmap?, ...)` shape, but
   `DocumentTile`'s tile is wrong for the new dense row design (160 dp wide,
   4:3 aspect, persistent "Document" badge). The list-row tile is 36 dp
   square with row-scoped chrome owned by the consumer.

This bead is the kernel side of wlt-q6n.6's architecture-correction note:
> non-trust kernel utility surfaces (renderer, image-bounding) IS architecturally
> correct to extend when the use case warrants it. The kernel exists to own
> hard-to-get-right pieces so feature modules don't replicate them.

## Proposed surface

Option A (preferred) — Compose-level facade:

```kotlin
package `is`.walt.passes.pdf.ui

@Composable
public fun rememberPdfThumbnail(
    document: PdfDocument,
    pdfFile: ParcelFileDescriptor,
    renderer: PdfRendererBinder,
    targetSizePx: IntSize,
    page: Int = 0,
    cache: PdfThumbnailCache? = null,
): PdfThumbnailState

public sealed interface PdfThumbnailState {
    public data object Loading : PdfThumbnailState
    public data class Rendered(
        public val image: ImageBitmap,
        public val pageAspect: Float,
    ) : PdfThumbnailState
    public data class Failed(public val kind: DocumentRejectedKind) : PdfThumbnailState
}

public class PdfThumbnailCache(maxSize: Int)  // public wrapper over RenderedPageCache<Bitmap>
```

Lifecycle semantics (mirror `DocumentDetailScreen`'s `OpenDocument` discipline):
- `produceState`-style: emits `Loading` until the binder call completes.
- `awaitDispose` closes any held bitmap if not cached, or hands it to the cache
  for shared rows.
- `NonCancellable` wrap on `binder.transact` (same as `renderOrDiscard` today)
  so a scroll-induced dispose still cleans up the ashmem region.
- A single shared `PdfThumbnailCache` provided at list scope (via parameter
  or `CompositionLocal`) lets all visible rows share a cap.

Option B — Suspend-function facade (if Compose-typing the kernel surface is
unwelcome):

```kotlin
public suspend fun renderPdfThumbnail(
    pdfFile: ParcelFileDescriptor,
    renderer: PdfRendererBinder,
    page: Int,
    targetSizePx: IntSize,
): Result<DecodedPage>  // DecodedPage already exists; would become public
```

Option C — Minimal: make `RenderedPageCache<V>` and `decodePage` `public`.
Consumer reimplements the `produceState` glue and `renderOrDiscard`. Cheapest
to ship; weakest abstraction guarantee.

Preference is A. It hides the right things (binder transact, ashmem cleanup,
cache wiring) without forcing the consumer to learn the SharedMemory layout
or the LRU eviction contract. Internal `DocumentView` can migrate onto the
same surface in a follow-up.

## Trust-bearing properties this surface MUST preserve

- D3 (isolated process): renderer is still bound through `PdfRendererService`
  by the caller. The new facade does not open its own binder; it consumes one
  the caller already has.
- D4 (no extraction): facade body uses only `render(...)`; no
  `getText` / `getMetadata` / `getAnnotations` paths are added or wrapped.
  Update `PublicApiSurfaceTest` (or its `passes-pdf-ui` counterpart) to lock
  this.
- D7 (4 MP cap): the cap lives in `PdfRendererService`; the facade just passes
  `widthPx`/`heightPx` through. The service rejects oversize requests as
  today; the facade returns `Failed(RendererFailed)` in that case.
- D5 (no signature affordance): the facade emits an `ImageBitmap` only. It
  exposes no field that could be styled as a verification badge. Trust signals
  remain on `DocumentTrustCaption` / `DocumentView` chrome, untouched.
- Decompression-bomb defense (ADR 0005 D7 / D2): unchanged — `PdfRenderer` on
  the service side is the choke point.

## Non-goals

- No new render-quality knobs (DPI, color profile, etc).
- No multi-page sprite-sheet rendering. Each call renders one page.
- No prefetch policy in the facade itself; cache eviction is access-ordered
  LRU like today.

## Test additions

- `PdfThumbnailStateSurfaceTest` — surface lock by reflection on the sealed
  hierarchy (same pattern as `RenderedPageCacheTest` + the surface lock tests).
- A unit test that a dispose between `binder.transact` returning and
  `produceState` emitting `Rendered` still closes the SharedMemory.
- A unit test that a fresh `Rendered` against the same `(documentId, page)`
  evicts the previous bitmap from the cache and the eviction callback fires.

## Consumer (walt-android wlt-q6n.6) — what it would do after this lands

```kotlin
val cache = remember { PdfThumbnailCache(maxSize = 8) }
LazyColumn {
    items(documents) { doc ->
        val state = rememberPdfThumbnail(
            document = doc.toPdfDocument(),
            pdfFile = sharedPdfFileFor(doc.id),  // walt-side resource
            renderer = sharedRenderer,            // walt-side bound client
            targetSizePx = IntSize(108, 108),
            cache = cache,
        )
        DocIconTile(state)
    }
}
```

The shared `renderer` and per-PDF `pdfFile` lifetimes are still walt-side
concerns (already handled by `DocumentRenderer`/`OpenDocument` in walt-android).

## Acceptance

- New public surface compiles, passes surface-lock tests.
- `DocumentView` either migrates to the new surface or has a follow-up bead
  tracking the migration (don't bundle).
- Documentation in `docs/adr/0005-pdf-document-support.md` notes the
  consumer-facing facade in the D3/D4 section so the trust posture is explicit.
close_reason: rememberPdfThumbnail + PdfThumbnailState + PdfThumbnailCache shipped in passes-pdf-ui (PdfThumbnail.kt). DocumentView and FullScreenDocumentView migrated onto the new facade. PdfThumbnailSurfaceTest pins API shape (arm list, per-arm field shape, no extraction-shaped accessors). ADR 0005 D4 updated. Follow-up wpass-7v8 tracks the instrumented Compose tests called out in the bead's test plan (dispose-during-render + cache eviction).

title: ADR 0005 follow-on: zoom lives in full-screen surface only
description:
wpass-0nn amended ADR 0005 to declare zoom a feature. 2026-05-15 design pivot moves zoom from the inline DocumentView to a dedicated full-screen surface (wpass-jil); inline returns to fixed 1x. ADR 0005 needs a follow-on amendment recording:

1. Inline DocumentView: zoom is NOT a feature. Display is fixed 1x within the inline page area.
2. Full-screen detail surface: zoom (pinch + pan) IS a feature, gated behind a 'Tap for full screen' banner.
3. Trust caption (D5 non-suppressible) behavior in full-screen under zoom: pick one and document it -- (a) docks to a screen edge and stays visible regardless of pan/zoom, or (b) pans/zooms with the page but a duplicate docked indicator stays visible. Recommend (a) for simplicity and stronger non-suppressibility guarantee.
4. 4 MP per-bitmap cap (D7) holds in full-screen; sub-rect re-render path (wpass-f4b) is the mechanism that keeps the page sharp within the cap.
5. No new binder methods. Render transaction is extended in place per wpass-f4b.

Update PassesADR0005Test (or equivalent enforcement test) if the ADR text changes alter any assertions.
notes: Filed alongside wpass-jil and wpass-ny4. ADR text edit should land before or with the implementation beads.
close_reason: ADR 0005 follow-on addendum landed in PR #72 (wpass-5n1 branch).

title: passes-pdf-ui DocumentView: remove inline pinch-zoom and pan
description:
Revert/remove the inline pinch-zoom + pan gesture surface added in wpass-1wq. Per 2026-05-15 design decision, zoom lives only in the full-screen surface (wpass-jil); inline DocumentView returns to a fixed 1x display.

Scope:
- Remove transformable/graphicsLayer scale/translation gesture handling from DocumentView pages.
- Remove the gesture-priority gating that flipped between HorizontalPager swipe and pan based on zoom > 1 (since zoom is no longer possible inline, pager swipe is always primary).
- Preserve the gesture-surface code in a reusable form (file move or extracted composable) so wpass-jil can mount it on the full-screen surface without re-implementing.
- Update / delete any tests that asserted inline pinch behavior. Add a regression test confirming inline DocumentView does NOT respond to pinch gestures.

Trust contract:
- No change to D5 / D7 / D4 / D8.
- Trust caption (D5) behavior inline is unchanged.

Coordinate with wpass-jil: gesture code lifted out of DocumentView should land in passes-pdf-ui in a shape the full-screen surface can consume.
notes: Filed alongside wpass-jil as the second half of the design pivot away from inline zoom.
close_reason: Implementation landed in PR #73 (wpass-6ag branch). Inline pinch removed from DocumentView; gesture surface relocated to internal/ZoomableImage.kt.

title: passes-pdf-ui: full-screen PDF surface with tap-for-fullscreen banner
description:
Add a full-screen PDF detail surface inside passes-pdf-ui, entered from a 'Tap for full screen' banner docked at the bottom of the inline DocumentView. Full-screen is the ONLY surface where zoom is available; inline DocumentView is fixed 1x.

Banner:
- Lives inside passes-pdf-ui DocumentView (themed via DocumentSemantics / DocumentTheme; walt-android supplies the tokens).
- Docked at the bottom of the page area, above the trust caption.
- Label text exposed via DocumentSemantics so walt-android controls the wording.
- Tap → full-screen route/surface.

Full-screen surface:
- Hosts a single PdfDocument page (or a pager across pages in the same document; decide in design phase).
- Renders via PdfRendererBinder using the wpass-f4b sub-rect render path so the page stays sharp under pinch-to-zoom and pan within the ADR 0005 D7 4 MP per-bitmap cap.
- Pinch-zoom + pan gestures live here. Re-uses the gesture surface code that previously lived in inline DocumentView (see wpass-1wq), relocated by the inline-pinch removal bead.
- Trust caption (D5 non-suppressible 'user-provided document') stays visible somewhere on screen. ADR 0005 follow-on bead will pin down whether it docks or pans with the page.
- Close affordance (back gesture / X button) returns to the inline DocumentView.

Trust contract:
- 4 MP per-bitmap cap unchanged.
- No new binder methods (wpass-f4b extends the existing render() transaction).
- D5 trust caption remains non-suppressible in full-screen.
- D4 (no extraction surface) unchanged.
- D8 (no share-out) unchanged.

Tests:
- Compose test: banner appears below the page area in DocumentView.
- Compose test: tapping the banner navigates to the full-screen surface.
- Compose test: full-screen surface shows the trust caption.
- Compose test: pinch gesture in full-screen drives a zoom-aware re-render call (mock binder).
- Compose test: inline DocumentView has no pinch/pan gestures (regression for the inline-pinch removal).

Depends on wpass-f4b (sub-rect render path) and the inline-pinch removal bead.
notes: Design decided 2026-05-15 in design discussion with Cole. Replaces inline pinch-zoom approach. Full-screen-only zoom keeps the inline surface simple, gives clear 'now inspecting' affordance, and concentrates the zoom-aware re-render path in one place.
close_reason: Implementation landed in PR #73 (wpass-6ag branch). FullScreenDocumentView + Tap for full screen banner; pinch fires sub-rect render; trust caption docked.

title: ADR 0005 amendment: zoom is now a feature; trust caption behavior under zoom
description:
Record the zoom feature as an addendum to ADR 0005. Today ADR 0005 frames DocumentView as 'minimally featured' in its Consequences section; pinch-zoom + pan was an implied non-feature. Adding it requires an explicit decision and a recorded rationale, regardless of which renderer design (tiled vs viewport) wins.

The addendum must:

1. Acknowledge that pinch-zoom + pan was previously implied non-feature, and state the user-need that motivates the change: scanning a PDF-embedded barcode (PDF417/QR/EAN) at a venue or gate requires the rendered bitmap to be enlarged beyond fit. The original ADR's 'minimally featured' framing covered share/export/search/auto-expiration -- security-coupled surfaces -- not view-side affordances that don't widen the kernel's egress or extraction surface.

2. Pin the 4 MP per-bitmap cap (D7) as unchanged. Both candidate renderer designs (tiled, viewport re-render) fit inside the cap. Raising the cap is a SEPARATE security-policy change requiring its own addendum.

3. Make an explicit decision on the trust caption (D5 non-suppressible 'user-provided document. Walt has not verified the source.') behavior under zoom. Two options:

   (a) Caption stays docked above the pager (current Column-row layout). It does not pan with the page. At any zoom level, the caption is on screen.
   (b) Caption pans with the page. Caption may be scrolled off screen if user pans up.

   Recommended: (a). The non-suppressible contract reads naturally as 'always on screen' and option (b) makes it suppressible-by-pan in practice. Option (a) matches the existing Column layout (caption row + pager row) and needs no layout change. Record this in the addendum.

4. Note that no new binder transaction methods are added by either renderer design; the existing render() transaction's parameter shape is extended (sub-rect + dims). D4 (no extraction methods) is unchanged.

5. Cross-reference the renderer bead (wpass-f4b) and UI bead (wpass-1wq) as the implementation children.

title: passes-pdf renderer: zoom-aware re-render path within the 4 MP per-bitmap cap
description:
Add a zoom-aware render path to the isolated-process renderer so a zoomed page remains sharp enough to scan a barcode without raising the ADR 0005 D7 per-bitmap 4 MP cap.

Today PdfRendererBinder.render(pdf, page, widthPx, heightPx) rasterises the entire page into a widthPx x heightPx bitmap (clamped by the renderer to <= MAX_PIXELS = 4 MP). At UI zoom, the bitmap pixelates because the rasterised pixel grid does not get denser when scaled in graphicsLayer.

Two design directions to evaluate; pick one in the design phase of this bead, document the trade in the bead notes, then implement:

  (a) Tiled rendering. Split the page into fixed-size tiles (e.g. 512x512 px each, in document-space coordinates). Render only the tiles currently visible in the zoomed viewport at the current scale. Bounded RAM independent of zoom factor; matches how PdfRenderer is typically used at scale (passing PdfRenderer.Page.render() a 4-arg form with destClip and a transform matrix). Cost: more book-keeping in the UI layer (mosaic composition, tile-level cache, fade-in as tiles arrive). Each tile <= 4 MP, so the D7 cap holds tile-wise.

  (b) Viewport re-render. On zoom-gesture-end, re-render the currently-visible document-rect at viewport resolution into a single bitmap <= 4 MP. Single bitmap per zoom level. Cost: re-renders on every pinch-end (potentially a perceptible blur-then-sharp transition); doesn't help during the pinch itself. Simpler, fewer moving parts.

The simpler call: probably start with (b) for v1, with the binder API shaped so (a) is reachable without another binder break later.

Binder API change: render() needs to accept a sub-region of the page (in document/normalised coordinates) and a render dimension. Suggested shape: render(pdf, page, viewportInDocument: Rect, widthPx, heightPx) where viewportInDocument is the fraction of the page to rasterise (default: full page 0..1 x 0..1 = today's behaviour). PdfRenderer.Page.render accepts a destClip + transform matrix that maps source-page coordinates to dest-bitmap coordinates; the renderer composes this from viewportInDocument and the page's natural size. Existing call sites pass full-page rect and work unchanged.

Trust contract:
- The 4 MP per-bitmap cap stays. PdfRendererService.MAX_PIXELS is unchanged. doRender's dimsOk check stays. Tiled rendering caps PER TILE at 4 MP; viewport re-render caps the single bitmap at 4 MP.
- No new binder methods. The existing render() transaction is extended with a sub-rect parameter; PublicApiSurfaceTest still passes (probe + render are the only methods).
- No new extraction surface (D4 unchanged). The renderer still only emits ARGB_8888 pixel buffers and shared-memory fds.
- No share-out surface change (D8 unchanged).

Tests:
- Unit: render with default full-page rect produces today's bitmap (regression).
- Unit: render with a quarter-page rect at full viewport resolution produces a bitmap whose pixels correspond to that page sub-region (compared against a fixture).
- Unit: render rejects a sub-rect outside [0, 1] x [0, 1] (RendererFailed).
- Unit: render rejects when sub-rect-mapped output dimensions exceed MAX_PIXELS.
- Defense-in-depth: render watchdog still fires on the new path (zoomed re-render is not exempt from the 5 s budget).

If raising the 4 MP cap is ever proposed instead of fitting within it, that requires an ADR 0005 amendment -- do NOT do it as part of this bead.
notes:
Design + implementation pulled out of the wpass-1wq landing session into its own future session. Scope is non-trivial: extend PdfRendererBinder.render() with a sourceRect parameter (RenderSourceRect sealed interface), update the wire format (PdfRendererBinderProxy, PdfRendererClient, PdfRendererBinderRoundTripTest), update PdfRendererService to use PdfRenderer.Page.render with a Matrix transform for sub-rect rendering, update PublicApiSurfaceTest for the new render param count (now 6 incl. Continuation).

A new full-screen detail surface (wpass-jil) is the only place where pinch-zoom + pan are available, entered via a 'Tap for full screen' banner inside DocumentView. This bead's renderer work is unchanged in shape -- still the sub-rect + Matrix transform via PdfRenderer.Page.render -- but the CALL SITE is the full-screen surface, not the inline DocumentView. Viewport re-render (option b) remains the recommended starting point. Companion beads:
  - wpass-jil: full-screen surface + banner (call site)
  - wpass-ny4: remove inline pinch (reverts wpass-1wq's gesture surface from DocumentView; gesture code is relocated to the full-screen surface)
  - wpass-5n1: ADR 0005 follow-on documenting zoom-lives-in-full-screen and trust-caption-under-zoom behavior

title: passes-pdf-ui DocumentView: pinch-zoom + pan gesture surface
description:
Add pinch-to-zoom and pan to DocumentView's page slot, scoped to the current page. graphicsLayer scale + translation driven by Modifier.transformable (or detectTransformGestures), tracked in a per-page state holder so swiping pages resets to scale=1.

Constraints:
- Must coexist with HorizontalPager. Gesture priority: when scale <= 1, parent HorizontalPager owns horizontal drags (page swipe). When scale > 1, the page consumes drags (pan within the zoomed page) until the user reaches the pan extent in the swipe direction, then defer back to the pager. Double-tap to toggle between fit and 2x is a reasonable affordance.
- Min scale 1.0 (cannot zoom out below fit). Max scale picked so a typical PDF417/QR barcode is comfortably scannable at typical scanner distance (target ~3-4x is a starting point; tune empirically).
- Translation bounded so the page cannot be panned entirely off-screen. Standard clamp: maxOffset = (scaledSize - viewportSize) / 2, clamped to >= 0.
- Trust caption (DocumentTrustCaption) stays on screen at all times. Decision recorded in the ADR 0005 amendment child bead. Default expectation: caption stays docked above the pager and does not pan with the page -- it sits in its own row in the Column already.
- Resetting state on page change: when the pager swipes to a new page, that page's transform state resets to scale=1 (no stickiness across pages).

Interaction with renderer: the rasterised bitmap at fit resolution will pixelate when zoomed. Visual sharpness at the zoomed viewport is the renderer-side bead's responsibility (parent's child 2); this bead is about the gesture surface and is correct against the existing fit-resolution bitmap. Sharpness is a follow-up the moment the renderer bead lands.

Tests:
- Instrumented test: pinch gesture increases scale; pan drags translation; double-tap toggles fit/2x.
- Instrumented test: when scale > 1, horizontal drag stays within the zoomed page and does not advance the pager.
- Unit (or instrumented) test: page swipe resets zoom state for the new page.
- DocumentSurfaceLockTest / DocumentTrustSurfaceTest stay green -- trust caption remains visible at all zoom levels.
close_reason: Implemented pinch-zoom + pan + double-tap toggle in DocumentView. Per-page zoom state (resets on page change). Gesture priority: pinch always consumed locally; single-touch drag consumed only when scale > 1 (canPan = { scale > MIN_SCALE }), so single-touch swipe at fit still advances HorizontalPager. Translation clamped so page cannot pan off slot. Constants MIN_SCALE=1, MAX_SCALE=5, DOUBLE_TAP_SCALE=2.5. Instrumented tests added: pinchToZoomDoesNotAdvanceThePagerAndKeepsTheTrustCaptionVisible, doubleTapOnThePageDoesNotAdvanceThePager, singleTouchHorizontalDragAtFitScaleStillAdvancesThePager. Trust caption stays in Column row above pager -- structurally outside the zoom transform. Renderer-side sharpness at zoom is follow-up wpass-f4b; this surface is correct against existing fit-resolution bitmap.

title: Zoom-to-scan: full-screen PDF surface for barcode scanning
description:
Enable users to enlarge ticket barcodes (EAN/QR/PDF417) on PDF passes enough for a terminal scanner to read them. Today DocumentView is a HorizontalPager of fixed 360x480dp pages with ContentScale.Fit -- no zoom, no pan -- which makes PDF tickets close to unusable for the #1 import-a-PDF use case (scan-a-barcode at a venue or gate).

Approach (2026-05-15 design pivot): zoom lives in a dedicated full-screen detail surface in passes-pdf-ui, entered from a 'Tap for full screen' banner docked inside the inline DocumentView. Inline DocumentView stays at fixed 1x. Full-screen is the only place pinch-zoom and pan are available. Concentrating zoom in one surface keeps the inline view simple, gives a clear 'now inspecting' affordance, and keeps the zoom-aware re-render path in a single call site.

Trust contract preserved end-to-end:
- ADR 0005 D7 4 MP per-bitmap cap is unchanged. Sharpness under zoom comes from re-rendering a sub-rect of the page at viewport resolution within the cap, NOT from raising the cap.
- ADR 0005 D5 trust caption ('user-provided document') remains non-suppressible -- visible in both inline and full-screen surfaces.
- ADR 0005 D4 (no extraction surface) and D8 (no share-out) unchanged.
- No new binder methods. The existing render() transaction is extended in place to accept a sub-rect parameter.

Child beads:
  - wpass-f4b: passes-pdf renderer sub-rect render path (extends PdfRendererBinder.render with a RenderSourceRect param)
  - wpass-jil: passes-pdf-ui full-screen PDF surface + tap-for-fullscreen banner
  - wpass-ny4: remove inline pinch-zoom + pan from DocumentView (reverts the wpass-1wq gesture surface; gesture code relocates to the full-screen surface)
  - wpass-5n1: ADR 0005 follow-on documenting zoom-in-full-screen-only and trust-caption-under-zoom behavior
  - wpass-0nn (closed, superseded): original ADR 0005 amendment declaring inline zoom a feature -- now superseded by wpass-5n1
  - wpass-1wq (closed, to be reverted): inline pinch-zoom + pan gesture surface -- reverted/relocated by wpass-ny4

Cross-repo: consumer-side wiring tracked as walt-android wlt-o72.4. walt-android wlt-o72.3 already confirmed PDF bytes are persisted at full resolution (no re-encode, no downscale), so higher-resolution re-render is feasible from existing on-disk bytes -- no storage change needed.

Consumer integration note: walt-android feature/passes/detail/DocumentDetailScreen.kt embeds DocumentView inside a verticalScroll with aspectRatio(360/480). With the design pivot, the embedded DocumentView is fixed 1x, so the previous nested-scroll / zoom>1 gating concern goes away on the inline surface; the full-screen surface takes the whole screen and is outside that scroll.
notes: Title and description rewritten 2026-05-15 to reflect the full-screen-only zoom pivot. Original title was 'DocumentView: pinch-to-zoom + pan for PDF pages' -- accurate for the abandoned inline-pinch design, misleading after the pivot.

title: Restyle DocumentTrustCaption to a flat icon+text treatment; add captionIconTint semantics slot
description:
CONTEXT
walt-android (consumer) renders a PDF document detail screen (DocumentDetailScreen) that embeds the kernel DocumentView. The kernel's non-suppressible DocumentTrustCaption ("User-provided document. Walt has not verified the source.") renders inside DocumentView as a filled colour-block (captionBackground fill + padded Text). It reads as part of the PDF surface and clashes with walt-android's flat, borderless house style. To get a brand-consistent disclaimer, walt-android added its OWN themed banner ABOVE the PDF (wlt-o72.5, PR #197). Net result: the user sees the disclaimer TWICE on the document detail screen.

FIX: move the flat styling INTO the kernel DocumentTrustCaption so there is exactly ONE caption, themeable by the consumer. walt-android then deletes its duplicate banner (consumer-side, wlt-o72.5).

SCOPE (passes-pdf-ui only):
1. DocumentTrustCaption.kt - restyle body from a single filled Text into a flat Row of [info icon] + [caption text]. Keep .background(captionBackground) so a consumer wanting a fill still gets one; a flat consumer sets captionBackground transparent.
2. Hand-author a small 24dp info-outline ImageVector inside passes-pdf-ui. Do NOT add material-icons-extended - the kernel stays dependency-light. Icon tints the vector, so its path fill colour is irrelevant.
3. DocumentSemantics.kt - add captionIconTint: ArgbColor slot for the icon tint. Default it to captionForeground (Kotlin allows referencing an earlier ctor param as a default) so the addition is non-breaking.

INVARIANTS (do not regress):
- ADR 0005 D5: caption stays NON-SUPPRESSIBLE. Restyle ONLY - no new param to hide it, no overload, no theme flag that removes it. DocumentTrustCaption signature stays (modifier: Modifier = Modifier). No ADR amendment needed (restyle, not a suppressibility change) - but call it out in the PR description for reviewer confirmation.
- TRUST_CAPTION_TEXT literal UNCHANGED (wording is load-bearing per D5) and still in a single Text node.
- Caption still renders inside both DocumentView and DocumentsLane (composition unchanged).
- DocumentSurfaceLockTest: documentTrustCaptionHasExactlyOneUserVisibleParameter (still 1) and documentSurfacesHaveNoOverloads (still 1 method) stay green.
- DocumentTrustSurfaceTest: verbatim-text assertions stay green - the icon+text Row still exposes the verbatim text node.
- DocumentPublicApiSurfaceTest.passesPdfUiCompiledClassesContainNoForbiddenStrings - new icon vector adds no forbidden strings.

TESTS TO UPDATE:
- DocumentPublicApiSurfaceTest.documentSemanticsDataClassExposesAllEightSlots - DocumentSemantics now has 9 slots; rename + add a read of captionIconTint.
- DocumentTrustSurfaceTest - its DocumentSemantics(...) construction uses 8 named args; still compiles with the defaulted 9th, but set captionIconTint explicitly for clarity.

CONSUMER COORDINATION (walt-android, separate repo/PR - wlt-o72.5 / PR #197):
- walt-android deletes DocumentTrustBanner + DOCUMENT_TRUST_BANNER_TEXT from feature/passes DocumentDetailScreen.kt.
- buildWaltDocumentSemantics sets captionBackground = transparent and captionIconTint = WaltOrangeAccent.
- Composite build: walt-android's o72-detail branch must point -PwaltPassesPath at this kernel branch's worktree, or this kernel PR merges first.

OUT OF SCOPE: moving the document metadata panel into the kernel - separate bead.

PR #70: https://github.com/walt-app/walt-passes-android/pull/70 (branch wpass-b6h-flat-trust-caption).

2. PAGE OVERFLOW FIX: DocumentPage sized its page Box with fillMaxWidth().aspectRatio(3:4), ignoring the pager height. On walt-android o72-detail (DocumentView in a short slot) the page overflowed up over the caption. Fixed with fillMaxSize + ContentScale.Fit letterbox; removed unused TARGET_PAGE_ASPECT_RATIO; added DocumentViewInstrumentedTest regression (runs under connectedCheck).

3. CAPTION BACKGROUND PLACEMENT: DocumentView's Column painted laneBackground behind the whole surface, so the caption sat on white. laneBackground moved onto the HorizontalPager (behind the pager only); Column paints nothing, caption composes on the consumer's screen background.

4. REVIEW NITS (PR #70 review): collapsed the now-vestigial page Box (contentAlignment was inert once the Image went fillMaxSize); dropped unused Box/Alignment imports; tightened DocumentSemantics KDoc on the captionIconTint field-order coupling. Review point 3 (fixed render-request size vs fillMaxSize display) tracked as follow-up bead wpass-ats.

title: Add minified-build behavioral regression coverage for the BouncyCastle R8 keep rules
description: PR #59 (wpass-at6) ships BouncyCastle keep rules in passes-core's META-INF/proguard/passes-core.pro, but the only test (shippedProguardRulesCoverThePassesCoreR8Footguns) asserts the .pro file contains three literal strings — a 'did someone delete the rule' tripwire, nothing more. It cannot, as a JVM unit test, verify the rules are SUFFICIENT under R8. The actual contract ('BouncyCastleProvider registers SHA256withRSA and PKIX in a minified build') was validated once, on-device, by the walt-android team. Silent re-break risks: a bcprov version bump relocating classes out of jce.provider/jcajce.provider; an AGP/R8 version bump changing shrinking behavior; a passes-core change dropping a transitive reference into e.g. jcajce.spec/jcajce.io. Each would re-break release-build signature verification while :passes-core:check stays green — the same bug class wpass-at6 just fixed. Recommended: a minified instrumented test in the walt-android consumer (the only place that can run R8) that imports a known-good Apple-signed pkpass against a minified build and asserts signature_kind=AppleVerified. Note: the test must live in walt-android; this issue is filed in passes-core's tracker to keep it associated with the fix — relocate to walt-android's tracker (wlt-*) if preferred. Surfaced in code review of PR #59.

Existing androidTest files in feature/passes/ are WalletListTest and EmptyStateTest only. No wlt-* tracker item exists for this work. The existing shippedProguardRulesCoverThePassesCoreR8Footguns test in passes-core stays as the .pro-file tripwire. title: passes-pdf: PdfImporter facade (URI → header-sniff → bindService → probe → thumbnail)
description:
The last load-bearing gap in `wpass-i2r`. Every other kernel-side child of the
epic has closed (`wpass-jsb` model/config/telemetry, `wpass-5v9` renderer service,
`wpass-11u` client binder, `wpass-pti` storage v2, `wpass-7wn` DocumentView), but
no kernel-side class actually *runs the import sequence*. Today a consumer
(walt-android) would have to compose:

  ContentResolver.openInputStream(uri)
    -> memfd-backed ParcelFileDescriptor
    -> size check (vs PdfImportConfig.maxBytes)
    -> isPdfHeader(firstBytes)
    -> Context.bindService(PdfRendererService)
    -> PdfRendererClient.probe(pfd)         (encryption + page count)
    -> PdfRendererClient.render(pfd, page=0, w, h)  (smoke thumbnail)
    -> PassRepository.insertDocument(label, bytes, pageCount, thumbBytes)

itself, which is precisely the parallel-implementation that CLAUDE.md's
"DECISIVE CONSTRAINT" forbids: trust-claim-bearing logic must live in this repo,
not in walt-android.

ADR 0005 G.1 (`docs/adr/0005-pdf-document-support.md:237`) explicitly names a
"single import entry point in `passes-pdf`" as the host for the API-34 runtime
gate, and the addendum's test table requires a unit test asserting `SDK_INT < 34`
returns "Android 14 or newer required" without invoking the renderer service.
Neither the entry point nor that test exists yet. `passes-pdf-core`'s
`PublicApiSurfaceTest:8` flags this directly: "There is no renderer or import
implementation yet (those land in wpass-5v9 / wpass-pdf.renderer-service)" -
`wpass-5v9` shipped only the server side; the importer was never filed.

# Module placement

Lives in `passes-pdf` (Android), NOT `passes-pdf-core`. The orchestration needs
`Context.bindService` and `ContentResolver`, both of which are Android framework
surfaces that the `-core` module is structurally forbidden from depending on.
`passes-pdf-core` continues to own only the pure-Kotlin contract types
(`PdfImportResult`, `DocumentRejectedKind`, `PdfImportConfig`, `isPdfHeader`).

# Surface

```kotlin
public sealed interface PdfImportSource {
    public class ContentUri(public val uri: Uri, public val resolver: ContentResolver) : PdfImportSource
    public class FileDescriptor(public val pfd: ParcelFileDescriptor) : PdfImportSource
}

public interface PdfImporter {
    public suspend fun import(
        source: PdfImportSource,
        displayLabel: String,
        persist: suspend (label: String, pdfBytes: ByteArray, pageCount: Int, thumbnailBytes: ByteArray) -> Unit,
    ): PdfImportResult

    public companion object {
        public fun create(
            context: Context,
            config: PdfImportConfig = PdfImportConfig(),
        ): PdfImporter = DefaultPdfImporter(context, config)
    }
}
```

The `persist` lambda is intentionally a callback rather than a `PassRepository`
dependency. `passes-pdf` and `passes-storage` are independent peers per CLAUDE.md
module rules; the consumer wires `passes-storage::PassRepository::insertDocument`
into this slot from walt-android-side composition (Hilt module). The importer
itself stays storage-agnostic and remains testable without spinning up SQLCipher.

# Sequence the implementation MUST honor (load-bearing)

1. `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < 34` → return `Rejected(UnsupportedAndroidVersion)`
   immediately, without touching `source`. (New `DocumentRejectedKind` arm; see
   "Cross-module impact" below.)
2. Materialize `source` to a bounded byte buffer via the memfd funnel:
   `ContentResolver.openInputStream(uri).copyTo(memfd_create-backed PFD)`. No
   `java.io.File`, no `createTempFile`, no on-disk plaintext (ADR F.1).
3. Size check vs `config.maxBytes` *during* the copy, fail-fast with
   `Rejected(OversizedAtImport)` before reading more than `maxBytes + 1` bytes.
4. Read first 8 bytes off the memfd → `isPdfHeader(...)` → on false,
   `Rejected(NotAPdf)`. Renderer service is NOT bound yet at this point.
5. `Context.bindService(PdfRendererService)` with `BIND_AUTO_CREATE`, await the
   `ServiceConnection`, wrap the `IBinder` as `PdfRendererClient`.
6. `client.probe(pfd)` → on `Rejected(kind)` return as-is; on `Ok(pages)`
   continue. (`probe` itself folds Encrypted / TooManyPages / RendererFailed.)
7. `client.render(pfd, page=0, widthPx=THUMB_W, heightPx=THUMB_H)` → on
   `Rejected(kind)` return as-is; on `Ok` reconstruct an ARGB_8888 bitmap from
   SharedMemory and encode it as PNG bytes for the thumbnail BLOB.
8. Invoke `persist(label, bytes, pages, thumbBytes)`; on success construct
   `PdfDocument` and return `Imported(doc)`.
9. `unbindService` in a `finally` block, regardless of outcome.

Telemetry: emit `onImportStarted` at step 2, `onImportSucceeded` at step 8, or
`onImportFailed(kind, durationMillis)` at any rejection. Use the
`DocumentTelemetryGuard` already on `PdfImportConfig`. Durations measured with
`SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()` to survive wall-clock skew.

# Cross-module impact

New `DocumentRejectedKind.UnsupportedAndroidVersion` arm is required for the G.1
test. That is a wire-format change on the binder side (`RejectedKindWire`) - but
since the renderer service is never invoked for this arm, no actual transaction
ever carries it. Still: update `RejectedKindWire.encode/decode`,
`RejectedKindWireSurfaceTest`, `DocumentRejectedKindHasExactlyTheFiveListedArms`
in `passes-pdf-core`'s `PublicApiSurfaceTest` (becomes six), and the matching
parity expectations in `wpass-kej`.

# Tests

- Unit: `SDK_INT < 34` returns `Rejected(UnsupportedAndroidVersion)` without
  touching `source`. (Closes the open ADR 0005 G.1 test debt.)
- Unit: header sniff failure short-circuits before `bindService`. Pin with a
  test that injects a fake `ServiceConnection` and asserts `onServiceConnected`
  is never called.
- Unit: size cap fails fast after `maxBytes + 1` bytes, not after full drain.
- Unit: each `DocumentRejectedKind` arm round-trips end-to-end through `import`.
- Unit: `unbindService` always runs - parameterize over success, every rejection
  arm, and a thrown exception inside `persist`.
- Unit: `persist` is invoked exactly once on success, never on rejection.
- Unit: `PdfImporter` surface lock (mirrors `PassParser`'s) - no `getText`,
  `getMetadata`, `extract*` helpers ever land here. Reflect over the class.
- Instrumented: import a benign PDF end-to-end with a real `PdfRendererService`,
  assert `Imported` with correct `pageCount` and a non-empty thumbnail.
- Instrumented: malformed PDF that crashes PDFium produces `Rejected(RendererFailed)`
  and the next import succeeds (service rebind path).

# Out of scope

- Multi-page rendering at view time. The importer renders page 0 only, as a
  smoke test plus thumbnail. The viewer (`wpass-7wn` `DocumentView`) owns page
  N rendering at runtime.
- Sharing, deletion, re-import. Owned elsewhere.

# Unblocks

- The wlt-4pg cross-repo wiring in walt-android.
- Closing of `wpass-i2r`. With this in, every kernel-side trust claim under the
  PDF epic is in this repo.

# References

- ADR 0005 D3, D7, F.1, G.1
- `docs/adr/0005-pdf-document-support.md:103,237,262,310`
- `passes-pdf-core/src/test/kotlin/is/walt/passes/pdf/PublicApiSurfaceTest.kt:8`
- `passes-pdf/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/pdf/android/PdfRendererClient.kt:18`

title: Extract passes-pdf-ui (or passes-ui-core) to restore module independence
description:

1. Extract a passes-pdf-ui module that depends on both passes-pdf and a new passes-ui-core (carrying isolated() + theme tokens). DocumentView and friends move there. passes-ui no longer depends on passes-pdf.
2. Confine the dep to implementation by introducing a thin DocumentSurface interface in passes-ui that PdfRendererBinder satisfies. Less restructuring, but adds an indirection that may not pull its weight.

PR #38 explicitly asks reviewers to choose; this issue tracks the deferred work regardless of choice.

title: passes-pdf: PdfDocument model, import config, telemetry interface
description:
The pure-Kotlin model and contract surface for the new passes-pdf module. No Android framework deps in this layer; service-side bits are filed separately as wpass-pdf.renderer-service.

# Public types
- data class PdfDocument(
    val id: PdfDocumentId,
    val displayLabel: String,           // filename, or 'PDF, added <date>' fallback
    val byteCount: Long,
    val pageCount: Int,
    val importedAtEpochMs: Long,
    val provenance: Provenance = Provenance.UserProvided,
  )
- enum class Provenance { UserProvided }   // single arm by design; signals that PDFs are NEVER signature-verified
- data class PdfImportConfig(
    val maxBytes: Long = DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES,
    val maxPages: Int = DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES,
    val renderTimeoutMs: Long = DEFAULT_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS,
    val telemetryGuard: DocumentTelemetryGuard = DocumentTelemetryGuard.NoOp,
  ) { companion object {
    const val DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES = 25L * 1024 * 1024
    const val DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES = 10
    const val DEFAULT_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000L
  } }
- sealed interface PdfImportResult { data class Imported(val doc: PdfDocument) : PdfImportResult; data class Rejected(val kind: DocumentRejectedKind) : PdfImportResult }
- enum class DocumentRejectedKind { OversizedAtImport, NotAPdf, Encrypted, TooManyPages, RendererFailed }
- interface DocumentTelemetryGuard {
    fun onImportStarted()
    fun onImportSucceeded(event: DocumentImportSucceededEvent)
    fun onImportFailed(event: DocumentImportFailedEvent)
    object NoOp : DocumentTelemetryGuard { /* ... */ }
  }
- data class DocumentImportSucceededEvent(val byteCount: Long, val pageCount: Int, val durationMillis: Long)
- data class DocumentImportFailedEvent(val outcome: DocumentRejectedKind, val durationMillis: Long)

# Discipline (mirrored from passes-core/TelemetryGuard)
DocumentTelemetryGuard accepts ONLY enums, counts, durations. No String parameters. No filename in events. Same load-bearing rule as passes-core: future addition of String params is a security-policy change.

# Header sniff
Provide a pure-Kotlin function that takes the first 8 bytes and returns true iff they match the regex /^%PDF-([12])\\.\\d/. Tested with: minimum (%PDF-1.0), maximum (%PDF-2.0), padding/whitespace prefix (rejected), non-PDF formats (rejected).

# Tests (JVM)
- PublicApiSurfaceTest pinning: types listed above; DocumentRejectedKind has exactly the 5 listed arms; Provenance has exactly UserProvided; defaults match D7 of ADR 0005.
- DocumentTelemetryGuardSurfaceTest: reflection-asserts no method parameter is String/CharSequence/ByteArray/Map.
- PdfHeaderSnifferTest covering versions and malformed prefixes.

# Module placement
Lives in passes-pdf:src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/pdf/. The Android service code is a sibling package (is.walt.passes.pdf.android) per wpass-pdf.renderer-service.

# Dependencies
- Blocks: wpass-pdf.storage-schema, wpass-pdf.renderer-service, wpass-pdf.ui-integration
- Blocked by: wpass-0ri (threat model), wpass-i2r (epic)

Parent: wpass-i2r

title: passes-storage: schema v2 with documents + thumbnails tables
description:
Schema migration v1 -> v2 to persist PDF documents alongside passes in the existing walt_passes.db SQLCipher database. Same key, same backup-exclusion XML, same irreversible-delete semantics.

# Schema delta
New tables (added to Schema.DDL and to the v1->v2 migration):

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
    id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    display_label       TEXT    NOT NULL,
    pdf_bytes           BLOB    NOT NULL,
    byte_count          INTEGER NOT NULL,
    page_count          INTEGER NOT NULL,
    imported_at_epoch_ms INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_documents_imported_at ON documents(imported_at_epoch_ms);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS document_thumbnails (
    document_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    bytes       BLOB    NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (document_id)
);

- Schema.VERSION bumps from 1 to 2.
- Schema.MIGRATIONS gains entry: 1 -> [the three statements above].
- Forward-only migration per ADR 0002.

# Repository surface
Add to PassRepository (or a sibling DocumentRepository, deciders' choice):
- suspend fun insertDocument(label: String, pdfBytes: ByteArray, byteCount: Long, pageCount: Int, thumbnailBytes: ByteArray): StorageResult<Long>
- fun observeDocuments(): Flow<List<DocumentRow>>
- suspend fun loadDocumentBytes(id: Long): StorageResult<ByteArray>      // returns the PDF for rendering; bytes never decoded here
- suspend fun loadDocumentThumbnail(id: Long): StorageResult<ByteArray>
- suspend fun deleteDocument(id: Long): StorageResult<Unit>               // CASCADE drops thumbnail; mirrors pass deletion contract

Defense in depth: insertDocument re-checks byteCount <= 25 MB and pageCount <= 10. The renderer-service already enforces; storage refuses out-of-bounds rows so a future caller bug cannot land an oversized blob.

# Telemetry
Extend StorageTelemetryGuard with:
- fun onDocumentImported(event: DocumentImportedEvent)
- fun onDocumentRejected(kind: DocumentStorageRejectedKind)
- fun onDocumentDeleted(event: DocumentDeletedEvent)

Where:
- data class DocumentImportedEvent(val byteCount: Long, val pageCount: Int)
- enum class DocumentStorageRejectedKind { OversizedAtStorage, TooManyPagesAtStorage }
- data class DocumentDeletedEvent(val byteCount: Long)

Same PII discipline as PassImported events: no labels, no thumbnail bytes, no IDs that could re-link to user data.

# Backup exclusion
Verify (with a test) that existing walt_passes_backup_rules.xml automatically covers the new tables since they are inside the already-excluded database. No XML changes required.

# Tests
- SchemaRoundtripTest: open v1 DB, run migration, assert documents/document_thumbnails tables exist with expected columns, indexes, FK + CASCADE.
- DocumentRepositoryTest: insert -> observe -> delete cycle; verify CASCADE drops thumbnail row.
- DocumentRepositoryBoundsTest: insert at 25 MB exact passes; 25 MB + 1 byte rejected with OversizedAtStorage; 10 pages exact passes; 11 pages rejected.
- BackupRulesAssertionTest: existing test extends to assert documents and document_thumbnails are inside the excluded DB file.

# Dependencies
- Blocks: wpass-pdf.ui-integration
- Blocked by: wpass-pdf.core-model (DocumentTelemetryGuard event types reuse the discipline pattern), wpass-0ri (threat model)

title: passes-pdf: isolated-process renderer service
description:
The android:isolatedProcess="true" Service that performs all PDF parsing and rendering. Load-bearing security control per ADR 0005 D3: a PDFium use-after-free here brings down the service, not the wallet.

# Service shape
class PdfRendererService : Service() {
    // Declared in passes-pdf manifest:
    //   <service android:name=".android.PdfRendererService"
    //            android:isolatedProcess="true"
    //            android:exported="false" />
    override fun onBind(intent: Intent): IBinder = ...
}

Internal binder contract (not AIDL, since the binding is intra-app and AIDL adds reflection surface; use a sealed Messenger or a private Binder subclass):

interface PdfRendererBinder {
    suspend fun probe(pdf: ParcelFileDescriptor): ProbeResult
    suspend fun render(pdf: ParcelFileDescriptor, page: Int, widthPx: Int, heightPx: Int): RenderResult
}

sealed interface ProbeResult {
    data class Ok(val pageCount: Int) : ProbeResult
    data class Rejected(val kind: DocumentRejectedKind) : ProbeResult
}

sealed interface RenderResult {
    data class Ok(val bitmap: SharedMemory /* or AshmemBitmap */) : RenderResult
    data class Rejected(val kind: DocumentRejectedKind) : RenderResult
}

# Rules the implementation MUST honor
1. Service has no INTERNET permission (manifest-level). Cannot accidentally hit the network.
2. Service receives PDF only via ParcelFileDescriptor of a MemoryFile/SharedMemory; never reads a path. The fd is dup'd by binder; main process closes its copy.
3. Render targets a SharedMemory-backed Bitmap of bounded size; reject any width*height > 4 MP.
4. probe() opens via PdfRenderer; if it throws SecurityException (encrypted) or any IOException at open, return Rejected(Encrypted) or Rejected(NotAPdf) accordingly.
5. probe() then reads pageCount; return Rejected(TooManyPages) if > 10.
6. render() runs on a watchdog: if PdfRenderer.openPage(N).render(...) does not return within renderTimeoutMs (default 5_000), kill the process via Process.killProcess(Process.myPid()). Main process observes RemoteException -> RendererFailed.
7. No extraction methods. The binder MUST NOT expose: getText(), getMetadata(), getAnnotations(), getAttachments(), getFormFields(). PublicApiSurfaceTest enforces.

# Permission scrub
Manifest of passes-pdf module declares ZERO uses-permission. Inherits no app permissions in isolated mode by design. CI lint asserts.

# Tests
- Instrumented: feed a benign PDF, render page 0, assert Bitmap dimensions == requested.
- Instrumented: feed a JS-laden PDF (with /OpenAction /JavaScript), render, assert no observable side effect (file write probe, network probe via VPNService stub).
- Instrumented: feed a malformed PDF that crashes PDFium; assert main process survives and binder returns RemoteException; assert next bind succeeds.
- Instrumented: feed an encrypted PDF; assert ProbeResult.Rejected(Encrypted).
- Instrumented: feed an 11-page PDF; assert ProbeResult.Rejected(TooManyPages).
- Unit: render watchdog times out and triggers killProcess (mock the renderer call with a stalling Job).
- ApiSurfaceTest: reflection-assert PdfRendererBinder has exactly probe + render; no extraction methods.

# Dependencies
- Blocks: wpass-pdf.ui-integration
- Blocked by: wpass-pdf.core-model, wpass-6m9 (renderer validation), wpass-0ri (threat model)

Parent: wpass-i2r
notes:
Skeleton landed in PR #36 on branch passes-pdf-renderer-service. Module includes:
- Manifest with isolatedProcess + exported=false + zero uses-permission
- PdfRendererBinder contract (probe + render only)
- PdfRendererBinderProxy (hand-rolled Binder, no AIDL)
- PdfRendererService with PdfRenderer-backed probe/render
- RenderWatchdog with injectable ProcessKiller

title: passes-ui: DocumentView composable + Documents lane + trust caption
description:
UI surface for PDFs in passes-ui. Renders via the passes-pdf service, integrates as a separate lane below the passes list, and pins the unverified-source trust signal so the user cannot confuse a PDF with a signature-verified PKPASS.

# Composables to add
- DocumentTile(doc: PdfDocument, thumbnail: ImageBitmap, onClick: () -> Unit)
    Used in the Documents lane. Shows thumbnail, displayLabel, and a small "Document" badge in a visually distinct register from passes (different corner shape OR different chrome color from PassesSemantics).
- DocumentView(doc: PdfDocument, renderer: PdfRendererBinder)
    Full-screen presentation. Horizontal HorizontalPager across all pages 0..pageCount-1. Page bitmap rendered on demand via renderer.render(...) and held in an LRU bitmap cache keyed by (id, page). Cache size bounded to ~3 pages.
- DocumentTrustCaption()
    Persistent caption visible on DocumentView and as a sticky header on the Documents lane: "User-provided document. Walt has not verified the source." Visual register matches the existing "Self-signed" pill in PassesSemantics.signatureBadge.

# Documents lane in the list screen
Below the existing passes list (or carousel). Header "Documents". Empty state hidden if no documents. The lane is visually distinct from the passes list (separate background shade or separator) so the user reads them as different concepts.

# What is FORBIDDEN in this surface
Per ADR 0005 D8 (no share-out):
- No Intent.ACTION_SEND construction in passes-ui (or passes-pdf). PublicApiSurfaceTest enforces via classpath scan.
- No "Share" / "Export" menu item.
- No tap-to-open of any URL extracted from PDF metadata (we do not extract).

Per ADR 0005 D4 (no extraction): DocumentView does not display anything from the PDF other than the rasterized page bitmaps and the user-supplied/filename label.

# Trust-claim parity (per TRUST_CLAIMS.md shape)
DocumentTrustCaption is non-suppressible. No 'enabled' parameter, no theme token that hides it. A document cannot present without the caption. Mirrors the ExpiredOverlayState rule for passes.

# Tests
- ScreenshotTest: DocumentTile and DocumentView in light/dark; assert visual differentiation from PassFront.
- TrustClaimSurfaceTest extension: DocumentTrustCaption present; no overload of DocumentView accepts a flag to hide it.
- PublicApiSurfaceTest: passes-ui has no member that constructs Intent.ACTION_SEND with mimeType "application/pdf". (Reflection / Kotlin metadata scan over compiled classes.)
- Instrumented: bind to PdfRendererService with a fake binder; render multi-page document; assert pager position changes drive new render() calls; assert LRU eviction past 3 pages.
- Instrumented: verify DocumentTrustCaption text bytes are wrapped in U+2068/U+2069 (FSI/PDI) since displayLabel is user-controlled (filename) and could carry bidi tricks. Mirrors B3 sheet bidi isolation.

# Dependencies
- Blocks: walt-android wiring (filed cross-repo)
- Blocked by: wpass-pdf.core-model, wpass-pdf.storage-schema, wpass-pdf.renderer-service

title: Validate PdfRenderer + isolated-process renderer assumptions
description:
Empirically confirm the security-relevant behaviors the architecture relies on, BEFORE writing the renderer service. If any assumption fails, the architecture changes (or PDF support is descoped). Cheaper to learn now than mid-implementation.

# Assumptions to verify
A. PdfRenderer does not execute JavaScript.
   Test: hand it a PDF with /JavaScript / /JS actions on /OpenAction. Confirm no execution evidence (no console output, no process-side effects, no network attempt observable via VpnService probe).

B. PdfRenderer does not process Launch / URI / SubmitForm actions during render.
   Test: PDF with /URI annotation, /Launch action on page open. Confirm no Intent fired, no network observed.

C. PdfRenderer does not make network requests during render.
   Test: PDF with external xref (e.g., RemoteGoTo). Mock VPN / observe with adb netstat. Confirm zero outbound from the renderer process.

D. PdfRenderer surfaces encrypted PDFs as a SecurityException (or equivalent flag) without prompting.
   Test: password-protected PDF. Confirm rejection at openPage path with no UI surface raised by the framework itself.

E. PdfRenderer can run inside an android:isolatedProcess="true" Service.
   Test: declare the service, bindService from main, render a benign PDF, return Bitmap over shared memory. Confirm:
   - Service has no /data/data access
   - Service cannot perform DNS lookup
   - Service cannot read SharedPreferences from main process
   - Service crash does NOT crash the main process
   - main process gets onServiceDisconnected and can rebind
   Test forced crash by feeding a deliberately malformed PDF; confirm RemoteException -> "could not render" UI, main process alive.

F. ParcelFileDescriptor + MemoryFile path delivers PDF bytes to the renderer without writing to disk.
   Test: use Linux memfd_create via MemoryFile; verify file descriptor passed across binder; confirm /proc/<service-pid>/maps shows no on-disk path for the PDF bytes.

G. CVE update path on Android 13+: confirm PDFium ships in the MediaProvider Mainline module (com.google.android.providers.media.module) on Pixel and at least one OEM, and that updates flow without OS update.
   Test: pm path com.google.android.providers.media.module; check com.android.media.providers package update history.

# minSdk / Android version matrix
- minSdk 26 (Oreo) PdfRenderer is API 21+ so available, but updates ship via Mainline only on API 30+. Document the exposure window.
- Determine: does Walt set minSdk lower than 30 for PDF support? Possibly raise minSdk for PDF feature only (feature-gated by Build.VERSION_SDK_INT) so users on older Android cannot import PDFs at all (acceptable v1 trade).

# Deliverable
- A research write-up under docs/research/pdf-renderer-validation.md with results per assumption A-G.
- Decision recorded in the doc: any failed assumption -> architectural fallback or descope.
- A small instrumented sample app under research/ if needed; deleted before merge to main.

# Acceptance
- Each of A-G has a recorded yes/no with reproduction steps.
- If any "no", the parent epic wpass-i2r is updated with the implication.

# Dependencies
- Blocks: wpass-pdf.renderer-service
- Blocked by: nothing

Parent: wpass-i2r
notes:
Source-level validation done in docs/research/pdf-renderer-validation.md. Two architectural implications recorded against wpass-i2r:

  F (FD transport): MemoryFile + ParcelFileDescriptor as stated does NOT meet PdfRenderer's seek requirement and forces a choice between (F.1) memfd_create via NDK syscall, no on-disk plaintext, or (F.2) plaintext temp file with documented at-rest exception. Decision: adopt F.1.
  G (Mainline CVE channel): PDFium ships in MediaProvider apex on API 34+, NOT API 33+ as the bead text said. Decision: gate PDF feature on Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 34 (G.1). Walt overall minSdk unchanged; older devices see Android-14-required gate.

  Both decisions require an ADR 0005 addendum before wpass-5v9 starts. A-E confirmed at source level (provisional yes); empirical device-matrix runs are a release-gate, owned by the maintainer with physical Pixel and OEM devices. Empirical rows in the doc are PENDING.

  Sample app NOT scaffolded; probe code is embedded as code blocks in the document, to be pasted into a throwaway research/pdf-probe Gradle module on a device-test branch by whoever runs the matrix.

title: PDF threat model + control inventory
description:
Freeze the PDF-import threat model and the three load-bearing controls in a doc reviewable alongside passes-ui/TRUST_CLAIMS.md, before any implementation lands.

# Deliverable
docs/PDF_THREAT_MODEL.md (or similar; single source of truth for the security posture).

# Required sections
1. Format-level threats (enumerate each, mark in-scope vs accepted-risk):
   - Embedded JavaScript
   - Launch/SubmitForm/URI/GoToR actions
   - AcroForm + XFA active content
   - Embedded file attachments
   - PDF digital signatures (explicitly NOT verified; rationale)
   - Network fetches at render time
   - JBIG2/JPEG2000/CCITT decoder-bug history
   - Object-graph attacks (deep nesting, malformed xref, oversized streams)
   - Encrypted PDFs (policy: reject at import, pending Q3)
   - Render bombs (huge bitmaps, recursive page trees)
2. Three controls and how each maps to threat coverage:
   - System renderer (PdfRenderer/PDFium via MediaProvider Mainline) -> kills JS, actions, network, XFA-form-submit at render time
   - Isolated process (android:isolatedProcess) -> contains decoder CVEs (UAF/OOB) within a service that has no DB/Keystore/network/data access
   - No-extraction discipline -> collapses Launch/URI/SubmitForm/XFA/JS/embedded-files surface
3. Per-control inventory mapped to PKPASS analogues (table mirroring TRUST_CLAIMS.md)
4. Explicit non-features (no signature verification; no text/metadata/annotation extraction; no URL surfaced; no metadata-driven labels; no renderer DB/Keystore/network/file access).

# Acceptance
- Reviewer can read PDF_THREAT_MODEL.md + the eventual ADR 0005 and identify, for each enumerated threat, the specific control that mitigates it OR the explicit accepted-risk rationale.
- No threat is left without either a control reference or an accepted-risk paragraph.
- Document is referenced from README "Scope" section and from ADR 0005.

# Dependencies
- Blocks: wpass-pdf.renderer-service, wpass-pdf.core-model, wpass-pdf.storage-schema, wpass-pdf.ui-integration
- Blocked by: nothing (this is the first deliverable)

# Trust-claim positioning
This document is what answers "show me, at a glance, why PDF import does not weaken Walt's local-only / no-PII / signature-honest posture." It is the analog of passes-ui/TRUST_CLAIMS.md for the PDF surface.

title: PDF document support (security-first import + render)
description:
Add PDF import to Walt as a sibling concept to PKPASS passes (pending Q1 confirmation), with security parity to the existing PKPASS pipeline.

# Threat model
PDFs permit embedded JavaScript, Launch/SubmitForm/URI/GoToR actions, AcroForm and XFA active content, embedded file attachments, attached digital signatures, network fetches at render time, decoder-CVE-heavy subformats (JBIG2, JPEG2000, CCITT), object-graph attacks (nested objects, malformed xref, oversized streams), encrypted documents, and render bombs (huge bitmaps, recursive page trees). Posture: every imported PDF is treated as hostile.

# Three load-bearing controls
1. System renderer only. android.graphics.pdf.PdfRenderer (PDFium, shipped via MediaProvider Mainline on Android 13+, picks up CVE fixes via Play System Updates). Narrow API: ParcelFileDescriptor in, Bitmap out. Does not execute JavaScript, does not process Launch/SubmitForm/URI actions at render, does not make network requests.
2. Isolated-process service. android:isolatedProcess="true" Service whose sole job is rendering. No app-data access, no inherited network, OS-level crash containment. A PDFium UAF brings down the service, not the wallet. Without this, the parser shares address space with SQLCipher keys and decoded passes; with it, blast radius is "user re-taps to view."
3. No extraction. Opaque-blob storage. No text/metadata/annotation/link extraction. No URL surfaced. No PDF-metadata-driven labels. Collapses the Launch/URI/SubmitForm/XFA/JS/embedded-files surface because Walt never invokes those codepaths.

# Module layout
- passes-pdf (NEW, Android): hosts the isolated-process renderer service, Binder contract, PdfDocument model, import-time validation. Self-contained for audit. No dep on passes-core or passes-storage.
- passes-core: no changes (sibling model).
- passes-storage: schema v1->v2 adds documents + document_thumbnails tables. Same SQLCipher key, same backup-exclusion XML, same irreversible-delete contract. New StorageTelemetryGuard events DocumentImported/DocumentRejected(kind)/DocumentDeleted.
- passes-ui: DocumentView composable bound to passes-pdf service; "Documents" list lane.
- walt-android side: registers application/pdf intent filter and in-app file picker MIME extension.

# Validation pipeline at import
1. Size check (main process) -> reject OversizedAtImport
2. Header sniff %PDF- 1.0..2.0 (main) -> reject NotAPdf
3. Encryption probe (isolated) -> reject Encrypted
4. Page-count sanity, ceiling 64 (isolated) -> reject TooManyPages
5. Smoke render page 0 thumb, 5s timeout (isolated) -> kill service + reject RendererFailed
6. Persist bytes + thumbnail.

PDF bytes reach the renderer via ParcelFileDescriptor over MemoryFile; renderer never sees a writable byte handle to anything else.

# Render pipeline at view time
Main composable -> PdfRendererService.render(page, width) -> Bitmap over shared memory. Multi-page = horizontal swipe, on-demand, LRU cache in main process.

# Explicit non-features (do not backslide without ADR amendment)
- No PDF digital-signature verification
- No text/form-field/annotation extraction
- No URL surfaced from PDF (no B3 analogue)
- No metadata-driven labels
- No DB/Keystore/network/file access from the renderer process

# Open questions (gate child beads + ADR 0005)
Q1 same-model vs sibling (recommend sibling)
Q2 list placement (recommend separate Documents lane)
Q3 encrypted PDF policy (recommend reject at import)
Q4 trust chrome loudness (recommend persistent caption, "Self-signed" register)
Q5 size + page caps (recommend 25 MB / 64 pages)
Q6 multi-page rendering (recommend full swipe on demand)
Q7 share-out (recommend yes, explicit-button only)
Q8 list label without user labeling (recommend filename, fallback "PDF, added <date>")

# Children
- wpass-pdf.threat-model (unblocked)
- wpass-pdf.renderer-research (unblocked)
- wpass-pdf.core-model (Q1)
- wpass-pdf.storage-schema (Q1)
- wpass-pdf.renderer-service (Q3, Q5)
- wpass-pdf.ui-integration (Q2, Q4, Q6, Q7, Q8)
- wpass-pdf.walt-android-wiring (cross-repo; mirrors wlt-4pg)

# ADR
ADR 0005 "PDF document support" drafted after Q1-Q8 answered.
notes:
2026-05-06 (wpass-6m9 source-level validation): two architectural implications recorded; ADR 0005 addendum required before wpass-5v9 starts.

F.1 (FD transport): MemoryFile + ParcelFileDescriptor as proposed in the bead does not satisfy PdfRenderer's seek requirement (PDFium issues lseek + pread64; ashmem-backed FDs do not honor that). Decision: pass PDF bytes via memfd_create (NDK syscall), wrapped in ParcelFileDescriptor. Implementation surface: ~30 lines NDK in passes-pdf/src/main/cpp/memfd.cpp + 1 Kotlin JNI shim. No on-disk plaintext at any point. passes-pdf gains its first JNI surface (single function, audit-friendly).

G.1 (Mainline CVE channel): PDFium ships in com.{google.android,android}.mediaprovider apex on API 34+ only, NOT API 33+ as the threat model and ADR 0005 currently state. Decision: gate PDF feature on Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 34. Walt overall minSdk unchanged; older devices see Android-14-required gate at the picker. Closes the stale-PDFium exposure window structurally.

A-E confirmed at source level (provisional yes); empirical device-matrix runs (Pixel 6/7/8, Pixel 4a, Galaxy S22/S24, Redmi Note 12) are a release-gate before wpass-5v9 ships, owned by the maintainer with physical hardware.

See docs/research/pdf-renderer-validation.md for full reasoning, AOSP source citations, and reproduction recipes.

title: passes-core: PassParser.create() factory glue (final implementation slice)
description:
Final slice: wire the four implementation slices (extraction wpass-8so [closed], pass.json deser wpass-7sl, manifest hash wpass-7l2, signature verify wpass-dw2, .strings parser wpass-ddc) into the public PassParser interface so PassParser.create(config).parse(source) returns a non-throwing ParseResult.

Currently passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/PassParser.kt:23 throws NotImplementedError. After this bead, that line is replaced with the real factory and walt-android can consume the parser end-to-end.

Scope:
- Replace the NotImplementedError factory in PassParser.kt with a real implementation. Construction takes ParserConfig; parse() takes PassSource and never throws.
- Pipeline order, top to bottom:
  1. extractSafely(source, config) → entries: Map<String, ByteArray> or Failure(MalformedReason). Failure → return ParseResult.Malformed(reason).
  2. manifestHashChain(entries) → Ok(manifestBytes) or Failed(reason). Failed → translate to ParseResult.Tampered or ParseResult.Malformed per the bead's failure-arm mapping.
  3. Signature handling: if 'signature' is absent in entries: when config.acceptUnsignedArchives → SignatureStatus.Unsigned; else → ParseResult.Tampered(SignatureCryptoFailure) (treat as a security event, not a structural failure). If 'signature' is present: verifySignature(signatureBytes, manifestBytes, config) → Ok(status) or Failed(tamperReason); on Failed → ParseResult.Tampered.
  4. parsePassJson(entries['pass.json']!!, config) → PassJsonDecodeResult.Success(passShape) or Malformed/Unsupported. Translate accordingly.
  5. For each entry whose name matches '<locale>.lproj/pass.strings', parseStrings(...) → fold into a Map<PassLocale, LocalizedStrings>. Apply ParserConfig.maxLocaleCount; trip → ResourceLimitExceeded(LocaleCount). Skip non-.strings files in .lproj/ directories silently (they are images for that locale; bind them into Pass.images keyed by locale-aware ImageRole if/when ADR 0001 is extended; for now: ignore).
  6. Image entries: every '<role>.png' (and '<role>@2x.png' / '<role>@3x.png' for retina variants per the existing ImageRole enum) in entries goes into Pass.images keyed by the right ImageRole. Unknown image basenames are silently dropped (PKPASS allows extras). Apply ParserConfig.maxImagePixelCount lazily — without a decoder in pure-JVM, validate via PNG IHDR parsing (8-byte signature + 13-byte IHDR with width/height as u32 BE). Width × height > maxImagePixelCount → ResourceLimitExceeded(ImagePixelCount).
  7. Assemble Pass(...) and return ParseResult.Success(pass, signatureStatus).
- Coroutine timeouts: ParserConfig today has no maxParseDurationMillis; do NOT add one in this PR (public surface is frozen until wpass-n6g). Instead, document in PassParser.parse's KDoc that the call is synchronous and that the consumer should wrap it in withTimeout(...) when running on a coroutine. File a follow-up bead if a built-in timeout knob is wanted later.
- TelemetryGuard: emit onParseStarted at the start, onParseSucceeded with the populated event on Success, onParseFailed with the populated event (carries the durationMillis and toFailureKind() of the result) on every non-Success arm. Use System.nanoTime() bracketing; never include pass content in the events (TelemetryGuard.kt's structural restriction enforces this at compile time).
- Concurrency: PassParser.create() returns an instance that is safe to call concurrently across threads. Each parse() call uses only stack-local state plus the immutable ParserConfig.

Out of scope:
- Coroutine timeout knob (separate bead if wanted; today wrap with withTimeout()).
- Encrypted-archive routing (wpass-m8v).
- Dedicated MalformedReason arms for structural rejections (wpass-n6g).
- maxTotalDecompressedBytes (wpass-oj8).

Tests:
- One end-to-end happy-path JUnit test per PassType (BoardingPass, EventTicket, Coupon, StoreCard, Generic) using a synthesized PKPASS archive built in-memory: extractor → manifest → signature → pass.json → .strings → final Pass.
- Unsigned archive: signature file absent + acceptUnsignedArchives=true → Success with SignatureStatus.Unsigned.
- Strict policy on unsigned: ParserConfig.Strict + no signature → Tampered(SignatureCryptoFailure).
- TelemetryGuard event ordering: onParseStarted → exactly one of onParseSucceeded / onParseFailed.
- Concurrency: 16 parallel parse() invocations on the same PassParser instance against the same PassSource.Bytes return the same Success.
- Each upstream slice's failure path forwarded correctly: zip-bomb → ResourceLimitExceeded(EntrySize); manifest hash mismatch → Tampered(FileHashMismatch); pass.json malformed → Malformed(InvalidPassJson); etc.
- PNG pixel-count limit: oversized PNG IHDR width × height → ResourceLimitExceeded(ImagePixelCount).
- maxLocaleCount trip when archive declares more .lproj/ directories than the cap.

Quality gates: ./gradlew :passes-core:check :passes-core:detekt all green. PublicApiSurfaceTest must continue to pass; specifically parserFactoryDoesNotThrow must remain green AND a new test should assert that PassParser.create().parse(SyntheticPkpass) does NOT throw and returns Success.

This bead unblocks walt-android wlt-4pg (consumer-side module-graph wiring).
