title: passes-core: Apple .strings localization parser
description:
Fifth slice of the PassParser implementation. Parse Apple .strings files (the PKPASS localization format inside <locale>.lproj/pass.strings) into the public LocalizedStrings type already declared in passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/Pass.kt:134.

Format reference (Apple Property List Strings file format):
- ASCII or UTF-8 / UTF-16 encoded text file.
- Each entry is either a quoted-string-pair: "key" = "value";
- Or a single-line comment: // … through end of line
- Or a block comment: /* … */ which can span lines.
- Whitespace and blank lines are ignored.
- Inside quoted strings, the recognized escapes are: \\, \", \n, \r, \t, and \Uxxxx (4-hex-digit Unicode codepoint).
- A backslash immediately before EOL is NOT a line-continuation. Apple's parser does not support that.

Scope:
- Add internal parseStrings(bytes: ByteArray, config: ParserConfig): StringsResult under passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/internal/.
- StringsResult is internal sealed: Ok(LocalizedStrings) or Failed(MalformedReason). For corruption use MalformedReason.InvalidPassJson — it is the closest existing arm; a future follow-up may introduce MalformedReason.InvalidStrings (coordinate with wpass-n6g).
- Detect encoding: BOM-sniff for UTF-16 LE/BE (FF FE / FE FF) and UTF-8 (EF BB BF). Default to UTF-8 in the absence of a BOM. Reject anything that is not valid UTF-8 / UTF-16 outright with a CharsetDecoder configured to error on malformed input.
- Enforce ParserConfig.maxJsonStringBytes per individual value (the .strings file is JSON-shaped enough that the same per-string-byte cap is the right knob; do not introduce a new knob in this bead — wpass-oj8 covers global decompressed footprint). Total file size is already bounded by ParserConfig.maxEntryBytes upstream.
- Hand-rolled lexer/parser, NOT a regex (regex on this format is brittle around comment nesting and escape sequences). Keep it tight: ~150 LOC of Kotlin should suffice. Walk a Char index, consume tokens, build a LinkedHashMap so iteration order matches file order.

Behavior:
- Empty file → Ok(LocalizedStrings(emptyMap())).
- Comments only → Ok(LocalizedStrings(emptyMap())).
- Duplicate keys: last write wins (matches Apple's behavior).
- Unterminated quoted string, unterminated block comment, missing '=' or ';' → Failed.
- Unrecognized escape sequence inside a quoted string → Failed (strict; do not silently pass through).

Tests:
- happy path: 5 well-formed entries with mixed comment styles between them.
- empty file.
- comment-only file.
- duplicate key (verify last wins).
- UTF-8 BOM, UTF-16-LE BOM, UTF-16-BE BOM all decode correctly.
- non-UTF-8 byte sequence with no BOM → Failed.
- escape sequences: \", \n, \\, \Uxxxx all round-trip.
- unrecognized escape sequence \x → Failed.
- unterminated quoted string → Failed.
- unterminated /* block comment → Failed.
- per-value maxJsonStringBytes trip → Failed (ResourceLimitExceeded).

Out of scope:
- Wiring per-locale .strings files into Pass.locales (parser-glue bead).
- BCP-47 locale tag validation (PassLocale is a value class wrapping a String; the consumer module owns BCP-47 parsing).

title: passes-core: PKCS#7 signature verification (BouncyCastle JVM)
description:
Fourth slice of the PassParser implementation. Verify the detached PKCS#7 / CMS signature over manifest.json bytes and surface a SignatureStatus per the lenient default policy (decision-wlt-0tn-q1: accept unsigned and self-signed by default, surface trust level via SignatureStatus).

Scope:
- Add internal verifySignature(signatureBytes: ByteArray, manifestBytes: ByteArray, config: ParserConfig): SignatureVerifyResult under passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/internal/.
- SignatureVerifyResult is internal sealed: Ok(status: SignatureStatus) where status is one of the four arms in the public SignatureStatus.kt (Unsigned not produced here — that comes from the parser-glue bead when the 'signature' file is absent; SelfSigned, AppleVerified, CertChainIncomplete are all produced here); or Failed(reason: TamperReason) for cryptographic failures (ManifestSignatureMismatch, SignatureCryptoFailure).
- Use BouncyCastle (already an allowed dep per CLAUDE.md). The relevant classes are CMSSignedData / CMSSignedDataParser, X509CertificateHolder, JcaX509CertificateConverter. Use Provider 'BC' explicitly so we are not at the mercy of platform defaults.
- Trust roots: bundle the Apple WWDR root and intermediate certs as resources under passes-core/src/main/resources/ (PEM or DER). The parser does NOT fetch certs over the network — CertChainIncomplete is the explicit arm for 'leaf signature validates but chain does not reach a known root and we will not perform external fetches'. Document the exact certs bundled and their source in a SECURITY-CERTS.md (or in the file's KDoc) so an auditor can verify the trust anchors.

Policy:
- Verify the CMS signature mathematically against manifestBytes. Mismatch → Failed(ManifestSignatureMismatch).
- Build the certificate chain from the leaf in the signature blob through any intermediates included in the signature, terminating at one of: (a) Apple WWDR root → Ok(AppleVerified); (b) self-signed leaf only → Ok(SelfSigned) IFF config.acceptSelfSignedCertificates; (c) chain extends but not to a known root → Ok(CertChainIncomplete) IFF config.acceptSelfSignedCertificates (treat 'incomplete' as a softer form of 'self-signed' for policy purposes); (d) chain rejected outright when config.acceptSelfSignedCertificates is false and the chain does not reach Apple → Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure).
- ParserConfig.acceptUnsignedArchives is consulted ONLY by the parser-glue bead (it decides whether to treat a missing 'signature' file as Unsupported vs Ok(Unsigned)). This bead is invoked only when 'signature' is present.
- BouncyCastle malformed-blob exceptions → Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure). Never propagate exceptions out of this function.

Tests:
- happy path AppleVerified: synthesize a CMS signature using a test cert chain that terminates at the bundled WWDR root.
- SelfSigned: signature uses an unrelated self-signed leaf; acceptSelfSignedCertificates=true → Ok(SelfSigned).
- CertChainIncomplete: leaf + intermediate but no root in the bundled set; acceptSelfSignedCertificates=true → Ok(CertChainIncomplete).
- Strict policy rejects: ParserConfig.Strict (acceptSelfSignedCertificates=false) on a self-signed input → Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure).
- Manifest tamper: signature valid but manifestBytes mutated by 1 byte → Failed(ManifestSignatureMismatch).
- Garbage signature blob → Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure).
- Constant-time digest comparison via MessageDigest.isEqual.

Out of scope:
- Manifest hash chain (separate bead, wpass-7l2).
- pass.json deserialization (separate bead).

title: passes-core: manifest.json hash chain verification
description:
Third slice of the PassParser implementation. Verify every file in the extracted archive against its SHA-1 hash declared in manifest.json. PKPASS uses SHA-1 here for compatibility; that is per the spec, not a security cipher choice — the actual integrity binding comes from the PKCS#7 signature over manifest.json bytes (separate bead, signature verification).

Scope:
- Add an internal manifestHashChain(entries: Map<String, ByteArray>): ManifestVerifyResult under passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/internal/. Pure function, no I/O.
- ManifestVerifyResult is internal sealed: Ok(manifestBytes: ByteArray) (returned bytes are the canonical manifest.json that signature verification will sign over) or Failed(failure: ManifestFailure). Map Failed to ParseResult arms in the parser-glue bead.
- ManifestFailure arms: Missing → MalformedReason.MissingManifest; Invalid → MalformedReason.InvalidManifest (parse error or wrong shape); EntryHashMismatch(name) → ParseResult.Tampered(TamperReason.FileHashMismatch); ExtraEntry(name) → MalformedReason.InvalidManifest (file in archive not in manifest = tamper-shaped, but PKPASS spec is silent on this; conservative choice is to reject); MissingEntry(name) → MalformedReason.InvalidManifest (manifest references a file not in archive).

Behavior:
- Parse manifest.json as a flat JSON object: { 'pass.json': '<sha1-hex>', 'icon.png': '<sha1-hex>', 'en.lproj/pass.strings': '<sha1-hex>', ... }. Hex-decode each value to a 20-byte hash.
- For every key in the manifest, look up the corresponding entry in entries map; SHA-1 the bytes via java.security.MessageDigest; constant-time compare against the manifest's hex-decoded value.
- The 'signature' file is NOT listed in manifest.json (it signs the manifest, so it cannot be self-referential). Treat 'signature' as exempt from hash verification but still required to be present iff config.acceptUnsignedArchives is false.
- Reject (a) any entry in archive that is not in manifest (other than 'signature') AND (b) any manifest key that has no corresponding archive entry.
- Constant-time comparison: use MessageDigest.isEqual().

Out of scope:
- Signature verification (separate bead). This bead returns the manifestBytes so the signature bead can hash-and-verify them in turn.

Tests:
- happy path: 5-entry archive with correct hashes → Ok with manifest bytes returned.
- one entry hash mismatch → Tampered(FileHashMismatch).
- missing manifest.json → Malformed(MissingManifest).
- garbage manifest.json (non-JSON or wrong shape) → Malformed(InvalidManifest).
- archive has extra file not in manifest → Malformed(InvalidManifest).
- manifest references file not in archive → Malformed(InvalidManifest).
- manifest contains 'signature' as a self-referential key → reject as Malformed(InvalidManifest).
- hex parsing: lowercase, uppercase, mixed case all accepted; non-hex character rejected.
- empty manifest (zero entries) → Malformed(InvalidManifest) since pass.json is mandatory per PKPASS.

title: passes-core: pass.json deserialization slice
description:
Second slice of the PassParser implementation (after wpass-8so). Land kotlinx.serialization-based deserialization of pass.json into the existing public Pass model in passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/Pass.kt.

Scope:
- Add an internal sealed PassJsonDecodeResult { Success(pass-shape), Malformed(MalformedReason) } under passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/internal/.
- Read pass.json bytes from the Map<String, ByteArray> handed back by extractSafely. Map exact key 'pass.json' (PKPASS spec).
- Use kotlinx.serialization with strict mode: ignoreUnknownKeys = true (PKPASS adds fields over time and we want forward-compat) BUT explicitly skip / refuse to surface dangerous fields: nfc, webServiceURL, authenticationToken, personalization, personalizationToken. These must be parsed-and-dropped per decision-wlt-0tn-q1 and the threat model in wpass-9vv.1.
- Apply ParserConfig.maxJsonDepth and maxJsonStringBytes via a custom Json configuration. The defaults are encoded in ParserConfig.kt; do not change them in this PR.
- Distinguish three failure modes: MalformedReason.MissingPassJson (entries does not contain 'pass.json'), MalformedReason.InvalidPassJson (kotlinx.serialization throws), and ParseResult.Unsupported(UnsupportedReason.FormatVersion(formatVersion)) when formatVersion != 1, plus Unsupported(UnknownPassStyle(raw)) for unrecognized style keys.
- Field mapping: every member of the public Pass type must be populated. PassType from the top-level style key (boardingPass, eventTicket, coupon, storeCard, generic). Colors via parseColor() that handles both 'rgb(R,G,B)' and '#RRGGBB' forms (matches the existing ColorValue contract). Front/back fields from the style-specific 'header/primary/secondary/auxiliary' / 'backFields' arrays (each entry produces a PassField). Barcode from 'barcode' or 'barcodes[0]' (PKPASS prefers barcodes plural since iOS 9). expirationDate from RFC-3339 string into PassInstant via java.time on the JVM (passes-core is JVM-only). voided is a top-level boolean. URLs in field values stay as inert text — B3 confirmation lives in the UI module.

Out of scope:
- Manifest hash verification (separate bead).
- Signature verification (separate bead).
- Image bytes / locales (the extractor already handed those back as bytes; the parser-glue bead wires images and per-locale .strings files into Pass.images and Pass.locales).

Tests: table-driven JUnit + Truth, fixture passes constructed in-memory (no checked-in binary fixtures). Cover: happy path for each PassType; missing top-level fields; unknown formatVersion; unknown style key; rgb(...) vs #RRGGBB; barcode vs barcodes[0]; nfc/webServiceURL/authenticationToken/personalization fields present (verify they are parsed but not surfaced on Pass); maxJsonDepth and maxJsonStringBytes trips → ResourceLimitExceeded.

title: passes-core: hardened ZIP extraction layer for PassParser
description: First slice of the PassParser implementation. Lands the safe-extraction layer that downstream parser slices (pass.json deserialization, manifest hash chain, PKCS#7 signature, .strings parsing) build on top of. title: BackupRulesAssertion: implement manifest-XML fallback for API 31+
description:
On API 31+ with target SDK >= 31, ApplicationInfo.dataExtractionRulesRes is on the hidden-API blocklist; getDeclaredField throws NoSuchFieldException, and BackupRulesAssertion.assertBackupRulesApplied collapses to Outcome.FieldUnavailable.

The author anticipated this in BackupRulesAssertion.kt's docstring: 'a manifest-XML fallback is the expected mitigation.'

Implementation sketch:
1. When readIntField returns null on a known-existent field name, fall through to a manifest-XML parse rather than surfacing FieldUnavailable.
2. Open AndroidManifest.xml via context.assets.openXmlResourceParser(applicationInfo.publicSourceDir, 'AndroidManifest.xml').
3. Walk to the <application> tag, read android:dataExtractionRules and android:fullBackupContent attributes (lookup by attribute resource ID; android.R.attr.dataExtractionRules is API 31+).
4. Resolve the attribute value to a resource ID and feed back into the existing validateResource path.
5. Unit-test the new code path against a Robolectric ApplicationInfo whose reflection-blocked fields force the fallback.

Until this lands, BackupRulesAssertionInstrumentationTest skips on API 31+ via assumeTrue (see comment in that test). The JVM-side BackupRulesAssertionTest still exercises the parser and contract logic against synthetic ApplicationInfo, so the trust claim has coverage on the JVM side even on the API levels where instrumentation skips.

Surfaced by wpass-ym0 CI matrix run on PR #20.
close_reason: Duplicate of wpass-2zv

title: passes-storage instrumentation tests fail on emulator (block wpass-ym0)
description:
The wpass-ym0 CI matrix surfaced three pre-existing defects in the instrumentation tests delivered by wpass-x5l. They pass static gates (compile, lint, detekt, ktlint) but had not been run end-to-end on an emulator before now.

Evidence: workflow run https://github.com/walt-app/walt-passes-android/actions/runs/25361823518 (PR #20).

Failures:

1. AutoBackupBmgrTest.bmgrBackupNowSucceedsAndExcludesPassesDatabase
   - On API 28: clean assertion failure. bmgr stdout was 'Running incremental backup for 1 requested packages.' — the assertion expects 'Success'.
   - On API 31/34/36: the test process crashes (no Java stack trace) shortly after bmgr returns, taking out the whole instrumentation run before the other 6 tests can execute.
   - Root cause hypothesis: bmgr backupnow is asynchronous; it queues a backup job and returns immediately. The 'Success'/'Failure' line lands later in logcat, not in bmgr's own stdout. The test needs either bmgr backupnow --sync (where supported) or a logcat-poll for the BackupManagerService completion line. The crash on newer APIs is likely a secondary effect of the assertion-failed test exiting while the backup engine is still running on a binder thread.

2. KeyUnavailableAcrossDataClearTest.envelopeWipedWhileDatabaseFilePresentSurfacesKeyUnavailable
3. KeyUnavailableAcrossDataClearTest.keystoreAliasDroppedWhileEnvelopePresentSurfacesKeyUnavailable
   - Both fail at the @Before bootstrap step with: 'First-time bootstrap of SqlCipher repo failed: Failure(error=KeyUnwrapFailed)'.
   - Root cause hypothesis: wipeStorageState() in @Before deletes the envelope sharedpref and the AndroidKeyStore master alias, but it does not delete the SQLCipher database file before bootstrapAndWriteOnePass() runs. Across the second @Test invocation in the same JVM, the leftover encrypted DB from the first test is unwrappable because the wipe deleted the envelope/alias the first run installed, so SqlCipherPassRepository.create() sees the existing DB on disk and tries to unwrap a key that is no longer there. The fix is to delete the DB file before bootstrap (the helper already does so in @Before via wipeStorageState(), but check ordering / sharing).

Correctly skipped on emulators (no action needed):
- KeystoreBackingMatrixTest.keyBackingIsStrongBoxWhenAvailable — assumeTrue skip (no FEATURE_STRONGBOX_KEYSTORE)
- KeystoreBackingMatrixTest.keyBackingIsSoftwareWhenHardwareUnavailable — assumeTrue skip on hardware-Keystore emulators
- KeystoreBackingMatrixTest.keyBackingIsTeeWhenStrongBoxNotRequested — assumeTrue skip on Software-only Keystore (API 28 google_apis emulator backs into Software, not TEE)

Also worth checking: BackupRulesAssertionInstrumentationTest.mergedManifestRulesAreApplied also FAILED on API 28; the textproto excerpt this bead was filed from did not include that error_message. Pull the api28 artifact from the run above to see the trace.

Once these fixes land, the wpass-ym0 PR (#20) should re-run green and can merge.

Blocks: wpass-ym0.
notes:
Failures 1, 2, and 3 addressed by PR #21: https://github.com/walt-app/walt-passes-android/pull/21

(1) AutoBackupBmgrTest: option-2 canary approach - poll logcat for BackupManagerService completion, assert blob contains canary file before asserting it does not contain walt_passes.db.

(2)+(3) KeyUnavailableAcrossDataClearTest envelope/keystore tests: replace direct envelope-XML deletion with prefs.edit().clear().commit() through the SharedPreferences API. The file-level delete left a stale cache that survived into the next test's bootstrap, causing KeyUnwrapFailed instead of KeyUnavailable.

STILL OPEN under this bead:
- BackupRulesAssertionInstrumentationTest.mergedManifestRulesAreApplied (separate root cause; needs diagnosis)
close_reason: Three of four failures fixed by PR #21 (canary-poll for AutoBackupBmgrTest, SharedPreferences-API clear for KeyUnavailableAcrossDataClearTest x2). The fourth (BackupRulesAssertionInstrumentationTest FieldUnavailable on API 31+) was reframed as a production-code gap in BackupRulesAssertion and tracked separately as wpass-2zv P2; the instrumentation test assumeTrue-skips on API 31+ until that lands. title: BackupRulesAssertion: manifest-XML fallback for greylist/blocklist regression
description:
Reflection on ApplicationInfo.fullBackupContent and ApplicationInfo.dataExtractionRulesRes works today via @UnsupportedAppUsage greylist access. Google has been gradually moving such fields to the blocklist; if either is restricted in a future Android release, the assertion regresses to Outcome.FieldUnavailable for any consumer running on that platform.

Scope:
- Investigate whether a public path to these fields exists (none today; track API surveys)
- If still no public path, add a manifest-XML fallback: parse the consumer's merged AndroidManifest.xml from the APK to extract android:fullBackupContent / android:dataExtractionRules attribute values, resolve to a resource id, and feed into the existing parseResource path
- Degrade from 'broken' to 'slower' rather than 'broken' to 'manual review'

Trigger condition: Outcome.FieldUnavailable observed on any tested API level, OR Android release notes flag either field as blocklisted.

Refs: review feedback on PR #18; BackupRulesAssertion KDoc reflection paragraph.
notes: Surfaced concretely by wpass-ym0 CI matrix run on PR #20: BackupRulesAssertionInstrumentationTest.mergedManifestRulesAreApplied returns FieldUnavailable on API 31+ because getDeclaredField('dataExtractionRulesRes') throws NoSuchFieldException under hidden-API blocklist for our target SDK. Bumping to P2; until this lands, BackupRulesAssertionInstrumentationTest assumeTrue-skips on API 31+ via inline assumeTrue (see that test's comment).
close_reason: Merged in #22 (bca827e). Manifest-XML fallback runs end-to-end on API 28/31/34/36; assumeTrue skip removed.

title: BackupRulesAssertion: support consumers that tools:replace the library rules
description:
walt-android (the primary consumer) will mirror passes-storage's exclude entries into its own res/xml files and use tools:replace="android:allowBackup,android:fullBackupContent" rather than inheriting the library-shipped rules. With that posture the merged ApplicationInfo.fullBackupContent points at the consumer's resource (e.g. backup_rules), not walt_passes_backup_rules, so BackupRulesAssertion.assertBackupRulesApplied returns FullBackupContentMismatch even when the consumer is doing the right thing.

Two paths:

(a) Add a content-matching mode: parse the resource the consumer's manifest actually points at, check it contains the required <exclude> entries (database walt_passes.db + sidecars, sharedpref is.walt.passes.storage.key_envelope.xml, plus the device-transfer block on API 31+). Returns Applied when entries are present even if the resource name differs.

(b) Document that the existing assertion is only valid for consumers who let the library rules pass through unmodified; consumers using tools:replace must implement their own equivalent test.

Recommend (a) because the trust claim ("pass data is excluded from cloud backup") is about the entries, not the resource name, and walt-android's posture is reasonable.

Wire into wpass-x5l so the device-test work assumes the post-fix assertion shape.

Refs: bd memory walt-android-backup-posture-2026-05-05-consumer; ADR 0002 D5; passes-storage/.../BackupRulesAssertion.kt.
notes: 2026-05-05: Re-review feedback addressed in commit 7cbab46 (PR #18). Pre-S coverage added, endToEnd hardened (asserts allowBackup=true precondition + cross-checks public vs seam paths), duplicate-section union, parser tolerances documented, parser wrapped in object. One item deferred per reviewer's explicit 'not blocking' (type indirection collapse). Disposition posted to PR. Awaiting merge.

design:
==============================================================
BRAINSTORMING PHASE COMPLETE (2026-05-03)
==============================================================

This document captures the architectural intent settled during
brainstorming. Architecture and planning beads (children of
this epic) carry forward the detailed design work.

==============================================================
Q1 RESOLVED: Pass acquisition model
==============================================================

PKPASS file import as primary acquisition path.

1a Signature policy: LENIENT + mathematical verify + provenance display + defense in depth [Position A].
- Parse PKCS#7 signature; verify mathematically; reject if manifest hash chain mismatches (tampering rejected unconditionally).
- Validate WWDR cert chain but DO NOT gate on it. Surface result in UI: 'Verified Apple issuer: X' / 'Self-signed' / 'Cert chain incomplete'.
- Allow self-signed and non-Apple-cert passes to import.

1b Register OS-level intent filter for 'application/vnd.apple.pkpass' MIME and '.pkpass' extension in walt-android app/AndroidManifest.xml.

1c PKPASS NFC payload field: parse-but-ignore. Never register the AID.

1d Manual entry and QR scan: deferred to v2.

==============================================================
Q2 RESOLVED: Naming
==============================================================
- Feature umbrella: 'Walt Passes'.
- Open-source repo: 'walt-passes-android' under github.com/walt-app.
- UI subtype labels (per PKPASS type): boardingPass='Boarding pass', eventTicket='Ticket', coupon='Coupon', storeCard='Store card', generic='Pass'.

==============================================================
Q3 RESOLVED: v1 scope
==============================================================
IN:
- All 5 PKPASS types via generic field-driven renderer.
- Front + back fields displayed.
- Barcode/QR rendering (PDF417, QR, Aztec, Code128) via ZXing; payload opaque text.
- Visual fidelity: bg/fg/label colors; logo, strip, background, thumbnail images.
- L1 full localization: all .lproj retained; re-render on locale change.
- Pass expiry display ('Expired' badge); no auto-delete.
- Encrypted local storage: SQLCipher with key in Android Keystore.
- Intent filter for .pkpass MIME.
- Q3.2 back-field actionables: Policy B3 (visible URL + confirmation sheet). HTML subset (b, i, br, a). URL scheme allowlist (http, https, mailto, tel). Custom Tabs.
- Q3.4 secure deletion: no undo, Android Auto Backup excluded for passes DB, no PII in logs, cached decoded data wiped, confirmation dialog. VACUUM skipped.
- CRUD: list, view detail, delete, type-chip filter.

OUT (deferred or never):
- NFC/transit, dynamic updates, lock screen integration (defer v1.5), notifications (defer v2), pass sharing (defer v2), manual entry (defer v2), QR scan (defer v2), multi-device sync, cloud backup, personalization, wearables, pass editing, pass export.

==============================================================
Q4 RESOLVED: Repo location, license, distribution
==============================================================
- Separate repo at github.com/walt-app/walt-passes-android.
- License: Apache 2.0.
- Distribution: Composite Gradle build for v1 (sibling-checkout, includeBuild). Planned future migration: GitHub Packages once v1 stabilizes.
- Repo bootstrap details deferred to architecture phase.

==============================================================
Q5 RESOLVED: Library shape — Option C repositioned
==============================================================
walt-android is closed-source. The trust-through-transparency goal
requires security-and-privacy claims to be auditable in walt-passes-android.
The repo is positioned as 'Walt's open pass-handling kernel,' not
a generic PKPASS library.

Three Gradle modules in walt-passes-android:

passes-core (pure Kotlin/JVM):
- ZIP extraction with hardening
- pass.json schema (kotlinx.serialization)
- manifest hash verification
- PKCS#7 signature parsing (BouncyCastle)
- WWDR cert chain analysis (non-gating)
- .strings parser
- Domain model (Pass, PassField, etc.)
- Result types (ParseResult, SignatureStatus)
- ParserConfig with secure defaults
- TelemetryGuard interface (PII-forbidden by signature)

passes-storage (Android):
- SQLCipher with Keystore-sourced key
- Encrypted blob persistence
- Decoded-field cache
- Backup-exclusion config
- Deletion + cache wipe
- No soft-delete

passes-ui (Android + Compose):
- Pass front/back composables
- Barcode/QR rendering (ZXing wrapper)
- B3 URL confirmation sheet
- Phone/email confirmation sheet variants
- 'Expired' badge
- Bounded image loading via ImageDecoder
- Theming contract (tokens passed in by consumer)

walt-android shrinks to:
- core/data-passes: Hilt wiring of passes-storage
- feature/passes: Compose screens consuming passes-ui composables with Walt theme tokens
- app: Manifest intent filter

DECISIVE CONSTRAINT: walt-android consumes walt-passes-android implementations directly.
No parallel reimplementation in walt-android of code bearing a trust claim.

==============================================================
TRUST CLAIM TO MODULE MAPPING (audit map for the README):
==============================================================
1. Parser hardening                       -> passes-core
2. Lenient sig + tamper detection         -> passes-core
3. Encrypted storage with hardware keys   -> passes-storage
4. No backup of pass data                 -> passes-storage
5. No PII in logs                         -> passes-core (TelemetryGuard) + passes-storage
6. B3 URL confirmation flow               -> passes-ui
7. Irreversible deletion                  -> passes-storage
8. Expired badge, no auto-delete          -> passes-ui + passes-storage

==============================================================
Required parser hardening (mandatory in passes-core):
==============================================================
- Bound archive size (10 MB cap), entry count, individual entry size, JSON depth.
- Reject zip-slip: canonicalize entry names, reject path traversal, reject symlinks.
- Allowlist file extensions in archive: .json, .png, .strings only.
- In-memory extraction; no attacker-controlled disk paths.
- Strict JSON deserialization with explicit field types; ignore unknown fields safely.
- Skip dangerous PKPASS fields entirely: nfc, webServiceURL, authenticationToken, personalization*.
- URLs treated as inert text in parser; B3 confirmation sheet at UI boundary.
- Coroutine timeouts around parsing.
- Pin dependency versions; CVE scanning in CI.

Walt-specific blast radius if parser RCE achieved (informational):
- Source code: not exfiltratable.
- DPAN keys: NOT reachable (Keystore/StrongBox non-exportable).
- Card metadata, transaction history: REACHABLE.
- Card cloning: not possible.
- Worst case: transaction history exfiltration.
- Mitigation: parser hardening above; consider isolated-process parsing in v2.

title: OPTIONAL: encode a parsed Pass back to an unsigned .pkpass for legacy (pre-retention) rows
description:
Encode a parsed `Pass` back into an UNSIGNED `.pkpass` archive (pass.json + images + strings) so passes imported before raw-byte retention (wpass K1) can still be exported in the same container as everything else.

## Status: OPTIONAL. Decide before building.
The alternative is for the consumer to export legacy passes as a JSON projection of the parsed model in its sidecar and re-import them through its own path. That avoids a kernel writer but creates a second, Walt-only pass shape to maintain. A kernel encoder keeps the container homogeneous (every pass entry is a pkpass) and is reusable. Pick whichever the implementer judges smaller; if the sidecar route is taken, close this bead with the reason.

## Constraints if built
- Output is honestly unsigned: no `manifest.json`/`signature` fabrication. Re-import lands as `SignatureStatus.Unsigned` and the consumer UI must have warned once at export time.
- Walt's own parser must accept the output (it does not require `passTypeIdentifier` / `teamIdentifier`; verify and pin). Apple-format validity is a non-goal.
- Round-trip test: parse(encode(parse(fixture))) == parse(fixture) for the model fields the kernel keeps.
- Colours, all field groups, barcode(s) incl. altText/messageEncoding, images by role, per-locale strings.
notes:
Decision (2026-09-08): BUILD the kernel encoder. Reasoning: (1) The bead's stated alternative, a JSON projection of the parsed model in Walt's sidecar, is already ruled out on the consumer side. Walt ADR 0009 Decision 7 says format v1 requires every pass entry to be a .pkpass and deliberately has no 'pass model in the sidecar' fallback, because that would be a second Walt-only pass shape with its own parser (a parallel reimplementation of trust-bearing types, forbidden by Walt ADR 0004 D2) and would let the sidecar assert pass content that never went through PassParser. So the real choice is encoder vs OMIT legacy passes from the export. (2) Fields: the kernel keeps type, serialNumber, description, organizationName, expirationDate, voided, 3 colours, 5 field groups (key/label/value/textAlignment), one barcode (format/message/messageEncoding/altText), 18 top-level image roles, per-locale strings. It drops passTypeIdentifier, teamIdentifier, relevantDate, locations, logoText, webServiceURL, authenticationToken, nfc, semantics, userInfo, barcodes[1..], localized images, field attributedValue/dateStyle/numberStyle/currencyCode, manifest and signature. None of the dropped keys is needed for re-import: PassJsonDecoder requires only formatVersion=1, serialNumber, description, organizationName and exactly one style key; passTypeIdentifier/teamIdentifier are not read at all (pinned by test). (3) Size: about 220 LOC main (PassEncoder.kt public surface + internal PassArchiveWriter) and about 250 LOC test; pure JVM, java.util.zip.ZipOutputStream, kotlinx JSON, no new dependency. (4) Trust angle: the output carries NO signature entry, so re-import lands as SignatureStatus.Unsigned under the lenient default and Tampered(SignatureCryptoFailure) under ParserConfig.Strict; nothing Walt produces can be mistaken for issuer-signed because the only provenance signal the kernel recognises is the CMS signature, which is never written. A manifest.json IS written: the parser rejects an archive without one (Malformed(MissingManifest)) and rejects entries the manifest does not list, so the hash index is required for the archive to be a pkpass at all. It is an integrity index (SHA-1 per entry), not provenance; SignatureStatus.Unsigned is documented as 'just a zipped manifest'. (5) Bounded output: the encoder takes a ParserConfig and refuses (sealed PassEncodeResult.LimitExceeded(ResourceLimit)) rather than emit anything the parser would reject on size, checking entry count, per-entry bytes, locale count, JSON string bytes via the parser's own enforceJsonLimits, strings value bytes with the lexer's conservative count, PNG pixel count, and total archive bytes. (6) Deterministic: fixed entry order (pass.json, manifest.json, images by role, locales by tag), sorted strings keys, fixed DOS timestamp expressed in local calendar time so the bytes do not depend on the device time zone; two encodes of an equal Pass are byte-identical.

Implemented 2026-09-08 on branch wpass-59i.4 (local commit, not pushed, bead left open for review). Files: passes-core PassEncoder.kt (public PassEncoder object + sealed PassEncodeResult: Success / LimitExceeded(ResourceLimit) / InvalidLocaleTag), internal PassArchiveWriter.kt, PassJsonEncoder.kt, PassStringsEncoder.kt; PassJsonDecoder.kt and DefaultPassParser.kt only widen their key/name tables to internal so the writer inverts them; PassEncoderTest.kt (10 tests: round trip of every kept field incl. altText/messageEncoding/colours/all field groups/images by role/per-locale strings, every style, strict refusal, passTypeIdentifier/teamIdentifier omitted and not required, fixed entry order, byte-identical across map order and time zones, strings escapes, invalid locale tags, one refusal per ResourceLimit arm). Docs: ADR 0001 D7, CLAUDE.md and README.md passes-core bullets. Gates green: :passes-core:test detekt ktlintCheck and ./gradlew check assemble assembleDebugAndroidTest. Consumer note: Walt ADR 0009 Decision 7 'With wpass-59i.4' branch applies once this merges; the one nuance versus its wording is that a manifest.json IS written (the parser requires it), the signature is not.

Review follow-up 2026-09-08 (second commit 82bd543, not pushed, bead open): ZIP timestamp moved to local 1980-01-02 (1980-01-01 encodes to the DOSTIME_BEFORE_1980 sentinel, which libcore on API 28-33 turns into a zone-dependent 0x5455 extra field); test pins zero extra length and exact DOS date/time bytes. SHA1_ALGORITHM and colour shifts hoisted to Constants.kt; Char.utf8Bytes shared with the strings lexer; inverted name tables internal with a drift test; isSafeLocaleTag refuses unpaired surrogates; ADR 0001 section renumbered D8 (D7 belongs to the wpass-59i.3 bundle reader), cites ADR 0002 D3 / D9, D4 amended for java.time. Gates green: passes-core test/detekt/ktlint and full check assemble assembleDebugAndroidTest (1025 tests, 0 failures).

Round-two review 2026-09-08 (fourth commit on the rebased branch, not pushed, bead open): InvalidLocaleTag is a payload-free data object; limit checks in parser order with ArchiveSize last; ZIP timestamp 1980-01-02 12:00 local; ADR 0001 D4 retitled (java.time off the public surface, expect/actual clause), D8 test table rows and lone-surrogate lossy note; ColorValue KDoc on the 24-bit mask. Gates green: passes-core test/detekt/ktlint and full check assemble assembleDebugAndroidTest.
close_reason: Merged in PR #239 (194c2b6): PassEncoder writes a parsed Pass back to an unsigned .pkpass (never a signature; re-import lands Unsigned, refused under Strict), bounded by the parser's own guards, deterministic on-device with a sentinel-safe ZIP timestamp. Built (not closed as sidecar route) because walt-android ADR 0009 D7 requires every export entry to be a pkpass. All CI legs green.

title: passes-barcode BoundedBitmapDecoder reads its PFD from the inherited offset (same idiom as wpass-07h)
description: BoundedBitmapDecoder.kt:39 reads the source PFD via AutoCloseInputStream(pfd.dup()) from the current offset with no rewind, the exact idiom wpass-07h fixed in passes-image's decodeRasterFromPfd (rewindToStart, ESPIPE swallowed). Today the barcode fd is decode-once (bind-per-call at import), so no consumer symptom exists; this is latent until a second consumer decodes the same fd. Apply the same per-decode rewind for symmetry, or fold the shared read-with-rewind into a common helper.

title: Validate DEFAULT_SYMBOL_DECODE_BUDGET_MS against a large image on-device
description:
wpass-sw2 measured the decode ladder on-device but at the WRONG SIZE to test the assumption the budget constant rests on.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (wpass-sw2, FP4, 2026-08-14): the reported boarding-pass artifact, 1080x2340 (~2.5MP). Full isolated-process bracket 816 ms and 801 ms, roughly 6x under the 5000 ms DecodeWatchdog expiry.

WHY THAT DOES NOT SETTLE IT: the ~10x low-end-ART factor behind DEFAULT_SYMBOL_DECODE_BUDGET_MS was applied to wpass-pl7.2's host-JVM peak of 495 ms AT 16MP. A 2.5MP measurement cannot confirm or refute a 16MP extrapolation. The on-device figure came in at ~1.6x the host figure for a much smaller image, which is suggestive that 10x is conservative but is not evidence at the size that matters.

WHAT TO DO: import a large image (12-16MP, e.g. a full-resolution camera photo carrying a barcode) through the same 'Upload a picture' path on real hardware and record the wall-clock. The ladder's cost is superlinear in pixel count, so this is where the watchdog risk actually lives - the epic's constraint 3 flagged exactly this ('TRY_HARDER on a full-resolution 12MP photo is already expensive').

If the figure lands anywhere near the 5000 ms expiry, DEFAULT_SYMBOL_DECODE_BUDGET_MS needs revisiting; the sandbox is KILLED on expiry and the composite path reports that as 'No code found'.

NOTE ON METHOD: the wpass-sw2 figures are a coarse ActivityManager bracket on the :barcodeDecoder process (spawn to kill), since the kernel barcode path carries no log statements by design. Same method works here; it overstates the ladder by including fork/bind/memfd/teardown, which is the safe direction for a budget check.

PII: use a synthetic or non-sensitive image. Record wall-clock and pass/fail only.

title: Confirm the live-camera roster cost on-device (FP4)
description:
wpass-pl7.3 measured the live-frame roster cost on a host JVM and the owner accepted the result, so this is confirmation work, not a blocker.

WHAT WAS MEASURED: see the table in wpass-pl7.3's NOTES, which is the authoritative figure set - do not copy numbers out of it, they moved once already when the fixture gained a quiet zone. In summary: adding Aztec + PDF417 costs ~4.6ms per 640x480 frame; QR is unaffected; Code128 pays all of it (3.5x) because TRY_HARDER makes ZXing append the 1D reader last.

WHAT WAS NOT MEASURED: the same frames on the FP4. Host-JVM figures establish the RATIO, which is what the accept/narrow decision turned on, but not the absolute per-frame budget.

WHY THE ABSOLUTE MATTERS. The number to carry to the device is NOT the roster delta but the no-symbol frame - every frame before lock-on - which the harness puts at ~16ms at 640x480 and ~30ms at 1280x720 on a fast desktop core. CameraX delivers a frame every 33ms at 30fps. If a no-symbol frame overruns that interval on a mid-range phone, frames are dropped and the effective analysis rate falls, which is what "slower lock-on" would actually be. The 1280x720 figure already consumes the whole interval on the host, so the finding to confirm is that ANALYZER RESOLUTION, not roster width, is the live budget's lever.

REPRODUCING: LiveFrameRosterLatencyHarness (passes-barcode-core, test source set, gated behind -Dwalt.latencyHarness) carries the fixtures and every roster variant. It is host-JVM only. Reaching the FP4 means either porting it to an androidTest, or instrumenting decodeYPlane in the walt-android live analyzer directly - the latter has the advantage of measuring real camera frames rather than synthetic ones, which matters twice over: the harness's clean renders cannot represent blur, glare, or angle, and its per-pixel noise defeats PDF417 detection above 640x480 in a way a real scene may not.

Deferred at the owner's request (no device installs in that session).
close_reason: Relocated to walt-android as wlt-l1u5.5 (child of consumer epic wlt-l1u5): the measurement target is the consumer's live analyzer (instrumenting decodeYPlane on real camera frames is the preferred route), so the bead belongs there. No kernel work remains; the host-JVM harness and accepted ratio figures stay in wpass-pl7.3's notes.

title: On-device pin for DocumentView's face-tint frame branch
description:
wpass-80y.5 added ScannableCardFaceTintInstrumentedTest so the scannable arm's faceTint routing is pinned by reading painted pixels (Robolectric cannot: captureToImage's forceRedraw handshake times out even at @GraphicsMode(NATIVE), probed with both rule types).

The document arm has no counterpart. DocumentView's frame is a Modifier.background, so both branches of documentFace() are invisible to a composition assertion — rewriting it to ignore faceTint, or to re-inline the pre-wpass-80y.5 isSpecified gate, leaves DocumentFaceTintTest green.

Work: add an androidTest to passes-document-ui mirroring ScannableCardFaceTintInstrumentedTest (transparent tint paints laneBackground, opaque tint reaches the frame), plus the managedDevices block and CI connected-tests step passes-document-ui currently lacks.

Note the wider gap found in the same review: passes-image declares managedDevices but CI's connected-tests job only invokes passes-storage and passes-barcode, so passes-image's androidTest never runs either. Worth folding into this bead or splitting out.

title: Split the C2 control-matrix cell out of the table
description:
docs/SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md's 'How each control is tested' matrix has a C2 row that is now a single ~1900-character table cell enumerating a dozen test names across five beads. It is past being readable as a table, and every wpass-80y child extended it further (wpass-80y.5 added the shared-tint-gate pins; wpass-80y.4 rewrote the wallet-row entry as a removal note).

Flagged in review of PR #207 as a pre-existing trend that those PRs extended rather than introduced.

Suggested shape: keep the matrix as a one-line-per-control index and move C2's enumeration into a subsection below it, grouped by what each pin protects (caption non-suppressibility / surface shape locks / concession pins / tint pins). C1 and C5 are trending the same way and should be checked while in there.

title: Decide whether CompactCodeView follows ScannableCardRowTile out
description:
The C1/C2 list-face code render concession in docs/SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md carries a Dormant marker (wpass-80y, 2026-08-08): the 26.08.08 rules block says 'No previews on list cards', so the consumer no longer renders an extracted code at list scale. That block deliberately kept CompactCodeView ('The concession is not withdrawn - CompactCodeView stays, and a host may still render an extracted code at list scale').

wpass-80y.4 deleted ScannableCardRowTile for exactly the disuse the Dormant marker describes, which makes the two decisions inconsistent on their face. Either the difference is real and should be stated (a code render is plausibly reusable mechanism; a row register is a specific list shape that is gone), or CompactCodeView and its concession follow the row tile out.

Check first whether walt-android composes CompactCodeView anywhere — wpass-80y.4 did not verify this, only that the concession is marked unexercised. If a consumer still composes it, this closes as no-change with a note on the asymmetry.

title: ScannableCardScreen: treat a fully transparent faceTint as no tint
description:
wpass-80y.1 gates the scannable card face on `faceTint.isSpecified` alone (ScannableCardScreen.kt CodeCard). wpass-80y.2 landed the document arm a day later with a stricter gate — `documentFaceIsTinted() = isSpecified && alpha > 0f` — because `Color.isSpecified` is true for `Color.Transparent`, so a specified fully transparent tint reads as 'tinted'.

Consequence on the scannable surface: a transparent tint paints a transparent face (host paint shows through) and `inkOn(Color.Transparent)` sees luminance 0, so it returns white ink. On a light host background that is white-on-light. Both KDocs say 'pass an opaque color', and the trust caption cannot be lost either way, so this is a legibility hazard for a careless consumer, not a trust-signal hole. Recorded as a known divergence in the 'colour carries no trust meaning' row of docs/SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md (wpass-80y.3).

## What

Give ScannableCardScreen the same gate the document arm uses, so a fully transparent tint falls back to `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface` + `onSurface` rather than painting nothing and deriving ink from a transparent colour. Consider hoisting the predicate rather than copying it — passes-ui and passes-document-ui have no dependency edge between them, and wpass-nbr already tracks a shared home for the duplicated CARD_RADIUS token.

## Tests

Mirror `DocumentFaceTintTest.fullyTransparentTintFallsBackToTheDefaultFrame` on the scannable side. Update the threat-model row to drop the recorded divergence once it lands.
notes: Fixed in PR #207 (branch wpass-80y.5). Gate hoisted to passes-ui-core as `faceIsTinted` rather than copied — both arms now share one predicate. Also extracted `facePaint` (internal, theme tokens injected) on the scannable side so the resolution is pinnable; verified the new test fails against the old gate. Threat-model divergence row replaced; C2 matrix updated. wpass-nbr (CARD_RADIUS/FACE_RADIUS dedup) deliberately left alone — it has an open constant-vs-theme-token question the predicate does not share.
close_reason: Merged as PR #207. Gate hoisted to passes-ui-core as faceIsTinted (shared by both arms); facePaint extracted so the resolution is pinnable; ScannableCardFaceTintInstrumentedTest added with a managed-device matrix and CI step, verified green on API 28/31/34/36.

title: Extract the repeated DocumentSemantics / ThemedHost test fixture in passes-document-ui
description:
Five test classes in `passes-document-ui/src/test` each re-declare the same placeholder `DocumentSemantics` and a private `ThemedHost` composable, and several re-declare a fake `PdfRendererBinder`:

- `DocumentTrustSurfaceTest`
- `DocumentViewPagerPrefetchTest`
- `ConsumerRenderFailureMappingTest`
- `DocumentFaceTintTest` (wpass-80y.2)
- plus the `androidTest` `DocumentViewInstrumentedTest`

Each new surface test pays the same ~15 lines of boilerplate, and the semantics fixtures have already drifted (`DocumentTrustSurfaceTest` sets `captionIconTint` explicitly; the others do not).

A shared test fixture — placeholder semantics + `ThemedHost` + a recording binder — would cut the per-test cost and stop the fixtures diverging. Keep the divergence that is deliberate (the explicit `captionIconTint` exercises a distinct non-default tint) as an override on the shared fixture rather than a separate copy.

Pure test-side cleanup: no production code, no surface change. Found in review of wpass-80y.2 (PR #204).

title: Hoist the shared card-anatomy radius onto one token (passes-ui + passes-document-ui)
description:
Both UI modules now hard-code the 26.08.08 design's card-anatomy radius of 20.dp for the same spec:

- `passes-ui/.../ScannableCardScreen.kt` — `CARD_RADIUS` (wpass-80y.1)
- `passes-document-ui/.../DocumentView.kt` — `FACE_RADIUS` (wpass-80y.2)

Two copies of one design token drift silently when the design revises the radius. `passes-ui-core` exists precisely so these two modules share primitives without depending on each other, and it is the obvious home.

## The question to settle first

Whether this should be a shared CONSTANT in passes-ui-core at all, or a THEME TOKEN on the sibling semantics types (`PassesSemantics` / `DocumentSemantics`). CLAUDE.local.md's theming rule is that walt-android is authoritative for visual values and `passes-ui` never hard-codes brand values — by that rule a corner radius arguably belongs in the semantics contract the consumer fulfils, not in a kernel constant. Both surfaces hard-code it today, so this is a pre-existing inconsistency the tint work inherited rather than introduced.

Deciding that is the substance of this bead; the mechanical dedup is small either way.

## Also in scope

The two surfaces implementing one spec already diverge on padding: `ScannableCardScreen` applies `CARD_PADDING = 18.dp` per the spec, while the document face keeps its pre-existing 16dp/8dp content inset. Either reconcile them or record why the document face differs (the page render is letterboxed content, not a laid-out card body, so the spec's card padding may simply not apply).

Found in review of wpass-80y.2 (PR #204).

title: ScannableCardRowTile: resolve the accent contract now that per-item colour is back
description:
Design source (authoritative for all design questions): https://www.figma.com/design/N26Fe2mNKzMoLnNkFXb4Kk/26.08.08---Pass-color-selector?node-id=0-1

## The conflict

`ScannableCardRowTile`'s KDoc pins the leading strip to `LocalPassesSemantics.current.unverifiedArtifact.accent` and is explicit that it must be "NOT the user's chosen card.color - that would re-create the verified-band read at list scale".

The 26.08.08 design gives every list card a class tint that the user can reassign per item. That is exactly the thing the KDoc refuses.

## Consequence for the standing plan

walt-android **wlt-fse** (collapse `ScannableCardSummaryRow` onto this tile) was sequenced behind two preconditions: chosen-colour removal (wlt-z17, done) and a `leadingSlot` parameter (wpass-2a2, done). Both landed - and then the design brought chosen colour back, for all four artifact classes rather than scannables only. The collapse is blocked again, on the original divergence.

## Decide one of

1. **Parameterize the accent** the way wpass-2a2 parameterized the leading slot, letting the consumer pass a tint, with the trust argument moved onto the wpass-80y.3 amendment (colour carries no trust meaning, so a consumer-chosen accent is no longer the hazard the KDoc describes). Unblocks wlt-fse.
2. **Decline the collapse permanently** and record that `ScannableCardSummaryRow` is a standing Walt-side divergence, the same documented-fallback posture as `WaltSecuritySheets` (wlt-owh) and `DocumentSummaryRow`. Close wlt-fse as superseded.

Option 1 only makes sense if wpass-80y.3 lands first and actually concludes colour is trust-neutral. Sequence accordingly; do not parameterize the accent ahead of the threat-model amendment that would justify it.

## Deliverable either way

The KDoc stops contradicting the shipped consumer design, and wlt-fse gets an unambiguous answer instead of sitting deferred against preconditions that have quietly reversed.
notes: Resolved in PR #208 (stacked on #207) as NEITHER option: the tile had no consumer, so the accent question was moot. Deleted ScannableCardRowTile + leadingSlot (wpass-2a2) + its tests; C1/C2 wallet-row concession marked WITHDRAWN (not deleted) in the threat model, with the conditions and re-argument bar recorded. HostedTypeRow's 'why this is bounded' argument re-based off the deleted tile onto 'no verified affordance on any list card'. Evidence: walt-android ScannableCardSummaryRow is a 14-line vestige, wallet list is WalletStack (wlt-38v8.3), zero references to ScannableCardRowTile anywhere. wlt-fse should be closed as superseded — its deletion target no longer exists. Noted for later: the CompactCodeView concession carries the same Dormant marker; keeping it was a deliberate separate decision.
close_reason: Merged as PR #208. Resolved as neither bead option: ScannableCardRowTile had no consumer, so the accent question was moot. Tile + leadingSlot + tests deleted; C1/C2 wallet-row concession marked WITHDRAWN in the threat model with the re-argument bar recorded.

title: passes-pdf and passes-image watchdog budgets are unobserved - not in the connected-tests matrix
description:
ci.yml runs connected tests for :passes-storage and :passes-barcode only. passes-pdf and passes-image carry the same 5000 ms isolated-process budget and the same cold-start-inside-the-budget shape that wpass-qw3 confirmed for passes-barcode, but no on-device leg exercises them, so their exposure to the same failure is unmeasured.

Adjacent finding ii from wpass-qw3. Two parts worth separating: (a) whether to add those modules to the matrix at all, given each added GMD leg costs runner wall-clock and wpass-qw3 had to serialize the existing two to stop them contending; (b) whether the onCreate warm-up landed for passes-barcode should be mirrored into PdfRendererService and ImageDecodeService regardless.
notes:
Branch review of the wpass-qw3 fix (PR #202) sharpened the second half of this issue: passes-image's ImageDecodeService and passes-pdf's PdfRendererService BOTH use the same watchdog-then-kill pattern with (a) no onCreate warm-up, so cold class-loading is inside the budget, and (b) no timeout/unavailable split in their reject taxonomies - ImageDecodeRejectedKind.DecoderUnavailable carries the same four-way conflation DecodeFailureReason.DecoderUnavailable did.

The root cause wpass-qw3 confirmed is a property of the isolated-worker PATTERN, not of barcode decoding: a freshly forked sandbox on a loaded machine spends its budget on class loading. passes-image runs the same ImageDecoder path in the same kind of sandbox.

So this issue now has three parts:
 (a) whether to add these modules to the connected-tests matrix at all (each GMD leg costs runner wall-clock, and wpass-qw3 had to serialize the existing two to stop them contending);
 (b) mirror the onCreate warm-up into PdfRendererService and ImageDecodeService regardless of (a);
 (c) mirror the timeout/unavailable taxonomy split into ImageDecodeRejectedKind, and consider whether passes-pdf's DocumentRejectedKind needs the same.

Note (c) has a cross-repo cost like the barcode one did - see wlt-ym8w in walt-android for the shape of the consumer break a taxonomy widening causes.

title: Give the 5000 ms decode/render watchdog budget an empirical basis
description:
The 5000 ms watchdog budget is carried verbatim by BarcodeDecodeConfig.DEFAULT_DECODE_TIMEOUT_MS, PdfImportConfig.DEFAULT_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS and ImageDecodeConfig.DEFAULT_DECODE_TIMEOUT_MS, and a grep of docs/adr and PDF_THREAT_MODEL finds no rationale for the value - only 'watchdog test covers timeout-then-kill' (ADR 0005 D7).

Step 4 of the wpass-qw3 recommendation, deliberately deferred: do NOT retune the number until there is a measured real-device baseline for what a benign decode actually costs, warm, across the API matrix. wpass-qw3 removed the cold-start component from the budget, so a baseline taken now measures decode work rather than class loading.

Note ipass-sry's lesson from the iOS kernel: wall clock measures the machine's contention, not the algorithm. That applies to how the baseline is TAKEN, not to the guard itself - CPU time would never fire on the blocked slow-loris read the watchdog exists to bound.

title: Create the dependabot labels the config references
description:
Dependabot reports on every run: 'The following labels could not be found: automated, dependencies.' The repo only has the nine GitHub default labels; .github/dependabot.yml asks for 'dependencies', 'automated', 'build-logic' and 'github-actions'. title: Threat model: amend C5 for composite image-decode (decoding of untrusted bytes now occurs, confined)
description: The composite barcoded-image artifact (wpass-8lu) lets consumers (walt-android epic wlt-yjn5) decode user-supplied image bytes to extract a barcode. title: Decision: live camera decode runs in-process, not in the isolated sandbox
description:
Record the architecture decision: LIVE camera decode runs IN-PROCESS, not in the `:barcodeDecoder` isolated sandbox.

Rationale (full evidence in the completed report bead wpass-7xo.1): the raw-YUV `ImageAnalysis` path invokes no still-image codec, so the hostile-file -> codec-RCE vector the sandbox exists to contain is structurally absent; and the `passes-isolation` transport is one-shot / blocking and cannot stream frames. The static-image path REMAINS isolated, because it does parse attacker-controlled compressed containers.

Consequence: the live path reuses only the pure-JVM `decodeLuminance` core; it declares no `CAMERA` permission and adds no Android dependency to the kernel. Consistent with the CLAUDE.md trust model (isolation is mechanism for the codec surface, not a blanket requirement).
acceptance_criteria: Decision captured with rationale and link to wpass-7xo.1; consistent with CLAUDE.md trust model (isolation contains the codec surface, which the live path lacks).
notes: Decision recorded as ADR 0008 (docs/adr/0008-live-camera-decode-in-process.md) and bd remember key decision-wpass-7xo-live-decode-in-process, both linking the evidence base wpass-7xo.1. Consistent with CLAUDE.md trust model + ADR 0005 D3: isolation is mechanism for the native codec surface, which the raw-YUV live path does not invoke.
close_reason: Decision captured: live-camera decode runs in-process. ADR 0008 + bd remember entry, both linked to wpass-7xo.1; consistent with ADR 0005 D3 / CLAUDE.md trust model.

title: Spike: OEM HAL ImageAnalysis output-format variability on walt.is degoogled targets
description:
Spike: confirm that CameraX `ImageAnalysis` delivers raw demosaiced `YUV_420_888` (the documented default) on the de-Googled devices the walt.is channel targets, versus any implementation-defined / differently-strided / PRIV output that would need extra handling and could conceivably route through a codec. The stride-padding nuance (ZXing #1387) hints at OEM variability.

Output: a device x output-format matrix and confirmation that no still-image codec sits in the frame path on the real target hardware. Informs the YUV frame adapter's input contract and robustness. May be executed partly consumer-side (walt-android holds the device matrix + the CameraX pipeline); file the consumer half there if so.

This is an open evidence gap flagged by the research (wpass-7xo.1), not a blocker for the kernel adapter, which is written against a `byte[]` + geometry signature.
design:
# Spike wpass-7xo.3 — OEM HAL ImageAnalysis output-format variability (COMPLETED 2026-06-05)

Resolves the one open empirical question ADR 0008 D1 flagged ("could qualify the
'no codec' claim on a specific device"). Outcome: the codec-absence claim holds
STRUCTURALLY across every walt.is target class; the only real variability is plane
geometry, which the `decodeYPlane` `byte[]` + geometry signature already absorbs.
No contract change required.

## Scope / method

This is the KERNEL-FACING half: what the Android platform CONTRACT guarantees across
HALs, which is what the pure-JVM `decodeYPlane` contract must be robust to. The
on-device EMPIRICAL half (dump real `ImageProxy` planes per physical device, confirm a
decodable luminance buffer) is the consumer's job and is already filed as `wlt-mwj.6`.
Method here: Android camera2 / CameraX platform docs + the CameraX-developers thread on
the `YUV_420_888` underlying format; builds on the verified evidence base wpass-7xo.1.

## Target hardware (walt.is)

Two distribution channels (docs/decisions-and-learnings.md): the direct-APK channel —
"Degoogled / GrapheneOS / privacy-focused", predominantly Pixel hardware on
GrapheneOS/CalyxOS plus Fairphone / LineageOS / e-OS — and the Google Play open-testing
channel — arbitrary stock-Android OEMs. minSdk 28 (Android 9). CameraX is the capture
API on the consumer side (wlt-mwj).

## Device x output-format matrix (contract-level)

| Target class | camera2 HW level | CameraX ImageAnalysis output (default) | Still-image codec in frame path? | decodeYPlane handling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pixel + GrapheneOS/CalyxOS (PRIMARY degoogled channel) | FULL / LEVEL_3 | YUV_420_888, well-formed 3-plane | NONE | zero-copy rowStride strip |
| Fairphone / LineageOS / e-OS (degoogled, modern SoC) | LIMITED–FULL | YUV_420_888 | NONE | rowStride strip; pixelStride repack if semi-planar Y |
| Stock-Android Play channel, modern OEM (Samsung/Xiaomi/…) | LIMITED–LEVEL_3 | YUV_420_888 | NONE | rowStride strip; pixelStride repack |
| Old/budget LEGACY OEM (Play long tail only) | LEGACY | YUV_420_888 (emulated over camera1; possible 1-px luminance shift) | NONE | works; 1-px shift tolerated by binarizer |

Across EVERY class the ImageAnalysis output is `YUV_420_888` and NO still-image codec
sits in the frame path. Variability is confined to (a) plane stride geometry and (b) a
LEGACY-only conversion-quality artifact — neither touches codec-absence.

## Findings

1. YUV_420_888 IS THE CROSS-DEVICE ANALYSIS FORMAT, NOT IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED.
   Official guidance: "if the goal is to maximize compatibility, use ImageFormat.YUV_420_888
   for frame analysis and ImageFormat.JPEG for still images." CameraX `ImageAnalysis`
   default output is `YUV_420_888` (RGBA_8888 only on explicit `setOutputImageFormat`
   opt-in). `IMPLEMENTATION_DEFINED` / `PRIVATE` (PRIV) is the OPAQUE GPU/preview-surface
   format (SurfaceView/SurfaceTexture); it is never delivered as readable bytes to an
   `Analyzer`, because CameraX requests `YUV_420_888` for the analysis stream. So the
   "PRIV format that needs extra handling / could invoke a codec" worry does not
   materialize on the ImageAnalysis path.

2. CODEC ABSENCE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT PER-DEVICE. camera2 `YUV_420_888` is raw demosaiced
   ISP sensor output. The still-image codec is a SEPARATE camera2 output format
   (`ImageFormat.JPEG`, and HEIC) consumed only by CameraX `ImageCapture` — a use case
   wlt-mwj does NOT bind (constraint #2). An ImageAnalysis stream bound to YUV therefore
   never routes bytes through libjpeg/Skia/libwebp/Quram. This is the structural basis
   ADR 0008 D1 rests on and it is HAL-independent: no OEM HAL turns an ImageAnalysis YUV
   stream into a codec-decoded stream.

3. THE REAL VARIABILITY IS PLANE GEOMETRY — ALREADY IN-CONTRACT. `YUV_420_888` is a
   generic 4:2:0 family: per-plane `rowStride` (padding, rowStride >= width) and
   `pixelStride` (1 for planar, 2 for semi-planar/interleaved Y) vary by HAL (ZXing
   #1387). `decodeYPlane(yPlane, width, height, rowStride, pixelStride, reverseHorizontal)`
   already absorbs both: zero-copy `dataWidth = rowStride` strip when `pixelStride == 1`,
   tight `packTight` repack when `pixelStride > 1`, and `reverseHorizontal` for the
   mirrored front camera. The `byte[] + ints` shape is exactly the right robustness
   envelope — confirmed, no signature change.

4. LEGACY-ONLY 1-PIXEL-SHIFT ARTIFACT (does NOT qualify codec-absence). The
   CameraX-developers thread "ImageAnalysis YUV_420_888 underlying format" documents that
   on SOME LEGACY-level devices CameraX's internal RGB->YUV conversion shifts the Y data
   by one pixel (CameraX-team-acknowledged, no API-layer fix; reproduces on e.g. Galaxy J2
   Pro but not OPPO A75 — inconsistent within LEGACY). This is a luminance-QUALITY bug,
   NOT a codec and NOT a format change: it does not invoke any still-image parser and does
   not alter the `byte[]` contract. A 1-px luminance shift is within QR/1D binarizer
   tolerance. It is also OUT OF SCOPE for the primary degoogled channel: Pixels are
   FULL/LEVEL_3, never LEGACY. It only touches the Play-channel long tail of old/budget
   LEGACY OEM hardware, and is the consumer's empirical concern (wlt-mwj.6), not a kernel
   contract issue.

## Where this tightens / qualifies the contract

The `decodeYPlane` signature needs NO change. The qualification is a USAGE constraint the
consumer (wlt-mwj) must honor, recorded so the audit trail is explicit:

- KEEP ImageAnalysis on the DEFAULT `YUV_420_888`; feed `getPlanes()[0]` (the Y plane) to
  `decodeYPlane`. If the consumer ever opts into `OUTPUT_IMAGE_FORMAT_RGBA_8888`, plane[0]
  is single-plane packed ARGB, NOT luminance — feeding it to `decodeYPlane` would hand the
  binarizer garbage. This is the one realistic way to misuse a correct kernel contract.
  (Added as guidance on wlt-mwj.6.)
- No crop is exposed in v1; the full plane decodes. A future crop overload is additive
  and breaks no caller (already noted in the KDoc).

## Kernel-facing conclusion

CONFIRMED: on every walt.is target class, CameraX `ImageAnalysis` delivers raw demosaiced
`YUV_420_888` with NO still-image codec in the frame path; the contract-relevant
variability (rowStride padding, pixelStride interleave, front-camera mirroring) is fully
absorbed by the existing `decodeYPlane` `byte[]` + geometry signature. The lone residual
(LEGACY 1-px luminance shift) is a quality artifact on the Play-channel old-hardware tail,
not a codec and not a kernel contract issue. ADR 0008 D1's "no codec" claim stands
unqualified for the standard raw-YUV case; the spike does not reopen the in-process
placement. The on-device per-model confirmation is handed to the consumer as wlt-mwj.6.

## Sources

- developer.android.com/media/camera/camerax/analyze (ImageAnalysis default YUV_420_888; RGBA_8888 opt-in)
- developer.android.com/media/camera/camera2/multiple-camera-streams-simultaneously (YUV_420_888 for analysis / JPEG for stills = max compatibility; PRIV = opaque preview/GPU)
- groups.google.com/a/android.com/g/camerax-developers/c/ubSCpBJKIJg (LEGACY 1-px-shift artifact, CameraX team)
- Evidence base: wpass-7xo.1 (codec-absence 3-0, ZXing #1387 stride nuance); ADR 0008 D1; decodeYPlane KDoc (YPlaneFrameDecode.kt)
acceptance_criteria: Documented target-device/output-format matrix; confirmation ImageAnalysis output is raw (no codec in the frame path); any extra adapter handling for the YUV frame decode identified.
close_reason: Spike complete: confirmed CameraX ImageAnalysis delivers raw YUV_420_888 with NO still-image codec in the frame path across all walt.is target classes (Pixel/GrapheneOS FULL/LEVEL_3 -> degoogled LIMITED+ -> stock OEM -> LEGACY tail). Codec-absence is structural (JPEG/HEIC is a separate camera2 format used only by ImageCapture, unbound by the live path), not per-device; PRIV is opaque GPU/preview, never delivered to an Analyzer. Only cross-HAL variability is plane geometry (rowStride/pixelStride), already absorbed by decodeYPlane - no contract change. LEGACY-only 1-px luminance-shift noted as a non-codec quality artifact on the Play-channel old-hardware tail. Device x output-format matrix + sources in design field; bd remember spike-wpass-7xo3-imageanalysis-yuv-codec-absence; ADR 0008 follow-up resolved (PR #133); consumer empirical half handed to wlt-mwj.6.

- Aligns with wlt-ygl's DocumentOpener direction - coordinate so the facade covers both PDF-open and image-decode worker shapes.

title: Remove ScannableCard.color, ScannableColor value class, and storage column (Stage 2 of chosen-colour tearout)
description:
## What

Drop the user-selectable colour feature from the kernel. After this lands:
- `ScannableCard.color: ScannableColor?` field removed.
- `ScannableCardCreateInput.color: ScannableColor?` field removed.
- `ScannableColor` value class deleted.
- `passes-storage` migration drops the `color` column from the scannable_cards table.
- Kernel version bump.

## Why

Walt (the sole consumer) has dropped the field in walt-android `wlt-z17` (Stage 1). With no consumer reading or writing the field, it's dead weight in the public API and dormant user-private data in the SQLCipher store. No kernel render surface ever read `card.color` - `ScannableCardScreen`, `ScannableCardTile`, and `ScannableCardRowTile` all theme via `MaterialTheme.colorScheme`, never via the card. The kernel `ScannableCardRowTile` KDoc is explicit that per-card user colour on the strip is the wrong shape ("would re-create the verified-band read at list scale"); the field's existence was a Walt-side feature the kernel tolerated rather than blessed.

## Hard precondition

**This bead cannot ship until walt-android `wlt-z17` lands.** If the kernel field disappears before Walt drops the `color = null` reference in `CreateScannableCardViewModel`, Walt fails to compile against the new kernel. Sequence:

1. `wlt-z17` lands in walt-android (kernel field still present, Walt passes `null`).
2. This bead ships in passes-android with a major-version bump (breaking public API change).
3. Walt bumps the kernel dep, compile errors surface at the now-deleted `color` parameter, Walt deletes those parameter passes.

Step 3 is a small follow-up in walt-android. File a tracking bead in walt-android for the version bump + cleanup once the kernel release is cut.

## Files to change

- `passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/ScannableCard.kt`
  - Line 22: drop `public val color: ScannableColor?`.
  - Lines 34-43: delete the `ScannableColor` value class and its KDoc.
- `passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/ScannableCardCreateInput.kt`
  - Line 17: drop `public val color: ScannableColor?`.
- `passes-core` validator (wherever `ScannableCardCreateResult.Success` constructs `ScannableCard` from `ScannableCardCreateInput`): drop the colour pass-through.
- `passes-storage` (Room/SQLCipher schema for scannable_cards):
  - Drop the `color` column from the entity / DAO.
  - Add a migration that drops the column. SQLCipher table-rewrite migration; preserve all other columns and row identity.
  - Update migration tests to cover the drop (existing rows survive, new rows omit the column).
- `passes-ui/src/test/kotlin/is/walt/passes/ui/PublicApiSurfaceTest.kt` line 272: drop the `assertThat(color.argb)...` assertion when constructing the test `ScannableCard`.
- Any other test fixtures across `passes-core`, `passes-storage`, `passes-ui` that build `ScannableCard` or `ScannableCardCreateInput` with a `color =` argument: drop the argument.

## Surface-lock impact

`ScannableCard` is a public data class with internal constructor (`@ConsistentCopyVisibility`). Dropping a field is a breaking change to:
- `equals` / `hashCode` (one fewer component).
- `copy()` signature (`color` argument gone).
- Component functions (`componentN` indices shift).

Public API surface-lock tests in `passes-core` and `passes-ui` need updating. Search for `ScannableColor` references in `src/test` and prune.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `ScannableColor` value class deleted; `grep -r ScannableColor src/main` returns empty across all kernel modules.
- [ ] `passes-storage` migration drops the column; migration test verifies existing rows survive with `color` data lost (acceptable per Walt's Stage 1 rationale - Walt already stopped reading it).
- [ ] All kernel tests pass.
- [ ] Public API surface-lock tests updated.
- [ ] Version bumped (major - breaking public API).
- [ ] Release notes mention this is a coordinated change with walt-android `wlt-z17`.

title: ScannableCardRowTile: add leadingSlot parameter for consumer-side format glyph
description:
## What

Add `leadingSlot: @Composable () -> Unit = {}` parameter to public `ScannableCardRowTile` (passes-ui), positioned between the leading accent strip and the label/format Column.

## Why

Walt (wlt-5wz) defers collapsing its consumer-side `ScannableCardSummaryRow` onto `ScannableCardRowTile` because the kernel tile has no slot for the leading format-glyph tile that visually rhymes the row with `PassSummaryRow`'s logo tile and `DocumentSummaryRow`'s page thumbnail. The kernel KDoc already documents the workaround ("Consumers wanting a richer leading slot ... layer that themselves in their own wrapper"); promoting the pattern to a first-class parameter lets Walt collapse fully.

Analog to wpass-48v / wlt-owh: kernel parameterizes the divergence point, consumer collapses its reimplementation. The trust-model contract (no signature dot, neutral kernel strip, FSI/PDI isolation on label, format token in mergedSemantics) is unaffected - `leadingSlot` is a visual hook, not a trust signal.

## Surface

```kotlin
@Composable
public fun ScannableCardRowTile(
    card: ScannableCard,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    leadingSlot: @Composable () -> Unit = {},  // NEW
)
```

Default empty `{}` preserves existing call sites and the current "minimal row" register. Consumer that wants the icon passes `leadingSlot = { ScannableFormatTile(...) }`. The slot sits inside the row's `mergeDescendants` block, so a slot composable that exposes only `Icon(contentDescription = null, ...)` won't add to the merged `contentDescription` - the format token still comes from the kernel-built string.

## Surface-lock impact

`scannableCardRowTileHasExactlyThreeUserVisibleParameters` (per kernel KDoc) becomes "...exactly four user-visible parameters" with the new test pinning `leadingSlot` as the only addition. Threat-model invariants (no signature affordance, no per-card colour on strip) stay pinned.

## Cross-repo references

- Consumer (Walt): wlt-5wz (decision deferred); future Walt-side collapse bead will depend on this issue.
- Walt decisions-and-learnings entry: "ScannableCardSummaryRow collapse onto kernel ScannableCardRowTile is deferred, not declined" (2026-05-19).
- Precedent for this shape: wpass-48v (security sheets emphasisStyle), wpass-pnb (this tile shipping in the first place).

## Definition of done

- `leadingSlot` parameter added with default `{}`.
- Surface-lock test updated to pin the 4-parameter shape.
- KDoc updated to document the slot (replace the "layer that themselves in their own wrapper" suggestion with "pass via leadingSlot" guidance).
- No behaviour change at existing call sites (default arg).
close_reason: Merged in PR #97 (commit a5898e1). leadingSlot parameter shipped; walt-android wlt-5wz can now collapse ScannableCardSummaryRow onto the kernel tile.
