title: passes-ui: ScannableCardRowTile sibling composable for homogeneous wallet-row register
description:
Parent: wpass-hy2 (kernel hooks for walt-android trust-aware host opt-outs).
Cross-repo source: wlt-6ub.4 (walt-android).
Consumer epic: wlt-6ub in walt-android (UX redesign for ScannableCard).

## What

Add a sibling composable in `passes-ui` exposing `ScannableCard` in a wallet-row register (label + leading accent slot only), so a consumer integrating ScannableCards inline with `PassSummaryRow` / `DocumentSummaryRow` does not need to reimplement the row Walt-side.

## Why

walt-android's ScannableCard UX (epic wlt-6ub, shipped 2026-05-18) renders ScannableCards inline with passes/PDFs in a single wallet list, mirroring `PassSummaryRow` pixel-for-pixel. The existing `ScannableCardTile` carries four hard-coded artifact-class distinguishers (`ScannableCardTile.kt:38-73`):

  1. Dashed outline
  2. Leading accent-colored band
  3. Smaller corner radius (8 dp vs PassFront's 16 dp)
  4. Non-suppressible `ScannableCardTrustCaption` ("Created by you")

None of those four can be selectively disabled today. The consumer currently has to reimplement the row Walt-side (`ScannableCardSummaryRow` in walt-android `feature/passes`). This is the documented fallback pattern, analogous to wpass-48v / wlt-owh for the security sheets. It works but it's the wrong long-term shape:

- The kernel's `ComposableSurfaceLockTest` is intended to catch drift on `ScannableCardTile`. A Walt-side rebuild bypasses that lock, so a future kernel restyle of `ScannableCardTile` doesn't propagate to the wallet-row register.
- Two consumers wanting the same wallet-row register would each reimplement the row, multiplying divergence.

## Proposed shape

Sibling composable (not a parameter on existing tile):

```kotlin
@Composable
public fun ScannableCardRowTile(
    card: ScannableCard,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
)
```

Why sibling, not parameter:

- The KDoc on `ScannableCardTile` and `ComposableSurfaceLockTest` lock the four-distinguisher contract very deliberately. A parameter to elide that contract is a sharper change than adding a second composable beside it.
- The sibling carries its own surface-lock test against accidental drift of *its* shape.
- Same shape as `PassSummaryRow` / `DocumentSummaryRow` already in the kernel — a row composable is the natural register at this surface.

## Trust contract guarantees

`ScannableCardRowTile` must preserve:

- `isolated()` wrap on `card.label` (FSI/PDI bidi-isolation against directional-format injection, same as `ScannableCardTile`).
- Detail-surface trust signal — `ScannableCardScreen` and its bottom-docked `ScannableCardTrustCaption` are untouched. The full trust caption surfaces when the user is about to *use* the artifact; this concession is list-row only.

## Threat-model concession

`docs/SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md` C1 / C2 today say the artifact-class distinction must hold at every surface. Cole's product call (2026-05-18) is to drop the distinction at the list-row register only, while preserving it at the detail surface. Bundle a doc update into this bead's PR:

- C1 / C2: add a "consumer-side concession" subsection documenting that a wallet-row register is permitted when (a) the row carries no signature dot, (b) the row has no coloured leading strip that could read as a verified band, and (c) the detail surface retains the non-suppressible bottom-docked trust caption.
- Reference the consumer epic (wlt-6ub) and consumer test invariant (`WalletListTest` pins "no scannable-card row owns a signature dot").

## Out of scope

- Any change to `ScannableCardTile`. Existing four-distinguisher contract stays.
- Any change to `ScannableCardScreen` or its bottom-docked caption. Detail-surface trust signal is untouched.
- Consumer-side rebuild. walt-android `ScannableCardSummaryRow` ships as the documented fallback regardless of whether this lands; once `ScannableCardRowTile` lands the consumer collapses into a kernel call.

## Definition of done

- `ScannableCardRowTile` exists in `passes-ui`, public.
- Surface-lock test in `ComposableSurfaceLockTest` (or sibling) locks its visual shape.
- `docs/SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md` updated with the consumer-side concession.
- KDoc on the new composable cites wpass-hy2 as parent and the wlt-6ub consumer epic as motivation.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #95 (squash-merged as 9413701). ScannableCardRowTile public, surface-lock pinned at param count 3, no overload, SCANNABLE_CARD_THREAT_MODEL.md C1/C2 concession subsection added. TalkBack reachability of the format token pinned by review fixes.

title: ScannableCardId leaks autoincrement row id through stringified surface
description:
The kernel-facing ScannableCardId.value exposed by passes-storage is the stringified SQLite autoincrement row id (see SqlCipherScannableCardStore.toCardOrNull and SqlCipherPassRepository.createScannableCard listAll path). Autoincrement is monotonic and not reset on delete, so anything outside the storage layer that surfaces or persists this id leaks 'approximate count of cards ever created'.

Impact is low on a single-user wallet (worst case: roughly 'user has had ~10 cards over time'), but the ScannableCardId KDoc frames the value as an opaque string identifier and the value-class shape was clearly chosen with opacity in mind. The current implementation weakens that framing.

Options:
1. Mint a UUID at insert time, store alongside the row id (keep INTEGER PRIMARY KEY for joins; expose UUID as ScannableCardId).
2. Acknowledge the leak in ScannableCardId KDoc and accept it (cheapest, most honest).

Picked up by review of PR #85. Deferred from wpass-lzi.6 since the leak is cosmetic on a single-user wallet.

title: passes-ui: PassFront — add showSignatureBadge parameter so consumers can suppress the in-card trust badge
description:
Source: walt-android epic wlt-byd, child wlt-fxz (surface #1 — 'Import confirm Verified path'). Parent kernel epic: **wpass-hy2**.

## Ask

Add an opt-in parameter to `PassFront`:

```kotlin
@Composable
public fun PassFront(
    pass: Pass,
    signatureStatus: SignatureStatus,
    telemetry: UiTelemetryGuard,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    locale: PassLocale = PassLocale("en"),
    nowEpochMillis: Long = System.currentTimeMillis(),
    showSignatureBadge: Boolean = true,  // NEW
)
```

When `showSignatureBadge = false`, the internal `SignatureTrustBadge` call inside `PassFrontSurface` (`PassFront.kt:140`) MUST NOT render. The header row keeps the organization-name slot but drops the trailing badge.

## Why

walt-android's import-confirm Verified surface (wlt-fxz) hosts the pass with its own `TrustChip(band = Verified)` on a metadata row directly above `PassFront`. Both badges carry the same trust signal — letting the kernel render its own would double-label the user with two visually different "this is verified" affordances.

The Walt wrapper cannot suppress `SignatureTrustBadge` from outside; it is private to `PassFront.kt`. Today the consumer either:

1. Ships with both badges (kernel + walt). Redundant, visually noisy.
2. Reaches into kernel internals — not an option.

An opt-in boolean is the honest API.

## Trust contract

This parameter does NOT touch the surrounding non-suppressible trust surfaces:

- `PassImportConfirm`'s `ImportTrustCaption` is unaffected (different composable, different surface).
- `onPassRendered(type, band)` telemetry still fires unconditionally on `PassFront` entry.
- The default (`showSignatureBadge = true`) preserves today's behavior exactly — the badge is only suppressed when the host explicitly opts out and disclosed the trust signal in its own chrome.

The trust contract on `PassFront` is that the *band* must be derivable and `onPassRendered` must fire — both still hold. The visual badge is a presentation, not a contract; a host that's already disclosed the band has standing to suppress one of two redundant renderings.

## Acceptance

- Default (`showSignatureBadge = true`) is behavior-identical to today — no visual change for existing consumers.
- `showSignatureBadge = false` renders `PassFront` without the trailing `SignatureTrustBadge` pill in the header row; everything else unchanged.
- `onPassRendered` telemetry fires regardless of the boolean.
- `PublicApiSurfaceTest` updated for the new parameter.
close_reason: Merged via PR #96 (e887c88) — passes-ui: R2 host opt-outs for PassFront and security sheets

title: Passes R2 UX redesign: kernel hooks for walt-android trust-aware host opt-outs
description:
Parent epic for kernel-side support of walt-android's second passes redesign (consumer epic: **wlt-byd** in walt-android repo). Design source of truth: `docs/design_handoff_passes_r2/README.md` in walt-android (sign-off ready).

## Background

walt-android is restyling six passes surfaces (import confirm, tampered rejection, pkpass detail, expired pass detail, B3 security sheets). The redesign keeps every kernel trust contract intact — non-suppressible target-string display (ADR 0005 D5), `DocumentTrustCaption`, `PassImportConfirm`'s issuer-trust caption, `PassFront` signature chrome — and where Walt wants a different visual treatment, it wraps or opts out at the host level rather than mutating kernel composables.

For six of the six surfaces, Walt can ship without any kernel edit. **For two of them, the host-side workaround is brittle enough that an opt-in kernel parameter is worth the small surface bump.** Those two are this epic.

## Design goals (consumer-side)

The redesign optimizes for one thing: **trust signals must read as trust signals, and nothing else should**. Specifically:

- A pass-issuer Verified band must not visually equate with a URL emphasis container. Today they do — both are orange `primaryContainer`.
- An expired pass on the detail screen is archival, not failure. The black `ExpiredOverlay` scrim reads as "something is wrong," but per kernel kdoc on `PassesListUiState` expired passes are kept and shown with the expired badge — they're meant to remain legible.

Both kernel changes here preserve the trust contract while letting hosts choose a layout that doesn't bleed trust semantics into unrelated surfaces.

## Children

- **wpass-d0k** — `PassFront`: add `showExpiredOverlay: Boolean = true` so consumers can suppress the expiry scrim. Default unchanged.
- **wpass-48v** — `B3UrlConfirmSheet` / `PhoneConfirmSheet` / `EmailConfirmSheet`: add `emphasisStyle: B3UrlEmphasisStyle = Container | DomainHero`. Default unchanged. Plus enabler: `B3UrlIntent.registrableDomain` exposed via `FieldLinkScanner`.

## Cross-repo links

- Consumer epic: **wlt-byd** (walt-android repo) — Passes redesign R2.
- Surface mapping:
  - wpass-d0k ↔ wlt-z8g (surface #5: expired pass detail)
  - wpass-48v ↔ wlt-owh (surface #6: URL/Phone/Email security sheets)
- Handoff doc: `docs/design_handoff_passes_r2/README.md` in walt-android.

## Non-goals (filed for clarity)

The walt-android epic floats other surfaces that could become kernel params. They are explicitly NOT in scope here because the host-side wrapper is the preferred shape:

- `PassImportConfirm.compactTrust` — Walt wraps the kernel composable; kernel composable untouched.
- `PassBack` flat-row variant — Walt stops calling `PassBack` on its detail screen; kernel `PassBack` stays for other consumers.
- `PassImportRejectionSheet` Tampered arm — Walt promotes Tampered to a full-screen takeover at the host level; sheet untouched for the other three `ParseFailureKind` arms.

If a future consumer wants any of these as kernel params, file separately.

## Trust contract guarantees

Both children preserve:
- Non-suppressible trust-claim text (issuer band on `PassFront`, full URL/phone/email verbatim in B3 sheets).
- Telemetry callbacks (`onSecuritySheetShown`, confirm/dismiss handlers) fire identically across layouts.
- `PublicApiSurfaceTest` / `DocumentSurfaceLockTest` updated for the new optional params; no breakage of existing call sites.

## Ship order

Independent. Either child can land first; consumer (Walt) ships its fallback today and migrates when a kernel param is published.
notes: Children expanded to 3: wpass-d0k (PassFront.showExpiredOverlay), wpass-48v (B3 emphasisStyle + registrableDomain), wpass-btz (PassFront.showSignatureBadge). All three are independent and optional; consumer ships fallbacks per epic constraints.
close_reason: All 5 children complete (wpass-48v, wpass-a9b, wpass-btz, wpass-d0k, wpass-pnb). Kernel hooks for walt-android trust-aware host opt-outs landed; consumer epic wlt-byd unblocked.

title: passes-ui: B3UrlConfirmSheet / PhoneConfirmSheet / EmailConfirmSheet — add emphasisStyle (Container | DomainHero) layout option
description:
Source: walt-android epic wlt-byd, child wlt-owh (surface #6 — 'URL/Phone/Email security sheets: domain-first restructure'). Handoff: `docs/design_handoff_passes_r2/README.md` (§6) in walt-android.

## Problem

`B3UrlConfirmSheet` puts the verbatim URL inside an orange `primaryContainer` emphasis container (`#d36b42`). That container reads visually identical to the Verified trust band — but **trust does not transfer from pass issuer to linked URL**. The current treatment implies a trust relationship that does not exist.

Same issue applies to `PhoneConfirmSheet` and `EmailConfirmSheet` (same orange container pattern).

## Ask

Add a parameter to all three confirm sheets:

```kotlin
sealed interface B3UrlEmphasisStyle {
    data object Container : B3UrlEmphasisStyle  // current behavior
    data object DomainHero : B3UrlEmphasisStyle  // new
}

@Composable
fun B3UrlConfirmSheet(
    intent: B3UrlIntent,
    fieldLabel: String,
    organizationName: String,
    emphasisStyle: B3UrlEmphasisStyle = B3UrlEmphasisStyle.Container,  // NEW
    onConfirm: () -> Unit,
    onDismiss: () -> Unit,
)
```

(Equivalent additions on Phone/Email sheets — naming TBD; could be `PhoneHero` / `EmailHero` variants of the same enum or sheet-specific enums.)

### DomainHero layout (URL sheet)

- Eyebrow `LEAVING WALT` (labelMedium 600 / 11sp / 0.2em / uppercase / `outline`).
- Hero: registrable domain (`Uri.host` minus `www.` / `m.` prefixes) — 26sp / 600 / line-height 1.05 / -0.035em, `onSurface`.
- Mono forensic row: full URL — `bodyMedium` 12sp / 400 / monospace / `outline`. Scheme + path slightly dimmer (`outline.copy(alpha = 0.7f)`).
- Provenance: `From the {fieldLabel} field on your {organizationName} pass.` (13sp / 400, `onSurfaceVariant`, `fieldLabel` SemiBold + `onSurface`).
- Hairline.
- Action row, 2 equal-width buttons: `OutlinedButton("Cancel")` + `Button("Open in browser")`.

Phone/Email variants follow the same shape: hero = formatted phone / address, mono row = raw digits / address, primary CTA = `Call` / `Compose`.

## Trust contract preserved

- Non-suppressible target string display (ADR 0005 D5 equivalent for B3): the full URL / phone / email is still shown verbatim — just in the forensic mono row rather than the orange container. Trust contract is layout-agnostic; both `Container` and `DomainHero` satisfy it.
- Telemetry: `onSecuritySheetShown` + the action-confirmed/dismissed callbacks fire on the same gestures in both layouts.
- Kernel still owns `ModalBottomSheet` lifecycle and callback dispatch.

## Enabler — registrable-domain extraction belongs in kernel

walt-android needs `registrableDomain: String` (e.g. `tixly.com` from `https://www.tixly.com/refunds`). Doing this consumer-side means every host hand-rolls a public-suffix list — bad.

Proposal: `FieldLinkScanner` already constructs `B3UrlIntent` with the parsed URL. Have it also populate `B3UrlIntent.registrableDomain` at construction time using a single PSL implementation owned by the kernel. Consumers read `intent.registrableDomain`; the `DomainHero` layout consumes it directly.

If PSL is too heavy a dep, fall back to `Uri.host` with `www.` / `m.` strip — document that as a known-imperfect best effort.

## Acceptance

- Default (`emphasisStyle = Container`) is behavior-identical to today.
- `DomainHero` renders the layout above on all three sheet types.
- `B3UrlIntent.registrableDomain` exposed (or equivalent helper on `FieldLinkScanner`).
- Kernel snapshot/screenshot tests cover both branches per sheet.
close_reason: Merged via PR #96 (e887c88) — passes-ui: R2 host opt-outs for PassFront and security sheets

title: passes-ui: PassFront — add showExpiredOverlay parameter so consumers can opt out of expired scrim
description:
Source: walt-android epic wlt-byd, child wlt-z8g (surface #5 — 'Expired pass detail: quiet archival'). Handoff doc: `docs/design_handoff_passes_r2/README.md` (§5) in walt-android.

## Ask

Add an opt-in parameter to `PassFront`:

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PassFront(
    pass: Pass,
    signatureBand: SignatureBand,
    nowEpochMillis: Long = System.currentTimeMillis(),
    showSignatureBadge: Boolean = true,
    showExpiredOverlay: Boolean = true,  // NEW
    ...
)
```

When `showExpiredOverlay = false`, the internal `ExpiredOverlay` (black scrim) MUST NOT render even if `ExpiredOverlayState.from(pass.expirationDate, nowEpochMillis)` would otherwise produce a non-`None` state. All other `PassFront` chrome (issuer trust badge if `showSignatureBadge`, etc.) behaves exactly as today.

## Why

walt-android's expired-pass detail screen reframes expired passes as quiet archival (`PAST PASS` eyebrow + `Expired {date}` pill + washed `PassFront` at alpha 0.78 + saturation 0.4). The kernel's black scrim fights that treatment.

Today walt-android works around this by passing `nowEpochMillis = Long.MAX_VALUE` so `ExpiredOverlayState.from(...)` returns `None`. That's a load-bearing lie about the current time — brittle and confusing to read in walt-side code. An explicit boolean is the honest API.

## Trust contract

This parameter does NOT touch any trust-claim-bearing chrome:

- Signature band / verified badge: gated by separate `showSignatureBadge` parameter, unchanged.
- `DocumentTrustCaption` (passes-pdf-ui): different surface, not affected.
- `PassImportConfirm` trust caption: different surface, not affected.

Only the expiry visual is suppressible. Issuer-level trust signals remain non-suppressible per ADR 0005 D5.

## Acceptance

- Default (`showExpiredOverlay = true`) is behavior-identical to today — no visual change for existing consumers.
- `showExpiredOverlay = false` + expired pass: `PassFront` renders without any expiry scrim.
- Kernel snapshot/screenshot tests cover both branches.
- `PublicApiSurfaceTest` updated for the new parameter.
close_reason: Merged via PR #96 (e887c88) — passes-ui: R2 host opt-outs for PassFront and security sheets

title: passes-ui: create-time confirmation dialog when a QR payload contains a known URI scheme
description:
## Why this issue exists

UI side of the create-time URI preview mitigation (parent epic pre-ship requirement #2). Consumes `QrPayloadKind` from Child 5's classifier and presents a per-scheme human-readable warning before the BarcodeCard is persisted.

Mirrors the pattern of `B3UrlConfirmSheet` in `passes-ui/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/ui/SecuritySheets.kt:40` — except triggered at **create time**, not at click time.

Without this bead, a phishing payload like `bitcoin:1A1zP1eP5QGefi2DMPTfTL5SLmv7DivfNa` slips into the user's wallet silently. With it, the user sees "When this QR is scanned, it will send Bitcoin to: 1A1zP1...DivfNa — confirm?" and can cancel.

## Deliverable

In `passes-ui`:

- `BarcodeCreateConfirmSheet(payloadKind: QrPayloadKind, onConfirm: () -> Unit, onCancel: () -> Unit)` @Composable
- Per-`QrPayloadKind`-arm warning text:
  - `Url(host)` → "When scanned, this QR will open: **example.com**"
  - `Phone(number)` → "When scanned, this QR will dial: **+44 7700 900000**"
  - `Sms(number)` → "When scanned, this QR will text: **+44 7700 900000**"
  - `Mailto(addr)` → "When scanned, this QR will email: **alice@example.com**"
  - `Geo(coords)` → "When scanned, this QR will show a location on a map: **51.5074, -0.1278**"
  - `Wifi(ssid)` → "When scanned, this QR will offer to join Wi-Fi network: **MyNetwork**"
  - `Bitcoin(addr)` → "When scanned, this QR will prepare a Bitcoin payment to: **1A1z...DivfNa**" (with masked middle for long addresses)
  - `Ethereum(addr)` → similar
  - `Magnet` → "When scanned, this QR will start a torrent download."
  - `Market(productId)` → "When scanned, this QR will open the Play Store: **com.example.app**"
  - `Intent(raw)` → "When scanned, this QR can trigger an app action. This is uncommon for loyalty cards. Continue?" (extra-strong warning)
  - `UnknownScheme(scheme, raw)` → "When scanned, this QR uses a scheme Walt doesn't recognize: **`scheme://`**. If you didn't expect this, cancel."
  - `PlainText` → dialog NOT shown (no warning needed; persist directly)
- Verbatim payload display (no normalization) below the warning — same posture as `B3UrlConfirmSheet`. Use the `isolated()` BiDi helper from `passes-ui-core` to render verbatim safely.
- **Cancel is the default action** (focused, prominent). Confirm requires explicit tap.
- Triggered ONLY for QR format. Linear formats skip this dialog (they don't auto-act when scanned).
- `@Preview` per `QrPayloadKind` arm

## Critical posture

The dialog is a **gate** at create time. The consumer's create flow must call this between input validation and persistence. If the user cancels, no `BarcodeCard` is created.
design:
## Module + file location

- Module: `passes-ui`
- Package: alongside existing `SecuritySheets.kt`
- File: append to `SecuritySheets.kt` (keeps confirmation surfaces co-located) OR new file `BarcodeCreateConfirmSheet.kt` if the existing file is large — judgment call when you see the file

## Pattern to mirror

`B3UrlConfirmSheet` in `SecuritySheets.kt:40`. Copy the:
- Bottom-sheet vs dialog choice (whatever B3 uses)
- Verbatim text rendering with `isolated()` BiDi protection
- Button layout (cancel default, confirm explicit)
- Trust-styling tokens

## Per-arm copy

The strings above are draft copy — they need product/legal review before final wording. Wrap each in a string resource so localization (GitHub #65) can address them later.

## Masked addresses

For long crypto addresses, mask the middle: `1A1zP1...DivfNa` (first 6 + last 6 of base58/hex). Implement as a helper in the dialog file.

```kotlin
fun maskAddress(addr: String): String =
    if (addr.length <= 14) addr else "${addr.take(6)}...${addr.takeLast(6)}"
```

## i18n

All warning text via `stringResource(R.string.barcode_create_confirm_url, host)`. Define string resources in the same module.

## Tests

- Snapshot per `QrPayloadKind` arm
- Verify cancel button has default focus
- Verify confirm requires an explicit tap (no auto-dismiss)
- Verify verbatim payload text uses `isolated()` rendering

Open questions:

4. i18n: all strings via stringResource for prep against GitHub #65 (localization). Confirm string-resource conventions.

Mirrors B3UrlConfirmSheet posture with inverted button prominence (Cancel filled+focused, Confirm text). PlainText short-circuits; requiresCreateConfirmation() exposed for callers. wpass-lzi.10 (cross-repo handoff) can now proceed.

title: passes-core: classify QR payload by URI scheme for create-time preview
description:
## Why this issue exists

A QR code can encode arbitrary text. A maliciously crafted "membership number" the user is asked to type in might actually be `bitcoin:1A1zP1eP5QGefi2DMPTfTL5SLmv7DivfNa` or `https://phishing.example/...` — when the user later shows it for *someone else* to scan, that someone's phone will interpret the URI and act on it (open a URL, dial a number, prefill a Bitcoin send, join a Wi-Fi network).

Per the 2026-05-17 security analysis (parent epic pre-ship requirement #2), the mitigation is a **create-time preview**: detect known URI schemes in the payload, surface them to the UI layer, so the user is shown "When this QR is scanned by someone else's phone, it will: open URL example.com" with an explicit confirm.

This bead is the **classifier** (pure logic, in `passes-core`). The UI dialog that displays the warning is sibling Child 9 (`passes-ui`).

## Deliverable

In `passes-core`:

- `QrPayloadClassifier` (object or class) with `fun classify(payload: String): QrPayloadKind`
- `QrPayloadKind` sealed interface:
  - `PlainText` — payload doesn't look like a URI
  - `Url(scheme: String, host: String?, raw: String)` — http or https
  - `Phone(number: String)` — tel:
  - `Sms(number: String)` — sms:
  - `Mailto(address: String)` — mailto:
  - `Geo(coords: String)` — geo:
  - `Wifi(ssid: String?)` — wifi:
  - `Bitcoin(address: String)` — bitcoin:
  - `Ethereum(address: String)` — ethereum:
  - `Magnet` — magnet:
  - `Market(productId: String)` — market: (Android Play Store)
  - `Intent(raw: String)` — intent: (Android — particularly dangerous)
  - `UnknownScheme(scheme: String, raw: String)` — looks URI-shaped, scheme not in allowlist
- Scheme detection via conservative regex (don't trust `java.net.URI` to reject malformed inputs cleanly — it accepts a lot)
- Returns enough structured info that Child 9 can construct a human-readable warning per scheme
- Unit tests across all scheme arms + edge cases:
  - URL with embedded credentials (`https://user:pass@host/`)
  - RTL hostname (`https://паγpal.com/`)
  - Punycode (`https://xn--80ak6aa92e.com/`)
  - Trailing whitespace
  - Embedded newline
  - Empty payload
  - Numeric-only payload (must classify as `PlainText`, not `Phone`)

## Critical posture

- Only applies to QR-format payloads. Linear barcodes (Code128, etc.) don't auto-act when scanned by phones.
- Conservative allowlist: an unrecognized scheme like `foo://bar` returns `UnknownScheme` with the raw string. The UI dialog (Child 9) shows "Walt doesn't recognize this scheme" warning.
- Bidi/control-char rejection happens upstream in Child 4; this classifier can assume clean input but defense-in-depth checks here are welcome.
design:
## Module + file location

- Module: `passes-core`
- Package: same as the other BarcodeCard files
- File: `QrPayloadClassifier.kt`, `QrPayloadKind.kt`

## Detection approach

`java.net.URI` is too permissive. Use a regex pre-filter for the scheme, then structured parsing per known scheme:

```kotlin
private val schemeRegex = Regex("""^([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*):""")
```

If the payload starts with a scheme (per RFC 3986), dispatch to per-scheme parsing. Otherwise return `PlainText`.

## Per-scheme parsing

- **http/https:** parse with `java.net.URI`, extract host. Reject if URI parse fails — return `UnknownScheme`.
- **tel/sms:** extract digits + plus sign.
- **mailto:** extract everything before `?` or end.
- **geo:** extract `lat,lon` or full body.
- **wifi:** parse `WIFI:T:<auth>;S:<ssid>;P:<password>;;` format, extract SSID only (do NOT expose password in the classifier output — UI shouldn't display it).
- **bitcoin/ethereum:** extract address (everything before `?`).
- **intent:** keep raw; Android `intent://` URIs encode actions and extras in a structured way but for the warning we just need "this is an Android intent — could do almost anything."

## What NOT to do

- DO NOT follow URLs or do any network lookup.
- DO NOT use `Uri.parse` (Android-only — passes-core is JVM).
- DO NOT trust `URI.getScheme()` alone; some malformed inputs return non-null schemes that aren't actually URIs.

## Tests

One test per `QrPayloadKind` arm. Add explicit tests for the edge cases listed in the deliverable. Property-based testing would be nice for URL hosts but not required.
acceptance_criteria: Classifier with unit tests across all QrPayloadKind arms including edge cases (creds-in-URL, RTL hostname, punycode); :passes-core:check green.
notes: Implementation + tests committed; PR https://github.com/walt-app/walt-passes-android/pull/82 (combined with wpass-lzi.4). Closes on merge.
close_reason: Merged in PR #82 (passes-core: input validator + QR URI classifier)

title: rememberPdfThumbnail: instrumented Compose tests for dispose-during-render and cache eviction
description:
Follow-up to wpass-5g7. The public Compose facade rememberPdfThumbnail (in passes-pdf-ui/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/pdf/ui/PdfThumbnail.kt) landed with a JVM-pure surface-lock test (PdfThumbnailSurfaceTest) that pins the API shape, but two behavioural guarantees called out in wpass-5g7's test plan still need instrumented coverage because they exercise the Compose runtime + Android SharedMemory / Bitmap together:

1. A dispose between renderOrDiscard returning RenderResult.Ok and produceState publishing Rendered closes the SharedMemory exactly once. Pattern: a RecordingBinder (same shape as DocumentViewInstrumentedTest.RecordingBinder) plus a Compose test that toggles the produceState key mid-render and asserts openSharedMemoryCount() == 0 after the dispose settles.

2. A fresh Rendered against the same (documentId, page) evicts the previous bitmap from the PdfThumbnailCache and the eviction callback fires Bitmap.recycle on the prior pixel buffer.

Both should live in passes-pdf-ui/src/androidTest/ alongside DocumentViewInstrumentedTest. RenderedPageCacheTest already covers the LRU contract at the cache-internal level; this bead is specifically the end-to-end thumbnail-facade integration.

title: DocumentView: derive PDF render-request size from actual layout constraints
description:
Follow-up from wpass-b6h PR #70 review (point 3). DocumentPage requests a fixed 360dp x 480dp (px) raster from the renderer, while the on-screen page is now sized fillMaxSize + ContentScale.Fit into whatever slot the consumer gives DocumentView. Pre-wpass-b6h the aspectRatio(3:4) frame roughly matched the request ratio; post-PR the request is decoupled from the display footprint.

Analysis at review time: no regression for the common case -- the pager width is unchanged by the PR, so for portrait (<=3:4) pages ContentScale.Fit stays width-bound and display scale is unchanged; pages wider than the slot ratio downscale (crisper). The narrow case where a bigger render would help is a tall slot + portrait page. ADR 0005 D7's renderer-side area cap also limits gains from a larger request.

Scope: derive requestWidthPx/requestHeightPx from the measured page constraints (e.g. BoxWithConstraints or onSizeChanged) instead of the TARGET_PAGE_WIDTH_DP/TARGET_PAGE_HEIGHT_DP constants, clamped to the D7 cap. Confirm visually on a large slot first to decide if it is worth doing.

title: Evaluate moving the PDF document metadata panel into passes-pdf-ui
description:
CONTEXT
walt-android's PDF document detail screen (DocumentDetailScreen, wlt-o72.2) renders a small metadata panel below the PDF - import date, page count, file size - under a 'Details' header, reusing walt-android's pkpass 'Details' header styling. All three fields are already on the kernel PdfDocument (importedAtEpochMs, pageCount, byteCount), so the kernel HAS the data.

QUESTION TO EVALUATE: should this metadata panel move into passes-pdf-ui (e.g. a new public DocumentDetails(doc: PdfDocument, modifier) composable + the date/size formatters), so every consumer renders document metadata consistently - the way the trust caption is being consolidated in wpass-b6h?

CONSIDERATIONS:
- For: consistency across consumers; the kernel already owns the data and (after wpass-b6h) the trust caption; avoids each consumer re-authoring formatters.
- Against: it is app chrome, not a trust surface; walt-android currently reuses its OWN pkpass 'Details' header for visual consistency WITH passes - a consumer-level concern; it expands a deliberately 'minimally featured' kernel surface (would warrant an ADR 0005 note - not a security amendment: the fields are import metadata already on the model, not extracted from PDF content, so D4 is not in tension).
- A new DocumentDetails composable is additive: it does NOT touch DocumentView's lock-tested 5-param signature, so DocumentSurfaceLockTest is unaffected.

DECISION OWNER: kernel team. If yes -> becomes an implementation bead. If no -> walt-android keeps the panel (current state, fine).

Deferred from the walt-android wlt-o72 epic; user chose 'caption to kernel now (wpass-b6h), metadata later'.

title: passes-ui: localize trust-claim-bearing chrome strings
description:
The trust-claim-bearing chrome in passes-ui is hardcoded English. Affects:

- PassImportConfirm: 'Add this pass?', 'Save pass', 'Cancel', and the four trust-band caption titles + bodies (Verified Apple issuer / Self-signed issuer / Issuer chain incomplete / No signature, plus the explanatory body lines).
- PassImportRejectionSheet: four title+body pairs (one per ParseFailureKind) and 'Close'.
- SecuritySheets: 'Open this link?' / 'Call this number?' / 'Send an email?' / 'Cancel' / 'Open link' / 'Call' / 'Compose'.
- PassFront badge text: 'Verified' / 'Unsigned' / 'Self-signed' / 'Signature unknown'.
- ExpiredOverlay: 'Expired' / 'Voided'.

Why this matters: the user must SEE AND UNDERSTAND the trust band before consenting to import. A non-English-speaking user is currently shown English copy and asked to make a security decision based on it, which weakens the audit-trail commitment in the project's purpose statement.

Why this lives here, not in walt-android: the strings are part of the trust-claim surface; if walt-android could supply alternate copy through string resources it pulls in itself, it could (intentionally or not) weaken the disclosure. The kernel must own the canonical translations.

Likely shape: bundle the chrome strings as a resource set (per-locale .arb-equivalent or Compose CompositionLocal of a strongly-typed PassesUiStrings interface) that walt-android can extend with locale resources but not override the English source. Alignment with Android i18n conventions vs. CompositionLocal-based theming is part of this issue's scoping.

Filed from PR review on wpass-9bs (commit 3bc12f6). Reviewer flagged as 'real gap, not MVP blocker.'

title: SignatureVerifier: snapshot PKIX path-build date to CMS signing time
description:
Verifier currently sets PKIXBuilderParameters.date to "now" implicitly (default behavior) and isRevocationEnabled=false. The 'now' default means a chain that was valid when the pass was signed but whose leaf has since expired downgrades from SignatureStatus.AppleVerified to SignatureStatus.CertChainIncomplete on the wall clock. Two concrete consequences:

1. Real Apple-signed pkpasses imported by users after their leaf cert's notAfter surface as CertChainIncomplete (a UI degradation) instead of AppleVerified, even though they were trustworthy when signed. Apple Pass Type ID certs are typically 1-year, so the affected window is large.

2. Test fixtures (passes-core/src/test/resources/.../apple-signed/) carry an implicit shelf life — the next maintainer has to renew when the fixture's leaf expires. The README in the fixture directory documents the renewal procedure (added in wpass-4js / PR #50), but the procedure exists only because of the 'now' default.

Fix: extract the signing time from the CMS signedAttrs (signingTime attribute, OID 1.2.840.113549.1.9.5), pass it via PKIXBuilderParameters.setDate(). For envelopes without the signingTime attribute, fall back to 'now' to preserve current behavior.

Cross-ref the discussion: SignatureVerifier.kt's 'No date-shift override' docblock already flags this. wpass-4js PR review (https://github.com/walt-app/walt-passes-android/pull/50) explicitly deferred to here.

Acceptance:
- Verifier reads signingTime from signedAttrs when present.
- Test that mints a chain whose leaf expired between signing and 'now', signs at the in-validity time, and asserts AppleVerified.
- Existing tests still pass.
- Fixture README's 'renewal procedure' section gets a follow-up note that this issue, once shipped, retires the renewal need.

title: Detect SafeTix / rotating-secret tickets at import; surface explain-and-link UX
description:
Background: SafeTix and similar rotating-credential tickets (Google Wallet rotatingBarcode pattern) cannot be imported into Walt by design. The rotation secrets are bound to the issuing wallet's account and never appear in any artifact Walt can receive — Save-to-Google-Wallet JWT carries only an object ID, the Ticketmaster app uses an explicit GMS intent, and Apple's companion-app pattern draws the QR from inside the Ticketmaster iOS app. See bd memories ticketmaster-import-closed-paths-2026-05 and safetix-mechanism-2026-05 for full research notes.

Walt's transparency-for-trust posture argues for honest UX rather than silent failure: when a user attempts to add a recognizable rotating-credential ticket, surface a clear typed message explaining why this kind of pass is wallet-bound, and offer a deep link to Google Wallet for that one ticket while making clear Walt holds everything else.

Concrete signals to detect (in walt-android import surface; passes-core has no Android intent surface):
- Shared/pasted URL matching pay.google.com/gp/v/save/* — likely Save-to-Google-Wallet JWT.
- Shared/pasted URL matching tickets.ticketmaster.* / am.ticketmaster.* / ticketmaster.dk/* / ticketmaster.* event ticket paths.
- Future: detection of the Google Wallet Save SDK output if/when it surfaces.

Out of scope: any attempt to parse the JWT for actionable content (it does not contain the rotation secret), any attempt to deep-link into the Ticketmaster app's ticket Activity (FLAG_SECURE blocks capture anyway), any reverse-engineering path.

This is a v2-ish enhancement; v1 scope (decision-wlt-0tn-q3) explicitly excludes manual entry and QR scan import. Filing as P3 to track the design conversation when import-flow polish gets attention.
notes: Posture and detection contract codified in ADR 0006 (docs/adr/0006-rotating-credential-ticket-scope.md, D2). Empirical basis in docs/research/rotating-credential-tickets.md. Committed as 8f4160d on branch adr-rotating-credential-tickets.

title: Sentinel pixel pattern in DocumentView instrumented test fakes
description:
DocumentViewInstrumentedTest's RecordingBinder allocates SharedMemory of the requested size but never writes pixels, so a regression where the consumer uses caller dims instead of renderer-reported dims (the C1 bug fixed in PR #38) would not be caught even on device. Add a sentinel byte pattern that the recorder writes deterministically and the test asserts round-trips through the bitmap reconstruction path with the renderer-reported (not requested) dimensions.

Source: PR #38 review feedback T1.

title: DocumentTelemetryGuard arm for consumer-side render failures
description:
DocumentView's bitmapFromSharedMemory uses runCatching { ... }.getOrNull() to swallow OOM, BufferUnderflowException, and SharedMemory-closed exceptions. The renderer service has its own DocumentTelemetryGuard for service-side failures, but the consumer-side blank-screen outcome is invisible to telemetry today. Add a DocumentTelemetryGuard.onConsumerRenderFailed(reason) arm with an enum (OutOfMemory, SharedMemoryUnavailable, DimensionMismatch, Other) and wire it from DocumentView. PR #38 has a justifying comment at the swallow point pointing at this issue.

Source: PR #38 review feedback C5.
close_reason: PR #47 — DocumentTelemetryGuard.onConsumerRenderFailed wired from DocumentView's bitmapFromSharedMemory boundary; ConsumerRenderFailure enum (4 arms); structural+behavioral PII locks updated; ./gradlew check green.

title: Cross-module parity test: passes-pdf-core renderer caps vs passes-storage DocumentBounds
description:
DocumentBounds.MAX_BYTES (25 MB) and DocumentBounds.MAX_PAGES (10) in passes-storage
are hardcoded duplicates of the renderer-service caps in passes-pdf-core (ADR 0005 D7).
Storage cannot import passes-pdf-core (the PdfDocument <-> documents-table mapping is
a consumer-defined seam), so the two constants have no compile-time link.

A cross-module test should assert lockstep so a future cap change in passes-pdf-core
cannot silently diverge from passes-storage. Options:

- Add a JVM test in passes-pdf-core's test sources that depends on passes-storage and
  asserts the public-API constants match.
- Or add a small integration-test module that depends on both and runs the parity check.

Either works. The check itself is a one-liner once the module dependency is in place.

title: passes-core: resolve CertChainIncomplete name-vs-meaning for expired-leaf case
description:
Follow-up from PR #28 third-pass review (wpass-dw2). chainReachesAnchor swallows every PKIX failure mode (chain doesn't reach root, leaf expired, intermediate untrusted, name-constraints violation, malformed extension) into a single 'false' return, then the classifier surfaces all of them as SignatureStatus.CertChainIncomplete. SignatureStatus.CertChainIncomplete's KDoc says 'intermediates required to reach a known root were absent' — but for an aged Apple-signed pass (expired leaf) the intermediates ARE present and chain correctly, just past notAfter. The status name lies.

This is structurally important because Apple-signed pkpass leaves are typically 1-year-validity, so almost every aged real-world pass eventually trips this path.

Two paths to resolve, in increasing intrusion order:
1. Documentation only: extend SignatureStatus.CertChainIncomplete's KDoc to include 'or any other PKIX failure mode (expired leaf, name-constraints, ...)'. Honest, no API change.
2. Add SignatureStatus.Expired as a fifth arm. Public-API change, propagates to SignatureStatusKind, toKind(), telemetry. UI consumers can render an 'aged Apple signature' chip distinct from 'unrooted'.

Recommended: pursue option 2 IF a UX consumer surfaces value, else option 1. Touches decision-wlt-0tn-q1 (signature trust display) and the surface is frozen until wpass-n6g, so coordinate timing.

Optional extension: revisit whether the path builder should snapshot to the CMS signing time embedded in the signed-attributes (would re-classify aged Apple-signed leaves as AppleVerified). Touches every aged real-world pass. File a sibling bead under decision-wlt-0tn-q1 if this is the chosen direction.

title: passes-core: add TamperReason.SignatureUntrusted arm to disambiguate strict-mode policy rejection
description:
Follow-up from PR #28 third-pass review (wpass-dw2). In strict mode (ParserConfig.acceptSelfSignedCertificates=false), a structurally valid, mathematically verified, cleanly-chained self-signed signature surfaces as TamperReason.SignatureCryptoFailure. Nothing crypto-failed — the math passed; the chain was rejected by policy. The current sealed interface has only ManifestSignatureMismatch and SignatureCryptoFailure, so the verifier reuses the latter as a catch-all.

Implications:
- Telemetry conflation. Oncall/auditor reading 'SignatureCryptoFailure' cannot distinguish 'BC blew up parsing the blob' (real tamper signal) from 'cert was self-signed and we are in strict mode' (policy/UX intent).
- Audit trail muddiness. Same pass under lenient → SelfSigned/Ok; under strict → SignatureCryptoFailure. Looks externally like the mode flip changed whether crypto worked, but it did not.

Scope:
- Add TamperReason.SignatureUntrusted (or similarly-named) arm to passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/ParseResult.kt.
- Update SignatureVerifier.classifyChain branch '!ctx.config.acceptSelfSignedCertificates' to emit Failed(SignatureUntrusted) instead of Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure).
- Update parser-glue mapping (wpass-qnc) to surface the new arm via ParseResult.Tampered.
- PublicApiSurfaceTest: add the new arm to the constructible-arms test, and to the toFailureKind exhaustive-when bridge if applicable.
- Update SignatureVerifierTest.strictRejectsSelfSigned and strictRejectsCertChainIncomplete to assert the new arm.
- Update SECURITY-CERTS.md if it references the strict-rejection arm anywhere.

This is a public-API change to TamperReason. Coordinate with the parser-glue bead (wpass-qnc) since it consumes this surface; ideally land before that bead does.

title: passes-core: cert-expiry downgrade test for SignatureVerifier
description:
Follow-up from PR #28 second-pass review (wpass-dw2). SignatureVerifier.kt KDoc lines ~70-75 documents that an Apple-signed pass with an expired leaf cert downgrades to SignatureStatus.CertChainIncomplete because PKIXBuilderParameters.date defaults to 'now'. Apple-signed pkpass leaves are typically 1-year-validity, so almost every aged real-world pass eventually trips this path. Currently no test exercises it.

Add tests that lock the documented behavior:
- Lenient (ParserConfig()): leaf with notAfter in the past, signed against a bundled anchor → Ok(CertChainIncomplete). Without the test, a future maintainer 'fixing' the path builder to use the CMS signing-time would silently flip behavior to AppleVerified.
- Strict (ParserConfig.Strict): same setup → Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure).

Implementation hint: the SignatureVerifierTest harness already synthesizes leaf certs with current-day dates (selfSign / signLeafWith helpers, lines ~250-310). Add an 'expiredLeaf' overload that accepts a notAfter offset.

Optional follow-up beyond this bead: revisit whether the policy should lock the path builder to the CMS signing time. Touches every aged real-world Apple pass. File a P3 under decision-wlt-0tn-q1 if pursued.

title: passes-core: regression test for trust-anchor loader fault-tolerance
description:
Follow-up from PR #28 second-pass review (wpass-dw2). The bug fix moved AppleTrustAnchors.trustAnchors() / knownIntermediates() inside the outer runCatching so a JAR-repackaging accident (proguard/R8 stripping the bundled .cer files, a corrupt .cer surviving build, etc.) downgrades to Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure) instead of throwing. The fix is currently locked only by code-review reading; a regression test would catch a future refactor that re-introduces the leak.

Implementation sketch:
- Extract a private 'verifyWithContextLoader(sig, manifest, loader: () -> VerifyContext)' helper. Both verifySignature (production, bundled loader) and verifySignatureAgainst (test seam, captured-anchors loader) route through it.
- Make VerifyContext internal so tests can construct one, OR add an internal-visible 'verifySignatureWithLoader' overload that accepts the loader directly.
- Test: pass a loader that throws (e.g. throws IllegalStateException, throws CertificateException), assert verifySignature returns Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure).
- Test: pass a loader that throws on first call but succeeds on the second; assert both calls return Failed (matches the lazy-cached re-throw shape AppleTrustAnchors actually exhibits).

Dependent: care needs to be taken to not bloat the file's TooManyFunctions count (currently 14/15).

title: passes-core: malformed-CMS corpus for verifySignature 'never throws' contract
description:
Follow-up from PR #28 review (wpass-dw2). The current SignatureVerifierTest covers garbage and empty signature blobs but does not exercise the broader space of structurally-plausible-but-malformed CMS envelopes (truncated SEQUENCE, oversize length tags, malformed signed-attributes, certificates store with no entries, signer SID that matches no included cert, etc.).

Add a small fuzz-style corpus (~10-20 hand-crafted byte arrays) that drives verifySignature and asserts every input either returns SignatureVerifyResult.Failed(SignatureCryptoFailure) or Failed(ManifestSignatureMismatch). Goal: lock in the 'no exception ever escapes the outer runCatching' contract beyond the single 64-byte test.

Optional: derive the corpus by mutating a known-good signature byte-by-byte and seeding interesting offsets (length tags, OID prefixes, signed-attributes start).

title: passes-core: AppleTrustAnchorsTest enumerate certs/ resource dir
description:
Follow-up from PR #28 review (wpass-dw2). AppleTrustAnchorsTest currently locks the documented set of bundled certs against fingerprints, but does not enumerate the contents of is/walt/passes/core/internal/certs/. A stray .cer (e.g. someone drops apple-wwdr-g7.cer next to the others without registering it) sits dead in the JAR with no signal.

Add a test that lists every *.cer file under the certs resource directory and asserts the set equals BUNDLED_TRUST_ANCHOR_FILENAMES + BUNDLED_INTERMEDIATE_FILENAMES. The sweep + the existing fingerprint pin together close both drift directions: a missing-from-resources cert fails fingerprint pinning; a present-but-not-registered cert fails the new sweep.

Implementation hint: use the same ClassLoader.getResource approach as AppleTrustAnchors.loadResource; walk the URL as a directory if it's a file: URL, or enumerate via JarURLConnection if loaded from a JAR.

title: passes-core: relax expirationDate parsing for naked-local timestamps
description:
PassJsonDecoder.parseExpiration uses OffsetDateTime.parse which requires an explicit offset (RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 with offset). PKPASS specs ISO 8601 / W3C-DTF, but in the wild some hand-authored passes emit naked-local timestamps (e.g. '2026-12-31T23:59:00' with no Z and no +HH:MM). Those currently surface as PassJsonFailure.InvalidShape and ParseResult.Malformed.

Decision needed: relax to DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE_TIME (which accepts both forms) and assume UTC for naked-local? Or keep strict and accept the recall hit? Wait for real-world fixtures showing this fires before relaxing — if it never fires in field telemetry, the strict posture is fine.

Trigger: spotted in PR #26 review for wpass-7sl. Not blocking the slice; surface for follow-up.

title: passes-core: add ParserConfig.maxTotalDecompressedBytes for global decompressed-footprint cap
description:
ParserConfig today caps maxArchiveBytes (compressed) and maxEntryBytes (per-entry decompressed) but not the total decompressed footprint. With defaults (maxEntries=256, maxEntryBytes=4 MB) the worst-case decompressed footprint is 1 GB, which is fine for PKPASS content (kilobytes in practice). The hazard is future drift: a consumer that loosens maxEntries to e.g. 4096 with the same maxEntryBytes would suddenly have a 16 GB ceiling without the change site flagging it.

Add a new field maxTotalDecompressedBytes (default ~64 MB or similar — derive from realistic PKPASS sizes). Enforce it in SafeArchiveExtractor.readEntryAndStore by tracking a running sum and returning ResourceLimitExceeded with a new ResourceLimit.TotalDecompressedSize value if the running sum exceeds the cap. ResourceLimit is a public enum so this requires coordination with the public API freeze; bundle with wpass-n6g if convenient.

Refs: PR #24 review pass 2 (memory ceiling observation).

title: passes-core: route encrypted/unsupported-method zips to UnsupportedReason instead of NotAZipArchive
description:
ParseResult.UnsupportedReason.EncryptedArchive (declared in passes-core/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/core/ParseResult.kt:74) is currently unreachable from the SafeArchiveExtractor pipeline. ZipInputStream natively supports only STORED (method 0) and DEFLATED (method 8); BZIP2/12, LZMA/14, ZSTD/93, and the encryption flag (general-purpose bit 0) all produce a ZipException or garbage-bytes outcome that the catch block maps to MalformedReason.NotAZipArchive. The user-visible failure is 'corrupted zip' even though the archive is structurally valid but uses an unsupported feature.

Fix: peek the general-purpose-bit-flag and compression-method of each entry header before handing it to the inflater. If the encryption bit is set, return ParseResult.Unsupported(UnsupportedReason.EncryptedArchive). title: Drop dead transaction wrapper around SqlCipherScannableCardStore.insert
description:
## What

`SqlCipherScannableCardStore.insert` (passes-storage/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/storage/internal/SqlCipherScannableCardStore.kt) wraps a single `insertOrThrow` in `beginTransaction()` / `setTransactionSuccessful()` / `endTransaction()`. The wrapper predates this bead — it was already wrapping a single statement before `wpass-q5p` removed the colour write. Now that nothing coordinates with that insert atomically, the transaction is dead ceremony.

## Why

Flagged in the wpass-q5p code review (PR #98). Not a bug; the concern is reader-signal: a `beginTransaction` block reads as "multiple writes coordinated atomically" and invites cargo-culting in adjacent stores. Adjacent `delete` and other store methods follow the same wrap-around-single-statement pattern, so check whether they should also lose the wrapper for consistency.

## Files to change

- `passes-storage/src/main/kotlin/is/walt/passes/storage/internal/SqlCipherScannableCardStore.kt` — drop the transaction wrapper from `insert` (and `delete` if it's similarly single-statement after audit).
- Audit `SqlCipherPassStore` and `SqlCipherDocumentStore` for the same pattern; either keep the wrapper consistently across the three stores or remove it everywhere it wraps exactly one statement.

## Out of scope

- Any cross-table write that actually does need a transaction. Don't unwrap multi-statement writes (insert+image rows in the pass store, for example).
- Behaviour change. This is a code-clarity cleanup; tests should not change.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Single-statement writes in the three SqlCipher stores are not wrapped in `beginTransaction` / `endTransaction`.
- [ ] Multi-statement writes still are.
- [ ] `:passes-storage:testDebugUnitTest` and instrumentation suite green.
- [ ] Decision recorded inline (one-line comment) on any store method where the wrapper is intentionally retained.

title: Walt-native PKPASS rotating-barcode extension (architecture exploration)
description:
Architecture concept surfaced during 2026-05-07 deep-research into Ticketmaster import paths. Because Walt is its own wallet (not Apple Wallet), it can define and honor a Walt-namespaced extension to PKPASS — e.g. userInfo.waltRotatingBarcode — that carries TOTP rotation parameters mirroring Google's RotatingBarcode REST schema: secret (base16), periodMillis, algorithm (TOTP_SHA1), valuePattern with {totp_value_n}/{totp_timestamp_seconds} substitutions, optional initialRotatingBarcodeValues for offline.

Why this is interesting:
- The PKPASS userInfo field is the spec-blessed app-specific data slot; Apple Wallet ignores unknown keys, so a PKPASS carrying both a static fallback barcode (for Apple Wallet) and userInfo.waltRotatingBarcode (for Walt) interoperates cleanly.
- The signed manifest stays static — the SECRET is signed, not the rendered code — so Walt's existing PKCS#7 verify and manifest hash chain remain meaningful.
- No webServiceURL polling, no APNS rate-limit issues, no companion-app entitlement requirement.
- Trust-claim aligned: a clean, audit-friendly public extension spec living in this repo is exactly what the transparency-for-trust posture is set up to ship.

The constraint is adoption: incumbents (Ticketmaster, AXS, Eventim) will not issue Walt-flavored bundles, but smaller ticketing platforms, festivals, season-ticket holders, conference issuers, and self-issuers may.

EXCLUDED from v1: decision-wlt-0tn-q3 explicitly OUTs dynamic updates and webServiceURL polling. Surface area would need its own threat model (TOTP secret at rest in SQLCipher; secret-touching code paths in passes-core). 

This bead is a placeholder for the v2/v3 architecture discussion. Linked memory: walt-native-rotating-barcode-extension-concept-2026-05.
notes: Long-term seam codified in ADR 0006 D3. Schema sketch and rationale in docs/adr/0006-rotating-credential-ticket-scope.md (D3) and docs/research/rotating-credential-tickets.md ('PKPASS rotation feasibility' section). Committed as 8f4160d on branch adr-rotating-credential-tickets. Threat model not yet written; required before any implementation work.

title: passes-core: SID-collision and DN-equality comments in SignatureVerifier
description:
Follow-up from PR #28 second-pass review (wpass-dw2). Two undocumented invariants in SignatureVerifier.kt that a future maintainer should be able to read off the code:

1. firstSignerWithCert (line ~135) picks the first SignerInformation and its first matching cert. PKPASS spec is single-signer; but if a malformed CMS blob ships two X509CertificateHolders with the same SignerId (issuer+serial collision, constructible), getMatches(...).firstOrNull() resolves to one of them in BC's iteration order. Not exploitable (the chosen cert's math still has to verify, attacker can't promote to AppleVerified), but worth a one-line comment that the single-match assumption is correctness-by-the-verify-step, not by-the-pick.

2. isSelfSigned (line ~225) compares cert.subjectX500Principal != cert.issuerX500Principal. X500Principal.equals does RFC-2253 normalization, not raw DER-bytes comparison. A pathological cert with logically-identical-but-encoded-differently DN could bypass this fast path, but the second check (cert.verify(cert.publicKey)) catches it on signature math. Worth a comment that the order is correctness-by-the-second-check, not by-the-first.

Pure doc work, no code change. Bundle both edits into one PR.

title: passes-core: document single-signer assumption in firstSignerWithCert
description:
Follow-up from PR #28 review (wpass-dw2). SignatureVerifier.firstSignerWithCert silently uses signerInfos.signers.firstOrNull(). Real-world pkpass blobs have exactly one signer, but the choice to ignore signers 2..N is undocumented and a future maintainer would need to re-derive whether multi-signer support is missing-on-purpose or missing-by-oversight.

Add a one-line KDoc comment on firstSignerWithCert noting: 'pkpass carries exactly one signer per spec; multi-signer blobs are unsupported and we choose the first deterministically.' No code change required.

title: passes-core: PassJsonFailure.UnknownFormatVersion - distinguish missing from non-1
description:
Internal PassJsonFailure.UnknownFormatVersion carries 'version: Int' with sentinel 0 for the missing-or-non-integer case (formatVersion absent, or formatVersion is a string / array / object). The KDoc acknowledges the sentinel; the parser-glue bead can choose to coalesce missing-version onto InvalidPassJson if the UI calls for it.

A cleaner shape would be 'version: Int?', distinguishing 'present-but-unsupported' (e.g. formatVersion=2) from 'missing-or-malformed' (formatVersion absent). The parser-glue bead could then route the missing case to InvalidPassJson and the unsupported case to UnsupportedReason.FormatVersion(v) without re-parsing.

Trigger: spotted in PR #26 review for wpass-7sl. Cosmetic, not blocking.

title: passes-storage: migrate to PackageManager.getApplicationInfo(String, ApplicationInfoFlags) at next minSdk bump
description:
BackupRulesAssertion.loadApplicationInfo calls the deprecated PackageManager.getApplicationInfo(String, Int) overload. The replacement PackageManager.getApplicationInfo(String, ApplicationInfoFlags) is API 33+. Currently emits a deprecation warning only; no functional impact.

title: BackupRulesAssertion: group environment-error Outcome arms under Outcome.EnvironmentError
description:
Outcome.PackageInfoUnavailable and Outcome.FieldUnavailable both represent 'environment is broken, not the consumer's fault', distinct from the consumer-misconfig surface (MissingExcludes, NoBackupRulesConfigured, RulesResourceUnreadable). Today consumers must enumerate both arms by hand if they want to distinguish 'consumer did something wrong' from 'test runner blew up'.

Refactor: introduce sealed interface Outcome.EnvironmentError : Outcome with PackageInfoUnavailable and FieldUnavailable as its arms. Pattern matching becomes:
  is Outcome.EnvironmentError -> ...
  is Outcome.MissingExcludes / NoBackupRulesConfigured / RulesResourceUnreadable -> ...

Defer trigger: revisit when a third 'environment' arm is needed, or when a consumer asks to discriminate the two categories.

Refs: review feedback on PR #18, declined as 'do later' because the surface is stable today and the grouping doesn't yet pay for itself.

value: Bytecode-scan trust-claim pattern: PublicApiSurfaceTest walks every is/walt/passes/<module>/**/*.class via classLoader.getResources('package/path') (PLURAL — getResource returns only the first classpath root, missing main vs test) and fails closed if it finds forbidden raw UTF-8 strings (ACTION_SEND, application/pdf). Cleaner than reflection because string constants are reachable in the bytecode regardless of how they're constructed. The test class itself is exempted via filename prefix so its own needles don't trip.

Ticketmaster SafeTix mechanism (research 2026-05-07): rotating PDF417 (US) / QR (EU) encoding [bearer_token::eventKey_TOTP::customerKey_TOTP::unix_timestamp]. Two RFC 6238 SHA-1 TOTPs at 15s step. Generation fully client-side once secrets provisioned. Google Wallet receives secrets via Google Tickets API rotatingBarcode field (totpDetails.parameters[].key, base16) and computes TOTP locally; the save-to-wallet JWT carries only an object ID, not the secrets. Apple Wallet pre-2018 issued static PKPASS; 2019+ migrated to companion-app pattern where Ticketmaster's iOS app draws the rotating QR over a Wallet-launcher pass. Bearer token alone is what venue scanner looks up; rotating TOTPs are anti-screenshot enforcement. Secrets re-issued ~20h pre-event via Partner API (gated to vetted partners only). Reverse-engineered by conduition.io (July 2024, https://conduition.io/coding/ticketmaster/); third-party SafeTix renderers (TicketGimp, Amosa, Secure.Tickets) require DevTools secret extraction in violation of ToU + DMCA §1201 + active 2025 Ticketmaster patent suit.

Walt + ticketing standards-track landscape (research 2026-05-07): EUDI Wallet under eIDAS 2.0 (Reg. EU 2024/1183) lists 'tickets, social passes, loyalty cards' as explicit Electronic Attestation of Attributes (EAA) use cases. W3C Verifiable Credentials 2.0 became a W3C Recommendation 2025-05-15. EWC large-scale pilot (24 countries, ~80 partners) tested travel/event credentials, including Lufthansa+Amadeus boarding-pass pilot in 2025. Member-state delivery mandate: 2026-09. OpenID4VCI is the issuance protocol of record. No major ticketing platform (Ticketmaster, AXS, Eventim) has announced EUDI participation. Regulatory levers do NOT currently compel: DMA Article 6(7) opens NFC chip access on Apple/Google but not application-layer ticket payloads; Ticketmaster is below DMA gatekeeper thresholds. GDPR Article 20 covers user-provided data per WP29 — excludes derived/inferred outputs (the rotating secret). US v. Live Nation jury verdict April 2026 found liable; DOJ amended complaint specifically called SafeTix anticompetitive; remedy phase pending but no proposed wallet-interop remedy. OPEN Ticketing Ecosystem (formerly GET Protocol) is opt-in/blockchain, no major issuer participates. Realistic Walt position for v3+: structural alignment as an OpenID4VCI/EUDI-Wallet-compatible holder when ticketing issuers eventually emit VCs; this is the only standards-track path with regulatory weight, on a 1-2 year horizon.

DECISION wlt-0tn Q3.4 (2026-05-03): Pass deletion mechanism. VACUUM SKIPPED. Approach = items 1+3+4+5+6 from the safeguard list: no undo/no trash bin, Android Auto Backup explicitly excluded for passes DB (allowBackup=false or backup rules excluding passes), no PII in logs (existing core/telemetry rule applies), cached decoded data wiped on delete, confirmation dialog matching DeleteCardUseCase pattern. Item 2 (VACUUM after delete) deemed unnecessary; protection layers SQLCipher + non-exportable Keystore key + Android FBE + backup opt-out + app sandboxing make freed-page bytes unreadable without breaking all four layers. Rationale: practical 'no history' guarantee delivered without VACUUM cost; flash wear-leveling means VACUUM cannot guarantee bit-level erasure anyway; encryption layers are the load-bearing control.

DECISION wlt-0tn Q4 (2026-05-03): Repo location, license, distribution. (4a) SEPARATE REPO at github.com/walt-app/walt-passes-android (renamed from 'walt-passes' on 2026-05-03; not monorepo subdir). (4b) LICENSE = Apache 2.0. Rationale: standard for Android libraries (AndroidX, Hilt, OkHttp); maximizes reuse without forcing copyleft on consumers; Walt's privacy/security promises live in code, not license; walt-android can pick its own license independently. FOSS pass-app field precedent (PassAndroid/FossWallet/Catima all GPLv3) is for apps not libraries. (4c) DISTRIBUTION = Composite Gradle build for v1 (walt-passes-android checked out as sibling, walt-android settings.gradle.kts uses includeBuild('../walt-passes-android')). Iteration speed during v1 API churn matters more than published artifacts. PLANNED FUTURE: GitHub Packages migration once v1 stabilizes (user explicit preference over Maven Central). (4d) Repo bootstrap details (CI, README, CoC, contributing guide, security policy) deferred to architecture phase as a single child bead.

passes-image-decode is an Android-only module (NOT pure-JVM, needs android.graphics, so deliberately not named -core) holding the single bounded ImageDecoder mechanism decodeBounded(rawBytes, BoundedDecodePolicy). Created in wpass-gnp as step 1 of wpass-i9x. Consumed by passes-barcode (software allocator, OOM->ImageTooLarge) and passes-ui (default allocator, OOM propagated); policy/caps/rejection-taxonomy stay with each consumer. Sits below both peers like passes-isolation, adds no edge. wpass-i9x step 3 isolated image-document service will reuse it.

Live-camera barcode kernel (wpass-7xo): CameraX ImageAnalysis delivers raw YUV_420_888 with NO still-image codec in the frame path on ALL walt.is targets - this is STRUCTURAL (codec is the separate ImageFormat.JPEG output used only by ImageCapture, which wlt-mwj does not bind), not per-device. PRIV/IMPLEMENTATION_DEFINED is the opaque GPU/preview format, never delivered as readable bytes to an Analyzer. Real cross-HAL variability is only plane geometry (rowStride padding, pixelStride interleave) - already absorbed by passes-barcode-core decodeYPlane(byte[]+width+height+rowStride+pixelStride+reverseHorizontal). Lone residual: a LEGACY-only 1-pixel luminance-shift CameraX conversion artifact (Play-channel old-hardware tail; Pixels are FULL/LEVEL_3, never LEGACY) - a quality bug, not a codec, within binarizer tolerance. Consumer usage constraint: keep ImageAnalysis on default YUV_420_888 and feed getPlanes()[0] (Y); never feed an RGBA_8888 plane into decodeYPlane. Confirms ADR 0008 D1; spike wpass-7xo.3.

walt-android backup posture (2026-05-05): consumer plans to keep allowBackup=true with explicit per-surface excludes mirrored into the app's own res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml + backup_rules.xml, NOT inherited from passes-storage. App manifest already uses tools:replace="android:allowBackup,android:fullBackupContent" which overrides library contributions. Implication for passes-storage: BackupRulesAssertion (which checks appInfo.fullBackupContent against library resource name walt_passes_backup_rules) will fail on walt-android because the merged manifest will reference walt-android's own xml resource name, not the library's. Assertion needs either (a) a content-matching mode that parses the consumer's rules XML and checks for required exclude entries, or (b) explicit doc that the assertion only works for consumers who let the library rules through unmodified. Source: walt-android Claude session report, 2026-05-05. Re-evaluate at wlt-4pg integration.

DECISION wlt-0tn Q3.3 (2026-05-03): Localization = L1 full localization, keep all locales. At display time pick locale = device locale, fall back to English, fall back to first-available. Re-render automatically on device locale change. All .lproj directories retained on disk. Use Android system fonts for non-Latin scripts. Trust Compose for RTL layout. .strings parser required (small, well-known format).

Walt-native PKPASS rotating-barcode extension concept (research 2026-05-07): because Walt is its own wallet (not Apple Wallet), it can interpret a Walt-namespaced extension field in PKPASS — e.g. userInfo.waltRotatingBarcode — without violating the PKPASS spec (Apple Wallet ignores unknown keys; userInfo is the spec-blessed app-specific data slot). Proposed schema mirrors Google's RotatingBarcode REST type (https://developers.google.com/wallet/reference/rest/v1/RotatingBarcode): secret (base16), periodMillis, algorithm (TOTP_SHA1), valuePattern with {totp_value_n}/{totp_timestamp_seconds} substitutions, optional initialRotatingBarcodeValues for offline. Walt computes TOTP locally at render time; the signed PKPASS manifest stays static (the secret is signed, not the rendered code). Architectural wins: no webServiceURL polling, no APNS rate-limit issues, no companion-app entitlement. Adoption is the chicken-and-egg constraint: major incumbents (Ticketmaster, AXS, Eventim) will not issue Walt-flavored bundles, but smaller ticketing platforms, festivals, season-ticket holders, and conference issuers looking for a non-walled-garden option could. Trust-claim alignment: a clean, audit-friendly public extension spec living in passes-android is exactly the kind of format the repo is positioned to ship. EXCLUDED from v1: decision-wlt-0tn-q3 explicitly OUTs dynamic updates/webServiceURL/manual entry. Should land as a v2/v3 architecture discussion bead, not a near-term build.

DECISION wlt-0tn Q1 (2026-05-03): Pass acquisition = PKPASS file import as primary path. Sub-decisions: (1a) Signature policy = LENIENT + mathematical verify + provenance display + defense in depth [Position A]. Always verify PKCS#7 signature mathematically and reject tampering (manifest hash mismatch). Validate Apple WWDR cert chain but DO NOT gate on it; surface result in UI as 'Verified Apple issuer: X' / 'Self-signed' / 'Cert chain incomplete'. Allow self-signed and non-Apple-cert passes to import. Rationale: Position A is field-leading among FOSS pass apps (PassAndroid/FossWallet/Catima/Google Pass Converter all do ZERO verification). Strict+WWDR was Position B, declined to avoid WWDR root distribution + rotation maintenance burden, ecosystem friction with self-issuers, and harder-to-use library for downstream consumers. Parser hardening (size limits, zip-slip, schema-strict JSON, bounded image decoding, parse-but-ignore for nfc/webServiceURL/personalization) is the load-bearing security control regardless of signature policy. (1b) Register OS-level intent filter for application/vnd.apple.pkpass MIME and .pkpass extension in walt-android app/AndroidManifest.xml so users can tap a .pkpass anywhere and Walt offers to import. (1c) PKPASS NFC payload field: parse-but-ignore in v1. Never register the AID. Documented exclusion to avoid HCE/AID conflict with payment. (1d) Manual entry and QR scan: deferred to v2. v1 ships PKPASS file import only. Walt's process-RCE blast radius (if parser bug exploited): card cryptographic keys remain non-exportable from Keystore/StrongBox; transaction history exfiltration is the realistic worst case.

DECISION wlt-0tn Q2 (2026-05-03): Naming. (2a) Feature umbrella = 'Walt Passes'. (2b) Open-source repo = 'walt-passes-android' under github.com/walt-app org (originally provisioned as 'walt-passes' on 2026-05-03; renamed same day to add the platform suffix in anticipation of a future walt-passes-ios sibling). (2c) UI subtype labels per PKPASS type, not pushed back on: boardingPass='Boarding pass', eventTicket='Ticket', coupon='Coupon', storeCard='Store card', generic='Pass'. Maven coordinates preview (firms up in Q4/Q5): group=is.walt, artifacts=passes-core + passes-ui (module names unchanged by rename).

Live-camera barcode/QR decode runs IN-PROCESS, not in the :barcodeDecoder isolated sandbox (passes-barcode). Rationale: CameraX ImageAnalysis emits already-decoded raw YUV_420_888 pixels; ZXing PlanarYUVLuminanceSource consumes only the Y-plane byte[] with no JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF/Skia container parsing, so the hostile-file -> native still-image codec RCE vector the sandbox exists to contain (libwebp CVE-2023-4863 class) is STRUCTURALLY ABSENT. The pure-JVM com.google.zxing:core adds only logic/DoS risk, never native RCE. Also the passes-isolation transport is one-shot fromBytes(ByteArray)/blocking transact() and cannot stream ~30fps frames. The STATIC-image path stays isolated because it parses attacker-controlled compressed containers; a 'scan from saved photo' affordance must route through the existing isolated BarcodeImageDecoder, never a new in-process codec call (raw-YUV ImageAnalysis ONLY, never ImageCapture/JPEG). Kernel decode core stays pure-JVM (passes-barcode-core decodeLuminance + symbology allowlist) and declares NO CAMERA permission; consumer (walt-android wlt-mwj) owns CameraX + CAMERA + confirmation. Consistent with CLAUDE.md / ADR 0005 D3: isolation is mechanism for the codec surface, not a blanket requirement. Evidence: bead wpass-7xo.1. Recorded as docs/adr/0008-live-camera-decode-in-process.md.

DECISION wlt-0tn Q3 v1 SCOPE SUMMARY (2026-05-03): IN: all 5 PKPASS types (boardingPass, eventTicket, coupon, storeCard, generic) via generic field-driven renderer; front + back fields; barcode/QR rendering (PDF417/QR/Aztec/Code128); colors, logo, strip, background, thumbnail images; full localization L1 (all locales retained); pass expiry display with 'Expired' badge; encrypted local storage (SQLCipher + Keystore); intent filter for .pkpass MIME; back-field URLs/phones/emails via Policy B3 (visible URL + confirmation sheet); secure deletion (no undo, backup opt-out, no logged PII, cached data wiped, confirmation dialog). OUT: NFC/transit, dynamic updates (webServiceURL), lock screen integration (defer v1.5), notifications (defer v2), pass sharing (defer v2), manual entry (defer v2), QR scan import (defer v2), multi-device sync, cloud backup, personalization, Apple Watch/wearables, edit pass, search/filter, pass export.

DECISION wlt-0tn Q3.2 (2026-05-03): Back fields are IN for v1. Actionable content (URLs, phone numbers, emails) handled via Policy B3: visible URL/value + confirmation sheet before action. Render limited HTML subset only (b, i, br, a). URL scheme allowlist: http, https, mailto, tel only. Open external URLs via Custom Tabs. Long URLs show truncated middle in label, full URL in confirmation sheet. No JavaScript, no CSS, no external image loads, no auto-fetch, no link preview.

ScannableCard (a.k.a. BarcodeCard in bead text) consumer-wiring work lives in walt-android beads, NOT in a passes-android doc. Filed beads: wlt-xwt (DI) → wlt-bd8 (create flow UI) → wlt-1ng (home lane) → {wlt-f3r (edit/delete UX), wlt-q3i (max brightness)}. Parent epic here: wpass-lzi. Closed source bead: wpass-lzi.10. Kernel API references (validator, classifier, sheet, tile/screen, repository methods) travel inside each wlt-* bead's description.

DECISION wlt-0tn Q5 (2026-05-03): Library shape = Option C repositioned as 'Walt's open pass-handling kernel'. Three Gradle modules in walt-passes-android repo (renamed from walt-passes 2026-05-03; module names unchanged): (1) passes-core: pure Kotlin/JVM, parser+model+signature+strings parser+TelemetryGuard interface; (2) passes-storage: Android-only, SQLCipher with Keystore key, backup exclusion, deletion+cache-wipe; (3) passes-ui: Android+Compose, pass front/back composables, barcode/QR, B3 URL confirmation sheet, expired badge, bounded image decoding, theming contract. Walt-android wraps thinly: core/data-passes (Hilt+repository wiring), feature/passes (Compose screens consuming passes-ui with Walt theme tokens), app (manifest intent filter). DECISIVE CONSTRAINT: walt-android uses walt-passes-android implementations directly; NO parallel reimplementation in walt-android of any code bearing a trust claim. Rationale: walt-android is closed-source; trust-through-transparency requires security-and-privacy claims to be auditable in walt-passes-android, so storage/UI/parser all live there. README leads with transparency-for-trust framing, not library-for-reuse.

FOSS PKPASS signature policy field survey (2026-05-03): PassAndroid (ligi, Feb 2025), FossWallet (SeineEloquenz, Apr 2026), Catima, and Google's Pass Converter all skip PKCS#7 signature verification entirely. None verify manifest hashes, none validate WWDR cert chain, none surface provenance in UI. FossWallet has explicit 'TODO check signature before returning' at app/src/main/java/nz/eloque/foss_wallet/persistence/loader/PassLoader.kt:140 — unimplemented. PassAndroid uses zip4j extractAll() at android/src/main/java/org/ligi/passandroid/ui/UnzipPassController.kt:71-75 with no validation. Field hardening is also thin: no size limits, no image dimension caps, FossWallet has no zip-slip canonicalPath check. Implication for walt-passes: even 'lenient' (mathematical verify + provenance display + parser hardening) puts Walt ahead of every comparable FOSS pass app. Strict-with-WWDR would be unprecedented among FOSS pass apps — no prior art for cert-chain plumbing, WWDR root distribution, or rotation handling.

Why Ticketmaster SafeTix tickets cannot be imported into Walt — closed paths and rationale (research 2026-05-07): (1) Intent intercept of 'Add to Google Wallet' SDK — PayClient.savePasses(jwt) is an explicit intent to GMS, not interceptable; the web variant pay.google.com/gp/v/save/<JWT> is an auto-verified Google App Link (assetlinks.json), competing filters lose to Google Wallet on Android 12+. (2) JWT decode — Google's documented best practice keeps secrets server-side via object:insert; the JWT carries only an object ID. Ticketmaster follows this. Even if intercepted, payload is useless for reproducing barcodes. (3) Screen capture / accessibility — Ticketmaster's ticket Activity sets FLAG_SECURE: blocks MediaProjection, recents thumbnail, system screenshot, and a11y bitmap retrieval. Hard OS block. (4) Smart Tap HCE at gate — requires Google-provisioned merchant collector ECDH keys; cryptographically impossible without Google merchant onboarding. (5) PKPASS webServiceURL polling at TOTP cadence — Apple ~20 push/pass/day cap, Google Wallet 3/day; 15s rotation would need ~5760/day. Two orders over. (6) Reverse engineering — categorically off-limits for Walt's transparency-for-trust posture; DMCA §1201 exposure + 2025 patent suit. Bottom line: no FOSS or commercial third-party wallet (PassAndroid, FossWallet, Pass2U, WalletPasses, Catima) has solved holding a SafeTix ticket; the closed-loop is intentional product design, not an accidental gap.

walt-passes-android (and probably other walt repos) enforces sha_pinning_required=true and allowed_actions=selected with verified_allowed=true on GitHub Actions. Effects: workflows MUST reference actions by 40-char SHA (with version comment); only github-owned + verified-publisher actions run. android-actions org is NOT verified, so android-actions/setup-android@<sha> still fails the allowlist check and produces a startup_failure with NO annotation surfaced via the GitHub API or gh CLI — the only diagnostic is checking GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/permissions and verifying the publisher org's is_verified flag. Workaround: use ubuntu-latest's preinstalled Android SDK at $ANDROID_SDK_ROOT and top up specific platforms/build-tools via sdkmanager, instead of the action. gradle/actions and the actions/* org are verified, so they work fine SHA-pinned.
